equip.cite: Accessory structures generally (§ 7.01.01)
equip.text: "Any number of different accessory structures may be located on a parcel, provided that the following requirements are met... A. There shall be a permitted principal structure on the parcel... B. All accessory structures shall comply with standards pertaining to the principal use, unless exempted or superseded elsewhere in this chapter. C. Accessory structures shall not be located in a required buffer or landscape area. D. Accessory structures shall be included in all calculations of impervious surface water and stormwater runoff. E. Accessory structures shall be shown on any concept development plan with full supporting documentation. F. No accessory buildings used for industrial storage of hazardous, incendiary, noxious or pernicious materials shall be located nearer than 100 feet from any property line."

equip.cite: Accessory buildings, lots in recorded subdivisions or under 250 ft deep (§ 7.01.02.A.1)
equip.text: "a. Accessory buildings shall only be placed in side and rear yards and shall be set back three feet from side and rear property lines. b. Accessory buildings on lots facing multiple rights-of-way may be placed in any secondary front yard but shall be set back a minimum of three feet from the adjoining front property line and shall not impact visibility from any adjacent intersection or driveway. (1) If placed in a secondary front yard that abuts a primary front yard on an adjacent property, structures shall not be placed within any required front setback. c. Accessory buildings closer than five feet to the principal structure must meet the setbacks of said principal structure."

equip.cite: Accessory buildings, lots not in recorded subdivisions and lots 250 ft deep or greater (§ 7.01.02.A.2)
equip.text: "a. Accessory buildings shall be set back three feet from side and rear property lines and shall not be within any required front setback. b. [same secondary front yard rule] c. Accessory buildings closer than five feet to the principal structure must meet the setbacks of said principal structure."

equip.cite: Ground-mounted telecommunication utility structures (§ 7.01.05)
equip.text: "Ground-mounted telecommunication utility structures that provide public or private telecommunication utilities, including, but not limited to, cable internet, DSL, dialup, or fiber optic services, not to include telecommunication towers subject to section 7.05.05, may be placed on vacant or improved property, subject to the following standards: a. Structures shall not be placed closer than three feet to any property line. b. Structures shall not obstruct visibility from any adjacent driveway or intersection. c. Structures shall not modify, impede, or substantially affect any required landscape buffer in any way as to disrupt such buffer's ability to provide an audible or visual screen as required by chapter 6 of this LDC." This is the closest analogue in the code to a ground-mounted generator enclosure, but it is written for telecommunication utilities and does not name generators.

equip.cite: Building height exclusions (§ 6.00.02.E.3)
equip.text: "Calculation of maximum building heights shall not include water towers, utility facility, or appurtenances or attachments such as chimneys, elevator shafts, antennas, decorative architectural features, steeples, air conditioning equipment enclosures, cupolas, weather vanes, and other similar building features. All appurtenances or attachments which are exempt for purposes of calculating the maximum height shall not be habitable."

equip.cite: Eave overhangs (§ 6.00.02.B.3)
equip.text: "No eave overhang shall be closer than three feet from any property line."

equip.cite: Swimming pools (§ 7.01.04.A)
equip.text: "Swimming pools shall be placed only in side and rear yards. There shall be at least six feet between a building and the water's edge of an outdoor swimming pool. There will also be at least six feet between any side or rear property line or building line and the water's edge of an outdoor swimming pool."

equip.cite: Screen rooms, enclosed patios, porch coverings (§ 7.01.02.D)
equip.text: Allowed in R-1E, R-1, R-2, R-3 and MU: "1. Shall be at least three feet from any rear property line. 2. Shall not be placed within any front or side setback area."

equip.cite: Utility equipment serving manufactured homes, flood provisions (§ 5.05.13.H)
equip.text: "Utility equipment. Utility equipment that serves manufactured homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential, section R322."

equip.cite: Setbacks abutting unopened or terminating rights-of-way (§ 6.00.02.F.2)
equip.text: "For applicable properties, the front setback along such unopened or terminating right-of-way may be the same as the side setback according to the underlying zoning district... Such setback standard shall also apply to any accessory structures placed on an applicable property subject to all other applicable standards contained in chapter 7 of this Code."

equip.cite: NOT FOUND
equip.text: The words generator (as equipment), standby, emergency power, condenser, propane, LP-gas, HVAC, 'mechanical equipment' and 'pool equipment' appear nowhere in this LDC. 'Generator' occurs only in § 8 as 'traffic generators'. There is no permitted-projection / encroachment-into-a-required-yard section naming generators or A/C equipment, and no mechanical equipment screening standard.

equip.cite: Exterior equipment must be shielded from view - new single-family and duplex (§ 2.06.15 B.(5), PDF p.138)
equip.text: 'Exterior equipment, including, but not limited to, air conditioning equipment, heat pumps, generators and pool equipment, shall be shielded from view.' These design standards 'shall apply to all new single-family and duplex residential development. Mobile homes, properties within the Urban Code District, additions and restoration development are excluded from these provisions.'

equip.cite: Equipment tanks must meet principal-structure setbacks (§ 2.04.04 A.5, PDF p.102)
equip.text: 'Architectural features such as cornices, eaves, gutters, fireplaces, flower boxes, bay windows, decorative molding and balconies, and front staircases designed complementary to the principle structure, which are part of the structure or attached thereto, may project no more than three feet into a required setback area. Equipment tanks, filters, stairwells, stairways attached post construction, and enclosed floor space are not considered architectural features and, therefore, must meet principal structure setbacks, unless otherwise varied pursuant to other sections of the land development regulations.' This is the clause that governs an LP tank or a pad-mounted generator treated as an equipment tank: it gets no yard encroachment at all.

equip.cite: Setbacks must be free of structures over four feet (§ 2.04.04 A.4, PDF p.102)
equip.text: 'Excluding street walls, fences, and entryway arbors and bowers a setback must be free of structures that are higher than four feet.'

equip.cite: Accessory structure setbacks (§ 6.09.02 C, PDF p.545)
equip.text: '1. Setbacks. Accessory structures shall not be located between the front facade of the principal building and the front property line and shall only be permitted in side and rear yards, subject to minimum five-foot side and rear setbacks from the property line. On corner lots the side setback shall be ten feet. 2. Separation. There shall not be less than five feet separation between an accessory structure and the principal building. 3. Size. In a residential district the height of an accessory structure shall not exceed the height of the principal structure and the footprint of an accessory structure shall not exceed 50 percent of the footprint of the principal structure...' Not more than three accessory structures (excluding satellite antenna systems, swimming pools, fences, walls, hedges, enclosures and awnings) may be located on a parcel (§ 6.09.02). § 6.09.01: 'In cases of conflict with provisions in the Urban District Code, East Stuart District Code or S.E. Ocean Boulevard Overlay Zone, the provisions in those sections shall prevail.'

equip.cite: East Stuart - shielding from street (§ 3.02.04 F.2, PDF p.220-221)
equip.text: 'Shielding from street. Sheds, exposed pumps, electrical meters, heat pumps, generators, pool equipment, air conditioning compressors, clothes lines, antennas, satellite dishes, outdoor storage, and similar structures and uses shall not be located between the front of a building and a street. Listed items and similar structures shall be shielded from view from public rights-of-way. All rooftop utilities and facilities, such as air conditioning units, shall be screened so as to not be visible from public view, including from balconies and windows of adjacent buildings.' ('generators' is hyphenated across the line break in the printed page as 'genera- tors'.) Figure ESN-09 sets 'Placement for Accessory Structures and Outbuildings' at 5' rear/side.

equip.cite: Creek District - shielding from street (§ 3.04.04 F.2, PDF p.291)
equip.text: Identical text: 'Shielding from street. Sheds, exposed pumps, electrical meters, heat pumps, generators, pool equipment, air conditioning compressors, clothes lines, antennas, satellite dishes, outdoor storage, and similar structures and uses shall not be located between the front of a building and a street. Listed items and similar structures shall be shielded from view from public rights-of-way. All rooftop utilities and facilities, such as air conditioning units, shall be screened so as to not be visible from public view, including from balconies and windows of adjacent buildings.' Figure CD-09 sets 'Placement for Accessory Structures and Outbuildings' at 5' rear/side in all four Creek columns.

equip.cite: Urban Code - prohibited uses in front yard (§ 3.01.03 F / H, PDF p.190)
equip.text: 'Prohibited uses in front yard. The following uses shall be prohibited within all Urban Code Districts: 1. Clothes lines and other clothes drying apparatus. 2. Electrical meters. 3. Air conditioning equipment, including window units on the building facade. 4. Antennas and satellite dishes. 5. Chain link fences. 6. Fences greater than four feet in height. 7. Stockade fences.'

equip.cite: Urban Code - screens (§ 3.01.04 N, PDF p.192)
equip.text: 'Screens. All rooftop utilities and facilities such as air conditioning units, as well as all exterior mechanical equipment, shall be screened so as to not be visible from public view, including from balconies and windows of adjacent buildings.'

equip.cite: Urban waterfront - equipment height in a vista (§ 3.01.03 E.1.d, PDF p.171)
equip.text: 'A vista shall be a designated area along the side of a property that provides an unobstructed view from any public right-of-way to the St. Lucie River or its tributaries, and shall be the same width as the required side setback. Only ten-foot clear trunk plant material and decorative fencing shall be located within the vista. Any equipment such as air conditioning units within a vista shall be not more than three feet in height, unless required by any applicable flood zone regulations.'

equip.cite: Screening of mechanical equipment in service areas (§ 6.04.10 B, PDF p.513-514)
equip.text: 'Buffering and screening. Loading areas or docks, outdoor storage, trash collection, mechanical equipment, trash compaction, truck parking, recycling, rooftop equipment and other service function areas shall be fully screened and out of view from adjacent properties at ground view level when located along primary facades or within view of public rights-of-way or residentially zoned properties.'

equip.cite: No structures or mechanical equipment in a common boundary buffer (§ 6.04.06, PDF p.508)
equip.text: 'Buffer use. No structures, mechanical equipment, trash receptacles, parking areas, or internal driveways shall be located in the common boundary buffer within 15 feet of the property line.'

equip.cite: Parapet concealment of roof equipment (§ 2.04.07 A.2, PDF p.106)
equip.text: 'A parapet wall shall not exceed 24 inches in height, provided however, a greater height of up to ten feet may be permitted by the city development director if necessary to conceal rooftop utilities such as stairway and elevator bulkheads and other roof equipment. No height of greater than 24 inches shall be permitted for more than 40 percent of any facade of a building.'

equip.cite: S.E. Ocean Boulevard Overlay - utility devices (§ 3.03.02 A.3.e and B.3.d, PDF p.270, 272)
equip.text: 'All utility devices and trash receptacles must be visually screened from public right-of-way.'

equip.cite: No separation distance to windows, air intakes or LP tanks found
equip.text: Nothing in the LDC sets a numeric clearance between a generator or other mechanical equipment and a window, an air intake, a property line, or an LP tank. The only numeric equipment distance printed anywhere in the code is the three-foot height limit on equipment in a UW vista. 'Propane' and 'LP gas' appear only in the Ch. XII definition of a gasoline or other motor fuel service station and in the telecommunications-tower siting review. Those separations are presumably left to the Florida Building Code and NFPA.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment — exemption from side and rear setbacks (the governing rule)
equip.text: Section 3-903.I, Required setbacks: 'I. Mechanical equipment. 1. Except as provided in subsection H(2) of this section, air conditioning equipment, pool equipment and similar mechanical equipment not enclosed within a building shall be exempt from side and rear setback requirements but shall be screened from any public right-of-way and adjacent properties. 2. No air conditioning equipment, pool equipment or similar mechanical equipment shall be permitted within a reduced side setback which has been approved as a Level One flexible standard development or as a Level Two flexible development.'

equip.cite: Definition of 'mechanical equipment' (brings generators and propane tanks within the rule above)
equip.text: Article 8 definitions: 'Mechanical equipment means outdoor mechanical, electrical, and communication equipment including heating, air conditioning, and ventilation equipment; venting and vent terminations for commercial hoods; mechanical penthouses; electrical and communication equipment, panels, and cabinets; satellite dishes; pool equipment such as heaters, filters, and pumps; generators; propane tanks; and similar features.' The code contains no separate 'generator' or 'standby power' section; generators are regulated as mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: Swimming pools and screened pool enclosures
equip.text: Section 3-903.H: 'Swimming pools and screened pool enclosures shall comply with the setbacks required in the applicable zoning district for the principal use, unless otherwise permitted pursuant to flexibility criteria in that district.' (This is the subsection H referred to by 3-903.I.1 and 3-903.I.2.)

equip.cite: Freestanding radio and television antennas
equip.text: Section 3-903.G: 'Freestanding, (i.e., not affixed on top of a building), radio and television antennas shall be set back from all property lines a distance equal to 50 percent of the height of the antenna.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment — placement and screening (design standards, Article 3 Division 5)
equip.text: : 'D. Mechanical equipment. 1. Equipment shall be placed on roofs or to the rear or side of buildings and shall not be placed between any right-of-way and the principal structure(s). 2. Equipment screening. a. Ground-mounted mechanical equipment shall be screened from public view by landscape materials or architecturally finished walls and enclosures designed consistent with the exterior facade of the building or other fencing as approved by the Community Development Coordinator. b. Rooftop-mounted mechanical equipment shall be screened by a parapet wall, articulated roofline or other roof screen, or similar device that is integrated into the building's architectural design and of a height equal to or exceeding the height of the equipment being screened. c. Elevator equipment rooms or similar mechanical equipment enclosures shall be designed to complement the design of the street-facing building facades and shall be clad on all sides in material used on street-facing facades.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment — US 19 District
equip.text: Appendix B, Section B-606: 'Outdoor mechanical, electrical, and communication equipment, including heating, air conditioning, and ventilation equipment; venting and vent terminations for commercial hoods; electric meters; mechanical penthouses; electrical and communication equipment, panels, and cabinets; satellite dishes; and similar features shall be located and designed to meet all of the following standards. A Equipment Placement — Equipment shall be placed on roofs or to the rear or side of buildings and shall not be placed in front setbacks or between any street and any building. B Equipment Screening — 1. Ground-mounted mechanical equipment shall be screened from public view by landscape screens or architecturally-finished walls and enclosures designed consistent with the exterior facade of the building. 2. Rooftop-mounted mechanical equipment shall be screened by a parapet wall, articulated roofline or other roof screen, or similar device that is integrated into the building's architectural design and of a height equal to or exceeding the height of the mechanical equipment being screened. 3. Elevator penthouses shall be designed to complement the design of street-facing building facades and shall be clad on all sides in material used on street-facing facades.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment — Downtown District
equip.text: Appendix C, Section C-606: 'A. Equipment Placement. Equipment, shall be placed on roofs or to the rear or side of buildings and shall not be placed in front setbacks or between any street and any building. B. Equipment Screening. 1. Ground-mounted mechanical equipment shall be screened from public view by landscape screens or architecturally-finished walls and enclosures designed consistent with the exterior façade of the building. 2. Rooftop-mounted mechanical equipment shall be screened by a parapet wall, articulated roofline or other roof screen, or similar device that is integrated into the building's architectural design and of a height equal to or exceeding the height of the mechanical equipment being screened. 3. Elevator equipment room or similar mechanical equipment enclosures shall be designed to complement the design of street-facing building façades and shall be clad on all sides in material used on street-facing façades.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment — height exception
equip.text: : '(3) Elevator equipment rooms and like mechanical equipment enclosures shall be permitted to project up to 16 feet higher than the maximum height otherwise specified for the zoning district assigned to the property.' Also '(1)... radio and television antennas shall be permitted to project ten feet higher than the maximum height otherwise specified for the zoning district within which the antenna is located. Parabolic and other geometrically shaped antenna shall not be permitted this height increase.' and '(4) Parapet walls constructed on buildings with flat roofs shall be permitted to extend not higher than 42 inches over the maximum height specified for the zoning district in which the building is located.'

equip.cite: Fuel storage at marinas
equip.text: : 'No fuel storage facility or sanitary pump-out station holding tank shall be located over water.'

deerfield_beach.source: Land Development Regulations, Chapter 98, Article III (Zoning District Regulations), Sec. 98-61 Schedule of dimensional regulations, plus the per-district stand

gen.cite: Generators — landscape screening (Sec. 98-80(j)(2))
gen.text: "(2) Generators. a. New development. Generators and above ground gas tanks shall be fully screened on all visible non-accessible portions with hedge material equal to the height of the generator and the gas tanks. b. Existing development. Except when determined by the urban forester that screening is impracticable, generators and above ground gas tanks installed on existing developed properties shall be fully screened on all visible non-accessible portions with hedge material equal to the height of the generator and the gas tanks. c. In cases where nonresidential property abuts residential property, the city can require such additional landscape as is necessary to protect the aesthetics and minimize the impact on the abutting residential area."

equip.cite: A/C units, pool circulation pumps and similar mechanical equipment (Sec. 98-73(1)b)
equip.text: "Yard encroachments such as, air conditioning units, pool circulation pumps and similar mechanical equipment may be located within a required rear, side or waterfront yard, provided there are no encroachments closer than three feet from the adjacent lot line and are screened from public view."

equip.cite: Accessory structures in R-districts (Sec. 98-73(1)a)
equip.text: "Accessory structures may be located within a required rear yard provided, however, no accessory structure may be erected or located: 1. Within a public utility easement, unless approved by the public utility and the City of Deerfield Beach; 2. In a required front yard; 3. In excess of 15 feet in height.; 4. Within five feet of any side or rear lot line and within 15 feet of the street side (corner) lot line, and waterfront lot line."

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening (Sec. 98-71(f))
equip.text: "All mechanical equipment shall be screened in a manner approved by the development review committee and the community appearance board."

equip.cite: Above-ground elements — screening (Sec. 98-80(j)(1))
equip.text: "Dumpsters, sewer lift stations, transformers, switchboxes, air conditioning units, mechanical equipment, cabinets, pedestals and all other above ground freestanding utility equipment or enclosure elements shall be fully screened on all non-accessible portions with a 36-inches-tall, continuous hedge at time of planting."

equip.cite: Yard encroachments generally (Sec. 98-71(c))
equip.text: "Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as hereinafter provided..." — the listed exceptions are sills/belt courses (12 in.), roof overhangs/cornices/eaves (not over one-third of the required yard, max 5 ft.), chimneys/fireplaces/pilasters (2 ft.), awnings (no closer than 1 ft. to a lot line), fire escapes/stairways/balconies (5 ft. into a rear yard, 3 ft. into a side yard). Mechanical equipment is not in this list; it is handled by Sec. 98-73(1)b.

equip.cite: Liquefied petroleum gas bulk storage — definition (Sec. 98-3)
equip.text: "Liquefied petroleum gas bulk storage means a single container with a capacity of 2,000 gallons or more or multiple containers with an aggregate capacity of 4,000 gallons or more.". In I-2 the code permits "Liquefied petroleum gas storage, fill and distribution, provided: a. Bulk storage of liquefied petroleum gas is not permitted"; in I, "Storage of petroleum products and liquefied petroleum gas if solely for the use of the permitted use".

gen.cite: Permanent emergency generators (general, § 4.02.01 D.13)
gen.text: Permanent emergency generators may be placed within the rear yard with a 10-foot rear yard setback. Permanent emergency generators may encroach into side yards up to 36 inches. Generators are not permitted to encroach into required front yards. For single-family and two-family dwelling units, see LDC section 5.03.07 for exceptions and requirements. Above-ground fuel tanks for the generators are subject to the same setbacks; however, underground tanks are not subject to setback requirements. In order to reduce noise during required routine exercising of the generators, this exercising is restricted to operating the generator for no more than 30 minutes, once every seven days, during the hours of 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. and shall not exceed sound level limits for Manufacturing and Industrial uses as set forth in Ordinance No. 90-17, the Noise Ordinance, as amended. All permanent emergency generators must be equipped with sound attenuating housing to reduce noise.

gen.cite: Permanent emergency generators at facilities with fuel pumps (§ 4.02.01 D.13.a)
gen.text: Permanent emergency generators and related fuel storage installed at existing facilities with fuel pumps may encroach into any required side or rear yards, provided the encroachment does not create a hazard to pedestrian or vehicular traffic.

gen.cite: Permanent emergency generators at assisted living facilities and nursing homes (§ 4.02.01 D.13.b)
gen.text: Permanent emergency generators and related fuel storage installed at existing assisted living facilities or nursing homes that are subject to LDC section 5.05.04 E. may encroach into any required side or rear yards or buffers, provided the encroachment does not create a hazard to pedestrian or vehicular traffic.

gen.text: Non-waterfront/non-golf-course lots AND waterfront/golf-course lots, row 'Permanent emergency generators': Front = 'Not permitted in front of building'; Side = SPS (calculated same as principal structure for the zoning district); Rear = 10 feet; Structure to structure (if detached) = N/A. Footnote 1 to that row: see LDC section 4.02.01 D for exemptions and exclusions from required yards.

gen.text: Permanent emergency generators for single-family and two-family dwellings shall be permitted as an accessory use and located in accordance with LDC section 5.03.07 Table 1.

table.caution: § 5.03.07 D overrides all of the above for fuel type: a diesel or gasoline generator must sit at least 15 ft from ANY lot line.

gen.cite: Generator location and measurement (§ 5.03.07 C.3)
gen.text: Permanent emergency generators may be located in the required front, side and rear yard setback in accordance with the following in Table 1. All distance setback and separation requirements shall be measured from the most restrictive of the generator's enclosure or exhaust outlet and adhere to the following: (a) When located underneath the dwelling unit, the exhaust outlet shall be vented outside of the dwelling unit above the roof line. (b) Generators may be allowed in the front yard, at a distance no greater than six feet from the dwelling unit in zoning districts with 35 feet front yard setback or greater and shall require a vegetative screen. For corner lots, the generator may be allowed in the front yard which has the longest street frontage utilizing the side yard generator setback standards in Table 1. (c) Generators located in the rear yard of a waterfront lot shall require a vegetative screen.

gen.cite: Diesel and gasoline generators (§ 5.03.07 D)
gen.text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, diesel or gasoline powered generators shall be set back a minimum of 15 feet from any lot line.

gen.cite: Carbon monoxide detector (§ 5.03.07 C.4)
gen.text: If any exterior wall openings are within 10 feet of the generator's exhaust outlet, at least one carbon monoxide detector shall be installed inside the structure near the exterior wall openings and on each floor level.

gen.cite: Manufacturer's locational specifications (§ 5.03.07 C.1)
gen.text: Permanent emergency generators shall adhere to all generator manufacturer's locational specifications and applicable federal, state, and local code requirements. The manufacturer's locational specifications shall be concurrently reviewed with the applicable electrical, structural, mechanical, gas piping, and storage tank permits.

equip.cite: Ground mounted air conditioners, pool equipment, well pumps (§ 4.02.01 D.9)
equip.text: Fences, walls and hedges, subject to section 5.03.02, ground mounted air conditioners, unenclosed pool equipment and well pumps, are permitted in required yards, subject to the provisions of section 4.06.00. This includes air conditioners that are ground mounted and those required to be elevated to meet flood elevation, including their supporting structures, provided the minimum separation of structures is maintained.

equip.cite: Window- or wall-mounted air conditioning units (§ 4.02.01 D.6)
equip.text: Window- or wall-mounted air conditioning units, chimneys, fireplaces, bay windows, or pilasters shall not project over two (2) feet into a required yard.

equip.cite: Every required yard open and unobstructed (§ 4.02.01 D.3)
equip.text: Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from thirty (30) inches above the general ground level of the graded lot upward to the sky except as hereinafter provided or as otherwise permitted in this LDC.

equip.cite: Accessory structures in A and E districts (§ 4.02.03 C)
equip.text: All accessory structures in Rural Agricultural (A) and Estates (E) zoning districts must meet principal structure setbacks.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment excluded from height limit (§ 4.02.01 D.1)
equip.text: The height limitations contained in LDC subsection 4.02.01 A. Table 2 do not apply to infrastructure in support of the building, such as mechanical penthouses, elevator shafts, stair shafts, mechanical equipment, mechanical screening, spires, belfries, cupolas, flagpoles, antennas, wireless communication facilities, water tanks, fire towers when operated by a branch of government, ventilators, chimneys, feed storage structures, silos, windmills, airport control towers, or other appurtenances placed above the roof level and not intended for human occupancy or for commercial purposes, subject to conditions a-d.

taylor_county.name: Taylor County
taylor_county.source: Land Development Code, Chapter 42. There is NO consolidated dimensional table. Setbacks are prose, grouped by land use district and by use category, in Sec. 42-

equip.cite: Accessory structures and uses generally (§ 42-407)
equip.text: "Accessory structures and uses are allowed in any land use district in connection with any principal lawfully existing use, subject to the requirements of section 42-432. All accessory structures or uses shall meet the requirements for the land use district in which the structure or use is located, as provided in section 42-409."

equip.cite: General standards for accessory structures (§ 42-432)
equip.text: "Any number of different accessory structures in the mixed use urban development land use district may be located on a parcel, provided that the following requirements are met: (1) No person shall construct an accessory structure within any land use district without first having obtained a permit for such construction from the county building official. (2) All accessory structures shall comply with standards pertaining to the principal use, unless exempted or superseded elsewhere in this chapter. (3) Accessory structures shall not be located in a required buffer, landscape area or minimum building setback area unless exempted or superseded elsewhere in this chapter. (4) Accessory structures shall be included in all calculations of impervious surface water and stormwater runoff. (5) Accessory structures shall be shown on a development plan." Note § 42-431: "Accessory structure permits are not required in other land use districts."

equip.cite: Storage buildings, private garages, carports, greenhouses, gazebos (§ 42-433, mixed use urban development only)
equip.text: "(1) No accessory buildings used for industrial storage of hazardous, incendiary, noxious or pernicious materials shall be located closer than 100 feet from any property line. (2) Storage buildings, gazebos, greenhouses, utility buildings and the like shall be permitted only in compliance with standards for distance between buildings and setbacks, if any, from property lines. (3) Storage and all other buildings regulated by this section shall be permitted only in side and rear yards, and shall not encroach into any required building setback. (4) Storage and other buildings regulated by this section shall be included in calculations for impervious surface, floor area ratio or any other site design requirements applying to the principal use of the lot."

equip.cite: Swimming pools and screen enclosures (§ 42-434, mixed use urban development only)
equip.text: "(1) Swimming pools shall be permitted in rear and side yards and shall not encroach into any required building setback except as otherwise set forth in this section. (2) Screen enclosures shall be considered a part of the principal structure and shall comply with standards for minimum distance between buildings, yard requirements and other building location requirements of this chapter, except that a swimming pool and its screened enclosure may be constructed to within eight feet of the rear property line... (4) No overhead electric power lines shall pass over any pool, nor shall any power line be nearer than ten feet horizontally from the pool's water edge."

equip.cite: Hard court recreational facilities (§ 42-438)
equip.text: "(1) Hard court recreational facilities shall be permitted only in side and rear yards and shall not encroach into required building setbacks. (2) Backstops, side stops and enclosures for hard court recreational facilities shall not exceed 14 feet in height."

equip.cite: LP gas storage as a land use (§ 42-408(9)e and (11))
equip.text: Under the public service/utility use group: "LP gas storage and/or distribution facilities for up to 2,000 gallons. This shall not be construed to prevent retail sales of LP gas in canisters or similar prefilled containers." Above that threshold it becomes an industrial use: "Such uses include, for example, LP gas storage and/or distribution exceeding 2,000 gallons, junkyards or..." These are use classifications, not setbacks.

equip.cite: Natural buffers (§ 42-715, Minimum setback guidelines)
equip.text: "A minimum 35-foot natural buffer shall be required from all wetlands and a 75-foot natural buffer shall be required from perennial rivers, streams and creeks identified as regionally significant areas within the comprehensive plan. The location of any dwelling structure shall be prohibited within these buffer areas, although nonintensive resource-based recreation activities shall be permitted within these buffer areas. For all uses other than single-family residential, agricultural and silvicultural adjacent to a work of the district as established in F.A.C. ch. 40B-4, a minimum buffer setback shall be required for rivers, streams and creeks, and their floodways, as required within such rule." Despite the section title, this prints no district setback.

equip.cite: Measurement of setbacks in subdivisions (§ 42-716.5)
equip.text: "Henceforth from the effective date of Ord. No. 2006-12, [adopted Aug. 7, 2006], all setbacks in subdivisions in the county, shall be measured from the edge of the right-of-way or easement, as established by the county engineer."

equip.cite: Steinhatchee height exceptions (§ 42-719(c)(2))
equip.text: "Church spires, chimneys, water towers, transmitter towers, smokestacks, flagpoles, television antennas, and similar structures and their necessary mechanical appurtenances, may, where specifically permitted by the commission, be erected above the height limits established in subsection (c)(1) of this section." (32 ft. cap in the Steinhatchee area.)

equip.cite: Intensive animal husbandry separation (§ 42-717(c)(4)b)
equip.text: For intensive activities subject to major development review, the planning board may impose "Minimum setbacks of buildings or activity from adjoining property, but not less than 500 feet from the property line and not less than 1,320 feet from a residential structure". Not a mechanical-equipment rule, but the only large separation distance the code prints.

AG1.minLotNote: No minimum lot area is printed. § 42-382(1) prints a density: "New residential development is allowable, not to exceed one unit per 20 acres" (§ 42-383 table: 1 du/20 ac). § 42-382(1) also says clustered residential units have a "minimum lot size of one acre".
AG1.lotWidthNote: § 42-720 prints a "Minimum Frontage in Feet" of 60 for AG 1, not a lot width. § 42-720(a): "the length of residential lots which are less than ten acres shall not exceed three times the width."
AG1.note: Agricultural 1. Setbacks recorded are § 42-717(c)(1), conventional single-family dwellings, which applies to Agricultural 1, Agricultural 2 and Agricultural/rural residential alike. Two alternative regimes for vested nonconforming lots of record: less than 2 acres — front 30, side 10, rear 15; 2 acres or more — front 50, side 20, rear 30. All permitted agricultural structures: 50 ft. from any lot line.

AG2.heightNote: No district height limit; Steinhatchee overlay 32 ft. only.

AGR.heightNote: No district height limit; Steinhatchee overlay 32 ft. only.

AGR.note: Agricultural/rural residential. The code abbreviates it AGR in § 42-382 and AGRR in the § 42-720 table. Setbacks per § 42-717(c), same as AG1/AG2. Maximum impervious surface ratio 40%; minimum open space ratio 60%.

MUR.lotWidthNote: § 42-720 prints "Minimum Frontage in Feet" of 170 for MURR, not a lot width.

gen.cite: Air conditioning units and mechanical equipment (including pool pumps and generators) - Sec. 516(7)
gen.text: "Air conditioning units, and mechanical equipment (including pool pumps and generators). In the R and PRO districts shall be setback a minimum of ten feet from the side plot line, five feet from the rear plot line, and shall not be located in the front yard less than 25 feet from the front property line. Air conditioning units, and mechanical equipment (including pool pumps and generators), are not permitted in the first 25 feet from the front property line in any land use district. Proposals which would place mechanical equipment in the front yard more than 25 feet from the front property line shall require planning and zoning board approval. Existing air conditioning units, and mechanical equipment (including pool pumps and generators), that were previously permitted and installed within the required yards may be replaced in their current location." (Appendix A, Sec. 516(7)).

gen.cite: Mechanical equipment screening - CR district design guidelines, Sec. 593 area (PDF p.533)
gen.text: "Mechanical equipment, including air conditioning (HVAC) units, generators, utility meters, antennae, and play equipment, should be screened from view from public rights-of-way except for alleyways. When installed on walls, appropriate landscaping or screening should be used so the equipment is not visible from the public right-of-way. When installed on roofs, they should be screened by surrounding roof features such as parapets or decorative elements. Vertical encroachment beyond the allowable building height in the Community Residential (CR) district is not permitted for mechanical equipment or its screening."

gen.cite: Generator noise - Ch. 15 noise ordinance (PDF p.274)
gen.text: Prohibits operating an internal combustion engine "except through a muffler or other device which will effectively prevent loud or explosive noises therefrom, except for the testing of emergency generators as required by law during the hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. weekdays."

gen.cite: Home occupation - Sec. 515 (PDF p.515)
gen.text: "No home occupation shall be conducted that requires the use of an electrical generator."

equip.cite: Air conditioning noise and anchorage - Ch. 6, Sec. 6-3 (PDF p.143)
equip.text: "All individual air conditioning units installed in walls or windows shall be securely anchored to the walls by approved methods..." and "(b) The following special requirements shall apply to the control and regulation of noise nuisance from air conditioning machinery: (1) All equipment existing or hereafter installed, regardless of location, shall be maintained in good working order. Equipment so located that normal operating noises create a nuisance to adjacent owners or occupants shall be provided with soundproofing, or sound-absorbing baffels, or enclosures, as approved... (2) All equipment on outer walls, on roofs, or in other exposed locations, which are unduly noisy, and which causes valid complaints from adjoining property owners or occupants, may be required to be relocated, redesigned and/or enclosed in noise-retarding materials..." No distance is given.

equip.cite: Accessory structures generally - Schedule of Regulations, R districts, 'Accessory Buildings' column
equip.text: "Location: In rear yard only as defined in Sec. 201, not less than 15 ft. from the main building and not less than 10 ft. from any plot line of contiguous plot that bounds a side or front yard or not less than 5 ft. from any other plot line... Accessory building shoreline setback; 15 ft."

equip.cite: No generator or mechanical-equipment placement rule in the Land Development Code
equip.text: Searching the whole document for generator, standby, emergency power, condenser, compressor, mechanical equipment, HVAC, air conditioning, pool pump, propane, LP-gas and liquefied petroleum turns up no setback, placement or screening standard for outdoor mechanical equipment in Chapters 50 or 54. The only rules that name a generator are in the noise ordinance (Chapter 10) and the parking ordinance.

equip.cite: Noise ordinance exemption for generators - Sec. 10-66(9)
equip.text: "Generators may be used during or as a result of an emergency or for the purpose of refrigerating medicines, or operating medical devices in the event of power outages even if it would not otherwise constitute an emergency situation; additionally a generator may be operated for no more than 30 minutes per month for maintenance purposes;".

equip.cite: Commercial-vehicle generator noise (PDF p.297)
equip.text: "No tractor-trailer, construction vehicle, or other commercial vehicle parked within 100 feet of the residential property shall have its engine, motor, generator, or other externally audible equipment running between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. except when the vehicle is being moved into or out of the parking area." And "No recreational vehicles or watercraft parked in any residential district within 50 feet of another residence shall have its engine, motor, generator or other externally audible equipment running between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m."

equip.cite: Accessory buildings in residential districts - Sec. 50-102(a)(2), (4)
equip.text: "Accessory buildings, garages, nonpermanent carports and screen enclosures shall be permitted in the side and rear yards only. No accessory buildings, garages, nonpermanent carports or screen enclosures shall be located in the front yard." Accessory buildings and nonpermanent carports in residential districts shall be "a. Located at least five feet from a lot line; b. Accessory buildings shall be located at least 35 feet from the 86.9 contour line of Lake Conway and nonpermanent carports shall be located at least 50 feet from the 86.9 contour line of Lake Conway; c. Located at least six feet from all other accessory buildings, nonpermanent carports, garages, or screen enclosures, on the same lot; d. Have a height of no more than 15 feet from the natural grade of the land;... g. A total maximum square footage of 300 square feet per accessory structure;... i. On corner lots, accessory buildings and nonpermanent carports shall be set back 20 feet from all rights-of-way." Note that an 'accessory building' is defined as "any building which is not structurally attached to the principal building, and has floor area larger than 25 square feet."

equip.cite: Yards / permitted projections - Sec. 54-132
equip.text: "(a) Every part of a required yard shall be open from its lowest point to the sky, unobstructed, except for the ordinary projections of sills, belt courses, cornices, buttresses, chimneys, flues and eaves attached to the primary structure and accessory buildings for not more than 24 inches... (d) Roof projections shall not extend into any required yard in excess of 24 inches... (g) In all districts, no structure shall be erected closer than 15 feet from a side street lot line or any intersection street right-of-way." No mechanical equipment is named among the permitted projections.

equip.cite: Public utilities - Sec. 54-134
equip.text: "Structures or uses required for such public utilities as gas substations, electric substations, telephone dial exchange buildings, radio and television stations and towers may be located in any district, as a special exception upon approval by the board after a review of the request and a detailed plot plan showing all improvements to be made. Security fences, a minimum of six feet in height shall be required around any gas or electric substation."

equip.cite: Screening between commercial and residential - Sec. 50-73(d)(1)
equip.text: "Wherever commercially zoned property abuts residentially zoned property, the owners and occupants of the commercial property must provide for the construction of a screening wall. The screening wall shall be a masonry wall at least eight feet in height."

gen.cite: Generators, permanently installed (Sec. 7.08.04, PDF p.590-591)
gen.text: The following standards shall apply to all permanently installed generators: (a) Generators are prohibited in the required front and street side yard and prohibited in front of the front building line of the principal structure. (b) Generators may be operated for testing purposes one (1) time per week, excluding Sundays, for a period not exceeding thirty (30) minutes between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. (c) A maximum of one (1) generator is allowed per single-family, duplex, or townhouse residential dwelling unit and one (1) generator is allowed per multiple family building. (d) Generators shall be set back a minimum of ten (10) feet from the rear property line in all zoning districts. (e) Generators shall be set back a minimum of three (3) feet from the side interior property line(s) in all zoning districts, but shall not be located within an easement.

gen.cite: Accessory structure definition includes generators (Article 3, Definitions, PDF p.527)
gen.text: "Accessory structures include all noise-producing equipment, such as air conditioning units, pool equipment, generators and the like that contribute to the comfort, convenience, or necessity of occupants in the principal building."

gen.cite: Yard encroachments (Sec. 7.07.06, PDF p.584)
gen.text: The enumerated permitted encroachments are cornices/awnings/eaves/gutters (2 ft, no nearer than 5 ft to a lot line); sills, leaders and belt courses (12 in.); fences and hedges; bay windows, oriels, balconies and chimneys (3 1/2 ft, no nearer than 5 ft to a side lot line or 15 ft to a rear lot line); and outside stairways (3 1/2 ft into a side or rear yard, no nearer than 5 ft to a side lot line). Generators, A/C condensers and pool equipment are NOT listed as permitted yard encroachments - they are governed by Sec. 7.08.04 and by the accessory-structure rules.

equip.cite: Accessory structures in general (Sec. 7.07.09, PDF p.586)
equip.text: (a) Accessory structures shall not be placed in the front yard. They may be placed in side yards, provide no structures are closer to the lot lines than five (5) feet, and provided further, that on a corner lot accessory structures are closer to the rear lot line than five (5) feet except when the rear property line abuts a public right-of-way. When the rear property line abuts a public right-of-way, accessory structures may be no closer than seven and one-half (7 1/2) feet from the property line. (b) Waterfront lots or lots of such "depth" as to allow a structure to be set back from a public right-of-way by a minimum of twenty-five (25) feet and a minimum of ten (10) feet from a principal dwelling are exempted from this provision. (c) A detached accessory structure defined as a building, shall not be located closer than ten (10) feet to the principal building, nor closer than five (5) feet to the side and rear lot lines, nor closer than ten (10) feet to any other accessory building on the same lot. [As printed - subsection (a) reads "are closer to the rear lot line than five (5) feet"; the code prints it that way.]

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment, CRA zoning overlay (Sec. 7.09.04(a)(6), PDF p.599)
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment for multifamily residential, nonresidential, office, commercial or industrial developments shall not be allowed any closer than ten (10) feet to either the property line or zoning district boundary line of a single-family or duplex residential development or zoning district; and shall be screened from adjoining property and from public view." (Applies within the Community Redevelopment Area zoning overlay; per Sec. 7.09.03 these standards apply in addition to or instead of, and supersede conflicting, standards found elsewhere in the LDC.)

equip.cite: Service areas and screening, CRA zoning overlay (Sec. 7.09.04(a)(4), PDF p.598)
equip.text: "Utilities and service areas. Building sites should locate service elements like trash dumpsters, loading docks and mechanical equipment away from the street front wherever possible. When elements such as dumpsters, utility meters, mechanical units and service areas cannot be located away from the street front, they should be screened..." ("should" = suggested guideline, not a regulatory requirement, per Sec. 7.09.03.)

equip.cite: Roof-mounted equipment, CRA zoning overlay (Sec. 7.09.04(b)(9), PDF p.601)
equip.text: "Roof-mounted electrical, mechanical, air conditioning and communications equipment shall be completely screened from adjacent properties and public view from the public right-of-way. The equipment screening shall be such that the equipment is not visible within a two hundred-foot radius. The radius shall be measured from the exterior side of the screen to a point ten (10) feet above finished grade. All mechanical equipment must be equipped with the manufacturer's recommended sound attenuation."

equip.cite: Yard exemptions (Sec. 7.07.05(b)(1), PDF p.583)
equip.text: "The following structures shall be exempt from the minimum yard requirements set forth in this Code, provided however that these exemptions shall not permit encroachment into the visibility triangle: a. Underground and overhead utility equipment; b. U.S. Post Office authorized mail boxes; c. Bus shelters and bus benches; d. Public bicycle shelters; e. Backflow preventers; f. Any similar structure or device as determined by the city manager or designee."

equip.cite: Non-habitable accessory buildings (Sec. 7.08.07(b), PDF p.595)
equip.text: "(3) Non-habitable accessory buildings may be located as close as five (5) feet from the abutting interior side or rear property lines, with approval from the building official... and may be located no closer than five (5) feet to a street corner side property line. (5) In no event shall a non-habitable accessory structure or any part thereof, be permitted within an easement. (6) No accessory buildings used for industrial storage of hazardous, incendiary, noxious or dangerous materials shall be located nearer than one hundred (100) feet from any property line." Maximum height 12 ft.

equip.cite: Swimming pools (Sec. 7.08.08(b), PDF p.596)
equip.text: "(1) No portion of a swimming pool outside a building shall be located at a distance less than six (6) feet from a building measured from the building to the water's edge. (2) No portion of a swimming pool outside a building shall be located at a distance less than four (4) feet from any side or rear property line, or building line measured from the property line to the water's edge."

equip.cite: Corner lots (Sec. 7.07.05(c), PDF p.583-584)
equip.text: "On lots having frontage on more than one (1) street at an intersection, a required front yard shall only be required on one (1) street frontage; the required side yard fronting the other street shall be reduced by fifty (50) percent of the required front yard for the district, but shall not be less than fifteen (15) feet."

equip.cite: Height exclusions for mechanical appurtenances (Sec. 7.07.04(b), PDF p.582)
equip.text: "...the height limitations of this Code shall not apply to chimneys, spires, cupolas, gables, scenery lofts, domes, birdhouses, monuments, water towers, water tanks, smokestacks, or other similar roof structures and mechanical appurtenances... provided, however: (1) No such structure, when located on a building roof, shall occupy an area greater than ten (10) percent of the total roof area. (2) No such structure shall be used for any purpose other than a use incidental to the main use of any principal building. (3) No such structure over thirty-five (35) feet in height, excluding signs, shall be located nearer to a lot line less than a distance equal to its height, except for public or private utility facilities/use..."

st_petersburg.name: St. Petersburg
st_petersburg.source: City Code Part II, Chapter 16 (Land Development Regulations). District list from Sec. 16.10.010.1 'Zones'. Every base district's envelope was read from its own

equip.cite: Ancillary equipment - definition (Sec. 16.50.020.4.2.A)
equip.text: 'For the purposes of this section, "ancillary equipment" means: 1. Standard equipment such as air conditioning compressors, central heating equipment, swimming pool and spa pumps and filters, lawn irrigation pumps, propane tanks, and similar equipment listed in the setbacks, allowable encroachments section; and 2. Renewable energy devices and other sustainable development technologies including, but not limited to, solar photovoltaic (pv) panels, solar hot water, solar pool heaters, tankless water heaters, geothermal heat pumps, gray-water systems and rainwater harvesting devices, such as rain barrels and cisterns.' A permanently installed standby generator is not named; it would fall under 'similar equipment'.

equip.cite: Ancillary equipment, residential - setback (Sec. 16.60.050.2 chart, PDF p.1321)
equip.text: 'Ancillary equipment, residential (see accessory structures section for additional requirements).' Side and Rear: 'No closer to property line than 3 ft.' Street side: 'No more than 4 ft. from setback line.' The same two figures are printed for both district groups, the NT, NTM, CRT, CCT, IT group and the NS, NSM, NMH, NPUD, CRS, CCS, IS, P group. No front-yard row is printed for ancillary equipment.

equip.cite: Ancillary equipment, commercial - setback (Sec. 16.60.050.2 chart, PDF p.1321)
equip.text: 'Ancillary equipment, commercial (see accessory structures section for additional requirements).' Side and Rear: 'No closer to property line than 5 ft.' Street side: 'No closer to property line than 10 ft.' Same for both district groups. The chart header adds: 'Ancillary Equipment, refer to Section 16.50.020.4.2.(C) for development standards for zoning districts not listed in this chart.'

equip.cite: Ancillary equipment in traditional and suburban zoning districts (Sec. 16.50.020.4.2.B)
equip.text: '1. Setbacks shall comply with those listed in the Setbacks, Allowable Encroachments Section. 2. The base of ground-mounted equipment shall not exceed one foot above ground level. Elevated equipment shall be mounted on a cantilevered platform attached to the side of a structure and not exceed one foot above the minimum design flood elevation required by City Code for flood protection. If the base of ground-mounted equipment exceeds one foot above the ground level or design flood elevation then it shall be located behind the rear facade of the structure or on top of the roof. 3. Existing equipment that was lawfully installed in a nonconforming location shall be permitted to be replaced with equipment of a reasonably equivalent or lower industry rating or performance standard. 4. The sides of any new or replacement equipment facing or visible from a street, excluding alleys, shall be screened with material that is compatible with the architectural style of the principal structure, landscaping, or a six-foot-tall decorative fence or wall.'

equip.cite: Ancillary equipment in all other districts (Sec. 16.50.020.4.2.C)
equip.text: 'In all other zoning districts, ancillary equipment shall comply with the following: 1. Where a nonresidential use abuts another nonresidential use, no setback shall be required. 2. Where a nonresidential use abuts a residential use or zoning district, ancillary equipment shall be subject to a setback equal to one-half of the setback required for the principal building. 3. All ancillary equipment shall be shielded from view from the adjacent properties and streets, excluding alleys, by a solid enclosure such as a fence or wall. Fences and walls shall be subject to the height restrictions and design standards of the zoning district.'

equip.cite: Ancillary equipment - allowable height encroachment (Sec. 16.60.020.3, PDF p.1311)
equip.text: Allowable Height Encroachments table, additional height bonus: 'Ancillary equipment - rooftop: 15 ft.' and 'Ancillary equipment, housing for: 15 in.' 'When a variance to height has been granted, no additional height bonus which is set forth in this section is allowed.'

'All mechanical equipment and utility functions (e.g. electrical conduits, meters, HVAC equipment) shall be located behind the front facade line of the principal structure. Mechanical equipment that is visible from the primary street shall be screened with a material that is compatible with the architecture of the principal structure, landscaping, or a 6-foot-tall decorative fence or wall.' (The trailing 'landscaping, or a 6-foot-tall decorative fence or wall' appears in the NTM, CRT and some other districts; the shorter form ending at 'principal structure' appears in NSM, NPUD, CRS, CCT, IT, IS, IC and RC.)

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening, IS district accessory structures and equipment (Sec. 16.20.110.6)
equip.text: 'All mechanical equipment (ground or roof), including, but not limited to, air conditioning condensers, heating units, electric meters, satellite dishes, irrigation pumps, ice machines and dispensers, outdoor vending machines, and propane tanks, displays and refilling areas, visible from the public right-of-way, an adjacent neighborhood zoning district or adjacent residential use shall be screened using architectural features consistent with the principal structure.'

equip.cite: Landscaping adjacent to mechanical equipment on site (Sec. 16.40.060, PDF p.997 and p.1002)
equip.text: 'Mechanical equipment, (e.g. backflow preventers, utility cabinets, air conditioners, etc.) visible from streets, excluding alleys, shall be landscaped with a continuous hedge comprised of shrubs planted no more than 30 inches on center or a decorative fence or architectural feature. Landscaping shall be installed no less than three feet from the equipment to allow for access, maintenance and required air flow.'

equip.cite: Wooden platform for energy meter in a flood zone (Sec. 16.60.050.2 chart, PDF p.1324)
equip.text: Side and Rear: 'No closer to property line than 2 ft. for platforms up to 3 ft. above grade, or no closer to property line than 2.5 ft. for platforms up to 4 ft. above grade, or no closer to property line than 3 ft. for platforms up to 5 ft. above grade.' Same for both district groups.

equip.cite: Accessory storage structure use restriction (Sec. 16.50.020.4.1)
equip.text: 'Use restrictions. The structure shall only be utilized for storage and shall not be used for operation of mechanical equipment.' - an exempt accessory storage shed cannot be used to house running mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: General encroachment limits (Sec. 16.60.050.1 and .2)
equip.text: 'When a variance to a setback has been granted, no additional encroachment which is set forth in this section is allowed.' 'Required building setbacks that are less than what is required by this section shall supersede setbacks established by this section. No structure shall encroach in or over any easement where the structure would interfere with the use of the easement for its intended purpose... Encroachments are not allowed in connection with zero lot line structures. Encroachments for a structure or other improvement taller than 12 inches above grade is prohibited within the view triangles of waterfront yards.'

equip.cite: Emergency generator noise (City Code Sec. 11-53(12), outside Chapter 16, PDF p.504)
equip.text: 'Emergency generators and other emergency equipment. a. Generators and other equipment designed to be used during emergency situations shall be exempt from this article during periods of emergency. b. Testing of generators and other equipment designed to be used during an emergency situation is exempt from this article between the hours of 10:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Any testing shall use the minimum time necessary for the test and shall not occur more than once a week. The time of the testing shall be scheduled to impact the least number of properties possible. c. Generators and other equipment designed to be used in emergency situations, which are not being tested or being used in a period of emergency, shall comply with section 11-54.'

equip.cite: Site plan submittal (PDF p.1418)
equip.text: 'Mechanical equipment - Location of all HVAC equipment, backflow preventers, water meters, generators, transformer boxes and speaker boxes, etc.' must be shown on the site plan.

equip.cite: No generator section
equip.text: Chapter 94 contains no section governing standby generators, emergency power, air conditioning condensers or pool equipment as such.

equip.cite: Sec. 94-2, definition of 'Essential services'
equip.text: "Essential services are limited to certain utilities installations of water, sewer, gas, telephone and electrical systems such as substations, lift stations and similar installations. Electric or gas generation plants are not essential services under this definition." Essential services are a conditional use in R-1AA, C-1A, C-1, C-2, M-1 and ROS (in ROS 'subject to buffering').

equip.cite: Sec. 94-204(c)(6), Building exterior standards on major city thoroughfares
equip.text: "Dumpsters and mechanical equipment such as air conditioners and compressors shall be screened from public view. The screening design shall be compatible with and part of the building design." This section applies to all new development on property abutting 19th Street, Crill Avenue, Husson Avenue, Madison Street, Main Street, Moody Road, Moseley Avenue, Palm Avenue, Reid Street, St. Johns Avenue, State Road 19, US 17 and Zeagler Drive; single family detached and duplex units, locally designated historic districts and sites, properties in a downtown overlay zone, and walls or roofs not visible from a major thoroughfare are exempt.

equip.cite: Sec. 94-203(f), Downtown design standards - roofs
equip.text: "Parapets shall be required when necessary to shield rooftop equipment from view (also for Periphery)."

equip.cite: Sec. 94-187, Setbacks for utility poles, fences and walls
equip.text: "(a) Utility poles as required by public utility companies shall not be required to meet the setback requirements for structures. (b) On residentially zoned property, fences and walls used as fences may be erected or maintained along or adjacent to a lot line to a height not exceeding six feet. Any fence constructed forward of the established front building line shall not be over four feet in height. However, no solid fence or wall shall be constructed forward of the established building line in front yards."

equip.cite: Sec. 94-188(d), Disaster shelters (the closest thing to an at-grade equipment allowance)
equip.text: "Underground shelters intended for occupancy by more than two families are permitted at any location in any yard, notwithstanding other provisions of this chapter, provided the structure or its overburden does not exceed 30 inches above the natural grade of the yard."

equip.cite: Sec. 94-189, Swimming pools
equip.text: "No swimming pool shall be so located, designed, operated or maintained as to interfere with the rights of the adjoining property... Swimming pools shall be classed as an accessory use and shall be subject to all yard requirements of accessory uses. All swimming pools shall be enclosed by a fence, wall or equivalent barrier a minimum of six feet in height." The 'yard requirements of accessory uses' are set by Sec. 94-183 (Location of accessory buildings and uses) and Sec. 94-184 (Yards), which are on the code pages missing from this PDF - see gaps.

gen.cite: Permanently installed generators — setback (§ 82-277(1))
gen.text: 'Setbacks. Pads for permanently installed generators shall be located or installed, as far from the property line as possible but in no case less than five feet from any property line and no more than the legal allowable distance from a structure required by the most current version of the National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standard for "Engines Located Outdoors" (NFPA 37 - 4.1.4). Generators installed in enclosed spaces such as mechanical rooms or garages shall be installed in compliance with the most current version of NFPA 110 & 111. This provision shall not place any additional limitations on generators not located within any required setback.' The section heading limits it: 'Special regulations for permanently installed generators and accompanying fuel tanks for properties developed prior to the effective date of this ordinance.'

gen.cite: Permanently installed generators — pad elevation (§ 82-277(2))
gen.text: 'Vertical elevation. When a permanently installed generator is located within an "AE" flood zone, the top elevation of the pad shall be no lower than the base flood. In "X" or "X-500" zones, the minimum elevation of the pad shall be set at an elevation no less than eight inches above the roadway crown. The pad shall be a minimum of three and one-half inches thick and comply with all of the standards of the Florida Building Code, established engineering standards and the manufacturer's installation requirements and/or guidelines.'

gen.cite: Generator fuel tanks (§ 82-277(3))
gen.text: 'Fuel tanks for accompanying permanently installed generators. Above-ground fuel tanks are accessory structures subject to the setbacks of the appropriate zoning district.' In R-1 that is § 82-274(3): 50 ft front (one story), 20 ft side, 25 ft rear.

gen.cite: Generator and fuel tank screening (§ 82-277(4))
gen.text: 'Screening. Generators and above-ground fuel tanks shall be screened from public view by landscaping or other material acceptable to the building official.'

gen.cite: Generator testing (§ 82-277(5))
gen.text: 'Testing. The testing of a permanently installed generator shall be limited to once per week for a period of no more than 30 minutes between 8:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., and further limited to Monday through Saturday.'

gen.cite: Generator permits (§ 82-277(6))
gen.text: 'Permits required. Permits for a residential generator for standby electrical power and accompanying fuel tank permit and any plumbing associated therewith permit shall be obtained from the town building official prior to the installation of the generator and fuel tank.'

gen.cite: Equipment pad definition (§ 82-1)
gen.text: 'Equipment pad means any structure or enclosures constructed of any materials intended to house or support any piece of equipment located permanently on a property such as, but not limited to, air conditioners, swimming pool pumps and heaters, well and irrigation pumps, water softeners, etc., with the exception of stand-by generator equipment that is intended for temporary emergency back up electrical service specified in section 82-277.' A separate definition: 'Air conditioning pad means a concrete slab or other device employed to support any air conditioning system, placed on the finished grade of a lot or otherwise projecting from an exterior wall of any structure.'

equip.cite: Equipment pads are structures (§ 82-1, definition of 'Structure')
equip.text: 'Structure means anything constructed or erected, the use of which requires permanent location on the ground or attached to something having permanent location on the ground and shall include equipment pads, antennas, sheds, docks and piers or other structures... In addition, any concrete, asphalt or other permanent surfacing placed upon a lot, such as but not limited to a patio, appurtenances or a pool decks adjacent to a swimming pool, with the exception of equipment pads shall not be considered a structure for the purpose of this chapter or for the purpose of determining setback lines.' So an equipment pad must meet the setback; a patio or pool deck need not.

equip.cite: Administrative waiver for an encroaching equipment pad (§§ 82-141, 82-142(5)a)
equip.text: § 82-141: 'the town building official shall grant administrative waivers for certain building encroachments into the setbacks that do not exceed one foot and for certain concrete equipment pads that do not encroach more than three feet into the setbacks.' § 82-142(5): the waiver is granted only if 'the building encroachment is no greater than one foot, or the equipment pad encroachment is no greater than three feet, into the setback requirement in effect on the date that the encroachment was created', adjacent owners have filed letters of no objection or 15 days have passed with none, the structure was built under a valid permit, the violation was a good faith error, and 'the setback violation existed prior to September 26, 2006.' This is after-the-fact relief for an existing encroachment, not a permission to build a new pad in the setback.

equip.cite: Accessory buildings and structures — location (§ 114-741)
equip.text: "Accessory buildings and structures, including apartment, garages, and utility sheds, shall not be constructed, erected or placed in any required front or side yard. Apartments, garage apartments, detached garages and other accessory structures greater than 300 square feet shall be located only in the buildable area of a lot and not in any required yard setback. Utility sheds or storage buildings that do not exceed 300 square feet may be located up to five feet of any rear lot line."

equip.cite: Accessory structures — general rules (§ 114-742.A)
equip.text: "Accessory structures and uses are permitted in conjunction with any principal use, provided that they are recognized as clearly incidental and subordinate to the principal use and do not alter the characteristics of the lot(s).... 2. Unless otherwise specified within this section: a. Accessory structures and uses in all zoning districts shall be prohibited in the required front yard or side setback and are to be located behind the principal structure on the lot.... 5. For double frontage lots and corner lots, accessory structures or uses shall not be located within the required yard setback unless screened by a hedge or wall at least six feet in height. 6. No accessory structure or use shall be permitted in any platted easement, unless otherwise specifically permitted by the easement dedication.... 7. All accessory structures require the issuance of building permits by the city building department." And, printed immediately before subsection A: "h. Any specific accessory use or structures which are not addressed within this chapter shall not be located on any lot."

equip.cite: Accessory structures on single-family or duplex lots (§ 114-742(2))
equip.text: "a. Accessory structures 300 square feet or less in floor area may be located in the rear and shall be set back at least five feet from the rear lot line yard provided a minimum five-foot separation is maintained from other building. b. The maximum height of accessory structures 300 square feet or less shall not exceed 12 feet. c. Accessory structures greater than 300 square feet in floor area shall be located within the building area.... f. A minimum five-foot separation between accessory structures and the principal building on the site shall be maintained. g. Accessory structures shall not cause the building coverage on the lot to exceed the maximum building coverage established for the zoning district."

equip.cite: Exceptions to minimum yard or lot coverage requirements (§ 114-761)
equip.text: "Every part of every yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground up by any structure, except as follows:" — the list covers only (1) breezeways and porte cocheres, (2) screened swimming pool enclosures, (3) outdoor covered patio areas (not less than 15 feet from a rear property line), and (4) building overhangs: "a. Sills or belt courses may project up to 12 inches into a required yard. b. Movable awnings may project up to three feet into a required yard except that, where such yard is less than six feet in width, such projection shall not exceed one-half the width of the yard. c. Building overhangs, chimneys, fireplaces or pilasters may project up to two feet into a required yard. d. Fire escapes, stairways and balconies which are not covered or not enclosed may project up to five feet into a required front or rear yard, or up to three feet eight inches into a required side yard. e. Hoods, canopies or marquees may project up to three feet into a required yard, but shall not be closer than one foot to any lot line." NO mechanical equipment, generator, condenser, pool pump or fuel tank is named anywhere in this list.

equip.cite: Swimming pools (§ 114-742.D)
equip.text: "1. Setbacks: a. Front yard. Swimming pools or appurtenances thereto shall be prohibited in any required principal front yard building setback. b. Corner side yard. Swimming pools or appurtenances thereto shall be prohibited in any required side yard building setback. c. Rear yard. The edge of deck for swimming pools shall not be closer than five feet from the rear and side property line. 2. Location in relationship to the principal structure. No swimming pool shall be constructed closer than five feet from any building; provided, however, that this paragraph shall not apply to swimming pools which are an integral part (footers) of new construction..."

equip.cite: Exceptions to height regulations (§ 114-744)
equip.text: "The height limitations contained in section 114-765 shall not apply to spires, belfries, cupolas, antennas, water tanks, ventilators, chimneys or other appurtenances usually required to be placed above the roof level and not intended for human occupancy."

equip.cite: Portable storage units (§ 114-745(e))
equip.text: "Portable storage units may be placed in any driveway area, but must be a minimum of 20 feet from the edge of any roadway and five from any side lot line." Size limited to 16 ft long by 8 ft wide on residential property; 30 days in any six consecutive months.

equip.cite: Shipping / intermodal containers (§ 114-742.E)
equip.text: Permitted only in CC-1, I-1 and I-2. "7. Shipping containers shall be located behind the front plane of a principal structure and shall not be located within the principal rear and side yard setbacks of the CC-1 (Commercial Corridor), I-1 (Wholesale-Light Industrial) and I-2 (Heavy Industrial) zoning districts, except that such containers that have a footprint of less than 250 square feet will be allowed to be placed within eight feet of the rear property line. 8. Shipping containers shall not be located within any easement.... 12. No plumbing or air conditioning shall be permitted inside of a shipping container."

equip.cite: Generators and compressors on recreational vehicles (§ 114-791(k))
equip.text: "The operation of compressors, generators or other noise-generating equipment associated with an RVE when parked on residential premises is prohibited." This is the only occurrence of the word "generators" in a placement/operation rule in the zoning chapter, and it bans RV generator operation on residential premises — it says nothing about a fixed standby generator.

equip.cite: Air conditioners — noise exemption (§ 26-29(b)(1))
equip.text: "The following uses and activities shall be exempt from noise level regulations except as listed in Table 1: (1) Air conditioners when functioning in accord with the manufacturers' standard mufflers and noise-reducing equipment in use and in proper operating condition according to standards promulgated by the American Refrigeration Institute."

equip.cite: Fixed-location mechanical equipment — site plan content (PUD preliminary plan, § 114-771)
equip.text: The preliminary plan must show the "Conceptual configuration of site including locations of proposed buildings, structures, fixed-location mechanical equipment (e.g., irrigation pumps, compactors, compressors, etc.), access drives and parking areas." A submittal requirement, not a setback.

equip.cite: Above-ground tanks in flood hazard areas (§ 94-46(b), (c))
equip.text: "Above-ground tanks, not elevated. Above-ground tanks that do not meet the elevation requirements of subsection (c) shall be permitted in flood hazard areas provided the tanks are anchored or otherwise designed and constructed to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions of the design flood, including the effects of buoyancy assuming the tank is empty and the effects of flood-borne debris." "Above-ground tanks, elevated. Above-ground tanks in flood hazard areas shall be attached to and elevated to or above the design flood elevation on a supporting structure that is designed to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement during conditions of the design flood." Anchoring/elevation only — no horizontal separation distance.

equip.cite: Utility equipment serving manufactured homes (§ 94-44(f))
equip.text: "Utility equipment that serves manufactured homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322."
