polk_county.name: Polk County
polk_county.source: Land Development Code, Chapter 2, § 205, Table 2.2 — Density and Dimensional Regulations for Standard Districts (with footnotes 1–24 at § 205); accessory and me

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment — projection into a setback (§ 208.B.4, PDF p.125)
equip.text: "Sills, eaves, cornices, chimneys, flues, mechanical equipment and similar projections may project into a setback area not more than three feet and shall not extend over adjacent properties except in accordance with Section 755 (zero-lot-line design)."

equip.cite: Accessory structure setbacks (§ 208.F, PDF p.126)
equip.text: "Accessory structure setbacks shall be in accordance with the district dimensional standards in Table 2.2." Table 2.2's interior side and interior rear cells are printed as Principal Structure / Accessory Structures, so the second number is the accessory setback (e.g. RL-4: interior side 7 / 5, interior rear 10 / 5).

equip.cite: Accessory structure location (§ 209.D.1–2, PDF p.127)
equip.text: "Accessory structures shall be located in the side or rear yard meeting the required setbacks. Only those accessory structures located within the Agriculture/Residential Rural land use district that are part of a bona fide agricultural use shall be permitted within any yard (front, side, or rear)..." "They shall not be located in a required buffer, minimum accessory structure setback area, public rights-of-way, or easement (unless authorized by the easement or approval is obtained from the easement holder)."

equip.cite: Attached accessory structures (§ 209.F, PDF p.127)
equip.text: "Roofed accessory structures physically attached or connected to the principal structure shall be considered a part of the principal structure and shall be subject to the same standards as the principal structure unless exempted or superseded elsewhere in this Code."

equip.cite: Prohibited accessory structures (§ 209.E, PDF p.127)
equip.text: "Vehicles, vehicle parts, boilers, walk-in freezers, and mobile homes shall not be used as accessory structures in any district."

equip.cite: A/C units in the non-residential compatibility area (§ 220.D, PDF p.135)
equip.text: In the 50-foot compatibility area between a non-residential use and abutting residential, the following are prohibited: "3. Air conditioning units greater than five tons. If said unit has a capacity of less than five tons, the unit shall be located to reduce off-site impacts." Also prohibited there: dumpsters, outdoor sales/storage/display, loading facilities, drive-thrus, grease traps, wastewater lift stations, gasoline pump islands.

equip.cite: Ground-mounted accessory equipment for solar / wind energy systems (§ 206, PDF p.110)
equip.text: "Required accessory equipment may be permitted on the roof or ground provided accessory equipment located on the ground shall meet all accessory structure setbacks." Same section: "Shall not emit noise exceeding 50dBA as measured at the property line. The described level may be exceeded during short-term events such as utility outages and/or severe wind storms."

equip.cite: Storage of liquid propane tanks (§ 231, PDF p.155)
equip.text: "The storage of any liquid propane gas tanks for retail sale shall be protected with bollards. Bollards shall be placed between the tank storage unit and vehicle parking. All bollards shall be no more than three feet on center and each bollard shall be at a minimum four inches in diameter and six feet in length, with three feet anchored in 12 inches of concrete. All bollards shall extend the full length of the cabinet storing the liquid propane gas or tanks." This governs retail LP storage only; it is not a residential generator-tank rule.

equip.cite: Emergency generators — narrative disclosure only (§ 303, PDF p.277)
equip.text: For electrical power facility / substation conditional uses the application narrative must include "An explanation of any plans for back-up/emergency electrical power generators, where and when they would be used for the proposed project." No setback or clearance is attached.

safety_harbor.source: Comprehensive Zoning and Land Development Code. Article II District Regulations, Sections 25.01-25.14 (each district has its own "Dimensional Regulations" subse

gen.cite: Mechanical equipment (Sec. 36.05) - names generators explicitly
gen.text: "No mechanical equipment including, but not limited to, heating, air conditioning, refrigeration equipment, generators, propane tanks, plumbing lines, ductwork, and transformers shall be located within a primary front yard. Ground-mounted mechanical equipment may be located within a secondary front yard if opaque screening is provided around all sides of the equipment. Screening shall include an opaque decorative fence or wall or a non-opaque fence with opaque vegetative screening. All screening shall be a minimum of one (1) foot higher than the height of the mechanical equipment being screened and a maximum of six (6) feet in height. For the purposes of this section, the front yard of a corner lot shall be the side of the property from which the property is addressed. The other side facing a street shall be considered a secondary front yard. Ground-mounted mechanical equipment not on single-family residential property shall be screened from public rights-of-way, pedestrian areas, and any adjacent residential property using landscaping or other acceptable material. Rooftop mechanical equipment shall be completely screened from all ground level views by a parapet wall or other architectural feature integrated to the building." (Ord. No. 2019-01, Sec. 2, 1-22-2019.)

equip.cite: Yard encroachments (Sec. 38.00(A)(6))
equip.text: "Air conditioning units and other similar accessory equipment may be located in any required side, rear, or secondary front yard subject to Section 36.05." Sec. 38.00(A) opens: "Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from 30 inches above the final grade of a lot upward, except as provided for by the following:" and Sec. 38.00(A)(1) adds "Structures less than 30 inches in height above finished grade are not considered yard encroachments." No numeric separation from a property line is stated for mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: Accessory structures (Sec. 36.00(G))
equip.text: "Accessory structures shall be located as follows: (1) No closer than ten (10) feet to the primary structure; and (2) No closer than five (5) feet to a lot line; and (3) No closer than six (6) feet to any other accessory structure; and (4) Not forward of the front face of the primary structure; except that an arbor, trellis, pergola, or gazebo unenclosed by walls or other minor decorative landscape feature may be permitted in a front yard with prior approval of the Planning and Zoning Director." Sec. 36.00(G)(6): "Accessory structures, excluding swimming pools, may occupy not more than thirty-five (35%) percent of a required rear yard and not more than five percent (5%) of a front yard." Sec. 36.00(G)(7): accessory structures shall not exceed 12 ft in height (25 ft inside the Community Redevelopment District on an alley lot with privacy-protecting upper windows).

equip.cite: Swimming pools and pool equipment (Sec. 36.02(C)-(D))
equip.text: "Swimming pools and spas and screened cages for swimming pools may occupy a required rear or side yard, provided that no part, including pool decking and other customary accessory structures associated with swimming pools, is located closer than five (5) feet to a lot line. Pools, screened cages and decks may not be placed within an easement, unless documentation is provided with the permit application demonstrating that there are no utilities or storm sewers within the easement, the improvements do not impede or restrict drainage flow, and that a partial easement vacation was approved on the property." And: "Accessory swimming pools shall maintain a three (3) foot separation from the water's edge to the primary structure."

equip.cite: Lots abutting an alleyway (Sec. 23.07)
equip.text: "Where the rear or side yard of a lot abuts an alleyway, one-half (1/2) of the alleyway width up to a maximum of ten (10) feet may be considered as a portion of the required yard for the primary structure. Provided, however, the required yard shall not be reduced to less than two (2) feet from a rear property line and three (3) feet from a side property line... This provision does not apply to accessory structures or accessory dwellings."

equip.cite: Pavers (Sec. 36.06) - relevant to an equipment pad
equip.text: "Interlocking pavers or a continuous grouping of pavers, not part of a driveway, are permitted within any yard, provided that no paver is located closer than three (3) feet to a lot line unless the applicant submits drainage data for review by the City Engineer... Pavers shall not be within three (3) feet of a meter box and require a paver waiver if installed over a utility."

equip.cite: Height limitation exclusions (Sec. 23.08)
equip.text: "The height limitations of this Code shall not apply to residential chimneys, flagpoles, radio towers, television antennae, water towers, transmission towers and cables, smokestacks, church spires and domes, cupolas, parapet walls, or other minor decorative architectural features, no more than five feet above the peak of the roof, as determined by the Planning and Zoning Director." Mechanical equipment is not on this list.

equip.cite: Low structures may encroach into the required setback (Sec. 5.01.03.B footnote, PDF p.457)
equip.text: "* Any structure 30 inches or less from grade may encroach into the required setback if maintenance of structure and firefighting abilities are not compromised." The asterisk is attached to both the 7.5 ft and the 9.5 ft side/rear setback paragraphs. This is the only encroachment allowance printed in the LDR and is the provision most likely to govern a ground-mounted generator, condenser or pool pump; the code does not name any of those pieces of equipment.

equip.cite: Minimum distance between buildings (Sec. 5.01.03.C, PDF p.457)
equip.text: "Minimum distance between adjacent buildings shall be the sum of the required side or rear yard setbacks except as follows: Where an adjacent structure exists and is not in conformity with side or rear yard requirements... 1. The minimum distance between adjacent buildings shall be ten (10) feet. 2. If either building exceeds twenty-five (25) feet in height, the minimum distance between adjacent buildings shall be twelve (12) feet. 3. Distance shall be measured at the narrowest space between structures, whether a main living unit, principal structure, open deck, or an accessory use, and shall not include roof overhang (eave)."

equip.cite: Nothing permitted in a required buffer (Sec. 5.02.03, PDF p.459)
equip.text: "No accessory structures, garbage or trash collection points or receptacles, parking, or any other functional use contrary to the intent and purpose of this LDR shall be permitted in a required buffer area. This does not prohibit the combining of compatible functions such as buffering and drainage facilities." Because side and rear yards for non-single-family uses are set by the Sec. 5.02.00 buffer requirements, this effectively bars a generator pad from those yards.

equip.cite: Accessory structure definition (Sec. 3.01.02, PDF p.407)
equip.text: "Accessory Structure. A structure not greater than 3,000 square feet of floor area, and not over two stories in height, the use of which is customarily accessory to and incidental to that of the dwelling(s) and which is located on the same lot."

equip.cite: LP gas storage (Sec. 3.02.02.G.6, PDF p.412)
equip.text: "LP gas storage and/or distribution facilities up to one thousand (1,000) gallons. This shall not be construed to prevent retail sales of LP gas in canisters or similar pre-filled containers." This is a use-permission entry, not a setback.

equip.cite: Floodplain: accessory structures and equipment (Sec. 4.02.01, PDF p.447)
equip.text: Accessory structures are permitted below the base flood elevation only if used solely for parking or storage, and if in Zone A/AE other than coastal high hazard areas they are one story and not larger than 600 sq. ft. Elevator equipment must be elevated to or above base flood elevation plus one (1) foot.

wilton_manors.name: Wilton Manors
wilton_manors.source: Code of Ordinances, Appendix A - Unified Land Development Regulations (ULDR), Part 2, Article 20 (District Regulations). Districts established at Sec. 020-010,

gen.cite: Generators and mechanical equipment in the Urban Center Districts (ULDR Sec. 030-050 [printed subsection (O), Additional site features], PDF p.742)
gen.text: "(N) Commercial uses restriction in setbacks. No outdoor commercial uses are allowed within any setback facing a single-family residential property. (O) Additional site features. No dumpster enclosure, generator or mechanical equipment shall be located within the required setback facing a single-family residential property." (Ord. No. 2021-011, § 2, 8-24-21; Ord. No. 2023-005, § 2, 12-12-23.) This is the one place in the Wilton Manors code that names a generator as a site feature and gives it a placement rule. Note it forbids the generator in the required setback facing single-family, not a fixed distance - the operative distance is whatever Sec. 030-040 requires for that yard, which where a single-family use is abutted runs from 30 to 65 feet depending on district, tier, lot size and lot depth.

gen.cite: Yard encroachments - air conditioning compressors (ULDR Sec. 045-030(B)(1), PDF p.781)
gen.text: "Allowable yard encroachments. Every part of a required yard shall be open to the sky, except as follows, and as otherwise permitted within the ULDR: (1) Sills, belt courses, roof overhangs, roof gutters, air conditioning compressors, chimneys, cornices, cantilevers, green walls and ornamental features may project into a required yard a distance not to exceed thirty-six (36) inches." (Ord. No. 2020-005, § 3, 5-26-20.) Generators are NOT in this list.

gen.cite: Generator noise (Code of Ordinances, noise section, subsection (6) Emergency generators, PDF p.635)
gen.text: "(6) Emergency generators. a. Testing of generators shall be conducted for the minimum duration and at the minimum frequency recommended by the manufacturer, but in no case shall said testing exceed one (1) hour in any one (1) day. b. Testing shall only be conducted between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 7:00 p.m. daily. c. The sound emissions from generators shall not exceed sixty-eight (68) dBA when measured at a distance of twenty-three (23) feet from the generator. d. When the generator is located on the same parcel as the complainant, the indoor sound level limits in Table 1 shall apply." Immediately following: "(7) Heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) equipment on residential property. No person shall operate or cause to be operated any HVAC equipment on residential property which exceeds forty (40) dBA between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. daily when measured within the premises of a complainant." The 23-foot figure is a MEASUREMENT distance for the noise test, not a setback.

gen.cite: Emergency generators required for residential multifamily dwellings (Code of Ordinances § 5-28, PDF p.236-237)
gen.text: "Residential multifamily dwellings must have an available generator and fuel source on the property or have proof of a current contract posted in the elevator machine room or other place conspicuous to the elevator inspector affirming a current guaranteed service contract for such equipment and fuel source to operate the elevator on an on-call basis within twenty-four (24) hours after a request. The emergency generator system that uses fuel (regulated substances) for its power source shall comply with the requirements of Chapters 62-761 and 62-762 F.A.C. and Broward County Code of Ordinances Chapter 27 Article X, Storage Tanks, Pollution Control Code as amended." "(c)... the term 'alternate power source' means a system that provides an independent source of electric power during a loss of power supply and includes a supply of fuel sufficient to sustain the emergency power source for at least seven (7) days during a power outage. An emergency power system may include a generator, batteries, and other essential accessories needed to power such emergency power system." "(d)... any person, firm, or corporation operating residential multifamily dwellings shall have a generator key located in a knox box posted at or near the generator." Applies to each newly constructed residential multifamily dwelling at least two stories and up to 74.99 feet high without a primary entrance on the first floor. No placement distance is printed.

equip.cite: Screening of mechanical equipment (ULDR Sec. 150-180(A), PDF p.939)
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment such as air conditioning compressors, pool pumps, sprinkler pumps and electrical transformers shall be screened on at least three (3) sides. Such screening shall meet the minimum requirements of Section 150-120 herein at time of planting and shall exceed the vertical height of the object by at least six (6) inches within two (2) years of issuing a certificate of occupancy. Subject to approval by the Community Development Services Director or designee, a residential property owner may use an existing wooden fence to screen mechanical equipment in lieu of landscape materials."

equip.cite: Screening and placement in the Urban Center Districts (ULDR Sec. 030-041(D) and Sec. 030-050(A)(H), PDF p.739-740)
equip.text: Sec. 030-041(D): "Loading areas, mechanical equipment, transformer boxes, dumpster enclosures. Structures and uses that are required in in this Article to be screened shall not be located adjacent to a frontage line, and shall not be visible from any public rights-of-way." Sec. 030-050(A): "Appurtenances may be permitted to extend above the building height limit for a distance sufficient to accommodate building design and screening for mechanical equipment such as elevator shafts and cooling towers and condensers, as provided in Section 045-020." Sec. 030-050(H): "Mechanical equipment screening. Building design shall include appropriate screening for mechanical equipment. Screening for such mechanical equipment shall be designed as an integral part of the building and located away from a frontage line."

equip.cite: Rooftop equipment screening (ULDR Sec. 045-020, PDF p.781)
equip.text: "[Screening shall be provided] to reduce any noise and to block from view such equipment from adjacent properties or rights-of-way. The elevation of the screening device shall be not less than the elevation of the roof equipment unless the applicant provides a line-of-site study justifying a lower screening device or alternate method of screening." The same section allows rooftop solar PV or solar water heater systems to exceed the height limit by not more than 5 feet without screening, green-roof structural components by not more than 5 feet, and the top of a wind turbine by not more than 4 feet.

equip.cite: Utility sheds (ULDR Sec. 045-070, PDF p.784)
equip.text: "Utility sheds may occupy a required rear yard only, provided they are not located closer than five (5) feet to a rear lot line. No more than one utility shed shall be constructed upon any lot. When the property on which a utility shed is to be constructed abuts a canal or waterway, no utility shed shall be permitted in the required yard adjacent to any seawall or canal."

equip.cite: Pools, decks and screen enclosures (ULDR Sec. 045-060(A), PDF p.784)
equip.text: Setback table: Pool - Front Yard 5 feet, Side Yard 5 feet, Rear Yard 5 feet. Deck - Front Yard 3 feet, Side Yard 3 feet, Rear Yard 3 feet. Screen enclosure or roofed structure - Front Yard 20 feet, Side Yard 5 feet, Rear Yard 5 feet. Footnote: "Setback measurement is to the water's edge for pools; edge of deck for decking; edge of screen enclosure for screen enclosures; and edge of overhang for roofed enclosures." Sec. 045-060(B): "A walk space at least eighteen (18) inches wide shall be provided between a pool and any walls, fences or screen enclosure."

equip.cite: Accessory buildings generally (ULDR Sec. 025-020, PDF p.703)
equip.text: "No accessory building shall be constructed upon a lot until the construction of the main use building has been actually completed or construction of main and accessory buildings is concurrent. No accessory building shall be used, and no accessory use established, unless the main use has been established or the principal building on the lot is also being used in accordance with all requirements of these regulations." Sec. 025-010 adds that a use or building not listed in Article 25 "may be permitted as an accessory use or building provided that it is meets the criteria for an accessory uses and buildings relative to the principal use." Article 25 sets no general accessory-structure setback; the ULDR does not print one outside the utility-shed and pool rules.

equip.cite: LP gas / propane as a principal use (ULDR Sec. 055-030 area, PDF p.808)
equip.text: A telecommunications-siting restriction refers to a site whose "proposed or existing principal use includes the storage, distribution, or sale of volatile, flammable, explosive, or hazardous wastes such as LP gas, propane, gasoline, natural gas, and corrosive or dangerous chemicals." This governs tower siting, not tank placement; there is no LP-gas or propane tank placement standard in the Wilton Manors code.

wakulla_county.name: Wakulla County
wakulla_county.source: Code of Ordinances ch. 5 (Zoning Regulations and Districts), Article III, Secs. 5-23 through 5-44, plus the Crawfordville Town Plan districts in Secs. 5-64 thro

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures - front yard bar (Sec. 6-1(3)(d))
equip.text: All accessory uses and structures shall be arranged and maintained so as not to encroach on any required front yard.

equip.cite: Accessory structures in residential districts - 5 ft side and rear (Sec. 6-1(4))
equip.text: In residential districts and on any lot used for residential purposes, accessory structures shall be at least five feet from side and rear lot lines.

equip.cite: Accessory structures generally (Sec. 6-1(3)(b),(c))
equip.text: All accessory uses and structures shall comply with the use limitations applicable in the zoning district in which they are located, and shall comply with the property development regulations applicable in the zoning district in which they are located.

equip.cite: Accessory structures in the RMH-2 Mobile Home Park district (Sec. 5-44(6)3)
equip.text: An accessory structure shall not exceed two stories or 25 feet in height. Accessory structures expressly permitted in RMH-2 include 'garages, carports, storage rooms, and other structures which are customarily incidental to the principal building'.

equip.cite: Accessory structures in the Crawfordville Core District (Sec. 5-63(3))
equip.text: The zero-foot front and side setback reductions for non-residential and mixed use structures expressly do NOT apply to accessory structures.

equip.cite: 'Light infrastructure' as a principal use (definition, Sec. 4-2(106))
equip.text: Light infrastructure: Fundamental utility facilities and systems necessary to support the operations and activities associated with an area, characterized as being small in scale for their setting and/or not having the potential to produce significant negative off-site impacts. Light infrastructure shall include, but shall not be limited to, water wells, water tanks, sewage pump stations, and electric substations. Light infrastructure is a listed PRINCIPAL USE in P-1, P-2, AG, RR-5, RR-2, RR-1, RR-1(a), RSU-1, RSU-2, R-1A, R-1, R-2, R-3, RTH, RMH-1, RMH-2, CTTP, CO, C-1, LDR and other districts, and as a principal use it is subject to the district's own setbacks, not to the accessory-structure rule.

equip.cite: Manufactured home utility equipment (Sec. flood ordinance, PDF p.693)
equip.text: Utility equipment that serves manufactured homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential, Section R322, as applicable to the flood hazard area.

equip.cite: Mobile home park emergency power
equip.text: Not a siting rule, but printed in the RMH-2 context and worth knowing: nothing in Wakulla's ch. 5 or ch. 6 gives a generator, A/C condenser or pool pump its own setback or encroachment allowance.

equip.cite: Home occupations (Sec. 6-10)
equip.text: No mechanical equipment shall be used or stored on the premises in connection with a home occupation, except such that is normally used for purely domestic or household purposes. No electric motor having greater than one-third horsepower rating shall be used in any home occupation.

equip.cite: Wireless communication accessory equipment buildings (Sec. 6-52(a))
equip.text: 'Accessory equipment building for wireless communication facilities' means any building, cabinet, or equipment enclosure constructed for the primary purpose of housing the electronics, BACKUP POWER, POWER GENERATORS and other free standing equipment associated with the operation of antennas. Siting is governed by Secs. 6-51 to 6-58, not by the district tables.

equip.cite: Setback from water (Sec. 6-?, PDF p.319)
equip.text: No improvement shall be located less than 50 feet from the mean high-water line of any body of water; 'improvement' includes buildings and structures, swimming pools, street pavements, curbs and gutters, street signs, ACCESSORY BUILDINGS, STORAGE SHEDS, SEPTIC TANKS, and similar improvements to real property. 'Body of water' includes any natural lake, river, stream, brook, manmade or natural canal, bay, estuary, gulf, ocean or sea.

sumter_county.name: Sumter County
sumter_county.source: Land Development Code (Code of Ordinances ch. 13), art. IV div. 2 - Sec. 13-412 Dimensional standards-General (incl. Table 13-412A Building Setbacks from Roads)

equip.cite: Setbacks apply to accessory structures (Sec. 13-412(a))
equip.text: The setback distances in Tables 13-413A and 13-416A shall be the minimum setback distances from side and rear lot/parcel lines for all substantial above ground structures, including accessory structures, and in or below ground structures, unless specified otherwise in this Land Development Code.

equip.cite: Accessory use setbacks (Sec. 13-510(b))
equip.text: Accessory uses must comply with setback standards pertaining to the principal use except as noted in the sections that follow. The exceptions listed, however, shall not apply to road setbacks contained in Table 13-412A.

equip.cite: Small accessory buildings, reduced setback (Sec. 13-510(b)(1))
equip.text: In residential zoning districts, accessory buildings of not more than one hundred (100) square feet shall be required to observe a one (1) foot setback from lot lines, provided such building does not exceed ten (10) feet in height. Accessory structures with reduced setbacks shall not be located within the front yard.

equip.cite: Underground storage tanks (Sec. 13-510(b)(2))
equip.text: Underground storage tank setbacks shall be ten (10) feet to any wall or surface of the tank, excluding piping. Front setback from a maintained road right-of-way may be administratively reduced by the county administrator or designee upon demonstration of compliance with the Florida Building Code and good cause.

equip.cite: Number and size of accessory structures (Sec. 13-510(c))
equip.text: (1) Agriculture and rural residential districts: There is no limit on the number of accessory structures allowed. However, the aggregate size of all accessory buildings shall not exceed the size of the principal building. Bonafide agricultural sites are exempt from this provision. (2) All other districts: There shall be no more than three (3) accessory structures on a site. The aggregate size of all accessory structures shall not exceed sixty (60) percent of the size of the principal building. Permeable garden features such as pergolas, arbors, and trellises shall not be included in this calculation.

equip.cite: Swimming pools, spas and screen enclosures (Sec. 13-518)
equip.text: (a) Setbacks for in ground and above ground swimming pools/spas and screen enclosures shall be no less than five (5) feet, provided adjacent property is protected from damage due to excavation. In-ground swimming pool setback shall be measured to the inside face of the pool's vertical wall. (b) Pool enclosures with walls or roofs of more solid or durable material than screening shall comply with principal building setbacks. (c) No swimming pool, spa, deck, or screen enclosure shall be located within an easement or drainage swale.

equip.cite: Setbacks from water bodies (Sec. 13-412(b))
equip.text: The required building setback from on or off-site ditches and canals shall be ten (10) feet, measured from the normal high-water elevation contour of the adjacent water body. See section 13-901 for other provisions applicable to properties abutting surface water bodies.

equip.cite: What counts as a structure for road setbacks (Sec. 13-412(c)(1))
equip.text: As used in this section, the terms 'building' or 'structure' includes any substantial structure which by nature of its size, scale, dimensions, bulk, or use tends to constitute a visual obstruction or generate activity similar to that usually associated with a building. Purely aesthetic, non-habitable features such as stacked stone, knee-walls or other similar structures shall not be subject to these provisions so long as they are of limited scale and obtrusiveness. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the following structures shall be deemed to fall within this description: a. Gas pumps and overhead canopies or roofs. b. Fences running along lot lines adjacent to public street rights-of-way if such fences, by reason of their height or opaqueness, constitute a threat to public safety and welfare.

equip.cite: Measurement / two-foot allowance (Sec. 13-412(c)(2)b)
equip.text: Measurement shall be to the nearest vertical wall or support of the building or structure, provided any above ground extension of the building does not encroach into the required setback more than two (2) feet, or onto adjoining property. Any above ground encroachment of more than two (2) feet into the required setback will require a compensating setback increase in the structure's wall or support.

equip.cite: Corner-lot setback exception (Sec. 13-412(c)(3)b)
equip.text: Notwithstanding the requirements of Table 13-412A, where deemed necessary to allow reasonable use of the property for placement of a principal structure, the applicable setback on corner lots established prior to the effective date of this chapter and having less than seventy-five (75) feet road frontage may be reduced by one (1) foot for every road frontage foot less than seventy-five (75) feet, but in no case may the setback be less than fifteen (15) feet.

equip.cite: Flood-resistant construction - mechanical, plumbing and electrical systems (Sec. 9-40(i)(5))
equip.text: Have mechanical, plumbing and electrical systems, including plumbing fixtures, elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus one foot.

equip.cite: Flood-resistant development - recreational vehicles and park trailers (Sec. 9-44(a)(5))
equip.text: Have mechanical, plumbing, and electrical systems above the design flood elevation, except that minimum electric service required to address life safety and electric code requirements is permitted below the design flood elevation provided it conforms to the provisions of the electrical part of the building code for wet locations.

equip.cite: Manufactured home utility equipment (Sec. 9-41(g))
equip.text: Utility equipment that serves manufactured homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322, as applicable to the flood hazard area.

equip.cite: Coastal Construction Code - location of construction (Sec. 6-62)
equip.text: Construction, except for elevated walkways, lifeguard support stands, piers, beach access ramps, gazebos, and coastal or shore protection structures, shall be located a sufficient distance landward of the beach to permit natural shoreline fluctuations and to preserve dune stability. This is a narrative standard, not a measured setback, and it applies only within the coastal building zone (the land area from the seasonal high-water line to a line 1,500 feet landward of the coastal construction control line; 5,000 feet, or the entire island, on coastal barrier islands).

equip.cite: Buildings seaward of the coastal construction control line (Sec. 9-37(c))
equip.text: Buildings and structures extending, in whole or in part, seaward of the coastal construction control line and also located, in whole or in part, in a flood hazard area shall be designed and constructed to comply with the more restrictive applicable requirements of the Florida Building Code, Building Section 3109 and Section 1612, or Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322.

equip.cite: Beach services and beach amusements setback (Secs. 5-83, 5-87(a))
equip.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to provide or offer any beach service, or any beach amusement, within ten feet of the boundary line of the property on which such person is authorized to conduct business. (This governs commercial beach concessions, not equipment pads.)

equip.cite: Propane cylinders on the beach (Sec. 5-?, PDF p.200, p.202)
equip.text: Storage boxes or booths may not be used to store flammable liquids including, but not limited to, gasoline or liquid propane. All beach fires must be fueled solely by propane gas or organic wood material via an elevated fire pit not to exceed three feet in diameter.

equip.cite: Mechanical Code (Art. VIII, ch. 6)
equip.text: Chapter 6, Article VIII (the former Mechanical Code, Secs. 6-291 to 6-315) was REPEALED IN ITS ENTIRETY by Ord. No. 05-33, Sec. 2a, adopted July 5, 2005. The Florida Building Code, Mechanical now governs, adopted through Sec. 6-28. No county-specific mechanical equipment placement rule survives in this volume.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment and fuel storage tanks at a house or duplex (§ 4.4.1.G)
equip.text: Section 4.4.1 is 'One-and-two-family development.' Subsection G, 'Mechanical Equipment and Fuel Storage Tanks', reads in full: 'Ancillary mechanical equipment and storage tanks for propane, natural gas, or other material shall be located on the side or rear of the primary structure and shielded from view from the right-of-way with a fence, wall, or vegetation. This regulation will become effective on July 1, 2027, or upon amendment, expiration, or repeal of Chapters 2023-304 and 2023-349, Laws of Florida; voluntary compliance is encouraged in advance of the effective date of this provision.' This is the city-wide residential rule a standby generator and its LP tank fall under — note the deferred effective date of July 1, 2027.

equip.cite: Accessory structure setbacks in the standard and activity center districts (footnote 1 to Tables 3.2.3.2 and 3.3.1.2, identical text)
equip.text: 'Residential accessory structures may be located in side or rear yards only. Minimum setbacks of ten (10) foot rear (twenty (20) foot waterfront) and five (5) foot side apply to accessory structures three hundred (300) SF or smaller. Accessory structures larger than three hundred (300) SF, other than swimming pools, screen enclosures, tennis courts and other similar recreational facilities, shall maintain the same required setbacks as the primary structure. Non-residential accessory structures may be located in any yard and must meet the primary structure setbacks.' A generator pad is well under 300 SF, so in a standard or activity center district the operative figures are 5 ft side and 10 ft rear (20 ft waterfront), and it may not be placed in a front yard.

equip.cite: Landscape buffer can override the setback (footnote 2 to Table 3.2.3.2)
equip.text: 'If the width of a required landscape buffer per Chapter 4, Article III, Section 4.3.12. exceeds the minimum setback the buffer requirement establishes the minimum setback.' The activity center version adds: 'If a maximum or minimum setback conflicts with an easement, the setback may be adjusted to the minimum necessary to ensure the structure does not impact access to the easement.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment landscaping (§ 4.3.9)
equip.text: 'Mechanical equipment, visible from a public right-of-way or other public area, shall be landscaped with a continuous hedge. When the equipment is situated in a location unsuitable for vegetation due to lack of sun or insufficient size, a decorative fence or architectural screen, consistent with the design of the primary structure, may be used in place of the hedge. Landscaping shall be installed no less than three (3) feet from the equipment to allow access, maintenance, and airflow.'

equip.cite: Equipment shielding, non-residential design (§ 4.4.4.G)
equip.text: 'Equipment Shielding. Mechanical equipment shall be located on the roof and shielded from view on all sides, including the top, to ensure it is not visible from all rights-of-way, sidewalks, navigable waterways, and adjacent structures. In instances where equipment cannot be located on the roof, the equipment shall be shielded from view from the public by a one hundred percent (100%) opaque wall or fence and landscaping.'

equip.cite: Wellen Park Villages — AC and pool equipment in the side yard (§ 3.4.1 Village Footnote (2))
equip.text: 'Air conditioning equipment, above ground pool pumps, and the like shall be permitted In side yard setbacks EXCEPT Type F structures with side yard setbacks of three (3) feet. Type F structures shall place air conditioning and pool equipment within the front or rear yard setbacks and shall be screened to maximum extent possible.'

equip.cite: Wellen Park Villages — AC units and mechanical equipment (§ 3.4.1 Village Footnotes (15) and (17))
equip.text: (15): 'AC units and mechanical equipment shall be allowed in side yard setbacks.' (17): 'Air-conditioning units and mechanical equipment shall be allowed in side yard setbacks no closer than one and one-half (1.5) feet from lot line.' The 1.5 ft figure in (17) is the only numeric clearance the code gives for mechanical equipment on a lot line.

equip.cite: Wellen Park Village A — utility facilities exempt from setbacks (§ 3.4.1 footnote WA.2 and WA.3)
equip.text: WA.2: 'Fences, walls, columns, decorative features, and utility facilities such as lift stations, storage tanks, ground mounted transformers and wells shall be exempt from any setback standard (except Type F side yard setbacks).' WA.3: 'Air conditioning equipment: pool pumps, and the like shall be permitted in side yard setbacks (except Type F).' WA.4: 'Setbacks for accessory structures such as pool cages and pool equipment shall be 5-feet from the rear property line.'

equip.cite: Wellen Park Village D — mechanical equipment in side yards (§ 3.4.1 footnote WD.4)
equip.text: 'Setbacks may be reduced to zero (0) feet when the subject parcel is adjacent to public/private right-of-way, easement, open space tract or water body that is at least thirty (30) feet in width. Air conditioning units, pool pumps and other mechanical equipment shall be permitted in side yard setbacks.' Villages B and C carry the matching exemption for utility facilities: 'Fences, walls, columns, decorative features, and utility facilities such as lift stations, storage tanks, ground mounted transformers and wells shall be exempt from any setback standards.'

equip.cite: Toledo Village — utility facilities (§ 3.4.1 Village Footnote (19))
equip.text: 'A minimum ten (10) foot distance will be maintained between residential lot/tract lines and the Pond Control Water Elevation Line. Utility facilities, fences, walls, entry monuments, signs and other decorative features shall not be subject to any setbacks.'

equip.cite: Wellhead protection exemption for emergency generators (Chapter 6)
equip.text: In the wellfield protection provisions, among the facilities prohibited near a wellhead — 'Facilities for the bulk storage, handling, or processing of materials on the Florida Substance List (Chapter 442, Florida Statutes, as amended)' — the code adds: 'Wellhead emergency generators which are required are exempt, but the high...' (the exemption continues on the page). This is the only place the word 'generator' appears in a siting rule, and it concerns the city's own wellhead generators, not private standby units.

equip.cite: Mobile food vendors using a generator (§ 3.2.5 use standards)
equip.text: 'A fire extinguisher must be located on-site when a mobile food vendor uses a generator or open flame.'

west_park.source: Code of Ordinances, Chapter 42 ZONING, Article V District Regulations. Two consolidated tables plus two narrative regimes: § 42-199 'Residential districts desig

equip.cite: Air conditioning units projecting into a required yard (§ 42-197(b))
equip.text: 'Yard encroachments. All required yards shall be open and unobstructed from ground to sky except as follows or as otherwise permitted in this section for zero lot line developments: sills or belt courses, cornices, buttresses, ornamental features, chimneys, flues, eaves, awnings and air conditioning units may not project over 36 inches into a required yard.' This is the city's only numeric equipment-in-the-yard rule: an A/C unit may project into a required yard, but by no more than 36 inches. A generator is not named in the list.

equip.cite: Accessory structures in residential districts (§ 42-197(c))
equip.text: '(1) On a plot containing a one-family detached or two-family dwelling, side and rear yards not abutting a street may be reduced to five feet for accessory uses and buildings. (2) Accessory buildings may not exceed one story on any plot containing a one-family detached dwelling. (3) Accessory buildings shall not exceed half the height of any principal building on plots containing two-family or multiple-family dwellings... (4) One-story accessory buildings shall be at least ten feet from any other accessory building and from any principal building on the same plot. The distance between any principal and accessory buildings on the same plot, where the accessory building is higher than one story, shall be half the height of the highest principal building. (5) The aggregate floor area of all accessory buildings shall not exceed five percent of the plot area. (6) No accessory building shall contain more than 50 percent of the floor area of the principal building. (7) No more than one primary building and one accessory building shall be permitted in residential zoning districts.'

equip.cite: Easements (§ 42-197(a))
equip.text: 'No permanent structure except a wood or chainlink fence shall encroach upon or into any easement of record. No structure or use shall encroach upon or obstruct access through any easement specifically granted for ingress or egress purposes.'

equip.cite: Screening of equipment (§ 42-573(3))
equip.text: 'Screening of equipment. Dumpsters, mechanical equipment, A/C units, electrical transformers and all aboveground equipment shall be screened on at least three sides by landscape material that is equal to the height of the element at installation. Such screening shall not interfere with normal operation of equipment and shall be maintained at the height of the element or no more than one foot above.' § 42-570(e)(3) adds: 'Ficus spp., when planted as a hedge, may be used to meet the requirements of dumpster enclosure, mechanical equipment and electrical transformer screening only.'

equip.cite: Residential landscaping to screen mechanical equipment (§ 42-571 / xeriscape provisions)
equip.text: '...no more than ten trees and 30 shrubs required per acre. The purpose of these shrubs shall be to screen air conditioning units and other mechanical equipment.' and 'Where possible, a minimum of two trees shall be required in the front of the lot. Shrubs shall be incorporated in a manner on the site so as to be a visual screen for mechanical equipment or other accessories to the residence.'

equip.cite: Service areas and mechanical equipment in the Transit-Oriented Corridor (§ 42-327)
equip.text: '(a) Service bays, mechanical equipment and delivery areas, to the greatest extent possible, shall be fully enclosed, screened or located within the interior of the building. These areas shall not be visible from streets or properties with adjacent residential or hotel uses. (b) Central air conditioning is required. (c) It is preferred that all exterior equipment be placed on the roof and shall be architecturally screened. If not architecturally screened, then landscape screening to the height of the element shall be required.'

equip.cite: Open air storage in residential districts (§ 42-197(e)(2))
equip.text: 'The open air storage of any item is prohibited in residential zoning districts with the exception of usable lawn, garden or pool furniture or equipment, barbecues, toys, bicycles or trash cans being used by the residents of the dwelling on the plot where such items are stored.'

equip.cite: Nuisances (§ 42-197(o)(1))
equip.text: 'Nothing shall be allowed on or in any structure, land, or water body in any district that shall in any way be offensive or obnoxious by reason of the emission of odors, gases, dust, smoke, vibration or noise (including the crowing of cocks, barking of dogs, or any noises or odors emanating from any animal, fish or fowl). Nor shall anything be constructed or maintained that would in any way constitute an eyesore to adjacent property owners or residents or to the community.'

This is the only appearance of the word 'generator' in the zoning chapter, and it is about temporary events.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment — service areas (commercial, public facility and industrial areas only)
equip.text: § 94-4(c): "Service areas; purpose and intent. Service areas, including, but not limited to, loading, storage, mechanical equipment, and solid waste disposal, shall serve to diminish, in a safe manner, the visual impacts of service functions that may distract or have a negative impact on the streetscape, landscape and/or the overall community image." § 94-4(d): "Buffering and screening standards. Loading areas, docks, outdoor storage, propane tank displays and refilling areas, trash collection, mechanical equipment trash compaction, vehicular storage, recycling, rooftop equipment and other service function areas shall be fully screened and out of view from adjacent properties at ground view level and in view of roadway corridors." Per § 94-2 chapter 94 applies "in all commercial and public facility zoning districts, commercial and public facility and industrial components of PUD districts, DRIs, business park districts, and industrial zoned areas." No distance is given.

equip.cite: Accessory sheds / storage buildings (residential districts)
equip.text: "Such shed, storage building, or similar structure shall be five feet from any side and/or rear property line unless the dwelling unit is on a corner lot in which case such shed, storage building, or similar structure shall have a 25-foot setback from all street side property lines." One per lot, maximum 160 square feet and 12 feet in height, placed at the rear of the dwelling unit (§§ 102-62(4), 102-82(2), 102-102(2), 102-132(2), 102-162(4), 102-192(5), 102-222(3)). This governs enclosed accessory buildings, not an unenclosed equipment pad.

equip.cite: Swimming pools and associated decks (AG)
equip.text: § 102-65(12): "Swimming pools and associated decks with or without screen enclosures shall maintain a minimum 15 feet setback from any side or rear property line. Pools shall not be located within the front yard of any lot or within any easement."

equip.cite: Swimming pools, decks, patios, screen enclosures (RSF-1, RSF-2)
equip.text: § 102-105(12) (and the parallel provision in § 102-85): "Swimming pools, associated decks, and patios, with or without screen enclosures, shall maintain a ten-foot setback form [sic] any rear property line. The setback from any side property line shall be equal to the setback for the principal structure on the property." For lots of 50×110 dimension or smaller the rear setback is five feet. "Pools, associated decks, and patios, with or without screen enclosures, shall not be located within the front or side yard of any lot or within any easement."

equip.cite: Standby generators — city sewage pumping stations only
equip.text: § 70-342(f): "Emergency power provisions; generators and emergency power connections.... any newly constructed lift station shall be provided with an on-site standby, diesel power generator and automatic transfer switch. Such generator shall be capable of operating the station at peak flows (i.e., with all equipment operating). The generator shall be enclosed within a weatherproof, locking enclosure and shall have a base mounted, dual-walled fuel tank with sufficient capacity to operate the station for three days, based upon anticipated flow rates." This is a utility construction specification for city lift stations, not a zoning setback for a private generator.

equip.cite: Noise — essential services exemption

jackson_county.name: Jackson County
jackson_county.source: Code of Ordinances ch. 42, Planning, art. III, Land Development Regulations. Jackson has no zoning districts and no dimensional table: land is classified by FUT

equip.cite: Accessory building/structure definition (Sec. 42-56, PDF p.268)
equip.text: "Accessory building/structure means a building or structure which is clearly incidental or subordinate to and customarily utilized in connection with a principal building located on the same lot. Such buildings or structures may not be used for human habitation. Examples of accessory structures are detached garages, carports, storage sheds, pole barns, and hay sheds." The code defines accessory structures but prints NO setback, placement or screening rule for them.

equip.cite: Everything portable counts as a structure (Sec. 42-56, PDF p.270)
equip.text: "Any structure built for the support, shelter or enclosure of persons, animals, chattel, or property of any kind. Any accessory building, canopy, shelving, rack, and each and every type of portable equipment shall be considered buildings or structures within the meaning of the definition." A generator enclosure would be a structure under this definition - but there is no district setback for it to satisfy.

equip.cite: Accessory dwelling units (Sec. 42-72(1)b, PDF p.303)
equip.text: "2. An ADU shall be located within or as an accessory structure to the principal structure. The height of the accessory structure may not be greater than two stories. 3. Detached ADUs shall be located in the side or rear yard.... 7. ADUs shall be included in the maximum impervious area requirements of the parcel." This is the only rule in the code that places an accessory structure in a particular yard.

equip.cite: Solar farms and hydro panel farms (Sec. 42-74(2), PDF p.305)
equip.text: "f. All solar or hydro panels and other above-ground structures, excluding transmission line poles, shall be located at least 50 feet from any lot line under separate ownership unless more stringent regulations exist in state or federal regulations.... d. Physical access to a solar farm or hydro panel farm shall be restricted by fencing with a minimum height of six feet... i. Where ground-mounted solar or hydro panels face abutting residential developed or designated parcels or public roadways, the panels shall be made of glare reducing materials or shall be visually screened from said abutting parcels and roadways. The screening type used may be natural or manmade but must meet a minimum opacity of 75 percent at the time of installation. j. Fixed panel solar arrays or hydro panels shall be considered pervious. The impervious cover calculation shall include the support posts of the panels, and roads or impervious driveway surfaces, parking areas, and building/structures on site. h. All solar or hydro panels and devices are considered structures." This 50-foot setback for on-site energy equipment is the nearest analogue in the code to a generator-pad rule, but it is written for solar farms as a principal use.

equip.cite: Industrial outdoor activity separation (Sec. 42-81(b), PDF p.312)
equip.text: "Industrial uses with outdoor storage of materials and supplies, or industrial activity which takes place outdoors, shall provide visual screening of the outdoor activity, landscaping, and a separation of at least 50 feet between the proposed activity and adjacent nonindustrial activity or vacant land."

equip.cite: Commercial noise at the property line (Sec. 42-80(b), PDF p.310)
equip.text: "Commercial development with outdoor activities which emits sound should not exceed 70 decibels from the property line."

equip.cite: Borrow pits (Sec. 42-68(d), PDF p.296-297)
equip.text: "Borrow pit operations are prohibited within 660 feet of residential development, paved public roadways, and public parks/recreation areas... Borrow pit development shall require installation and maintenance of a visual landscape buffer that obscures the site by a minimum of 70 percent to a minimum height of eight feet. This includes a buffer of native vegetation no less than 25 feet deep surrounding the pit."

equip.cite: Data centers and their generators are prohibited (Sec. 42-850 through 42-857, PDF p.405-409)
equip.text: Ord. No. 2026-04 prohibits data centers and all "associated facilities" in unincorporated Jackson County, defining an associated facility to include "cooling equipment, mechanical equipment, electrical equipment, generators, battery energy storage systems, fuel storage, water treatment or cooling-water facilities, security facilities, utility yards, equipment yards, telecommunications equipment, or other supporting infrastructure." Sec. 42-856 directs staff to prepare future amendments addressing, among other things, "setbacks; buffers; screening; landscaping; noise; vibration; lighting; thermal impacts;... backup generators; fuel storage; battery storage; fire suppression" - i.e. the county acknowledges it has no such standards today. This ordinance targets data centers, not a standby generator at a house or business.

equip.cite: Telecommunication tower setbacks (Sec. 42-6xx, PDF p.366-367)
equip.text: "All new telecommunication towers shall, at a minimum, be setbacks from property boundaries a distance consistent with other principal uses in the zone in which it is located. If the new telecommunication tower is to be located on property adjacent to residentially designated property, the telecommunication tower shall be setback from said residentially designated property a minimum distance equal to one-third the height of the tower or the [certified fall zone], whichever is greater. If there is no certified fall zone... a setback the distance equal to the height of the proposed telecommunications tower shall be used instead. Guy anchors for guyed towers shall be located a minimum of 25 feet from any property boundary." Note the tower rule assumes district setbacks exist for "other principal uses in the zone"; none are printed.

gen.cite: Standby generators as accessory structures — LDC §§ 3.1.9 and 7.10.10
gen.text: A standby generator is treated as an accessory structure; Venice prints no generator-specific setback exemption. It must be at least 5 ft from any side or rear property line, may not be located in any front yard, and may not sit in a utility or drainage easement, a right-of-way, or a visibility (sight) triangle. Mechanical equipment is exempt from building-height limits but not from these placement rules.

bradenton.source: Code of Ordinances, Appendix A - Land Use Regulations (LURs), Chapter 3 (District Regulations). Districts established at subsections 3.1.1 (residential), 3.1.2

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment and gas tanks, non-residential buildings (LUR subsection 5.2.2.10, PDF p.825)
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment, including, but not limited to heating, ventilating, and air conditioning machinery; and natural or propane gas tanks (except where said natural or propane gas is sold to the public), shall be screened from public view, and screening may include any combination of landscaping and building material. If building material is to be utilized for screening purposes and visible from the right-of-way, such materials shall be consistent with the architectural design of the principal structure." (Ord. No. 4065, § 3, 1-14-26.) This is a screening rule only - no distance is printed.

equip.cite: Accessory structures, residential buildings (LUR subsection 5.1.2, PDF p.818)
equip.text: "Accessory structures shall not be located within the front yard except as otherwise noted and shall maintain a five-foot setback from any side or rear property line, except as otherwise noted. Accessory structures shall be limited by the ground coverage maximums as listed on schedule 3.2.2.1 'Dimensional and Area Regulations, for Residential Districts'.... Accessory structures that are larger than 120 square feet and/or include a wall height greater than ten feet are subject to conformance with the following compatibility standards: a. The architectural style, exterior materials and colors match that of the principal structure. b. If the overall height of the structure exceeds 12 feet, the roof pitch shall match that of the principal structure." A generator pad is not named in the list of enumerated accessory structures (5.1.2.1 detached garage/carport, 5.1.2.2 swimming pools, 5.1.2.3 storage buildings/greenhouses/utility sheds/bath houses, 5.1.2.4 garbage can and dumpster enclosures, 5.1.2.5 driveways and parking areas, 5.1.2.6 gazebos/lanais, 5.1.2.7 fences and hedges), but that list is prefaced "include, but are not limited to, those listed below."

equip.cite: Accessory structure setback in the dimensional schedules
equip.text: Schedule 3.2.2.1 row "Accessory building & structures, except fences (7) - side and rear": 5 ft in every residential district (R-1, R-2, R-3, UV, R-4). Footnote (7): "With the exception of fences, accessory buildings or accessory structures shall not be placed on easements." Schedule 3.2.2.2 row "Accessory building/structure setback in feet, side or rear (11)": none in UV (both frontages), UC and UCBD; 10 ft in UCC, SCC, P and I. Footnote (11): "Pervious wood decks for outdoor seating may extend to side and rear property lines at the discretion of the PCD director. No deck or structure pursuant to this allowance may extend over any water body or wetland."

equip.cite: Propane tanks and gasoline pumps (Schedule 3.2.2.2 footnote 14, PDF p.761)
equip.text: "Gasoline pumps and propane tanks shall meet a 25-foot front setback and shall be landscaped." (Ord. No. 4069, § 8, 3-25-26.) This is the only printed distance in the Bradenton code that attaches to a fuel tank.

equip.cite: Propane cylinders and heat-producing appliances (Code of Ordinances § 42-45, PDF p.501)
equip.text: "Sec. 42-45. Storage/use of propane, heating, and cooking appliances. (a) No person shall place or maintain gas or propane cylinders on porches, breezeways, balconies, or attached garages in multi-unit or multi-story buildings. (b) No person shall store or use any charcoal, gas, or wood-fired heaters, grills, barbecues, or smokers on porches, balconies, or breezeways of any multi-unit or multi-story buildings. (c) No person shall store or use any heat-producing device or appliance which is determined by the AHJ to be unsafe due to its application or use." (Ord. No. 2770, § 1, 12-15-04; Ord. No. 4022, § 2.C., 10-11-23.)

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical equipment (LUR subsection 6.1.5.6, PDF p.850)
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment on rooftops should be screened, preferably behind a parapet roof. Latticework, louvered panels, and other treatments that are compatible with the building's architecture may also be appropriate." Advisory ("should"), part of the architectural design standards.

equip.cite: Ground-mounted equipment analogue - satellite antennas (LUR subsection 5.1.2.13.e residential / 5.2.2.6.b non-residential)
equip.text: "All ground-mounted satellite antennas shall be screened from view by a six-foot-high wood or masonry fence or plants, being 80 percent opaque when viewed between two and six feet above grade. Said antennas shall be set back from the rear and side property lines by a distance equal to their height, but no less than the required side or rear set back for the zone district. In no case shall said antennas be located closer to the front property line than the front face of the building to which it is accessory." Recorded because it is the nearest printed treatment of a ground-mounted piece of equipment; it does not name generators.

equip.cite: Generators
equip.text: The word "generator" appears in this document only in the phrases "traffic generators" and "major traffic generators" (subsection 4.1.3, road classifications). There is no standby-generator, emergency-power or backup-power section anywhere in the Bradenton Code of Ordinances or its Land Use Regulations, and no separation distance to windows, air intakes or property lines for one. The clauses that would reach a generator pad are the 5.1.2 residential accessory-structure five-foot side/rear setback, the Schedule 3.2.2.1 / 3.2.2.2 accessory-structure setback rows, and the 5.2.2.10 screening requirement.

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures — location (§ 7.09.01, 'Minimum size and location requirements for accessory uses and structures')
equip.text: '(1) Accessory uses and structures shall be located on the same parcel as the principal structure. (2) Accessory uses and structures shall be located to the side or rear of a principal structure. (3) Accessory uses and structures shall not be located within any required setbacks or easements. (4) Accessory uses and structures shall not be greater in size or height than the principal structure. Structures built to store a personal RV or boat may follow the height limitation of their zoning district. (5) The minimum distance between an accessory structure and the principal structure shall be five feet. This does not include decks, patios or similar installations intended to be attached to a primary structure. (6) Accessory uses and structures within side yards (with the exception of garages and accessory dwelling units) shall be screened with fencing or landscaping if located within 50 feet of a public roadway.'

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures — general standards (§ 7.09.01)
equip.text: '(1) Accessory uses and structures shall be constructed with or after the principal use. (2) Accessory uses and structures shall be compatible in design and materials with the principal structure. (3) Commercial accessory uses and structures must be approved via the site plan review process. (4) If an accessory structure is to be connected to electric, it shall use the same meter as the principal structure. (5) Residential accessory uses such as garages, greenhouses, workshops, or sheds shall not be rented or inhabited. This does not apply to accessory dwelling units meeting the criteria outlined in section 7.09.01.01 below. (6) Lots that are one acre or less may have up to two accessory structures. (7) Lots that are greater than one acre may have up to three accessory structures.'

equip.cite: Minimum accessory building setbacks, Table 7.02.01
equip.text: Table 7.02.01 prints a separate 'Minimum accessory building setback (ft.)' row, which for several districts is looser than the principal-structure setback: R-1 Side 15 / Rear 15; R-1 A Side 15 / Rear 15; R-2 Side 5 / Rear 5; R-3 Side 5 / Rear 5; C-1 Side 15 / Rear 15; C-2 Side 7.5 / Rear 7.5; C-3 Side 15 / Rear 15; IND Side 15 / Rear 30. No front accessory setback is given in that row. Note that § 7.09.01 separately forbids an accessory structure in ANY required setback, so the table's accessory figures and § 7.09.01(3) must be read together.

equip.cite: Rooftop HVAC concealment (§ 7.10.02, large retail projects)
equip.text: 'Flat roof lines, rooftop equipment, and heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) units shall be effectively concealed from any facade view by adjacent land uses of lesser intensity, and public right-of-way.' And at § 7.10.02(c): 'a. Effective concealment of flat roof lines, rooftop equipment, and heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) units from any facade view by adjacent land uses of lesser intensity, and public right-of-way. The parapet design shall be a minimum of three feet in height and shall incorporate a three dimensional...' This is a screening standard for large retail, not a ground-equipment setback.

equip.cite: Ground mounted earth station antennas (§ 7.09, PDF p.617)
equip.text: 'Placement shall not be allowed in the front yard of any lot or parcel in any residential zoning district. Compliance with side and rear setback is required. (e) Ground mounted earth station antennas shall be erected at a minimum height which allows satellite reception, not to exceed ten feet. Said measurement shall be calculated from the established grade to...' This is the closest analogue in the code to a ground-mounted equipment placement rule, and it applies only to earth station antennas.

equip.cite: Food truck generators (§ 7.09.30, mobile food vendors)
equip.text: 'Food trucks operating within a food truck park must not operate a generator at the site, except when necessary in the case of an emergency.' The only use of the word 'generator' in the Land Development Code, and it is a prohibition on operation, not a placement standard.

equip.cite: Flood-hazard placement of service equipment (§ 4.02, floodplain protection)
equip.text: 'Electrical, heating, ventilation, plumbing, air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, including duct work, shall be designed and/or located so as to prevent water from entering or accumulating within the components during conditions of [the design flood]'. And § 4.02.13.8 Utility equipment: 'Utility equipment that serves manufactured homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322.' These govern elevation and flood resistance, not horizontal clearance.

equip.cite: Highway Enhancement Zone front yard setbacks (Table 3.04.01, § 3.04.02.01.01)
equip.text: 'For purposes of this regulation, any portion of a property fronting on a major roadway listed in section 3.04.01.03 above shall be considered to be a front yard. The front yard setback for each HE Zone is established by Table 3.04.01. If the zoning classification of the property requires a greater front yard setback, the greater setback shall apply.' Table 3.04.01 Required Front Yard Setbacks: 'HE Zone 1 — 35 feet; HE Zone 2 — 35 feet; HE Zone 3 — 35 feet; HE Zone 4 — 12.5 feet; HE Zone 5 — 35 feet; HE Zone 6 — 12.5 feet; HE Zone 7(A) — 12.5 feet; HE Zone 7(B) — 25 Feet; HE Zone 8 — 25 feet; HE zone 9 — 12.5 feet.' The overlay 'extends 300 feet from each side of the right-of-way of the highway' (§ 3.04.01.03). § 3.04.02.01.02: 'Permitted uses within the front yard setback required by the highway enhancement zone include entrance driveways, sidewalks, signs (subject to the restrictions defined herein) and required landscaping. Parking lots and circulation drives shall not be permitted within the front yard setback.'

equip.cite: Downtown Development Overlay build-to-lines (§ 3.05.03.01)
equip.text: 'To achieve the objectives of this ordinance, new development within the Downtown Development District shall adhere to build-to-lines prescribed in this ordinance. These build-to-line standards shall supersede the setback standards prescribed for existing zoning. The primary building developed on each property shall adhere to the following build-to-lines: (1) In no event shall a primary building be constructed at a distance from the street right-of-way adjoining its front yard than the setback distance prescribed by the zoning classification of the property. (2) The build-to-line for properties fronting on US Hwy 441 shall be 15 feet. (3) The build-to-line for all other areas shall be determined by the following criteria: a. The build-to-line shall match the dominant building line of the "contributing" structures existing within the block where the property is located. In the event, the building line of "contributing" buildings is varied; the building line of the "contributing" structure closest to the right-of-way shall be established as the build-to-line. b. If no "contributing" structure exists within the block, the build-to-line shall match the dominant building line of the existing structures within the block where the property is located...'

equip.cite: Municipal wastewater pump station standby generators (Appendix C, Manual of Development and Design Standards §§ 22.5 and 46.6)
equip.text: § 22.5 EMERGENCY OPERATION: 'All pump stations shall be provided with emergency power receptacles as specified in Section 48.9. In addition, stand-by emergency generators shall be provided at all wastewater pumping stations which are at critical points in the sewer system or which have a peak design capacity of 1,000 GPM or more. Determination of pump station critical points shall be at the discretion of the CITY. Such stand-by generator facilities shall comply with the requirements spelled out in Section 46.6. All such generators shall be rated and designed to operate the pump station under design conditions.' § 46.6.1 GENERAL: 'A standby power generator system shall be installed at pump stations as required by Section 22.5 for electrical power during the loss of normal power.' § 46.6.2.1: 'The generator set shall consist of a diesel engine directly coupled to an electric generator, together with the necessary controls and accessories to provide continuous...' These apply to CITY wastewater pump stations only, not to a generator on a private parcel, and they set equipment specifications, not clearances.

equip.cite: Accessory structures - general location
equip.text: Sec. 4-2, subsection 4-2.2.2.f: 'Accessory structures shall be allowed only in side or rear yards, unless otherwise specified herein.' Subsection 4-2.2.2.b: 'All accessory structures shall comply with standards pertaining to the principal use, unless exempted or superseded elsewhere in this Code.' Subsection 4-2.2.2.c: 'Accessory structures shall not be located in required buffer or landscape areas.' Subsection 4-2.2.2.d: 'Accessory structures shall be included in all calculations of impervious surface water and stormwater runoff.' Subsection 4-2.2.2.e: 'Accessory structures shall be subject to development review and shall require a site development plan with full supporting documentation as required in article II of this Code.' The definition of accessory structure at Sec. 3-1 reads: 'At a minimum, accessory structures shall include storage buildings and other structures used for storage, shops, garages, carports, utility buildings, greenhouses, swimming pools, decks, patios, fences and satellite dishes.' It does not name a generator, a condenser or a mechanical pad.

equip.cite: Accessory structure setback, per district
equip.text: Repeated verbatim in the development standards of R-1 (4-1.7.1.d.vii), R-2 (4-1.7.2.d.vii), R-3 (4-1.7.3.d.vii) and MU (4-1.7.4.d.vii): 'Minimum setbacks for accessory structures: Three feet from any abutting property line.' The COM, IND, REC, PI, CON, RT, DISTA and PUD development standards print no accessory-structure setback.

equip.cite: Storage buildings and similar accessory structures
equip.text: Subsection 4-2.2.3.b: 'Storage buildings, greenhouses, and the like shall not be located closer than three feet from any abutting interior property line or five feet from any alley right-of-way.' Subsection 4-2.2.3.c: 'Storage and other buildings regulated by this subsection shall be permitted only in side and rear yards.'

equip.cite: Private swimming pools
equip.text: Subsection 4-2.2.4.b: 'Swimming pools shall be permitted only in side and rear yards, and shall conform to accessory building setback requirements.' Subsection 4-2.2.4.e: 'No overhead electric power lines shall pass over any pool unless enclosed in conduit and rigidly supported, nor shall any power line be nearer than ten feet horizontally or vertically from the pool's water edge.' No pool-pump or pool-equipment clearance is printed.

equip.cite: Wellhead protection special treatment area
equip.text: Subsection 4-1.7.12.c, which applies as an overlay wherever mapped: 'i. The City shall prohibit installation of septic tanks within 200 feet of municipal potable water wells. ii. Uses which store, transfer, or use hazardous materials shall not be permitted within 200 feet of municipal potable water wells. iii. Underground storage tanks containing gasoline, diesel fuel, or other hazardous substances shall not be permitted within 300 feet of municipal potable water wells.' The 300-foot standard is written for underground tanks; the code does not extend it in terms to an above-ground generator day tank.

equip.cite: Supplemental performance standards (all districts)
equip.text: Subsection 4-1.8.2.a, Noise: 'No development shall be allowed adjacent to residential properties which causes unreasonably loud and raucous sound levels on such residential properties.' The factors listed are proximity to sleeping facilities, the land use and zoning of the area, time of day, duration, and whether the sound is recurrent, intermittent or constant. No decibel limit and no distance is given. Subsection 4-1.8.2.g, Eyesores and junk: 'No equipment, material, vehicle or product shall be stored or kept in such a manner as to present an offensive or unsightly appearance when viewed from any adjacent property.'

equip.cite: Generators in the general Code of Ordinances (not zoning)
equip.text: Sec. 42-62, Audio devices (parks chapter): 'No person shall operate or use any audio devices, including radio, television, musical instruments, or any other noise producing devices such as electrical generators, and equipment driven by motor engines, in such a manner at such times as to disturb other persons.' In the mobile food dispensing vehicle standards: 'L/P gas and generator storage and use shall be consistent with the Florida Fire Prevention Code' and 'Noise levels from any generator must not exceed manufacturer specifications.' Neither is a setback.
