brevard_county.name: Brevard County
brevard_county.source: Code of Ordinances, Chapter 62, Article VI (Zoning Regulations), Division 4 'Regulations for Specific Zoning Classifications' (§§ 62-1331 through 62-1574) — per

gen.cite: Air conditioning units and whole house / back-up generators (§ 62-2121(e)(5))
gen.text: 'Air conditioning units and permanently installed whole house or back up generators may project no more than four feet into the required side or rear setback and are not subject to separation distances between structures.'

gen.cite: Self storage mini-warehouses (§ 62-1837.5)
gen.text: Where a self storage mini-warehouse is located in the BU-1 classification, '(5) The use of generators of any kind is prohibited' and signage must be placed on each building indicating that no generator use is permitted.

equip.cite: Pool pumps, irrigation pumps and other mechanical appliances (§ 62-2121(e)(5), continued)
equip.text: 'Pool pumps and equipment, irrigation pumps and equipment and other electrical or mechanical appliances and equipment accessory to residential use are not structures and are not subject to setbacks or separation distances between structures.'

equip.cite: Other permitted projections into a required setback (§ 62-2121(e)(1)–(4))
equip.text: '(1) Stairs, fire escapes, and chimneys may project no more than four feet into the required side or rear setback. (2) Wing walls or other structural extensions from the primary structure, including planting boxes, may project into any required setback as long as they are four feet or less in height. (3) Roof overhangs of four feet or less may project into any required setback. (4) Elevated or cantilevered sun decks or balconies may project into the setback toward the water where the property is adjacent to a major water body.'

equip.cite: Accessory building and accessory use standards (§ 62-2100.5)
equip.text: Number of accessory buildings per lot is set by Table I: lot area 7,500 sf or less → 1; 7,501–25,000 → 2; 25,001–35,000 → 3; 35,001–45,000 → 4, plus one additional accessory building for each 15,000 sf of land area beyond 45,000 sf. 'Swimming pools, screened enclosures, docks, equipment/pump houses, and dog houses (not requiring a building permit) are exempt from the accessory building number limitation imposed by this section.' 'Setback provisions for accessory buildings can be found within the general or specific setback provisions stated within each zoning classification.' Each detached accessory building secondary to a single-family residential use shall not exceed 600 sf or 50 percent of the living area of the principal building, whichever is greater (administratively expandable to 1,000 sf on lots one acre or larger). Within commercial, industrial and government managed lands classifications, accessory buildings must meet all setback requirements for a principal structure and maintain a minimum spacing distance of 15 feet between structures.

equip.cite: Swimming pools and screened enclosures (§ 62-2123)
equip.text: 'Such swimming pools and screened enclosures shall be set back not less than five feet from the side and rear lot lines.' Swimming pools shall be set back not less than five feet to the rear of the front building line of the principal building exclusive of open porches, and shall not encroach into any drainage, utility or other easement. On corner lots screen enclosures must meet the minimum side street setback of the applicable classification; swimming pools on corner lots shall be set back five feet in addition to the required side street setback.

equip.cite: Seawall clearance (§ 62-2121(a))
equip.text: 'No construction shall be permitted within ten feet of any seawall or bulkhead, excluding a screen enclosure, landscaping retaining wall not to exceed 36 inches in height, or private boat pier or slip as an accessory use if permitted under the applicable zoning classification.'

equip.cite: Buildings for public assemblage (§ 62-2121(d))
equip.text: In areas other than commercial or industrial classifications, buildings for public assemblage for 25 or more persons 'shall be located no closer than 25 feet to any property line which abuts on a public highway or alley, or 50 feet to any property line abutting a lot under different ownership than that on which the structure is to be placed.'

equip.cite: Additional building height above 35 feet (§ 62-2101.5)
equip.text: All building heights above 35 ft, regardless of classification, must satisfy: the distance between the building and the lot line of any adjacent parcel shall be no less than the setback required by the applicable classification plus 1.25 times the building height in excess of 35 ft, i.e. [(X-35)×1.25]+Z; and in no event shall the ratio of the distance to a residentially zoned parcel's lot line to the structure height be less than two to one.

equip.cite: Underground utilities in PUD / RPUD / THPUD (§§ 62-1446(h), 62-1476(h))
equip.text: 'Large transformers shall be placed on the ground and contained within pad mounts, enclosures or vaults. The developer must provide landscaping with shrubs and plants to screen all utility facilities permitted aboveground.'

equip.cite: Zero lot line subdivisions (§ 62-1959)
equip.text: 'No windows, doors, air conditioning units or other openings or accessories shall be permitted within the zero side yard, and no portion of a structure, including appurtenances, shall project over or across any property line.' All structures must be built within the platted building envelope.

GU.note: § 62-1331. Minimum lot size 'an area of not less than five acres... minimum width of 300 feet and a minimum depth of 300 feet' (5 ac × 43,560 = 217,800 sf). Corner lot side street setback not less than 15 ft; if the corner lot is contiguous to a key lot, not less than 25 ft. Accessory buildings to the rear of the front building line, not less than 15 ft from side lot lines and 15 ft from the rear lot line.

PA.note: § 62-1332 Productive agricultural. Minimum lot 'not less than five acres... minimum width of 300 feet and a minimum depth of 300 feet' (217,800 sf). Maximum height 35 ft for residential structures and 45 ft for accessory structures.

AGR.note: § 62-1333 Agricultural. Minimum lot 'not less than five acres... minimum width of 200 feet and a minimum depth of 300 feet' (217,800 sf). Setbacks are for primary structures; on corner lots both street frontages are subject to the front yard setback. Accessory structures not less than 15 ft from side and rear lot lines, behind the front building line. Barns and stalls: front 125 ft, side 50 ft, rear 50 ft.

AU.note: § 62-1334 Agricultural residential (includes the AU(L) sub-classification). Minimum lot 'not less than two and one-half acres... minimum width of 150 feet and a minimum depth of 150 feet' (2.5 ac × 43,560 = 108,900 sf). If a corner lot is contiguous to a key lot the side street setback is not less than 25 ft.

ARR.heightNote: § 62-1334.5 sets no maximum height of structures; subsections (7) and (8) instead say there is 'no limit to the maximum floor area' of attached additions and of accessory structures. Building heights above 35 ft are governed by § 62-2101.5.
ARR.note: § 62-1334.5 Agricultural rural residential. Minimum lot 'not less than one acre... width of not less than 125 feet and a depth of not less than 200 feet' (43,560 sf). Corner lot side street setback not less than 10 ft; if contiguous to a key lot, not less than 15 ft. Barns, paddocks and stalls: front 50 ft, side 25 ft, rear 25 ft. Minimum floor area 700 sf.

REU.note: § 62-1335 Rural estate use. Minimum lot 'not less than two and one-half acres... minimum width of 200 feet and a minimum depth of 200 feet' (108,900 sf). Setbacks are for principal structures. If a corner lot is contiguous to a key lot the side street setback is not less than 25 ft. Accessory structures not less than 15 ft from side and rear lot lines, to the rear of the front building line.

RR-1.note: § 62-1336 Rural residential. Minimum lot 'not less than one acre... width of not less than 125 feet and a depth of not less than 125 feet' (43,560 sf). Corner lot side street setback not less than 15 ft; if contiguous to a key lot, not less than 25 ft. Accessory buildings not less than 15 ft from side and rear lot lines. Barns and stalls: front 125 ft, side 50 ft, rear 50 ft.

SEU.note: § 62-1337 Suburban estate residential use. Minimum lot 'not less than one acre (43,560 square feet)... width of not less than 125 feet and... depth of not less than 200 feet'. Setback subsection is headed 'Setbacks. (Also see special waterfront setbacks.)'. Corner lot side street setback not less than 15 ft; key lot 25 ft.

SR.note: § 62-1338 Suburban residential. Minimum lot 'not less than one-half acre... width of not less than 100 feet and... depth of not less than 150 feet' (0.5 ac × 43,560 = 21,780 sf). Corner lot side street setback not less than 15 ft; key lot 25 ft. Accessory buildings no closer than 10 ft to rear and side lot lines, minimum spacing 5 ft. Minimum floor area 1,300 sf.

EU.note: § 62-1339 Estate use residential. Minimum lot criteria table: EU 15,000 sf, width 100 ft, depth 100 ft. Corner lot side street setback not less than 15 ft; key lot 25 ft. Accessory buildings no closer than 10 ft to rear and side lot lines, minimum spacing 5 ft. Minimum floor area 2,000 sf.

EU-1.note: § 62-1339. Minimum lot criteria table: EU-1 12,000 sf, width 100 ft, depth 100 ft. Corner side street 15 ft, key lot 25 ft. Accessory buildings 10 ft from rear and side lot lines. Minimum floor area 1,800 sf.

EU-2.note: § 62-1339. Minimum lot criteria table: EU-2 9,000 sf, width 90 ft, depth 100 ft. Corner side street 15 ft, key lot 25 ft. Accessory buildings 10 ft from rear and side lot lines. Minimum floor area 1,500 sf.

RU-1-13.note: § 62-1340. Minimum lot 7,500 sf, width 75 ft, depth 75 ft (same for RU-1-13 and RU-1-11). Screen porches may be set back not less than 10 ft from the rear lot line. Corner lot side street setback not less than 15 ft; key lot 20 ft. Front setback may be reduced to 15 ft where an alley is provided and all lots use the alley for vehicular access.

RU-1-11.note: § 62-1340. Minimum lot 7,500 sf, width 75 ft, depth 75 ft. Screen porches 10 ft from rear lot line. Corner side street 15 ft; key lot 20 ft. Front may be reduced to 15 ft with an alley. Accessory buildings 7.5 ft from rear and side lot lines. Minimum floor area 1,100 sf.

RU-1-9.note: § 62-1341. Minimum lot 6,600 sf, width 66 ft, depth 100 ft. Screen porches 10 ft from rear lot line. Corner side street 15 ft; key lot 20 ft. Front may be reduced to 15 ft with an alley. Accessory buildings 7.5 ft from rear and side lot lines, minimum spacing 5 ft from all other structures. Minimum floor area 900 sf.

RU-1-7.note: § 62-1342. Minimum lot 5,000 sf, width 50 ft, depth 100 ft. Screen porches 10 ft from rear lot line. Corner side street 15 ft; key lot 20 ft. Front may be reduced to 15 ft with an alley. Accessory buildings no closer than 5 ft to rear and side lot lines, minimum spacing 5 ft. Minimum floor area 700 sf.

RU-2-6.heightNote: Same § 62-1371(8) structural height standards as RU-2-4 (35 ft or 45 ft depending on the abutting classification).
RU-2-6.note: § 62-1371. Maximum density 6 units per gross acre. All other standards as RU-2-4.

RU-2-8.sideNote: § 62-1371(5)c.3: not less than 7.5 ft for all single family residences and 10 ft for all other structures; corner lots at least 15 ft; key lot 25 ft.
RU-2-8.heightNote: Same § 62-1371(8) structural height standards as RU-2-4 (35 ft or 45 ft depending on the abutting classification).
RU-2-8.note: § 62-1371. Maximum density 8 units per gross acre. All other standards as RU-2-4.

RU-2-10.sideNote: § 62-1372(5)c.3: 'The side setback shall be not less than seven and one-half for all single family residences and ten feet for all other structures.' On corner lots at least 15 ft from the side lot line; if contiguous to a key lot, not less than 25 ft.
RU-2-10.heightNote: § 62-1372(8): 35 ft where the property abuts GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft where it abuts RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RU-2-15, RU-2-30, RP, BU-1-A, BU-1, BU-2, PBP, IU, PIP, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
RU-2-10.note: § 62-1372 Medium-density multiple-family residential. Minimum lot size 7,500 sf, width 75 ft, depth 75 ft. Maximum density 10 units per gross acre. Maximum lot coverage 40 percent. Accessory buildings not less than 7.5 ft from side and rear lot lines, to the rear of the front building line, minimum spacing 5 ft. Principal structures spaced at least 15 ft apart.

RU-2-12.sideNote: § 62-1372(5)c.3: not less than 7.5 ft for all single family residences and 10 ft for all other structures; corner lots at least 15 ft; key lot 25 ft.
RU-2-12.heightNote: Same § 62-1372(8) structural height standards as RU-2-10 (35 ft or 45 ft depending on the abutting classification).
RU-2-12.note: § 62-1372. Maximum density 12 units per gross acre. All other standards as RU-2-10.

RU-2-15.sideNote: § 62-1372(5)c.3: not less than 7.5 ft for all single family residences and 10 ft for all other structures; corner lots at least 15 ft; key lot 25 ft.
RU-2-15.heightNote: Same § 62-1372(8) structural height standards as RU-2-10 (35 ft or 45 ft depending on the abutting classification).
RU-2-15.note: § 62-1372. Maximum density 15 units per gross acre. All other standards as RU-2-10.

RU-2-30 (multifamily structures).sideNote: § 62-1373(5)b.3: 'The side setback shall be not less than seven and one-half [feet] for all single family residences and ten feet for all other structures.' On corner lots side setbacks at least 15 ft from the side lot line; if contiguous to a key lot, not less than 25 ft.
RU-2-30 (multifamily structures).heightNote: § 62-1373(7): 35 ft where the property abuts GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft where it abuts RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RU-2-15, RU-2-30, RP, BU-1-A, BU-1, BU-2, PBP, PIP, IU, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
RU-2-30 (multifamily structures).note: § 62-1373 High-density multiple-family residential. 'Minimum lot size for multifamily structures. An area of not less than 10,000 square feet is required for multifamily structures, having a width of not less than 100 feet and a depth of not less than 100 feet.' Maximum density 30 dwelling units per gross acre.

RU-2-30 (single-family residence or dupl.sideNote: § 62-1373(5)b.3: not less than 7.5 ft for all single family residences and 10 ft for all other structures; corner lots at least 15 ft; key lot 25 ft.
RU-2-30 (single-family residence or dupl.heightNote: Same § 62-1373(7) structural height standards (35 ft or 45 ft depending on the abutting classification).
RU-2-30 (single-family residence or dupl.note: § 62-1373(4)b: 'An area of not less than 7,500 square feet is required for a single-family residence or duplex, having a depth of not less than 75 feet and a width of not less than 75 feet.'

RRMH-1.note: § 62-1401 Rural residential mobile home. Minimum lot size table: RRMH-1 lot size 1 acre (43,560 sf), lot width 125 ft, lot depth 125 ft. Setbacks are for principal structures; if a corner lot is contiguous to a key lot the side street setbacks are not less than 25 ft. Accessory buildings to the rear of the front building line and not less than 15 ft from side and rear lot lines.

RRMH-2.5.note: § 62-1401. Minimum lot size table: RRMH-2.5 lot size 2.5 acres (108,900 sf), width 150 ft, depth 150 ft. Same setbacks, accessory-building and barn standards as RRMH-1. Minimum living area 600 sf.

RRMH-5.note: § 62-1401. Minimum lot size table: RRMH-5 lot size 5 acres (217,800 sf), width 300 ft, depth 300 ft. Same setbacks, accessory-building and barn standards as RRMH-1. Minimum living area 600 sf.

TR-1.note: § 62-1402 Single-family mobile home. Minimum lot size table: TR-1 7,500 sf, width 65 ft, depth 100 ft. Setback table: front 25, rear 20, side 7.5. On a corner lot the side street setback is not less than 15 ft including accessory buildings; if contiguous to a key lot, not less than 25 ft including accessory buildings.

TR-1-A.note: § 62-1402. Minimum lot size table: TR-1-A 5,000 sf, width 50 ft, depth 100 ft. Setback table: front 25, rear 20, side 5. Corner lot side street 15 ft (key lot 25 ft) including accessory buildings. Detached accessory buildings 5 ft from rear and side lot lines for the TR-1-A classification, minimum spacing 5 ft. Minimum living area 600 sf.

TR-2.note: § 62-1403 Single-family mobile home, TR-2. Minimum lot 'not less than one-half acre... width of not less than 100 feet and a depth of not less than 150 feet' (21,780 sf). Setbacks are for principal structures. Corner lot side street setback not less than 15 ft including accessory buildings; key lot 25 ft including accessory buildings.

TR-3.frontNote: § 62-1404(6)b street setbacks: individual structures within the park shall be set back not less than 20 ft from all public rights-of-way and not less than 15 ft from pavement edges of private streets.
TR-3.sideNote: § 62-1404(6)a perimeter setbacks: mobile homes and structures shall be set back not less than 50 ft from all property lines, unless the line is contiguous to property zoned TR-1, TR-1-A, TR-2, TRC-1, TR-3, RVP, BU-1, BU-1-A, BU-2, RP, TU-1, TU-2 or any industrial classification, in which case 15 ft; or contiguous to multiple-family residential, in which case 20 ft. Minimum distance between structures is 10 ft.
TR-3.rearNote: Same perimeter/street setback regime as above; no per-lot rear setback is printed.
TR-3.note: § 62-1404 Mobile home park. Minimum size of park site 10 acres. Minimum mobile home site 4,000 sf with minimum width 40 ft. Minimum floor area 500 sf. Maximum height of structures 35 ft; no accessory structure or addition to a mobile home may exceed 20 ft measured from final grade. Recreation area at least 20 percent of the gross park area.

TRC-1.note: § 62-1405 Single-family mobile home cooperative. Minimum site size 5 acres. Minimum lot size 'not less 6,000 square feet, having a width of not less than 65 feet and a depth of not less than 80 feet'. Setbacks are for principal structures; on a corner lot the side street setback is not less than 20 ft. Accessory buildings not less than 7.5 ft from rear and side lot lines, minimum spacing 5 ft.

RVP.sideNote: § 62-1406(7)c.2: 'The side setback shall be five feet on one side and ten feet on the other side.'
RVP.note: § 62-1406 Recreational vehicle park. Each parcel used for an RV park shall be a minimum of five acres. Each recreational vehicle site shall have a minimum area of 2,000 sf, minimum width 30 ft and minimum depth 60 ft. Front setback is measured from the lot line in a platted park or from the street in an unplatted park.

PUD.frontNote: § 62-1446(d)(4): except for single-family detached structures, setbacks between the nearest building wall and the edge of any public right-of-way or private street pavement shall be 25 ft unless waived by the board of county commissioners. For single-family detached structures on local public streets the front setback shall be a minimum of 20 ft (an attached open porch may be 10 ft).
PUD.sideNote: § 62-1446(d)(3)a: single-family detached structures shall be set back not less than 5 ft from the side lot lines for lots less than 75 ft in width, 7.5 ft for lots at least 75 but less than 100 ft in width, and 10 ft for lots at least 100 ft in width. On a corner lot the side street setback is not less than 15 ft; if contiguous to a key lot the side setback follows the front setback in (d)(4).
PUD.heightNote: § 62-1446(e): 35 ft where the property abuts land designated or zoned for single-family residential use; 45 ft where it abuts attached single-family, multifamily or institutional use; 60 ft where it abuts commercial use on the PUD plan or land zoned commercial or industrial. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
PUD.note: §§ 62-1441—62-1455 Planned unit development. 'The minimum lot size for detached single-family structures shall be an area not less than 5,000 square feet and having a width of not less than 50 feet', waivable by the board of county commissioners. Rear setback for single-family detached structures not less than 20 ft, except screened porches not less than 10 ft.

RPUD.frontNote: § 62-1466(d)(4): except for single-family detached structures, setbacks between the nearest building wall and the edge of any public right-of-way or private street pavement shall be 10 ft. For single-family detached structures on local public streets the front setback shall be a minimum of 10 ft (a solid-roofed open front porch may be 5 ft where a 6-ft sidewalk is provided).
RPUD.heightNote: § 62-1466(e): 35 ft where the property abuts land designated or zoned for single-family residential use (or as required for RPUD perimeter lots under (d)(13)); 35 ft where it abuts attached single-family, multifamily or institutional use.
RPUD.note: §§ 62-1461—62-1470 Residential planned unit development. 'The minimum lot size for detached single-family structures shall be an area not less than 4000 square feet and having a width of not less than 40 feet'; applicants proposing lots under 5,000 sf / 50 ft width must submit an RPUD development plan. Single-family detached side setback not less than 5 ft; rear not less than 20 ft (screened porches 10 ft).

THPUD.frontNote: § 62-1476(d)(3): 'The developer shall propose all primary and accessory building setbacks and separation distances between structures as part of the preliminary development plan document.' A minimum 25-foot setback shall be maintained between the wall of any structure and the property line along the perimeter of the THPUD unless waived by the board of county commissioners, plus a 25-foot-wide perimeter landscaped buffer tract from abutting property not under the developer's ownership.
THPUD.heightNote: § 62-1476(e): 35 ft where the property abuts land designated or zoned for single-family residential use; 45 ft where it abuts attached single-family, multifamily or institutional use; 60 ft where it abuts commercial or industrial use. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
THPUD.note: §§ 62-1471—62-1480 Tiny house planned unit development. Minimum THPUD size 0.5 acre, maximum 10.0 acres. 'The developer shall propose minimum lot dimensions (width, depth and lot area) as part of the preliminary development plan document' — no fixed minimum lot size is printed. Minimum floor area is designated by the developer up to a maximum of 900 sf of living area.

BU-1-A.sideNote: § 62-1481(5)a.3: where a side lot line abuts a residential zone the side setback shall be a minimum of 15 ft; where it abuts a non-residential zone, 5 ft; where it abuts a combination of commercial, industrial or residential zonings the respective setbacks apply to the affected side yard area.
BU-1-A.heightNote: § 62-1481(7): 35 ft where the property abuts GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft where it abuts RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RU-2-15, RU-2-30, RP, BU-1-A, BU-1, BU-2, PBP, PIP, IU, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
BU-1-A.note: § 62-1481 Restricted neighborhood commercial. Minimum lot size 'not less than 7,500 square feet... width and depth of not less than 75 feet'. Front setback 50 ft from the front lot line; rear setback 25 ft. Minimum floor area: all structures shall contain a minimum of 300 sf. Maximum floor area ratio governed by § 62-2110. No maximum lot coverage is printed.

BU-1.sideNote: § 62-1482(5)a.4: where a side lot line abuts a residential zone the side setback shall be a minimum of 15 ft; where it abuts a non-residential zone, 5 ft; combinations take the respective setbacks.
BU-1.rearNote: § 62-1482(5)a.3: 'The rear setback shall be 15 feet from the rear lot line. However, if the rear lot line abuts a dedicated 20-foot alley or roadway, the setback shall be five feet.'
BU-1.heightNote: § 62-1482(7): 35 ft abutting GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft abutting RA-2-4, R-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RP or BU-1-A; 60 ft abutting RU-2-15, RU-2-30, BU-1, BU-2, PIP, PBP, IU, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
BU-1.note: § 62-1482 General retail commercial. Minimum lot size, except for gasoline service stations, 'not less than 7,500 square feet... width and depth of not less than 75 feet'. Gasoline service station setbacks are governed by § 62-1835.7. Minimum floor area 300 sf. Maximum floor area ratio governed by § 62-2110.

BU-2.sideNote: § 62-1483(5)a.4: same regime as BU-1 — 15 ft where a side lot line abuts a residential zone, 5 ft where it abuts a non-residential zone, firewall/alley exceptions, corner lot side street 15 ft and key lot 25 ft.
BU-2.rearNote: § 62-1483(5)a.3: 'The rear setback shall be 15 feet from the rear lot line. However, if the rear lot line abuts a dedicated 20-foot alley or roadway, the setback shall be five feet.'
BU-2.heightNote: § 62-1483(7): 35 ft abutting GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft abutting RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RP or BU-1-A; 60 ft abutting RU-2-15, RU-2-30, BU-1, BU-2, PBP, PIP, IU, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
BU-2.note: § 62-1483 Retail, warehousing and wholesale commercial. Minimum lot size, except gasoline service stations, 7,500 sf with width and depth not less than 75 ft. Minimum floor area 300 sf. Maximum floor area ratio governed by § 62-2110. No maximum lot coverage is printed.

TU-1.heightNote: § 62-1511(8): 35 ft abutting GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft abutting RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RP or BU-1-A; 60 ft abutting RU-2-15, RU-2-30, BU-1, BU-2, PBP, PIP, IU, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
TU-1.note: § 62-1511 General tourist commercial. Minimum lot size 'not less than 15,000 square feet... width of not less than 100 feet and a depth of not less than 150 feet'. Maximum structural lot coverage 40 percent. Side setback: interior lot 15 ft; corner lot 15 ft, and not less than 25 ft if the corner lot is contiguous to a key lot.

TU-2.heightNote: § 62-1512(8): 35 ft abutting GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft abutting RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RP or BU-1-A; 60 ft abutting RU-2-15, RU-2-30, BU-1, BU-2, PBP, IU, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
TU-2.note: § 62-1512 Transient tourist commercial. Minimum lot size 'not less than 15,000 square feet... width of not less than 100 feet and a depth of not less than 150 feet'. Maximum lot coverage 40 percent. Side setback: interior lots 15 ft; corner lots 15 ft, and not less than 25 ft where contiguous to a key lot. Setbacks from the ocean on oceanfront property are governed by article XII.

PBP.frontNote: § 62-1541(5)a.1: 'The front setback shall be 25 feet from an internal access road or 50 feet from any public right-of-way.' SR 405/SR 407 corridor: 100 ft from an internal access road, or 200 ft from SR 405 or SR 407.
PBP.sideNote: § 62-1541(5)a.2: 'The side setback shall be 50 feet, or zero feet where a marginal access road is provided or where a single access is utilized by more than one lot from an internal road and parking facilities are shared.' SR 405/SR 407 corridor: 50 ft, with a 100-foot side street setback required where the lot is a corner lot.
PBP.rearNote: § 62-1541(5)a.3: 'The rear setback shall be 25 feet, or 40 feet if the rear lot line is the site periphery, or zero feet if the rear lot line abuts a railroad right-of-way.' SR 405/SR 407 corridor: 100 ft.
PBP.heightNote: § 62-1541(6): 35 ft abutting GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft abutting RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RU-2-15, RU-2-30, RP, BU-1-A, BU-1, BU-2, TU-1, TU-2, PBP, PIP, IU or IU-1. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
PBP.note: § 62-1541 Planned business park. Generally: minimum park size 5 acres; minimum lot size one-half acre (21,780 sf); minimum building size 2,500 sf; maximum structural coverage 50 percent of the lot; minimum common open space 20 percent of the site.

PIP.heightNote: § 62-1542(7): 35 ft abutting GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft abutting RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RU-2-15, RU-2-30, RP, BU-1-A, BU-1, BU-2, PBP, PIP, IU, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
PIP.note: § 62-1542 Planned industrial park. 'The minimum lot size shall be one acre, having a minimum width of 150 feet and a minimum depth of 200 feet. The minimum size of a planned industrial site as designated on the future land use map shall be three acres.' Front yard: all buildings set back from all street right-of-way lines at least 50 ft. Side yard: no building or wall closer than 50 ft to a side yard lot line.

IU.heightNote: § 62-1543(7): 35 ft abutting GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft abutting RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RP or BU-1-A; 60 ft abutting RU-2-15, RU-2-30, BU-1, BU-2, PBP, PIP, IU, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
IU.note: § 62-1543 Light industrial. 'All lots shall have a minimum size of 20,000 square feet, and have a minimum width of 100 feet and a minimum depth of 200 feet.' Front yard 40 ft from the front property line. Side yard: no building or wall closer than 15 ft to a side yard lot line; the width of a side yard which abuts a residential district shall be at least 100 ft, 20 ft of which shall be a buffer zone.

IU-1.heightNote: § 62-1544(8): 35 ft abutting GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft abutting RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RP or BU-1-A; 60 ft abutting RU-2-15, RU-2-30, BU-1, BU-2, PIP, PBP, IU, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
IU-1.note: § 62-1544 Heavy industrial. 'All lots shall have a minimum size of 40,000 square feet, and have a minimum width of 200 feet and a minimum depth of 200 feet.' Minimum building size 300 sf. Front yard: all structures set back not less than 40 ft from the front property line. Side yard: no building or wall closer than 20 ft to a side yard lot line.

EA.note: § 62-1571 Environmental areas. Minimum lot size 'not less than ten acres... width of not less than 125 feet and a depth of not less than 125 feet' (10 ac × 43,560 = 435,600 sf). Principal structures set back not less than 25 ft from the front or side street lot line, 10 ft from the side lot lines and 20 ft from the rear lot line.

GML.heightNote: § 62-1572(7): 35 ft abutting GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft abutting RA-2-4, RA-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RP or BU-1-A; 60 ft abutting RU-2-15, RU-2-30, BU-1, BU-2, PIP, PBP, IU, IU-1, TU-1 or TU-2. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
GML.note: § 62-1572 Government managed lands. Minimum lot size 'not less than 7,500 square feet... width and depth of at least 75 feet'. Side setback for corner lots 15 ft from the side lot line which abuts a road; if a corner lot is contiguous to a key lot, not less than 25 ft. All principal structures shall contain at least 300 sf of floor area.

IN(L).sideNote: § 62-1573(6)c: where a side lot line abuts a residential zone the side setback shall be a minimum of 15 ft; where it abuts a non-residential zone, 5 ft; combinations take the respective setbacks. On a corner lot the side street setback shall be 15 ft; if contiguous to a key lot, 25 ft. Setbacks for buildings for public assemblage shall be at least 50 ft where adjacent to residential parcels.
IN(L).heightNote: § 62-1573(7): 35 ft abutting GU, AGR, AU, ARR, REU, RU-1-7, RU-1-9, RU-1-11, RU-1-13, RR-1, EU, EU-1, EU-2, SEU, SR, RVP, TR-1-A, TR-1, TR-2, TR-3, TRC-1, RRMH-1, RRMH-2.5, RRMH-5, EA, PA or GML; 45 ft abutting RA-2-4, R-2-6, RA-2-8, RA-2-10, RU-2-4, RU-2-6, RU-2-8, RU-2-10, RU-2-12, RP or BU-1-A; 60 ft in the remaining case. Over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.

IN(H).sideNote: § 62-1573(6)c: 15 ft where a side lot line abuts a residential zone, 5 ft where it abuts a non-residential zone; corner lot side street 15 ft, key lot 25 ft. Buildings for public assemblage at least 50 ft where adjacent to residential parcels.
IN(H).heightNote: Same § 62-1573(7) structural height standards as IN(L): 35 ft / 45 ft / 60 ft depending on the abutting classification; over 35 ft must satisfy § 62-2101.5.
IN(H).note: § 62-1573 Institutional use, high intensity. Same minimum lot size (7,500 sf, width and depth at least 75 ft) and setbacks as IN(L); the one-acre minimum applies only to low-intensity permitted-with-conditions uses. High intensity institutional uses shall be located where commercial development is planned or established.

debary.source: Land Development Code, Chapter 4 (Zoning), Sec. 4.8 'Dimensional requirements' - Table 4-4 'Dimensional Standards - Conservation and Rural Districts', Table 4-5

equip.cite: No dedicated generator section
equip.text: The code prints no section on standby or emergency generators as such. The word 'generator' appears in a zoning sense only in the overlay-district mechanical equipment definition quoted below.

equip.cite: Service areas and mechanical equipment - Sec. 5.34 (OVERLAY DISTRICTS ONLY, Chapter 5)
equip.text: '(a) Service areas and mechanical equipment located on the ground, such as waste disposal containers, loading docks/spaces, air conditioning units, heating units, satellite dishes, irrigation pumps, propane tanks and refilling areas, utilities, lift stations, and the like shall be located in the rear or to the side of buildings and screened from public view (Figure 5-30). Screening shall, at a minimum, be at the same height as the equipment. Structural screening shall be architecturally integrated into the overall project design and shall be compatible, in terms of style, construction materials, colors, and finish, with the principal structure... (b) If mechanical equipment is located at-grade, and is visible from an adjacent street or sidewalk, it shall be inset into the building facade and screened with doors, or screened by a fence or street wall (see Figure 5-31). For the purposes of these standards, mechanical equipment shall include any heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) or electrical machinery but also includes air compressors, hoods, mechanical pumps, exterior water heaters, water softeners, utility and telephone company transformers, meters or boxes, garbage cans, storage tanks, generators, geothermal wells, and similar elements. Electric vehicle (EV) chargers are not deemed mechanical equipment.' NOTE: Chapter 5 is 'Overlay District Standards' and Sec. 5.34 sits in its Building Design Standards division, so this rule governs inside the overlay districts (Waterfront Use, Meadowlea, South 17-92, etc.), not citywide.

equip.cite: Accessory structures - Sec. 6.1 (citywide)
equip.text: 'Accessory buildings and structures are permitted ancillary to a principal structure... Every part of every yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground up, except as follows: (a) Accessory buildings and structures associated with a non-residential use shall meet all setback requirements for the principal building on the lot and shall not interfere with required landscaping. (b) Buildings and structures accessory to a residential use shall be located in accordance with the following: (1) Accessory structures shall not be located within any yard abutting a street. Accessory structures on all other yards (all yards not abutting a street) shall be located no less than five feet from the lot line. Accessory structures 600 square feet or greater require an increased building setback of 15 feet from the side and rear property lines.' Also '(c) No accessory structure shall exceed a height of 20 feet and cannot be taller than the principal structure.' and '(f) Principal and accessory structures, other than boat docks, boathouses and walkways, shall not be erected in platted easements.'

equip.cite: Exceptions to minimum yard requirements - Sec. 4.8(a)(2)
equip.text: 'Every part of every yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground up, except as follows: a. In all zoning classifications, accessory structures may be located in yards to the extent permitted by Chapter 6. b. In all zoning classifications, off-street parking lots may be in yards to the extent permitted by Chapter 7, but not within buffers. c. Moveable awnings, chimneys, pilasters, roof overhangs, unenclosed balconies and unenclosed stairways may project into any yard for 3 1/2 feet or half of the yard, whichever is less.' No generator, A/C, pool-equipment or LP-tank projection is named.

equip.cite: Exceptions to height regulations - Sec. 4.8(a)(4)
equip.text: 'Spires, belfries, cupolas, clerestory windows, antennas, water tanks, ventilators, solar panels, windmills, chimneys, or other similar accessory structures customarily required to extend above the roof level may extend for an additional ten feet above the maximum building height prescribed for the classification in which they are located.'

equip.cite: Screening of equipment and utilities (site/development plan standards, PDF p.285)
equip.text: 'a. Mechanical equipment located on the ground, such as air conditioning and heating units, satellite dishes, irrigation pumps, utilities lift stations and the like shall be screened from public view. Screening shall, at a minimum, be at the same height as the equipment... b. Equipment and appurtenances mounted on rooftops shall be kept to a minimum. All exposed rooftop mounted equipment and appurtenances shall be fully screened from view from any public right-of-way.'

equip.cite: Waterfront yard measurement - Sec. 4.8(a)(5)
equip.text: 'Such a yard shall be measured from the ordinary high-water mark on non-tidal waters whenever the ordinary high-water mark falls within the lot lines... provided, however, the yard on lots with seawalls shall be measured from the seawall or top of revetment.'

pensacola.name: Pensacola
pensacola.source: Code of Ordinances, Title XII Land Development Code, Chapter 12-3 ZONING DISTRICTS, Article I. There is no single consolidated schedule: each land-use district

equip.cite: Residential accessory structures — permitted location and distance to a property line (§ 12-3-55(4))
equip.text: 'a. Accessory structures shall not be permitted in any required front or required side yard except as exempted in this section. Accessory structures shall be permitted in a required rear yard. Figure 12-3.3 shows permitted locations for residential accessory structures.' Figure 12-3.3 notes: '1. Permitted only in shaded areas noted as buildable area or required rear yard. 2. Shall occupy not more than 25 percent of required rear yard area. For purposes of calculating this percentage in a corner lot rear yard, the yard shall be measured from the interior side lot line to the street right-of-way line. Swimming pools and their surrounding decking shall be exempt from this calculation. 3. Except for corner lots, accessory structures shall not be located closer than three feet from a property line in a required rear yard. 4. No part of an accessory structure may be located any closer than four feet to any part of the main dwelling unit. An open covered walkway no more than six feet wide may connect the main structure to the accessory structure. 5. Maximum height shall be determined as follows: i. Accessory structures located within three feet of the side and rear property lines shall have a maximum allowed height of 15 feet. ii. Accessory structures exceeding 15 feet must meet the side yard setback requirements of the principal dwelling unit. For every additional one foot that an accessory dwelling unit is set back from the rear property line above and beyond five feet, an additional one foot in height shall be allowed up to a maximum allowed height of 20 feet as measured at the roof peak.'

equip.cite: Required yards must be open to the sky; 24-inch projection limit (§ 12-3-64(a)(3))
equip.text: 'Every part of a required yard shall be open from its lowest point to the sky unobstructed, except for that portion occupied by permitted accessory structures, trees and shrubs and the ordinary projection of sills, belt courses, cornices, buttresses, ornamental features and eaves; provided, however, none of the above projections shall project into a required yard more than 24 inches. Open or enclosed fire escapes, outside stairways and landings projecting into a minimum yard or court not more than 3.5 feet and the ordinary projections of chimneys and flues may be permitted by the building official.'

equip.cite: Air conditioning condensing units — Pensacola historic district (§ 12-3-10(1)f.10, 'Miscellaneous mechanical equipment')
equip.text: 'i. Air conditioning condensing units shall not be mounted on any roof where they are visible from any street. ii. Air conditioning condensing units that are mounted on the ground shall be in either side yards or rear yards. No equipment shall be installed in a front yard. iii. Visual screening consisting of ornamental fencing or landscaping shall be installed around all air conditioning condensing units to conceal them from view from any adjacent street or property owner. v. Exhaust fans or other building penetrations as may be required by other authorities shall be allowed to penetrate the wall or the roof but only in locations where they can be concealed from view from any street. No penetrations shall be allowed on the front of the building. They may be allowed on side walls if they are properly screened. It is desirable that any penetrations occur on rear walls or the rear side of roofs.'

equip.cite: Air conditioning condensing units — North Hill preservation district (§ 12-3-10(2)e.x, 'Miscellaneous mechanical equipment')
equip.text: '(a) Air conditioning condensing units shall not be mounted on any roof where they are visible from any street. (b) Air conditioning condensing units that are mounted on the ground shall be in either side yards or rear yards. (c) Visual screening consisting of ornamental fencing or landscaping shall be installed around...' (the North Hill counterpart of the historic-district rule quoted above).

equip.cite: Zero-lot-line wall — no air conditioning units in the zero-lot-line wall (Table 12-3.3, R-ZL)
equip.text: 'Openings prohibited on the zero-lot-line side. The wall of the dwelling located on the lot line shall have no windows, doors, air conditioning units, or any other type of openings; provided, however, that atriums or courts shall be permitted on the zero-lot-line side when the court or atrium is enclosed by three walls of the dwelling unit.'

equip.cite: Screening of service areas and utility facilities (§ 12-3-56(c)(2))
equip.text: 'Specific uses or facilities. The following specific uses or facilities must be screened from public view from a public street and from adjoining property when the subject site is zoned or adjacent to property zoned residential, historic or preservation, redevelopment or airport. Screening material shall meet the requirements of subsection (d)(2)a of this section. a. Dumpsters or trash handling areas. b. Service entrances or utility facilities. c. Loading docks or spaces.'

equip.cite: Roof-mounted mechanical equipment screening (PDF p.864, design standards § 12-3-121)
equip.text: '...shall be screened from adjoining property and from public view. Roof-mounted electrical, mechanical, air conditioning and communications equipment shall be completely screened from adjacent properties and public view from the public right-of-way.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment in the redevelopment districts (§ 12-3-12(1)d.13, GRD)
equip.text: 'All mechanical equipment, satellite dishes and other similar equipment should be completely screened...' The same wording appears for WRD and WRD-1 (p.757).

equip.cite: Suspended air conditioning machines (Chapter on buildings, PDF p.1072)
equip.text: 'No person shall suspend an air conditioning machine from any building, or from the windows of any building or aperture of any building, so that the air conditioning machine extends beyond the wall...'

equip.cite: NOT FOUND
equip.text: No section of the Pensacola Land Development Code names a standby, emergency or permanent generator, an LP-gas or propane tank, or pool equipment in connection with a setback, separation or yard encroachment. The nearest applicable rules are the residential accessory-structure standards of § 12-3-55(4) (three feet from a property line in a required rear yard, not permitted in a required front or side yard) and the air-conditioning-condenser placement rules quoted above, which apply only inside the historic and North Hill preservation districts.

coleman.source: Land Development Code, Article IV (Zoning), Div. 3 - Table 13-423A 'Residential Zoning Districts Dimensional standards' (Sec. 13-423) and Table 13-425A 'Nonresi

equip.cite: Accessory uses - setbacks (§ 13-610(b))
equip.text: "Setbacks. Accessory uses must comply with setback standards pertaining to the principal use unless specified in section 13-440."

equip.cite: All structures, including accessory (§ 13-440(b)(1))
equip.text: "The distances in Table 13-440A shall be the minimum setback for all above or below ground structures, including accessory structures, unless otherwise specifically provided in section 13-610. The setback providing the greatest distance from the road centerline shall be used."

equip.cite: Side/rear lot lines, all structures (§ 13-440(c)(1))
equip.text: "The setback distances in Tables 13-423A and 425A shall be the minimum setback distances from side and rear lot/parcel lines for all substantial above-ground structures, including accessory structures, and in or below ground structures."

equip.cite: Small accessory buildings in residential districts (§ 13-440(c)(2)a)
equip.text: "In residential zoning districts, accessory buildings of not more than 100 square feet shall be required to only observe a one-foot setback from lot lines, provided such building does not exceed ten feet in height. Accessory structures with reduced setbacks shall not be located within the front yard."

equip.cite: Underground storage tanks (§ 13-440(c)(2)c)
equip.text: "Underground storage tank setbacks shall be ten feet to any wall or surface of the tank, excluding piping. Front setback from a maintained road right-of-way may be administratively reduced by the development services director upon demonstration of good cause."

equip.cite: Swimming pools / spas and screen enclosures (§ 13-440(c)(2)b)
equip.text: "Setbacks shall be as for other above-ground structures, or five feet for the outermost structure, whichever is less, provided adjacent property is protected from damage due to excavation, etc."

equip.cite: Above-ground extensions of a building (§ 13-440(a)(3)b)
equip.text: "Measurement shall be to the nearest vertical wall or support of the building or structure, provided any above-ground extension of the building does not encroach into the required setback more than two feet, or onto adjoining property. Any above-ground encroachment of more than two feet into the required setback will require a compensating setback increase in the structure's wall or support."

equip.cite: On-site utilities as accessory use (§ 13-610(c)(1)e)
equip.text: "On-site utilities, including water and sewer facilities, serving only the project on which they are located" are specifically presumed to be accessory uses in all zoning districts.

equip.cite: Nonresidential lot abutting residential (§ 13-440(e)(2))
equip.text: "Whenever a lot in a nonresidential district has a common boundary line with a lot in a residential district, and the property line setback requirement applicable to the residential lot is greater than that applicable to the nonresidential lot, then the lot in the nonresidential district shall be required to observe the property line setback requirement applicable to the adjoining residential lot."

equip.cite: Permit exemption, accessory buildings with no HVAC (§ 13-312)
equip.text: Additions and accessory buildings meeting the setback requirements are exempt from a development permit only where they do "not contain electrical, plumbing or HVAC fixtures" and are not larger than 100 sq ft (R2M, R2C, R4M, R4C, R6M, R6C) or 200 sq ft (A10, A10C, RR5, RR5C, RR2.5, RR2.5C, RR1, RR1C).

equip.cite: NOT FOUND
equip.text: The words generator, standby, emergency power, condenser, heat pump, LP-gas, 'mechanical equipment' and 'pool equipment' appear nowhere in this LDC as a placement or screening standard. 'Propane gas' appears only as a category in the Table 13-431A principal-use list. There is no generator-specific or A/C-specific encroachment, separation or screening section.

doral.source: Land Development Code (Subpart B), Chapter 53 Administration, Article II, Division 5, Sec. 53-127 'Zoning district development standards' - the two 'Development

gen.cite: Permanently installed stand-by generators - residential zones (Sec. 74-105 table, PDF p.958)
gen.text: "Permanently installed stand-by generators / Residential zones (A maximum of one generator may be permitted for a single-family residence, individual duplex unit or individual townhouse unit) (11) | Front - behind the front building line / Rear - Five feet / Interior side - 3 feet / Side Street - behind the side street building line".

gen.cite: Permanently installed stand-by generators - nonresidential zones (Sec. 74-105 table, PDF p.958)
gen.text: "Nonresidential zones | Permanent generator must comply with principal building setbacks, except that there shall be no spacing requirement from the principal building to the generator."

gen.cite: Generator note (11) to Sec. 74-105 (PDF p.959)
gen.text: "Permanently installed generators fueled by propane gas or natural gas not exceeding five feet in height from finished grade to the top of the generator shall be permitted as an accessory use in conjunction with a permitted residential use. Side street setback shall be behind the side street building line, unless completely screened from view by a wall or hedge. In no event shall a permanently installed generator be placed closer than ten feet to the side street property line. These requirements are in addition to all applicable county, state or federal requirements."

equip.cite: Air conditioning unit (Sec. 74-105 table)
equip.text: "Air conditioning unit | 3.5 feet into setback(1)" Note (1): "In no case shall the special setback exceed 50 percent of the minimum yard dimension."

equip.cite: Aboveground fuel storage tank (Sec. 74-105 table)
equip.text: "Fuel storage tank, aboveground(2)(7)(8) / Nonresidential zones | Ten feet from property line" Note (2): "Location within required yards permitted in rear and side yards only." Note (7): "Location within the required rear yard is prohibited on an atypical lot if structure is greater than four feet in height." Note (8): "Shall be screened properly from the right-of-way." The table prints no aboveground fuel storage tank setback for residential zones.

equip.cite: Purpose of the special setbacks (Sec. 74-104)
equip.text: "This section provides for specific accessory structures and architectural appurtenances and features to be located within required building setback areas. Recorded easements and required landscaped buffers shall supersede the minimum dimensions permitted by this section."

equip.cite: Storage building (Sec. 74-105 table)
equip.text: "Storage building(2)(7) / Residential uses (120 square feet or less) Five feet from property line / Residential uses (121 to 300 square feet) Seven and one-half feet from property line / Nonresidential uses (250 square feet or less) Ten feet from property line".

equip.cite: Renewable energy devices - ground installations (Sec. 74-66(13))
equip.text: "Ground installations shall comply with the site development criteria of the applicable zoning district except encroachment into side setback areas by up to 50 percent and rear setback to within five feet of the property line may be permitted if necessary upon approval of the planning and zoning director."

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening (Sec. 86-2(a), (b), PDF p.1151)
equip.text: "(a) Mechanical equipment shall be screened with either landscaping or wall. All wall mounted mechanic equipment must be painted to match the building and shall be placed on the side and/or rear of the building. Any mechanical equipment on the rooftop shall be screened from the right-of-way using architectural features such as parapets etc. Townhomes shall meet the provisions in this section. (b) All mechanical equipment for townhomes, surface and wall mounted, shall be placed on the side of the building which shall be screened with either landscaping or wall."

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical equipment, Live Local Act qualifying developments (Sec. 68-994(1)(3))
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment. All rooftop mechanical equipment, including but not limited to heating, ventilating, air conditioning machinery, accessory communication equipment, public utility service fixtures, and elevator facilities shall be screened from the public view by a parapet wall or similar solid barrier as approved by the Planning and Zoning Director."

equip.cite: Ground equipment cabinets for antennas (Sec. 74 art. XI)
equip.text: "Self-standing, nonsheltered equipment cabinets used in conjunction with antenna support structures or antennas, if located on the ground shall be deemed mechanical equipment similar to air conditioning units and shall be limited to a height not to exceed eight feet and an area not to exceed 80 square feet. There shall be no minimum spacing between accessory wireless equipment buildings and the building located on the property."

equip.cite: Shading of A/C units (Chapter 71, landscaping, PDF p.931)
equip.text: "All exterior air conditioning units, except for air conditioning units placed on the roof, shall be shaded by trees and/or shrubs as referenced in the landscape manual."

equip.cite: Steady mechanical noise (Sec. 26-128(13))
equip.text: "Steady, mechanical noise. The use of an air conditioner, electric motor, pool pump, exhaust fan, filter, or similar noise-producing mechanical equipment which causes frequent, habitual or long continued noise which is plainly audible at a distance of 100 feet from the building, structure or property line in which the mechanical equipment is located." (a prohibited noise).

lakeland.name: Lakeland
lakeland.source: Code of Ordinances of the City of Lakeland, Florida, Supplement No. 22 (April 2026), current through Ordinance No. 6121 enacted December 1, 2025. This document
lakeland.offsite: The zoning chapter is not in this jurisdiction's Municode document — the copy held here is a supplement or a stub. Nothing on this card is a setback for this jurisdiction; read the adopted code before siting anything.

equip.cite: No generator, A/C, condenser, pool equipment, LP-gas or mechanical-equipment placement rule exists in this document
equip.text: A full-text search of all 856 pages for generator, standby, emergency power, air conditioner/air conditioning, condenser, compressor, mechanical equipment, HVAC, heating and cooling, pool pump, pool equipment, propane, LP-gas, liquefied petroleum, fuel tank, aboveground storage tank and transformer returns no placement, setback, clearance or separation standard anywhere in the Code. The only hits are (a) the Chapter 18 business tax receipt fee schedule, which lists 'Mechanical contractor... Unlimited mechanical, air conditioning boilers, pressure vessels, lift station equipment, pressure and process piping, pneumatic control piping, gasoline tanks/pumps, chemical and fuel lines and related work... 127.50' and 'Class A air conditioning contractor... 127.50' and 'Class B air conditioning contractor... Limited to 25 tons cooling and 500,000 BTU heating... 127.50' (§ 18-67); (b) § 94-21's definition 'Gas includes natural gas, liquefied petroleum gas or manufactured gas', a utility-tax definition; (c) § 102-26's sewer definitions referring to 'air conditioners, refrigeration, cooling' as sources of non-contact cooling water and § 102-34(g)'s prohibition on connecting 'water-cooled air conditioning systems' to a building sewer; and (d) § 86-33(i) 'disposed of by the generator', where 'generator' means a waste producer, not a machine.

equip.cite: Noise Control exemptions (§ 70-48) — no standby-generator exemption
equip.text: 'The provisions of this article, except for those specific prohibitions set forth hereinabove, shall not apply to the following sounds: (1) The unamplified human voice; (2) Railway locomotives or cars; (3) Household or farming tools, appliances and equipment meeting manufacturer's specifications as to sound, if applicable; (4) Aircraft and airport activity conducted in accordance with federal laws and regulations; (5) Maintenance of public service facilities; (6) Law enforcement activities, including training; (7) Authorized target shooting; (8) Emergency signals during emergencies; (9) Emergency signal testing; (10) Motor vehicles operating on a public right-of-way subject to F.S. § 316.293; (11) Refuse collection and mosquito fogging; (12) Operation of any regulated utility; (13) Ordinary and customary construction activities exempt from or for which Lakeland has issued a development permit, provided such activity occurs between 7:00 a.m. and 9:00 p.m.; (14) Organized athletic contests; (15) Sounds relating to and originating within any area zoned for commercial use; (16) Sounds relating to and originating within any area zoned for industrial use; (17) Sounds relating to and originating from legal, pre-existing, nonconforming commercial and industrial activities; (18) Boats and boating activities; (19) Phosphate mining activity; (20) Emergency devices and vehicles used for the purpose of alerting persons of an emergency or the emission of sound in the performance of emergency work; (21) Lawful noncommercial public gatherings including, but not limited to, parades, festivals and school functions; (22) Reasonable operation of equipment associated with the following activities between one-half hour before sunrise and 10:00 p.m.: Lawn care; soil cultivation; maintenance of trees, hedges and gardens; the use of lawn mowers, saws and tractors; tree trimming and limb clipping. These exemptions do not apply to the specific prohibitions set forth in section 70-47, above.' (§ 70-48.) Unlike many Florida municipal noise ordinances, Lakeland's list does NOT name a standby or emergency electrical generator; the nearest categories are (3) household equipment meeting manufacturer's sound specifications and (20) emergency devices used in the performance of emergency work. Nothing here is a distance.

equip.cite: Vegetation clearance to electric wires (§ 38-57)
equip.text: 'Trees, etc., interfering with electric wires — Allowing to grow within five feet of electric wires.' This is the only clearance distance in the Code involving electrical equipment, and it governs vegetation, not generators or mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: Screening / buffering of a parked trailer (§ 66-7(f))
equip.text: Where the city commission permits a motor home, boat or trailer to be parked on a lot, it may impose conditions 'including without limitation a requirement for buffer fencing and noise mitigation measures.' No distance is printed.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment - the governing rule
equip.text: Sec. 34-902, Yard restrictions - General, all districts, paragraph (3), quoted in full: 'Any mechanical equipment, excluding public utility fixtures, including telephone, telegraph, electric and water and sewer facilities, shall not be located in the front yard and shall be located a minimum of five feet from any side or rear property line. When a nonresidential or multifamily use is located adjacent to any residential use, then such mechanical equipment shall be located a minimum of ten feet from any property line. Notwithstanding the foregoing, fuel oil and propane tanks that are placed completely underground may be located in the front yard provided that they are in compliance with the most current Florida Building Code and National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) standards and requirements.' This is the clause that governs a standby generator pad, an A/C condenser and a pool pump: no front yard, 5 ft from any side or rear property line, 10 ft from any property line where a nonresidential or multifamily use adjoins a residential use, and an underground LP or fuel oil tank may sit in the front yard.

equip.cite: Where Sec. 34-902 does not apply
equip.text: Sec. 34-436 (HIST-S), Sec. 34-475 (HIST-Z) and Sec. 34-507 (HIST-B) each provide that 'Yard setback encroachments that may be authorized in sections 34-902 and 34-903 are expressly prohibited' in that historic preservation district. Whether that removes the mechanical-equipment allowance of Sec. 34-902(3) in those three districts, or only the projection allowances of Secs. 34-902(1), (2) and 34-903, is not settled on the page.

equip.cite: Restriction on use of required yards
equip.text: Sec. 34-901(a): 'Every part of a required front, side and rear yard must be open to the sky and unobstructed except for accessory buildings in a rear or side yard, garden walls and fences, as permitted, and except for the ordinary projection of open porches, balconies, steps, sills, belt courses, cornices. (See sections 34-902(1) and 34-903.)' Sec. 34-901(b): 'Metal storage accessory buildings shall be permitted only in the following zoning districts: CG commercial general, CO commercial office, UTL utility, RV Park recreational vehicle park, and MH manufactured home community. All metal storage buildings shall have skirting and landscaping around the entire base of the structure, except in the RV park and MH zoning districts, where only skirting shall be required if landscaping is not possible.'

equip.cite: Setback of accessory structures
equip.text: Sec. 34-873, in full: 'Accessory structures shall provide a minimum of ten feet from rear and side lot lines and shall be set back by the required front setback in the district which is applicable.' Note that this ten-foot figure is more restrictive than the five-foot mechanical-equipment figure of Sec. 34-902(3), and that several district tables print their own 'Minimum accessory structure setback' of 5 ft (RS, R-DUP, HIST-S, HIST-Z, HIST-B) with the footnote 'If accessory structure is in the front yard, the front yard setback shall apply.' The code does not say on the page which figure controls a generator enclosure, so both are recorded.

equip.cite: Swimming pools and pool equipment
equip.text: Sec. 34-871(a): 'Swimming pools shall be set back at least 15 feet from the front property line and five feet from the side and rear property lines measured to the water's edge. Swimming pools may be enclosed by screening in the side and rear yards, providing a minimum five-foot setback is provided from the side and rear property lines to the screen enclosure.' Sec. 34-871(b)(4), for zero lot line communities: 'Pools, fountains, hot tubs/whirlpools, etc., that have jets, blowers, waterfalls, mechanical equipment, or any other mechanisms that generate noise, must be completely sound-insulated from adjacent houses with a minimum two-inch thick urethane insulation or better against all surfaces within two feet of the zero line.' Sec. 34-871(c)(2), for individual townhouse lots: 'Pools, fountains, hot tubs/whirlpools, etc., that have jets, blowers, waterfalls, mechanical equipment, or any other mechanisms that generate noise, must be completely sound insulated from the adjacent property with a minimum two-inch thick urethane insulation or better around the noise generator within five feet of the property line.' Sec. 34-871(c)(3): 'A minimum five-foot-high wall or fence, consistent with the architecture of the building, shall be installed along the side property lines to screen the pool or hot tub/whirlpool from the adjacent properties.'

equip.cite: Fuel pumps and tanks at a fuel service station
equip.text: Sec. 34-869(g): 'All fuel pumps, tanks, vents, pump islands and pump island canopies shall conform to setback requirements for the district except that no such pumps, tanks, vents, pump islands or pump island canopies shall be located closer than 25 feet to any side property line.'

equip.cite: Private utility structures in the REC-PRIV district
equip.text: Sec. 34-752(b)(1): 'All private utility structures shall be required to be screened with landscaping or other appropriate material in order to be completely screened from view from all streets and adjacent properties. In addition, there shall be no noise, smell, or other nuisance generated from a private utility structure. All private utility structures, other than submersible wells which are no greater than 25 square feet in area and three feet in height, shall be located a minimum of 250 feet from the side and rear property lines, and a minimum 50 feet from the front property line.' Sec. 34-752(b)(2): 'Submersible wells no greater than 25 square feet in area and three feet in height shall be set back a minimum 15 feet from any property line.'

equip.cite: Air conditioning in the RV Park district
equip.text: Sec. 34-566 note (e): 'All accessory structures shall be freestanding structures, not permanently attached to the RV and must not protrude beyond the front corner of the RV walls; however, protrusion may occur between tip-outs. No plumbing, air conditioning unit or ducts are permitted within an accessory structure. Electricity, however, shall be permitted to serve an accessory structure. Accessory structures, other than storage buildings, are permitted only when an RV is located on the lot. When an RV is removed from a lot, all accessory structures, other than storage buildings and cooking/barbecue grill structures, must also be removed. A freestanding air conditioning unit shall be considered an accessory structure (see definition of accessory structure in section 34-4).' This is the one place in the code that says in terms that a free-standing mechanical unit is an accessory structure.

equip.cite: Generators in the general Code of Ordinances (not zoning)
equip.text: Sec. 12-118 (noise chapter), closing sentence: 'This article shall not prohibit the operation or periodic testing of emergency engines, generators and other equipment necessary to maintain or restore regulated public utilities service or other necessary public services.' Construction-site rule in the buildings chapter: 'The building official may issue a permit for the use of a portable generator for a period not to exceed four days provided the permit applicant provides proof that neither permanent nor temporary electrical power is available at the work location. The portable generator shall be operated only during the times for permissible construction activities as set forth in section 12-127 of this Code. No fee shall be required for the issuance of such a permit.' Neither is a setback.

lantana.source: Code of Ordinances Chapter 23 (Zoning), Article V District Regulations — Secs. 23-92 through 23-105. Each district carries its own '(e) Building requirements' b

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment in residential zoning districts (the governing rule)
equip.text: Sec. 23-81(k)(3), Projections into setback areas: '(3) Mechanical equipment in residential zoning districts. Mechanical equipment shall not be allowed within the required side setbacks for new construction in residential zoning districts, however existing mechanical equipment may be replaced in its existing location.'

equip.cite: Definition of 'mechanical equipment'
equip.text: Sec. 23-3 definitions: 'Mechanical equipment includes but is not limited to air conditioning compressors and condensers, heating-ventilation equipment, electrical transformers, and pool or spa equipment, ground-mounted, roof-mounted or on pads.' NOTE: the definition is open-ended ('includes but is not limited to') but does not name generators, standby power equipment, LP-gas tanks or propane tanks. I found no section of the Lantana code that sets a siting standard for a standby generator by name.

equip.cite: Accessory uses — location
equip.text: Sec. 23-81(c): 'Accessory uses in residential districts shall be constructed to conform with the building and site regulations in the district where the structure is to be located, provided, however, that all accessory uses shall be located only in the side or rear yard at least six (6) feet from the principal building.' Each district section also repeats, in its '(c) Accessory uses' subsection, 'Accessory uses shall not be located within any required yard setbacks' — except Sec. 23-100(c) (P district), which as printed reads 'Accessory uses shall be located within any required yard setbacks'.

equip.cite: Architectural features and chimneys — permitted projections
equip.text: Sec. 23-81(k)(1)-(2): '(1) Chimneys. Chimneys may project into side and rear yards a distance not to exceed 24 inches, provided that a clear space of not less than 96 inches is left between such projection and the Lot Line adjacent. (2) Architectural features. No main walls of any building shall encroach on the front, side or rear setback areas, but architectural features such as canopies, cantilever slab projections (open balconies), cornices and similar features may project into the front, side and rear setbacks not more than twenty-four (24) inches, and there shall be not less than seven feet of clear headroom under any such projection. Eaves may project into the setbacks not more than thirty-six (36) inches.'

equip.cite: Standby generator REQUIRED at service stations (C1 district)
equip.text: Sec. 23-96(d)(6), C1 commercial district special exceptions: '(6) Service stations, except in CC or OMX. All new service stations shall permanently install a standby electrical generator with sufficient capacity to power the entire service station facility, not including vehicle washing/cleaning equipment, such that the loss of commercially supplied electrical power shall not result in the loss of service. Additionally, if any existing service station facility is renovated, reconstructed or remodeled in any way, where the total combined cost exceeds fifty thousand dollars ($50,000.00) during any twelve-month period, such service station shall be required to install a permanent standby electrical generator, which satisfies the criteria listed hereinabove.' This is a requirement to install a generator, not a setback or siting standard.

equip.cite: Underground utility installation (R1A only)
equip.text: Sec. 23-81(m): 'Within the single-family residential zoning district of R1-A, at the time of construction of any new buildings or structures located on any privately-owned property, such buildings or structures shall have an entirely underground location for all utility service lines, electrical distribution systems, wires and cables, which connect to and service such buildings or structures. This section shall apply to all new utilities located within town or rights-of-way within the town, as well as in easements or on private properties, except for restoration of service under emergency conditions, e.g., following a hurricane or similar disaster that damages overhead utility facilities.'

equip.cite: Lot coverage — what counts
equip.text: Sec. 23-81(l): 'Lot coverage shall be calculated to include the footprint of all above-grade structures under roof, and all swimming pools excluding, patio areas unless a screen enclosure is provided.'
