gen.cite: Generators, A/C and pool equipment — encroachment into a required setback (§ VII-1201(a)(7))
gen.text: "Window, wall-hung air-conditioning units and air-conditioning units installed at grade may project no more than three feet into any required setback in residential districts. Pool equipment and the screening wall for outdoor mechanical equipment, including, but not limited to, air-conditioning equipment and pool pumps required by subsection VI-102(u)(3) for single-family dwellings may project no more than 36 inches into any required sideyard setback. A generator at grade outside of Special Flood Hazard Areas or a generator elevated within Special Flood Hazard Areas may project no more than 36 inches into any required sideyard setback in residential districts."

gen.cite: Ground-mounted mechanical equipment, institutional uses in single-family and multiple family zones (§§ VI-204, VI-304)
gen.text: "Mechanical equipment. Mechanical equipment located on the ground, such as heating or cooling equipment, pumps, or generators shall be screened from the street and any abutting residentially zoned properties by walls, fences, or vegetation tall enough to screen the equipment. Mechanical equipment on roofs shall be screened from the ground level of any abutting residentially zoned properties." The same sections also provide: "Exterior storage. Exterior storage of materials and equipment is prohibited." (p.519).

gen.cite: Ground-mounted mechanical equipment, commercial, industrial, special purpose and mixed-use zones (§§ VI-503(i), VI-603(j), VI-703(i), VI-1005, VI-1103(g))
gen.text: "Mechanical equipment. Mechanical equipment, located on the ground, such as heating or cooling equipment, pumps, or generators must be screened from public streets and any adjacent properties. All rooftop mechanical equipment must be screened from the ground level of public streets and any adjacent properties by integrating it into building and roof design." (p.592, p.665, p.751).

equip.cite: General rule on required setbacks (§ VII-1201(a))
equip.text: "Encroachments into required setbacks. Every part of every required setback shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as otherwise permitted by these regulations. Except for setbacks adjacent to the Gulf of Mexico, the following encroachments are permitted in all setbacks." The list that follows also allows: sills and belt courses 12 inches; movable awnings 3 ft (not more than half the setback where the setback is less than 5 ft wide); chimneys, bay windows or pilasters 2 ft; unroofed and unenclosed fire escapes and stairways 5 ft into a rear setback or 3 ft into a side setback of a multifamily dwelling, hotel or motel; hoods, canopies, roof overhangs or marquees 3 ft but no closer than one foot to the zoning lot line; cornices, eaves or gutters 3 ft (not more than half the setback where it is less than 6 ft wide); fences, walls, poles, posts and customary yard accessories in all yards except Gulf-front waterfront yards; and structures up to 30 inches above the general ground level in all yards except Gulf-front waterfront yards.

equip.cite: Outdoor mechanical equipment screening wall, single-family dwellings (§ VI-102(u)(3))
equip.text: "Outdoor mechanical equipment. Screening wall in the absence of perimeter fencing or mechanical equipment elevated above grade. Prior to the issuance of a building permit which includes the installation of new exterior mechanical equipment or the relocation of existing mechanical equipment in a side yard in the absence of perimeter fencing or when outdoor mechanical equipment is elected above grade, the applicant shall submit documentation demonstrating that a screening wall, or screening fence has been provided... showing all air conditioning equipment, pool pumps and similar electrical-mechanical equipment, proposed to be placed outside the main structure in a side yard to be screened from adjoining properties with a screening wall. This screening wall shall be required regardless of the distance from the side property line to the mechanical equipment. Wall- or window-mounted outdoor mechanical equipment shall be exempt from the screening wall requirement.... (i.e., the replacement of existing mechanical equipment shall not require a screening wall). The screening wall shall be located in the side yard between the mechanical equipment and the closest property line. The screening wall shall be 18 inches higher than the equipment being shielded and at least as wide as the equipment being shielded. See section VII-1201 for allowable encroachment of the wall into the required setback."

equip.cite: Accessory buildings and structures (Table VI-203 notes; § VII-903)
equip.text: Table VI-203 note (4): "Minimum side and rear yard for accessory buildings shall be three feet." Note (6): "Minimum rear yard setback for accessory dwelling shall be ten feet." § VII-903: "Accessory buildings shall not exceed the maximum height requirement for the particular district in which it is located"; on waterfront lots "Accessory buildings shall not be allowed in front setbacks, shall not exceed ten feet in height, and shall not cover more than 50 percent of the yard in which they are located"; "Accessory structures shall not be located in any required waterfront setback" except uncaged swimming pools meeting stated conditions; "No accessory building shall be constructed, erected, or otherwise placed on a zoning lot that is not occupied by a principal building." (p.976-978).

equip.cite: Manufactured home lots (§ VII-602)
equip.text: "Development standards for manufactured home lots. All home lots in manufactured home parks shall conform to the following standards: a. Minimum lot size. 3,500 square feet. b. Minimum lot width. 50 feet. c. Setbacks. No manufactured home, carport or other structure shall be placed or erected closer to the back of the gutter line on any internal roadway than ten feet if a utility easement is provided, or 15 feet if a utility easement is not provided. No manufactured home shall be placed or erected closer than five feet to any side or rear manufactured home lot line, provided that roof projections, overhangs, rain gutters and air conditioners may project 18 inches into any required yard areas."

equip.cite: Exterior storage of equipment, production intensive commercial zones (§ VI-603(l)(4))
equip.text: "Exterior storage is allowed if the storage area complies with the standards of this section. Exterior storage is limited to 50 percent of the zoning lot area for all uses in the CI and ICD zones; however, there is no limit for such uses in the ILW, I, IGD and IHD zones. All exterior storage areas: shall meet all setback requirements applicable to the primary use; shall meet all applicable environmental performance standards of article VII, division 10 of this Code; shall be screened in accordance with article VII, division 3 of this Code; and shall be screened from public view along all street frontages. Except for an approved waste related use, storage of refuse, waste, junk or inoperative motor vehicles or the accumulation of inoperative equipment shall be prohibited."

royal_palm_beach.name: Royal Palm Beach
royal_palm_beach.source: Code of Ordinances Chapter 26 (Zoning), Article V Zoning Districts, Secs. 26-77 through 26-95 - each district carries its own '(4) Site development standards' b

equip.cite: Permanent and portable emergency power generators - Sec. 26-101(b)(4), Table 1, Note 1
equip.text: Table 1 ('Maximum Permissible Sound Levels for Inhabited Residential and Commercial Receiving Land') sets, for inhabited residential land: 'Fixed mechanical equipment (excluding permanent emergency power generators) - Anytime - 60 dBA' and 'Permanent and portable emergency power generators - See Note 1 below - 85 dBA'. Note 1 reads: '1. Permanent and portable emergency power generators may be allowed, subject to the following restrictions: A. The property owner must obtain a building permit from the village for the installation of the permanent emergency unit. The building department shall review all such permit applications to ensure that such installation minimizes the visual and acoustic impact on adjacent properties. Additionally, special attention shall be paid to the placement of the generator, the use of sound attenuating materials and the reasonable containment of sounds which will be created by the operation of any emergency use generator. B. The permanent and portable generator's maintenance cycle run shall only be permitted between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday only, and shall continue for no more than 30 minutes per cycle. C. Permanent and portable generators being utilized to allow normal residential and business functions to continue during a power outage may only be operated for nonmaintenance purposes when a state of emergency has been declared by the village or whenever there is a power outage.'

equip.cite: Definition of fixed mechanical equipment - Sec. 26-101(b)(3)h
equip.text: 'Fixed mechanical equipment shall mean mechanical equipment, such as an air-conditioning unit, water-cooling tower, swimming pool pump, fan, power generator or other similar power-source equipment permanently affixed to real property as distinguished from temporary, portable, nonfixed mechanical equipment.'

equip.cite: Accessory uses, buildings and structures - Sec. 26-57(b)(1)a
equip.text: 'Permanent. All permanent accessory uses, buildings and structures, including sheds, shall be located on the same lot as the primary structure or principal or main use and not within any required yard setbacks, except for play structures and sheds which must meet the side yard setback requirements for the zoning district in which they are located but which may be located ten (10) feet from the rear property line providing that no portion of the play structure or shed exceeds eight (8) feet in height. For sheds and play structures exceeding eight (8) feet in height, any design element of a shed or play structure exceeding eight (8) feet in height must be set back an additional one (1) foot in both the rear and side yards for every one (1) foot, or portion thereof, which exceeds eight (8) feet. All accessory structures over one hundred fifty (150) square feet shall match the architectural style of the principal/primary structure...' Sec. 26-57(b)(2): 'Height. No accessory use, building or structure shall exceed the height permitted in the district in which the principal use is located.'

equip.cite: Generators treated as accessory structures for site plan purposes - Sec. 26-40 (minor amendments)
equip.text: A minor amendment to a previously approved site plan includes: '(7) Addition of or modification to small accessory structures or other site improvements/features such as generators, sheds, traffic bollards (must be ornamental in nature), propane tank storage cages, air compressor service stations, ice merchandisers, or mail kiosks; relocation of loading spaces; and repurposing of recreational courts.'

equip.cite: Propane storage - Sec. 11-23 (Fire prevention)
equip.text: 'Except for where warranted on village-owned property, all propane storage tanks in excess of one hundred twenty-five (125) gallons capacity shall be installed underground. A maximum of two (2) above ground tanks of lesser capacity, not to exceed fifty-six (56) gallons each, can be installed aboveground on any one (1) lot. All propane storage tanks shall be installed in accordance with NFPA 58, as amended.'

equip.cite: Emergency generators required for automotive service stations - Sec. 26-101(m)
equip.text: 'All newly constructed automotive service stations which sell gasoline or other petroleum products shall have a permanently installed emergency generator. Existing automotive service stations which sell gasoline or other petroleum products shall be required to install permanent emergency generators whenever such service station is rebuilt after being destroyed to an extent of more than fifty (50) percent of its assessed value or whenever a revised site plan for such service station is submitted for approval which enlarges upon or alters in any way the original site plan for that service station... (2) The permanent emergency generators installed at service stations are also subject to the noise standards and restrictions set forth in subsection (b) at table 1 hereinabove.'

equip.cite: Emergency generator required for ALF/MCF/CCF - Sec. 26-60(13)
equip.text: 'Emergency generator. A sufficient emergency generator must be provided for ALF, MCF, and CCF. An emergency generator shall be sufficient to provide the necessary power to allow for (i) a climate controlled area of refuge within a common area that is large enough to accommodate all facility residents; (ii) an element of refrigeration in th[e]...'

equip.cite: Performance standards, general - Sec. 26-101(a)
equip.text: 'All uses and activities permitted as of right, special exceptions, or special permit in any district shall conform to the standards of performance described below and shall be constructed, maintained, and operated so as not to be injurious or offensive to the occupants of adjacent premises by reason of the emission or creation of noise, vibration, smoke, dust or other particulate matter, toxic or noxious waste materials, odors, fire and explosive hazard, or glare; so as not to allow any non-permitted use to occur on the property; and/or so as to be operated in such a manner as will allow for the continuation of essential services during times of emergencies due to events such as hurricanes or other natural disasters.'

equip.cite: Screening of service function areas / mechanical equipment - Sec. 26-73 (large scale commercial/industrial)
equip.text: '(2) Service Function Areas (SFA's) including but not limited to loading, storage, mechanical equipment, and solid waste disposal. a. Buffering and screening standards. Loading areas or docks, trash collection, mechanical equipment, trash compaction, vehicular storage, (excluding new and used cars) recycling, roof top equipment and other service function areas shall be fully screened from view of adjace[nt]...'. The MXS district repeats this at Sec. 26-95(9)(j).

equip.cite: Machinery noise hours - Sec. 26-101(b)(5)e
equip.text: 'Machinery construction work. The operation of any machinery, demolition equipment, construction equipment, power tools, equipment of semimechanical devices or undertaking construction work which emits a sound plainly audible across the property line of an inhabited residential property between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. However, this subsection shall not prohibit the use of temporary pumps or machinery which, because of its very nature and purpose, is required to be operated twenty-four (24) hours a day.'

jefferson_county.name: Jefferson County
jefferson_county.source: Land Development Code, ch. 50. Jefferson has no zoning districts in the usual sense and no per-district dimensional table: land use districts are the FLUM categ

equip.cite: Countywide building setback (Sec. 50-5.1.3(a), PDF p.513)
equip.text: "For all properties in the county, building placement shall adhere to the following standards: (a) Perimeter property setbacks. (1) The outermost wall of all buildings shall be constructed a minimum of ten feet from any side or rear perimeter boundary line and 25 feet from any public or private road easement line or right of way line. If there is no defined right-of-way or easement, the building construction setback shall be 55 feet from the centerline of the road driving surface. (2) All parking lot construction shall be a minimum of ten feet from any perimeter property line and shall provide landscaping as required herein." The rule is written for BUILDINGS; the code prints no accessory-structure or equipment-pad variant and no permitted encroachment into these setbacks.

equip.cite: Table 5.1.3 Building Placement Standards (PDF p.514)
equip.text: Multi-Family Residential and Non-Residential Site Plans - Perimeter Building Setbacks: Front 25 feet, Side-Corner 25 feet, Side-Interior 10 feet, Rear 10 feet. Interior Building Setbacks (Between Buildings): Front 50 feet, Side 20 feet, Rear 30 feet. Non-residential developments: minimum side separation of 20 feet, minimum front and rear separation of 30 feet.

equip.cite: Screening of equipment and machinery, Lloyd Historic Overlay (Sec. 50-2.8.0(e)(3)b.4, PDF p.479)
equip.text: "Dumpsters, sheds, equipment or machinery in support of a structure shall be shielded by appropriate fencing or buffering high enough to prohibit view from the street." This is the ONLY provision in the Jefferson code that addresses the screening or placement of equipment or machinery accessory to a building, and it applies only inside the Lloyd Historic Overlay District.

equip.cite: Rooftop equipment counts toward height (definition of height, PDF p.443)
equip.text: "When applied to a building, height shall be measured to the highest point of the coping of a flat roof or to the average height level between eaves and ridge for gable, hip, or gambrel roofs. Rooftop equipment shall be added to the measurement of the height of a building, as determined above, if the equipment extends more than four feet above the highest portion of the roof."

equip.cite: LP gas facilities (Sec. 50-2.1.x and Sec. 50-2.9.2(a)(3), PDF p.458, 461, 481)
equip.text: "LP gas storage and/or distribution facilities for 10,000 gallons or less" is listed as a general commercial use; facilities "including one or more storage tanks for liquids including chemicals, petroleum, or LP gas storage and/or distribution facilities exceeding 10,000 gallons" fall in the heavy industrial use group; and Sec. 50-2.9.2(a)(3) makes "LP storage and/or distribution facility in excess of 1,000 gallons" a special exception use in all land use districts. No separation distance or setback is printed for any of these.

equip.cite: Utility plants and electric power plants (Sec. 50-2.2.5(b), Sec. 50-2.9.2(a)(7))
equip.text: Utility plants are a special exception use in the industrial district; electric power plants are a special exception use in all land use districts under the transportation/utility overlay. Review criteria include "compatibility of the proposed district with adjacent and overlaid districts, and proposed means and methods of mitigating and potential incompatibilities due to nuisance, noise, glare, scale of facility, and appearance" - no distances are printed.

equip.cite: Noise limits by district (ch. 14, Table 1 and Table 2, PDF p.202)
equip.text: Sound level limits are set for the IB and IND land use districts (Table 1: 7:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. not regulated) and separately for any area of the county not in IB or IND (Table 2). "Residential property" for this purpose means property with habitually and lawfully occupied sleeping quarters located in CON, AG-20, AG-5, AG-3, MUBR, MUSR, R-1 or R-2.

AG-20.frontNote: Sec. 50-5.1.3(a)(1): "The outermost wall of all buildings shall be constructed a minimum of ten feet from any side or rear perimeter boundary line and 25 feet from any public or private road easement line or right of way line. If there is no defined right-of-way or easement, the building construction setback shall be 55 feet from the centerline of the road driving surface."
AG-20.heightNote: No maximum building height is printed for this or any other land use district. The only height limit in the code is 38 ft inside the Lloyd Historic Overlay District (Sec. 50-2.8.0(e)(3)a).
AG-20.coverageNote: The Sec. 50-2.6.0 table prints "N/A" in the Max Area of Impervious column for Ag. 20. Sec. 50-2.3.1(b) prints a conditional figure instead: "For institutional and public service uses, intensity of development by impervious surface coverage should not exceed 35 percent." The table's separate "Non-Residential Use Area" column prints 5%.
AG-20.minLotNote: Sec. 50-2.5.0: "There are no minimum lot sizes required in any land use category except where the development must be in compliance with state standards regarding onsite sewage disposal (septic tank systems) and potable water wells."
AG-20.note: Agriculture 20. Density one unit per 20 acres in all three utility scenarios (no water/no sewer, water/no sewer, water/sewer), with a family-transfer exception. Printed as "Agriculture 20 (AG-20)" in ch. 14.

AG-5.frontNote: Countywide Sec. 50-5.1.3(a)(1): 25 ft from any public or private road easement line or right of way line; 55 ft from the centerline of the road driving surface where no right-of-way or easement is defined.
AG-5.heightNote: No maximum building height is printed.
AG-5.coverageNote: Sec. 50-2.6.0 table prints "N/A" for Max Area of Impervious. Sec. 50-2.3.1(b): institutional and public service uses "should not exceed 35 percent" impervious. Non-Residential Use Area column: 5%.
AG-5.minLotNote: Sec. 50-2.5.0: no minimum lot sizes in any land use category.
AG-5.note: Agriculture 5. Density shall not exceed 1 unit per 5 acres, gross basis, family-transfer exception; clustering encouraged.

AG-3.frontNote: Countywide Sec. 50-5.1.3(a)(1): 25 ft from road right-of-way/easement line; 55 ft from road centerline where undefined.
AG-3.heightNote: No maximum building height is printed.
AG-3.coverageNote: Sec. 50-2.6.0 table prints "N/A" for Max Area of Impervious. Sec. 50-2.3.1(b): institutional and public service uses "should not exceed 35 percent". Non-Residential Use Area column: 5%.
AG-3.minLotNote: Sec. 50-2.5.0: no minimum lot sizes in any land use category.
AG-3.note: Agriculture 3. One unit per three acres, with family-transfer exception.

CON.frontNote: Countywide Sec. 50-5.1.3(a)(1): 25 ft from road right-of-way/easement line; 55 ft from road centerline where undefined.

CON.coverageNote: Sec. 50-2.3.2(b): "Intensity. This development standard is not applicable to the conservation district."

R-1.heightNote: No maximum building height is printed.
R-1.coverageNote: Sec. 50-2.6.0 table: Max Area of Impervious 35%. R-1.minLotNote: Sec. 50-2.5.0: no minimum lot sizes in any land use category.

Gross density shall not exceed one unit per acre, although clustering may be allowed; where clustering results in more than two dwelling units per acre, central water or sewer or both are required. For new lots containing floodplain, each lot shall contain a minimum of one-half acre outside the floodplain with no construction allowed within the floodplain.

R-2.frontNote: Countywide Sec. 50-5.1.3(a)(1): 25 ft from road right-of-way/easement line; 55 ft from road centerline where undefined.

LHOD (Lloyd Historic Overlay District).frontNote: Sec. 50-2.8.0(e)(3)6: "Building setbacks for all new buildings shall be a no less than 25 feet or more than 35 feet from any road right of way throughout the district." This is both a minimum AND a maximum setback, unlike the rest of the county.
LHOD (Lloyd Historic Overlay District).heightNote: Sec. 50-2.8.0(e)(3)a: "Structural height shall be limited to 38 feet or no more than two feet higher than the tallest adjacent structure (including a structure across a street)." 38 ft is the printed cap; the alternative is a relative standard.
LHOD (Lloyd Historic Overlay District).note: Overlay, not a base district. Density, intensity and permitted uses are those of the underlying mixed use - suburban/residential district. Floor area is limited to 5,000 sq ft of heated/cooled living area for residential structures, 5,000 sq ft gross floor area for non-residential structures, and 10,000 sq ft gross floor area for institutional uses.

Traditional Communities overlay.note: Overlay, not a base district (Sec. 50-2.7.0, Table 2.6.1 lists 18 named communities). No dimensional standards of its own: "Lots of record within a traditional community may be subdivided for infill development provided the resulting division does not exceed the density of properties within two lots in any direction from the subject lot of record." Infill is allowed only on lots of record as of July 19, 1990.

Transportation/utility overlay.note: Overlay (Sec. 50-2.9.0 et seq.). No dimensional envelope. Sec. 50-2.9.3(c): "Linear transmission facilities and associated rights of way and easements shall be marked, maintained and have setback requirements, in accordance with the applicable county, state and federal regulations pertaining to said facilities." Sec.

marion_county.name: Marion County

equip.cite: Accessory structures, including a generator — LDC § 4.2.6.C
equip.text: Marion County prints no dedicated generator ordinance and no special yard-encroachment allowance for mechanical equipment. A permanently installed generator is an accessory structure: it must sit in a rear or side yard — never in a required front yard — at the district's General Accessory setback, and on lots of one acre or less a minimum of 8 ft from the rear and side lot lines (§ 4.2.6.C.8). Only eaves, roof overhangs, pilasters, chimneys and fireplaces may protrude 2 ft into a required setback (§ 4.2.6.C.4), and that allowance does not extend to a generator. No structure may be placed over an easement without the easement holder's written approval (§ 4.2.6.C.3). Above-ground LP tanks follow the same accessory-structure setbacks plus Fire Code separation distances. Confirm placement with Marion County Growth Services (352-438-2600) before siting.

dunnellon.source: Code of Ordinances, Appendix A - Zoning. District list from Article VI, Section 6.1 "Classes of symbols"; dimensions from Section 6.2 "Schedule of dimensional r

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures (Sec. 3.12) - the general placement rule
equip.text: "(a) In residential districts all accessory buildings and uses shall be located only in the rear yard except that parking may be located in a side yard. (b) In residential districts all accessory buildings and uses in a rear yard shall be located at least eight feet from any lot line, meet required setback from any street, and at least five feet from any main building. Accessory buildings and structures shall not exceed two stories or 24 feet in height. In case of rear alleys, private garages not over one story in height may be located on the rear alley line."

equip.cite: Yard encroachments (Sec. 3.10)
equip.text: "Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as hereinafter provided or as otherwise permitted in the zoning code. (a) Sills or belt courses may project not over 12 inches into a required yard. (b) Movable awnings may project not over three feet into a required yard... (c) Chimneys, fireplaces or pilasters may project not over two feet into a required yard. (d) Fire escapes, stairways and balconies which are unroofed and unenclosed may project not over five feet into a required rear yard, or not over three feet eight inches into a required side yard, of a multiple dwelling, hotel or motel. (e) Hoods, canopies or marquees may project not over three feet into a required yard, but shall not exceed closer than one foot to any lot line... (g) Accessory uses and structures may be located in required yards as specified in section 3.12 of this article... (i) Accessory parking may be located in a required rear or side yard. (j) Flagpoles, clotheslines, birdhouses and other yard accessories are permitted in any yard if they do not constitute substantial impediments to vision or free flow of light and air across the yard." NOTE: this list does not name generators, A/C condensers, pool equipment or LP tanks. In Dunnellon a ground-mounted generator in a residential district falls under Sec. 3.12 - rear yard only, at least 8 ft from any lot line and 5 ft from the main building.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening, commercial development (Sec. 9.3-1(a)(3))
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment, electrical meter and service components, and similar utility devices, whether ground level, wall mounted, or roof mounted, shall be screened from view from public rights-of-way through one of the following methods: a. Landscaping. b. Uses of brick, wood, masonry, or PVC materials for screening. Such materials are to be compatible with the predominant materials and colors used for the principal building on the site."

equip.cite: Accessory structures and uses, commercial (Sec. 9.3-1(b))
equip.text: "Accessory uses and structures shall be integrated into the overall design of the site to ensure that visual and other impacts of these uses are fully contained or enclosed and out of view from adjacent properties and public streets. (1) Accessory uses and structures are loading docks, truck parking, outdoor storage, outdoor shopping cart storage areas, utility meters or cabinets, lift stations, HVAC equipment, dumpster, and other similar service facilities and functions. (2) Accessory uses and structures shall be designed to blend with the principal building through the use of color, building materials, and architectural features... (3) Loading docks and outside storage and displays shall be setback a minimum of 100 feet from any lots zoned for residential use... (5) Accessory uses shall not exceed the height of the principal building."

equip.cite: Height exclusions (Sec. 3.13)
equip.text: "Scenery lofts, towers, cupolas, steeples, domes, flagpoles, airplane beacons, broadcasting towers, antennas, chimneys, stacks, tanks and roof structures used only for ornamental or mechanical purposes may exceed the permissible height limit in any district."

equip.cite: District boundary line lots (Sec. 3.19)
equip.text: "(a) Where a business district is separated by a street from a residential district, then any lot in such non-residential district adjacent to the separating street shall be provided with a yard at least 25 feet in depth along such separating street. (b) Where a business district directly abuts on a residential district without any separator between them such as a street, alley, or other public open space, then any lot in such non-residential district shall be provided with a yard at least ten feet in depth adjacent to the residentially zoned property. (c) Where a warehouse use in a business district directly abuts on a residential district... at least 20 feet in depth. (d) Where a yard is required in this section, such yard may be used for walkways, driveways and landscaping, but not for any other use or purpose."

gen.cite: Mechanical equipment including generators — residential zones (§ 58-71(h)(3))
gen.text: 'Mechanical equipment, which includes air-conditioning equipment, swimming pool equipment, generators, and similar type equipment, shall not be located in any front yard or required side yard with street frontage unless totally shielded from view from the street by walls or vinyl fences otherwise complying with the zoning code. Mechanical equipment may be located up to ten feet from a rear lot line as long as they are adjacent to the accessory structure or principal structure. Mechanical equipment shall not be located in any required side yard or within ten feet from the rear lot line except that they may be permitted up to five feet from a side or rear property line if screened by a solid fence or wall that is at a minimum equal in height of the equipment. Propane tanks shall not be located within five feet of any side or rear lot line. Any mechanical equipment placed on a roof must be screened from view from surrounding properties and from public streets.' [].

gen.cite: Mechanical equipment including generators — nonresidential zones (§ 58-84(f)(2))
gen.text: 'Mechanical equipment, which includes air-conditioning equipment, swimming pool equipment, generators, and similar type equipment, shall not be located in any front yard or side yard with street frontage unless totally shielded from view from the street by walls or vinyl fences otherwise complying with the zoning code. Mechanical equipment may be located up to ten feet from a rear lot line as long as they are adjacent to the accessory structure or principal structure. Mechanical equipment shall not be located in any required side yard or within ten feet from the rear lot line except that they may be permitted up to five feet from a side or rear property line if screened by a solid fence or wall that is a minimum equal in height of the equipment. Propane tanks shall not be located within five feet of any side or rear lot line. Any mechanical equipment placed on a roof must be screened from view from surrounding properties and from public streets with material of a similar style to the building facade.' [].

gen.cite: Screening of generators and fuel tanks — landscape regulations (§ 58-334)
gen.text: (g) All ground-mounted utilities except electrical transformers shall be painted green or flat black unless a different color is required by City or State of Florida Code. (h) Air conditioning units, pool equipment, electrical equipment, utility boxes, generators, above-ground fuel tanks, and stored trash containers on private property shall not be easily visible from a public right-of-way. They shall be screened by structures, solid fences, trellises, and/or landscaping. Exceptions may be made for electrical equipment when determined appropriate by [the city]. [].

gen.cite: Wellhead protection exemption for emergency generators (§ 58-322)
gen.text: Prohibited within a wellhead protection zone are '(3) Activities which require the storage, use handling, production, or transportation of restricted substances, agricultural chemicals, petroleum products, hazardous/toxic wastes, industrial chemicals, medical wastes, etc. Wellhead emergency generator requirements are exempted, but require the highest level of engineering standards covering petroleum product storage and delivery.' [].

equip.cite: Accessory buildings and structures in residential zones (§ 58-71(h)(1), (4), (5))
equip.text: (1) 'No detached accessory use or structure shall be permitted in the required front yard. On double frontage lots or corner lots, no detached accessory use or structure shall be permitted in the required yards fronting on the streets. In addition, no storage sheds shall be permitted in the area between the building line of the main structure and street or streets, unless screened by an opaque fence or wall.' (4) 'Accessory structures or buildings, up to 150 square feet in size, may be located five feet from a side or rear interior property line. Accessory buildings over 150 square feet in size up to 400 square feet shall not be located closer than ten feet to any side or rear property line, and any two-story accessory building or any accessory building over 400 square feet shall meet the same rear and side setback as required for the principal structure. No accessory structure shall exceed a height of 16 feet unless located so as to comply with the setbacks of the principal structure.' (5) Summary table — Accessory Structure Size (square feet) / Side Setback (feet) / Rear Setback (feet): up to 150 — 5 / 5; 151—400 — 10 / 10; over 400 — Principal / Principal; Detached Garage up to 620 — 5 / 10. [].

equip.cite: Projections into setbacks (§ 58-71(g))
equip.text: 'Eaves, roof overhangs, canopies, chimneys and flues, and awnings may project into the minimum yard or setback areas up to three and one-half feet. Fabric canopies, awnings, balconies, etc., with ground supports, second floor open porches, two-story high columns or similar features are considered a structure, and to be part of the main structure, and thus shall observe the setback requirements of the districts in which they are located. Cantilevered bay windows which project from the wall at a minimum height of 24 inches above finished grade may project two feet into required setbacks and are limited to a maximum width of eight feet.' [].

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical equipment above the height limit (recurring clause in §§ 58-67, 58-68, 58-72—58-82)
equip.text: 'Parapet walls, or mansard roofs functioning as parapet walls, may be added to the permitted building height but in no case shall extend more than five feet above the height limits in this subsection. Mechanical penthouses, mechanical and air-conditioning equipment, elevator/stair towers and related nonoccupied structures may be permitted to extend up to ten feet above the height limits in this subsection.' In R-4 the clause adds: 'Mechanical and air-conditioning equipment shall be screened from view on the ground level and shall be located to the maximum extent possible so that they are not visible from any street.' [].

equip.cite: Air-conditioning compressors — Winter Park Pines / special subdivision standards (§ 58-71)
equip.text: 'Air-conditioning compressors shall observe a five-foot side setback.' (part of a list of special development standards that also states 'Chimneys and bay windows may encroach two feet into the setback. Side setback to a porte cochere is two feet. Rear screened porches may be connected to the garage. Other zoning provisions shall apply where applicable or not covered under this subsection.') [].

equip.cite: HVAC equipment — Elizabeth's Walk special standards (§ 58-69 area standards, item 15(a))
equip.text: 'HVAC equipment may be placed within the side yard setback lines for lots 1-32 and 48-71 Elizabeth's Walk. To screen the equipment from the adjacent lot, a minimum four-foot high stucco-concrete block and/or brick screen wall, shall be constructed on the side yard property line. If visible from the front street, landscaping shall be used in front of said HVAC equipment, so as to screen the equipment from the front.' [].

R-1A.frontNote: 'The front yard setback shall be calculated using 20 percent of the lot depth or the setback of the existing or most recently demolished home, whichever is greater.... The front setback shall not exceed a maximum ten-foot difference beyond the existing home.
R-1A.sideNote: 'The side setback for one-story homes or the first floor of two-story homes is equal to 30 percent of the lot width in feet equally divided on each side of the home, except the side setback is seven and one-half feet for lots which are 60 feet wide or less.' 'The side setback for two-story homes measured to the second story wall shall be 40 percent of the lot width in feet equally divided on each side of the home, except the second-floor side setback is ten feet for lots which are 60 feet wide or less.' Lots over 200 feet in width shall use the required setback for lots which are 200 feet in width.
R-1A.rearNote: 'The rear setback shall be 25 feet for a one-story structure and 35 feet for any second-story portion of any building. The rear setback may be reduced to ten feet when the rear yard of the residential property abuts non-residentially zoned property.' (§ 58-65(f)(8)).
R-1A.heightNote: No building shall have more than two stories. 'For properties with a lot area of 12,500 square feet or less, no building or portion thereof shall exceed 32 feet in height. For properties with a lot area over 12,500 square feet, no building or portion thereof shall exceed 35 feet in height. Flat roofs, which are those roofs with a roof pitch of 2:12 or less, shall not exceed 28 feet in height.
R-1A.note: § 58-65(e)(1): minimum lot area 8,500 sq ft with a minimum width at the building line of 75 feet; corner lots shall have an extra ten feet of lot width required. The § 58-65(f) table gives Floor Area Ratio 40% for lots 12,500 sq ft or less and '5,000 sq. ft. or 35%, whichever is greater' for lots over 12,500 sq ft, and Impervious Surface Ratio 50%.

R-1AA.frontNote: Same as R-1A: 20 percent of the lot depth or the existing/most recently demolished home's setback, whichever is greater (§ 58-65(f)(6)a.).
R-1AA.sideNote: Same as R-1A: 30 percent of lot width equally divided for one-story/first floor (7.5 feet for lots 60 feet wide or less); 40 percent of lot width for the second story (10 feet for lots 60 feet wide or less). (§ 58-65(f)(7)).
R-1AA.rearNote: 25 feet for a one-story structure and 35 feet for any second-story portion; may be reduced to ten feet where the rear yard abuts non-residentially zoned property. (§ 58-65(f)(8)).
R-1AA.heightNote: Two stories maximum; 32 feet for lots 12,500 sq ft or less, 35 feet for lots over 12,500 sq ft, 28 feet for flat roofs (pitch 2:12 or less), 40 feet permitted on lots over 50,000 sq ft with at least 100 feet of width at the building line if all side setbacks are increased to 35 feet. (§ 58-65(f)(3)b.)
R-1AA.note: § 58-65(e)(2): minimum lot area 10,000 sq ft with a minimum frontage at the building line of 100 feet; corner lots shall have an extra ten feet of lot width required. FAR 40% (lots 12,500 sq ft or less) / '5,000 sq. ft. or 35%, whichever is greater' (over 12,500 sq ft); Impervious Surface Ratio 50%.

R-1AAA.frontNote: Same as R-1A: 20 percent of the lot depth or the existing/most recently demolished home's setback, whichever is greater (§ 58-65(f)(6)a.).
R-1AAA.sideNote: Same as R-1A: 30 percent of lot width equally divided for one-story/first floor; 40 percent of lot width for the second story. Lots over 200 feet in width shall use the required setback for lots which are 200 feet in width. (§ 58-65(f)(7)).
R-1AAA.rearNote: 25 feet for a one-story structure and 35 feet for any second-story portion; may be reduced to ten feet where the rear yard abuts non-residentially zoned property. (§ 58-65(f)(8)).
R-1AAA.heightNote: Two stories maximum; 32 feet for lots 12,500 sq ft or less, 35 feet for lots over 12,500 sq ft, 28 feet for flat roofs, 40 feet on lots over 50,000 sq ft with at least 100 feet width at the building line if all side setbacks are increased to 35 feet.
R-1AAA.note: § 58-65(e)(3): minimum lot area 25,000 sq ft with a minimum frontage at the building line, which is the front setback line of the main residence, of 150 feet and a minimum frontage at the street and at the lake of 150 feet; corner lots shall have an extra ten feet of lot width required. FAR '5,000 sq. ft. or 35%, whichever is greater'; Impervious Surface Ratio 50%.

R-2 (single-family detached, lot over 70.rearNote: Rear yard, first floor 10 feet; rear yard, second floor 20 feet. Where the R-2 lot abuts single-family zoned property the rear yard setback shall be 25 feet to the first floor wall and 35 feet to the second floor wall (§ 58-66(f)(6)a.).

R-3 (single family).note: § 58-67(e)(1) development standards table. Minimum land area per unit 6,000 sq ft; max impervious coverage 60%; minimum off-street parking 2/unit. Maximum density 17 units per acre (§ 58-67(d)(3)). On corner lots the principal street front yard must meet a minimum 25-foot front setback and the secondary street(s) a minimum 20-foot setback (§ 58-67(e)(3)).

R-3 (duplexes).rearNote: Rear yard—one-story 10 feet; rear yard—two-story 25 feet. (§ 58-67(e)(1) table).
R-3 (duplexes).note: § 58-67(e)(1) development standards table, duplexes column. Minimum land area per unit 4,500 sq ft; max impervious coverage 65%; minimum off-street parking 2/unit.

R-3 (multi-family housing).rearNote: Rear yard—one-story 20 feet; rear yard—two-story 25 feet. (§ 58-67(e)(1) table).
R-3 (multi-family housing).heightNote: The table prints '35/30*' for max. building height.
R-3 (multi-family housing).note: § 58-67(e)(1) development standards table, multi-family housing column. § 58-67(d)(2): minimum building site for a multiple-family complex 15,000 sq ft with a minimum front width of 100 feet and a minimum depth of 100 feet; for properties under 15,000 sq ft the R-2 provisions apply. Minimum land area per unit 2,562 sq ft; max impervious coverage 70%; minimum off-street parking 2.5/unit.

R-4.frontNote: 'Building and accessory structures, 35 feet in height or less, shall meet the following setbacks: front yard of 25 feet; side yards of 20 feet; and a rear yard of 25 feet.
R-4.sideNote: 20 feet for buildings and accessory structures 35 feet in height or less, plus an additional five feet for each additional ten feet or fraction thereof above 35 feet in height. (§ 58-68(e)(1)).
R-4.rearNote: 25 feet for buildings and accessory structures 35 feet in height or less, plus an additional five feet for each additional ten feet or fraction thereof above 35 feet in height. (§ 58-68(e)(1)).
R-4.heightNote: 'The maximum building height in the R-4 district is 55 feet, however, if the property is located within the central business district, the maximum height is three stories and 40 feet and any third floor requires approval as a conditional use. Variances for more than three stories in the central business district are prohibited.' (§ 58-68(e)(5)).
R-4.note: Multifamily (high density R-4) district. § 58-68(d)(2): minimum building site for a multiple-family complex 20,000 sq ft with a minimum front width of 100 feet and a minimum depth of 100 feet; properties with less than 20,000 and at least 15,000 sq ft develop per the R-3 district. Maximum density 17 units per acre. Maximum floor area ratio 110 percent.

PURD.frontNote: The PURD district prints no setback numbers of its own.
PURD.sideNote: § 58-69(c)(11): 'The perimeter of the planned unit residential development shall contain a buffer or setback strip of 50 feet to any adjacent private property, if the development includes any building over 30 feet in height. Otherwise a buffer or setback strip of 20 feet shall be provided.... No buildings, parking lots or other structures may be located within this area.'
PURD.heightNote: § 58-69(b)(3): multiple-family dwellings permitted 'provided, however, in no case shall the building height as defined in this article exceed 35 feet. Parapet walls or mechanical equipment and related structures may be added to the building height but in no case shall extend more than five feet above the height limitation established in this section.'
PURD.note: Planned unit residential development. § 58-69(c)(2): overall density shall not exceed five units per acre for properties designated single-family in the comprehensive plan, increasable to eight units per acre for single-family, zero lot line or townhouse development in approved PURD areas, or ten units per acre for properties designated low density or multi-family.

O-1.frontNote: 'The front setback from all streets shall be a minimum of ten feet from the property line and a minimum of 15 feet on Orlando Avenue.
O-1.sideNote: 'Side yard setbacks shall be a minimum of five feet from each property line unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel, then a 15-foot setback shall be observed.' Within the Hannibal Square Neighborhood Commercial District area new buildings may be permitted zero-foot side setbacks unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel, then a 15-foot side setback.
O-1.rearNote: 'The rear setback shall be a minimum of 30 feet from the property line. The rear setback may be reduced to ten feet from the property line if the rear yard does not abut a residentially zoned property, and if the building is oriented towards the front of the property.' (§ 58-72(f)(1)).
O-1.heightNote: 'Building heights shall not exceed the height limits imposed by the maximum height map. For those properties shown with a two-story maximum, the maximum building height shall be 30 feet.
O-1.note: Office (O-1) district. 'The maximum floor area ratio and building lot coverage shall be 45 percent,' increasable by an additional five percent where the parking for that increment is entirely underground beneath the building footprint or the upper floors are cantilevered over it. Residential units are not permitted on the first or ground floor; with residential above, FAR may be up to 60 percent.

O-2.frontNote: 'The front setback from all streets shall be a minimum of ten feet from the property line.' Within the Hannibal Square Neighborhood Commercial District new buildings shall have a required ten-foot front setback. (§ 58-73(e)(1)).
O-2.sideNote: 'Side yard setbacks shall be a minimum of five feet from each property line unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel, then a 15-foot setback shall be observed.' Within the Hannibal Square Neighborhood Commercial District zero-foot side setbacks may be permitted unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel.
O-2.heightNote: 'Building heights shall not exceed two-story height limits, and the maximum building height shall be 30 feet for flat-roof buildings and 35 feet for peaked roof buildings.' (§ 58-73(e)(7)).
O-2.note: Office (O-2) district. § 58-73(d): 'There shall be no minimum building lot size except that each site shall have a minimum frontage of 50 feet on a publicly dedicated right-of-way.' Maximum floor area ratio and building lot coverage 45 percent, increasable by five percent for fully underground or cantilevered-over parking; up to 60 percent FAR where residential units are provided above the ground floor.

C-1.frontNote: 'The front setback from all streets shall be a minimum of 15 feet from the property line.' (§ 58-74(e)(1)).
C-1.sideNote: 'Side and rear yard setbacks from interior property lines within or adjacent to any other C-1 district parcel shall be a minimum of five feet from each property line but shall be 20 feet to any other non-C-1 zoned parcel and 35 feet to any residentially-zoned parcel.' (§ 58-74(e)(1)).
C-1.rearNote: Same as the side standard: five feet from interior property lines within or adjacent to another C-1 parcel, 20 feet to any other non-C-1 zoned parcel, 35 feet to any residentially-zoned parcel. (§ 58-74(e)(1)).
C-1.heightNote: Building heights shall not exceed the height limits imposed by the maximum height map: two-story maximum = 30 feet; three-story = 42.5 feet (40 feet within the central business district); four-story = 55 feet; five-story = 65 feet; eight stories = 95 feet. (§ 58-74(e)(8); § 58-85).
C-1.note: Commercial (C-1) district. it is a minimum parcel size for zoning the district, not a per-lot building-site minimum. Maximum floor area ratio and building lot coverage 45 percent, increasable by five percent for fully underground or cantilevered-over parking or for a hotel building; up to 60 percent FAR with residential above the ground floor.

CBD.frontNote: 'On all streets, buildings and structures shall be built to a zero-foot building setback from the property line or such front setback as is established by the average front setback of the existing buildings on that block of street frontage, whichever is greater.' This is a build-to standard, not a simple minimum. Canopies may extend over the sidewalks provided a clearance of nine feet, zero inches is maintained.
CBD.sideNote: 'No side yard setbacks shall be required on interior side property lines.' (§ 58-75(f)(4)).
CBD.rearNote: 'Buildings shall be setback no less than ten feet from the rear lot line.' (§ 58-75(f)(3)).
CBD.heightNote: 'Building heights shall not exceed the height limits imposed by the maximum height map. For those properties within the geographic areas shown with a two-story maximum, the maximum building height shall be 30 feet; for those properties shown with a three-story maximum height, the maximum building height may be up to 40 feet if approved via conditional use.
CBD.note: Central business district. The maximum floor area ratio for any building shall be 200 percent, including the floor area of any attached or detached above-grade private parking garage. Maximum residential density 17 units per acre (48 units per acre for the existing second floor of 444 W. New England Avenue).

C-3.frontNote: 'The front setback to all streets shall be a minimum of ten feet from the property line and a minimum of 15 feet on Orlando Avenue. For properties along Orange Avenue, the front setback may be reduced to the average front setback of the existing buildings within that block if approved by the city commission.' Within the Hannibal Square Neighborhood Commercial District area, a required ten-foot front setback.
C-3.sideNote: 'Side yard setbacks shall be a minimum of five feet from each property line, unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel, then a 15-foot setback shall be observed.' Within the Hannibal Square Neighborhood Commercial District area, zero-foot side setbacks may be permitted unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel, then 15 feet. (§ 58-76(e)(1)).
C-3.rearNote: 'The rear setback shall be a minimum of 30 feet from the property line unless the rear yard abuts a residentially zoned parcel, then a 35-foot setback shall be observed. The rear setback may be reduced to ten feet from the property line if the rear yard does not abut a residentially zoned property, and if the building is oriented towards the front of the property.' (§ 58-76(e)(1)).
C-3.heightNote: Building heights shall not exceed the height limits imposed by the maximum height map: two-story maximum = 30 feet; three-story = 42.5 feet, unless located within the central business district; four-story = 55 feet; five-story = 65 feet. (§ 58-76(e)(7); § 58-85).
C-3.note: Commercial (C-3) district. § 58-76(d): 'There shall be no minimum lot size area however the lot must have a minimum frontage of 50 feet on a major arterial street.' Maximum floor area ratio and building lot coverage 45 percent, increasable by five percent for fully underground or cantilevered-over parking or for a hotel building; up to 60 percent FAR with residential above the ground floor.

C-3A.frontNote: 'The front setback from all streets shall be a minimum of ten feet from the property line.' Within the Hannibal Square Neighborhood Commercial District, a required ten-foot front setback. (§ 58-77(e)(1)).
C-3A.sideNote: 'Side yard setbacks shall be a minimum of five feet from each property line unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel, then a 15-foot setback shall be observed.' Within the Hannibal Square Neighborhood Commercial District, zero-foot side setbacks may be permitted unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel.
C-3A.heightNote: Building heights shall not exceed the height limits imposed by the maximum height map (§ 58-77(e); § 58-85).
C-3A.note: Commercial (C-3A) district. § 58-77(d): 'There shall be no minimum lot area; however, the lot must have a minimum frontage of 50 feet on a street.' Maximum floor area ratio and building lot coverage 45 percent, increasable by five percent for fully underground or cantilevered-over parking; up to 60 percent FAR with residential above the ground floor. Maximum residential density 17 units per acre.

I-1.frontNote: 'The front setback shall be a minimum of 15 feet from the property line.... If a loading and unloading area is to be in front of the building, the front setback shall be increased to 35 feet.' (§ 58-78(d)(1)).
I-1.sideNote: 'Side yard setbacks shall be a minimum of five feet from each property line....
I-1.rearNote: 'The rear setback shall be a minimum of 30 feet from the property line.... The rear setback shall be waived for any lot having a railroad right-of-way as its rear lot line.' (§ 58-78(d)(1)).
I-1.heightNote: Building heights shall not exceed the height limits imposed by the maximum height map: two-story maximum = 30 feet; three-story = 42.5 feet; four-story = 55 feet; five-story = 65 feet. (§ 58-78(d)(6); § 58-85).
I-1.note: Limited industrial and warehouse (I-1) district. Maximum floor area ratio and building lot coverage 45 percent, increasable by five percent for fully underground or cantilevered-over parking or for a hotel building.

PQP.frontNote: 'The front setback shall be a minimum of ten feet from the property line.' Within the Hannibal Square Neighborhood Commercial District, a required ten-foot front setback. (§ 58-79(f)(1)).
PQP.sideNote: 'Side yard setbacks shall be a minimum of five feet from each property line unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel, then a 15-foot setback shall be observed.' Within the Hannibal Square Neighborhood Commercial District, zero-foot side setbacks may be permitted unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel.
PQP.heightNote: Building heights shall not exceed the height limits imposed by the maximum height map: two-story maximum = 30 feet; three-story = 42.5 feet (40 feet in the central business district when approved as a conditional use); four-story = 55 feet; five-story = 65 feet; up to eight stories = 95 feet. (§ 58-79(f)(6); § 58-85).
PQP.note: Public and quasi-public (PQP) district. § 58-79(e): 'There shall be no minimum building site size except that each site shall have a minimum frontage of 50 feet on a publicly dedicated right-of-way.' 'The maximum floor area ratio and building lot coverage outside of the central business district shall be 45 percent,' increasable by five percent for fully underground or cantilevered-over parking.

PR.frontNote: 'The front setback from all streets shall be a minimum of ten feet from the property line.' (§ 58-81(e)(2)).
PR.sideNote: 'Side yard setbacks shall be a minimum of ten feet from each property line to any nonresidentially-zoned parcels and 20 feet to any residentially-zoned parcels.' 'Based upon the size and scale of the building or structure, the city commission may impose greater setbacks as would be compatible with the characteristics of the adjacent properties.' (§ 58-81(e)(2)).
PR.rearNote: 'Rear yard setbacks shall be a minimum of 20 feet from each property line to any nonresidentially-zoned parcels and 35 feet to any residentially-zoned parcel.' (§ 58-81(e)(2)).
PR.heightNote: 'Building heights shall not exceed two story height limits and the maximum building height shall be 45 feet for buildings.' (§ 58-81(e)(4)).
PR.coverageNote: 'The maximum floor area ratio and building lot coverage shall be 20 percent for active recreational facilities and ten percent for passive recreational facilities.' Two figures are printed, depending on facility type, so no single coverage number is recorded. (§ 58-81(e)(3)).
PR.note: Parks and recreation (PR) district. Any buildings or structures erected within this district shall be approved by the city commission following a public hearing. No minimum lot area or lot width is printed.

MA.frontNote: § 58-82(g)(1): 'Any building constructed within this district shall adhere to the following minimum required setbacks for front, rear and side yards, as set forth in the office (O-1) zoning district.' — i.e. the O-1 standards apply: front minimum ten feet (15 feet on Orlando Avenue).
MA.sideNote: Per § 58-82(g)(1) the O-1 side standard applies: minimum five feet from each property line unless the parcel shares a common line with a residentially-zoned parcel, then 15 feet.
MA.rearNote: Per § 58-82(g)(1) the O-1 rear standard applies: minimum 30 feet, reducible to ten feet if the rear yard does not abut residentially zoned property and the building is oriented towards the front.
MA.heightNote: 'Building heights shall not exceed the height limits imposed by the maximum height map. For those properties shown with a two story maximum, the maximum building height shall be 30 feet; for those properties shown with a three story maximum height, the maximum building height shall be 42 feet. For those properties shown with a four story maximum height, the maximum building height shall be 55 feet.
MA.note: Medical arts (MA) district. Maximum floor area ratio 100 percent, which may be calculated on a campus-wide or area-wide collective basis. No separate building lot coverage figure is printed, so `coverage` is omitted.

suwannee_county.name: Suwannee County
suwannee_county.source: Codified Ordinances (this PDF). No zoning or land development chapter is codified in this volume — the Table of Contents runs Ch. 1 General Provisions through C

equip.cite: No generator / mechanical equipment placement rule
equip.text: This volume contains no provision on where a standby generator, A/C condenser, pool pump or LP tank may be placed relative to a lot line, and no accessory-structure or yard-encroachment provision. The only references to air conditioning are contractor-licensing categories (Ch. 22, Art. II) and 'room air conditioners' listed as white goods in the solid waste chapter (Ch. 62).

fort_lauderdale.name: Fort Lauderdale
fort_lauderdale.source: Unified Land Development Regulations (ULDR), Chapter 47. District list from Sec. 47-4.1 Listing. Dimensional standards read from the printed 'Table of dimension

gen.cite: Mechanical and plumbing equipment - the generator rule (Sec. 47-19.2.S)
gen.text: S. Mechanical and plumbing equipment. Mechanical and plumbing equipment, such as air conditioner compressors, generators, lawn irrigation pumps, and swimming pool accessories shall not be located in the required front yard, but may be located within the required side or rear yards, but shall be no closer than five (5) feet from any property line provided that no such structure exceeds five (5) feet in height measured from the grade, eight (8) feet in length and limited to an area of forty (40) square feet.

equip.cite: Aboveground storage tanks, residential (Sec. 47-19.2.JJ.1)
equip.text: 1. Aboveground tanks containing combustible liquids and liquid propane, residential properties. Except as provided in JJ.2., aboveground tanks when accessory to a building with a residential use shall not be located in the required front yard, but may be permitted in the required rear and side yards, but no closer than five (5) feet from any property line except where property is abutting a street or waterway. Where abutting a street or a waterway, such aboveground tanks shall be subject to the yard requirements of the zoning district where it is located. In the event that these requirements conflict with the Florida Building Code or the Florida Fire Prevention Code, the more restrictive requirement shall apply.

equip.cite: Aboveground storage tanks, multifamily and nonresidential (Sec. 47-19.2.JJ.2)
equip.text: 2. Aboveground tanks containing combustible liquids and liquid propane, multifamily and nonresidential properties. Aboveground tanks, when accessory to multifamily and nonresidential properties, shall meet the yard requirements of the zoning district in which they are located and shall be subject to the requirements of the Florida Building Code and the Florida Fire Prevention Code.

equip.cite: General accessory use and structure rules (Sec. 47-19.2.B, F, H, J)
equip.text: B. No accessory use or structure may be located within a required yard specified by the zoning district where the development site is located, unless specifically permitted by the ULDR. F. No accessory use or structure greater than two and one-half (2 1/2) feet in height shall be permitted within five (5) feet of the waterway as measured in accordance with Section 47-2.2.R., unless specifically permitted. H. No accessory use or structure shall be located on a corner lot within fifteen (15) feet of any side street property line. For other than corner lots, when an accessory use or structure is permitted in the front or rear yard, but is not expressly permitted in the side yard, such accessory use or structure shall be setback from the side property line a minimum distance equal to the required side yard required by the zoning district where the development site is located. J....in no instance shall the aggregate gross floor area of all accessory uses or structures on a parcel exceed forty-nine percent (49%) of the gross floor area of a principal building on the development site.

equip.cite: Roof mounted structures (Sec. 47-19.2.Z.1)
equip.text: 1. Roof mounted structures such as air conditioners and satellite dish antennae shall be required to be screened with material that matches the material used for the principal structure and shall be at least six (6) inches high above the top most surface of the roof mounted structure. Vent pipes, skylights, cupolas, solar collectors and chimneys shall not be subject to this provision.

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical equipment in the Regional Activity Center districts (Sec. 47-13)
equip.text: iii. Screening of rooftop mechanical equipment. All rooftop mechanical equipment, stair and elevator towers shall be designed as an integral part of the building volume and shall be required to be screened so as not to be visible from abutting residential uses or vacant residentially zoned property.

equip.cite: Landscape screening of equipment (Sec. 47-21.9)
equip.text: (c) Screening of Equipment: Dumpsters, mechanical equipment and electrical transformers shall be screened on at least three (3) sides by landscape material that is a minimum of thirty (30) inches in height.... Shrubs shall be incorporated in a manner on the site so as to be a visual screen for mechanical equipment or other accessories to the residence.

equip.cite: Separation from a fuel storage facility (Sec. 47-18, outdoor sales)
equip.text: Such sales will be permitted to be made from areas located a minimum of fifty (50) feet from: a. Any fuel storage facility of any kind; and b. Any area required to provide parking in connection with a restaurant or lounge.

gen.cite: Generators (stationary emergency) -- Ch. 16, Sec. 5(b), Special setbacks table
gen.text: The table row reads, verbatim: 'Generators (stationary emergency) (1), (8) | Refer to NFPA 58 requirements, as may be amended'. No distance in feet is printed. Note (1): 'In no case shall the special setback exceed 50 percent of the minimum yard dimension.' Note (8): 'Structure shall be screened from rights-of-way and adjacent properties using architectural features, opaque fencing or walls, consistent with the surrounding primary structures, or landscaping of sufficient density and maturity at planting to provide opaque screening. For generators and LP fuel storage tanks, there shall be a three-foot clearance area in front of the service panel, if applicable, for maintenance.'

gen.cite: Customer-owned generator interconnection (Ch. 16)
gen.text: '...been informed of the customer's intent to install an interconnected customer-owned generator. Off-grid systems shall be exempt from this requirement.' (; Ord. No. 2010-3, s. 3; Ord. No. 2021-13, s. 3) -- a utility-notification requirement, not a setback.

equip.cite: Air conditioning unit -- Ch. 16, Sec. 5(b)
equip.text: 'Air conditioning unit | 3.5 feet into yard (1)'. Note (1): 'In no case shall the special setback exceed 50 percent of the minimum yard dimension.'

equip.cite: LP Fuel storage tank -- Ch. 16, Sec. 5(b)
equip.text: 'LP Fuel storage tank (2), (7), (8): Residential zones | Refer to NFPA 37 requirements, as may be amended'. Note (2): 'Location within required yards permitted in rear and side yards only.' Note (7): 'Location within the required rear yard is prohibited on an atypical lot if structure is greater than four feet in height.' Note (8): screening plus a three-foot clearance area in front of the service panel for maintenance.

equip.cite: Scope of the special-setback section -- Ch. 16, Sec. 5(a)
equip.text: 'This section provides for specific accessory structures and architectural appurtenances and features to be located within required building setback areas. Recorded easements and required landscaped buffers shall supersede the minimum dimensions permitted by this section.'

equip.cite: PC-A Neighborhood District -- appurtenance encroachment (Ch. 17, Sec. 29(d)(6) footnote 3)
equip.text: 'The following appurtenances shall be allowed to encroach three feet into the side-yard setback; air conditioning equipment, pool pumps and related equipment, other equipment appurtenant to the residential use where otherwise permitted to be located outside, concrete pads associated with air conditioning equipment, and garage stoops.' -- This is the only place in the Port Orange LDC that names pool pumps and A/C pads together as permitted encroachments, and it applies only inside the PC-A Neighborhood District.

equip.cite: Roof-mounted mechanical equipment (Ch. 14, architectural design)
equip.text: 'Roof-mounted mechanical equipment shall be located within the area of the roof surface that is farthest away from adjacent residential uses or residential zoned property.' Equipment noise 'shall comply with the noise regulations set forth in the Code of Ordinances of the City of Port Orange, Florida.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment (definition and placement) - Sec. 30-6.10
equip.text: "For purposes of this section, mechanical equipment is defined as a heating, ventilation, or air conditioning unit placed outside of a building in addition to any utility-related equipment such as backflow preventers, pumps, transformers and similar equipment required to be installed on a development site. Mechanical equipment shall be located to minimize noise and visual impacts to adjacent property in a residential zoning district or a planned development district with predominately residential uses. A. Mechanical equipment shall be screened and sound attenuation shall be provided when adjacent to any property in a residential zoning district or a planned development district with predominately residential uses. B. Mechanical equipment shall not be located between the building and the street unless the utility company determines this to be the only feasible location. C. Screening, by wall, fence or vegetative matter, shall exceed the height of the equipment if the equipment is visible from the street or adjacent properties. Certain equipment, including rain barrels or cisterns, shall not require screening provided they are designed to blend with the building and are constructed with the same materials and colors. D. Roof-top mechanical equipment shall be enclosed by parapets or screen walls of the minimum height necessary to conceal it from the street and adjacent properties. E. Chiller plants and similar large-scale utility structures shall provide a six-foot high wall to hide the structure from the public street and adjacent properties. A six-foot wide landscaping strip planted with shrubs and trees shall be provided along the wall." Note: this section names no setback distance and does not name generators.

equip.cite: Projections into a required yard - Sec. 30-6.8 C.2
equip.text: "Every part of a required yard shall be open and unobstructed from its lowest point to the sky, except for the customary projection of sills, belt courses, cornices, open exit stairs, ornamental features and eaves; provided, however, that none of the above projections shall extend into a required yard more than 36 inches; and further provided that none of the above projections shall extend over any public right-of-way, except in the MU-1, MU-2, BUS, and transect zoning districts. Enclosed exit stairs, outside stairways, balconies, chimneys, flues or other projections shall not extend into any required yard." Note: the permitted-projection list does NOT include generators, A/C condensers, pool equipment or LP tanks.

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures, general - Sec. 30-5.34
equip.text: "All accessory structures and uses shall meet the following general requirements and the standards established in this chapter for each specific use or structure: A. No accessory structure may be built unless in conjunction with or after the start of construction of the principal use on the building site. B. No accessory use may be in operation unless the principal use on the site is also active. C. Except as otherwise specifically permitted by this article, accessory uses and structures shall be located on the same building site as the associated principal use. D. Accessory structures shall be no larger than 50 percent of the building square footage of the principal structure. E. Except as otherwise specifically permitted by this article, no accessory use or structure shall be located within the front or street side yard. F. Accessory structures shall conform to the principal building setbacks, unless noted otherwise in this chapter."

equip.cite: Small accessory structures in residential districts - Table V-5, note 7
equip.text: "Accessory pre-engineered or pre-manufactured structures of 100 square feet or less and one story in height may be erected in the rear or side yard as long as the structure has a minimum yard setback of three feet from the rear or side property line, is properly anchored to the ground, and is separated from neighboring properties by a fence or wall that is at least 75 percent opaque." Table V-5 also sets "Rear, accessory" = 5 ft in SF, RC, MH, RMF-5, RMF-6, RMF-7 and RMF-8.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment in mixed-use and nonresidential districts - Sec. 30-4.21 E
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment. All mechanical equipment shall be placed on the roof, in the rear or side of the building, and shall be screened with parapets or other types of visual screening."

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment in the transects - Sec. 30-4.13 C.4
equip.text: "The following shall not be located within the public sidewalk zone; utility poles including electrical transmission and distribution poles; light poles; mechanical equipment as defined in section 30-6.10; signs included in section 30-9.2A; and street furniture including benches, trash receptacles, and bicycle racks."

equip.cite: Utility uses permitted in all districts - Sec. 30-4.6
equip.text: "The following utility uses shall be allowed as permitted uses in all zoning districts: A. Electric, cable, or fiber optic facilities. 1. All underground transmission facilities; 2. All overhead utility transmission facilities not exceeding three feet in diameter and 75 feet in height; 3. All transformers, meters and associated appurtenances; and 4. Any electric structure or facility that is sited on property 10,000 square feet or less and no more than 20 feet in height (utility poles, light poles and telemetry towers shall not be considered a structure). B. Water facilities. All water mains, valves, hydrants, services, backflow preventers or any other appurtenances required to distribute and deliver potable water and to satisfy fire safety requirements.... D. Gas facilities. 1. All gas distribution facilities including gas mains, valves, services, meters or any other appurtenances required to distribute and deliver natural or LP gas; and 2. Any gate station, regulator station or similar structure that is sited on property 5,625 square feet or less with a structure height of 20 feet or less."

equip.cite: Screening of utility equipment in the PS district - Sec. 30-4.22 G.3.b.ii
equip.text: "Electrical transformers and other utility equipment shall be screened from public view."

equip.cite: Historic districts - certificate of appropriateness, Sec. 30-4.28
equip.text: "Appurtenances. Installation of air conditioning units, mechanical equipment, satellite dishes, solar collectors, and pool filtration systems" is listed among the actions requiring a certificate of appropriateness in a historic district.

equip.cite: Noise - Sec. 15-3(d)(8), continuously operating equipment
equip.text: "Pumps, air conditioners, air-handling equipment and other continuously operating equipment. No person shall operate or permit the operation of any pump, air conditioning, air-handling or other continuously operating motorized equipment in such a manner so as to cause a noise disturbance." (Chapter 15) The noise chapter's exemptions (Sec. 15-3(e)) cover emergency work and emergency vehicles but list no exemption for standby or emergency generators.

equip.cite: Food truck generators - Sec. 30-5.38 B.7
equip.text: "Any food truck generator(s) used must operate at a sound decible level of 60 db or less, measured at a distance of ten feet from the generator." This is the only place in the code that gives a generator a distance, and it applies to mobile food trucks, not to a permanent standby generator.

equip.cite: Fences and walls - Sec. 30-6.9 B.1
equip.text: "Fences located within a required yard setback, or within five feet of the front property line in districts requiring no minimum front yard, shall not exceed eight feet in height." Relevant because Sec. 30-6.10 C requires screening to exceed the height of the equipment.

Table V-10 gives no height in feet.

PD.rearNote: No fixed envelope; standards are set by the planned development ordinance (article III).
