gen.cite: PERMANENT EMERGENCY POWER GENERATORS - Sec. 20-30.A.6 (verbatim)
gen.text: 'Permanent emergency power generators, pool pumps and filters, irrigations pumps, and air conditioning units are permitted in the required rear and side yards, subject to the following restrictions: a. The property owner must obtain a building permit from the city for the installation of the permanent emergency power generator, air conditioning unit and aboveground or underground fuel tank. The building department and fire department shall review all such permit applications to ensure that such installation minimizes the visual and acoustic impact on adjacent property and the city engineer and the zoning department shall review all such permit applications to ensure that all engineering issues and setbacks are met consistent with the provisions of this section. Additionally, the sound of the operation of any emergency use generator and air conditioning unit shall meet the requirements of article IV of this chapter. b. The permanent emergency power generator and air conditioning unit shall be located no closer than three (3) feet from any property line for any lot that is part of a site plan approved by the city commission on or after January 1, 2018. c. For any lot that was part of a site plan approved by the city commission prior to January 1, 2018, the permanent emergency power generator and air conditioning unit may have no minimum setback from the property line. d. For any lot that was part of a site plan approved by the city commission prior to January 1, 2018, but for which a building permit has not been issued prior to that date, the following regulations shall apply: 1. Head to head placement of equipment on contiguous lots shall be prohibited. 2. There shall be a minimum front to back separation of ten (10) feet between units for limited situations that require placement within adjoining side yards. Approval is required by the city engineer to pair units and must show justification of need. 3. Proper swales and necessary slopes shall be developed, as approved by the city engineer, to ensure adequate drainage. 4. Air conditioning pads shall be located on or near the high points of the side yards to allow for adequate drainage. 5. Side yard fences shall be located no closer than five (5) feet behind the rear-most air conditioning pad for situations that require placement within adjoining side yards. e. The permanent emergency power generator's maintenance cycle run shall only be permitted between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m., Monday through Sunday, and shall continue for no more than thirty (30) minutes per cycle. f. Permanent emergency power generators may only be operated for non-maintenance purposes when a state of emergency has been declared by the city or whenever there is a power outage. g. All aboveground tanks shall be attached to the primary structure in accordance with the National Fire Code (NFPA 58), as amended. h. Underground fuel tanks that have a capacity of twenty thousand (20,000) gallons or less shall be located in accordance with NFPA 58, as amended. A buildable lot line shall be defined as the setback to a primary and accessory residential unit, screen enclosure and/or shed, whichever setback is closest to the property line. i. Any tank filled on site must be located so that the filling connection and fixed liquid level gauge are at least ten (10) feet from any external sources of ignition (i.e., open flame, window air conditioner, compressor, etc.) or direct vent or mechanical ventilation. j. All aboveground equipment must be screened from view from adjacent streets. This screening may include fencing, hedging, or walls with shrubs. k. A carbon monoxide detector shall be located within the structure, as determined appropriate by the fire department and/or building department.'

gen.cite: Fence-to-equipment separation - Sec. 75-170.G
gen.text: 'For drainage purposes, a minimum separation of eighteen (18) inches between adjacent fences and all outdoor mechanical equipment (such as pool pumps, HVAC condensers, water treatment systems, and generators) and utility cabinets shall be maintained for all new residential construction.'

gen.cite: Generator required for wireless facilities (Article 150)
gen.text: : a wireless communications facility compound may be enlarged 'if the wireless communications facility installation has the capacity to accommodate three (3) different users and provisions are made for a generator for each user on the site'; p.1171: an equipment facility may be up to 400 sq ft in gross floor area 'if the city approves placement of a generator within such equipment facility, but should not be more than ten (10) feet in height'.

equip.cite: Yard encroachments generally - Sec. 20-30.A
equip.text: 'Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as provided in this section and as otherwise permitted in this chapter. The exceptions enumerated in this section are intended to apply generally, and shall be superseded by district regulations that are more restrictive.' Item 1: 'Sills or belt courses may not project over twelve (12) inches into a required yard; and cornices, eaves, gutters, chimneys, fireplaces, bay windows and pilasters may not project over two (2) feet into a required yard or fifteen (15) percent of required yard depth, whichever is greater.' Item 12 lists 'Utility boxes and transformers' as permitted in a required yard.

equip.cite: Accessory buildings and structures - Sec. 15-5510
equip.text: 'A. Accessory buildings and structures shall comply with the setback and other restrictions for the district in which they are located, except as otherwise provided in this division. B. No accessory building or structure shall exceed two (2) stories or twenty-five (25) feet in height... D. No accessory building may be located so as to block fire and emergency vehicles from reaching any portion of a principal structure and shall be located a minimum of ten (10) feet from a principal structure. E. No accessory structure shall be placed within a utility or drainage easement without the written approval of the city engineer and all agencies having a right to the easement.'

equip.cite: Public utilities in any district - Sec. 20-60
equip.text: 'Accessory utilities necessary to the public health and convenience, such as gas, electric and telephone lines, equipment and mains and water and sewer lift stations and wells, may be located in any district.'

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical - Sec. 20-40.A
equip.text: 'The following rooftop structures may exceed the permissible height limit in any district to a maximum of twenty-five (25) percent of the maximum allowable height: 1. Penthouses, scenery lofts, stairs, equipment towers, cupolas, steeples and domes, the maximum gross area of the horizontal section of which does not exceed twenty-five (25) percent of the roof area; and 2. Rooftop chimneys, stacks, tanks, and roof structures used only for ornamental and/or mechanical purposes. Parapet walls may not extend more than forty-eight (48) inches above the allowable height of a building.'

equip.cite: Electric meters and utility screening - Sec. 75-170.E-F
equip.text: '...front facades shall be completely screened, and said screening shall be depicted in detail on the plans. In all other instances, electric meters shall be mounted on side or rear facades. F. All nonresidential buildings and multi-family buildings shall cluster utility meters in readily accessible locations.'

No dwelling structure shall be erected or altered so as to be within ten (10) feet of its [site boundary]'.

PRD.note: Planned residential development district. Minimum size of a PRD or PCD is 10 acres of contiguous land unless waived by the city commission. Maximum density is the density permitted by the adopted future land use map. Minimum floor area per unit: detached single-family 1,150 SF; attached single-family (RS-6 unit) 1,150 SF; one-bedroom multifamily or townhouse 750 SF; each additional bedroom 125 SF.

PCD.note: Planned commercial district (Division 40, shared with PRD). Sec. 10-4050.C.1: 'No minimum lot size shall be required within a PRD or PCD.' Height is determined by the city commission on an individual development basis (Sec. 10-4050.E). Minimum size 10 acres of contiguous land unless waived. No fixed setback, lot area, lot width or height schedule is printed.

VIP.note: Village in the Park zoning district (Division 85, Sec. 10-8505 et seq., added after the Article 10 tables). Its standards are written as design and master-plan requirements rather than a dimensional schedule; Sec. 10-8530.F prints: 'Minimum open space. A minimum of thirty percent (30%) of the master planned site shall be used for the purpose of open space' and Sec. 10-8515.A restricts the district boundaries.

Parkland Equestrian District.note: Division 80, Sec. 10-8010. An overlay created 'for the purpose of encouraging, maintaining, and promoting ownership and equestrian activities within the city limits' and defined by an adopted map. It sets equestrian management standards rather than a dimensional envelope; underlying district standards continue to apply.

gen.cite: Generators (Permanent Emergency Power System)
gen.text: Sec. 12-33(A)(12): '(12) Generators (Permanent Emergency Power System). (a) All districts: i. Generators shall meet the minimum yard requirements of the zoning district except as otherwise provided in section 12-88. ii. Generators shall comply with section 12-115 of the Land Development Code screening of outdoor equipment. iii. Generators shall comply with noise ordinance as established in chapter 15 of the Code of Ordinances. (b) All non-residential and multi-family districts: i. Generators shall be considered a site plan modification and shall follow procedures established in section 12-374, Modification of site plan. ii. Generators shall not be located within the required landscape buffer and/or required open-space. iii. Generators shall not be located within any required parking space.'

gen.cite: Air conditioners, generators and similar mechanical equipment — accessory setbacks
gen.text: Sec. 12-88(C) Accessory uses and structures table. Row 'Air conditioners, generators and similar mechanical equipment': Front = 'Required'; Side = '5 ft.'; Rear = '5 ft.'; Conditions = 'Must be located behind the front building line in all cases.' ('Required' means the full front yard required by the district.) This is the section 12-88 exception referred to by section 12-33(A)(12)(a)(i).

gen.cite: Screening of outdoor equipment
gen.text: Sec. 12-115, Minimum landscaping requirements for outdoor equipment or facilities: '(A) In all zoning districts, outdoor equipment or facilities (i.e. a/c units, swimming pool equipment, FPL boxes, generators, and aboveground containers) visible from the street, parking lot, driveway, or public access drive shall be screened from view on three (3) sides with shrubs. Shrubs are to be three (3) feet in height and planted twenty-four (24) inches apart at the time of planting. Required access to equipment box doors shall be incorporated into the overall design. In lieu of shrubs, the outdoor equipment or facilities/may be hidden from view from the street, parking lot, driveway or public access drive by a privacy wall of a height necessary to totally block the public view.'

gen.cite: Other accessory structures (context for the generator row)
gen.text: Sec. 12-88(C) same table: 'Storage sheds (not air-conditioned or designed for habitation)' Front Required / Side 5 ft. / Rear 5 ft., max 150 sq. ft. and must be located behind the rear building line. 'Open-sided accessory structures, such as gazebos and tiki huts', 'Open-air (non-roofed) recreational facilities', 'Patios and screen enclosed patios' and 'Pools': Front Required / Side Required / Rear '50% of requirement, not less than 10 ft.' 'Fences and walls' and 'Driveways and curbs' are Exempt from all three.

equip.cite: Under-ground containers for natural gas (Liquefied Petroleum)
equip.text: Sec. 12-33(A)(13): '(a) All districts: i. Container shall be located within the open space of the property at least ten (10) feet from any habitable building (whether such building is on the same lot or an adjacent lot), at least five (5) feet from any lot line, and at least ten (10) feet from the nearest line defining the buildable area of any adjacent lot. ii. Container and filling connection shall be setback a minimum of five-foot from driveway or parking area. iii. Container lid or top of container shall be at grade level.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment — height exception
equip.text: Sec. 12-89(b): 'Air conditioners and similar mechanical equipment necessary to the function of a building may exceed the building height limit of the particular zoning district by up to twenty-five (25) percent provided that such equipment is, to the maximum extent practicable, screened from view of from public rights-of-way and adjacent residential uses by means of a parapet or similar architectural features.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment — RAC districts
equip.text: Sec. 12-438.12-area design standards: '(3) Mechanical equipment is not permitted along any street frontage. Screening of all mechanical equipment is required.'

equip.cite: Air conditioning compressors and other equipment serving the principal structure (§ 78-181(c)(3)c)
equip.text: Air conditioning compressors or other equipment designed to serve the principal structure may be located in any required side or rear setback. Such equipment shall be located immediately adjacent to the principal structure, and shall allow at least three feet of yard that is free and clear of any machinery. Equipment of this nature shall be screened from view of adjoining properties.

equip.cite: Detached accessory uses and structures generally (§ 78-181(c)(3) and (c)(3)a)
equip.text: Detached uses and structures are permitted in all districts, provided the uses and structures are separated from the main structure by not less than five feet... Accessory uses and structures shall not be located in required front, rear, or side setbacks in any residential district, except as provided herein. On double-frontage lots and through lots, accessory uses and structures may only be located in side yards, outside of the required setback. On a corner lot, an accessory structure shall not be allowed in the side yard facing the street right-of-way.

equip.cite: Detached accessory structures in AR and AE (§ 78-181(c)(9))
equip.text: Detached accessory structures in the AR zoning district shall have a side yard and rear yard setback of 25 feet. Detached accessory structures in the AE zoning district shall have a side yard and rear yard setback of five feet. Detached accessory structures may not be located within an established easement or required landscape buffer.

equip.cite: Mechanical and service equipment screening (§ 78-195)
equip.text: Roof, wall, and ground-mounted mechanical equipment shall be screened from public view. Mechanical equipment screening enclosures or structures shall be constructed and installed in a manner consistent with the architectural style, color, and materials of the principal use. Landscape screening must include a dense planting and/or earth berming in accordance with article V, division 8 of this chapter.

equip.cite: Definition of "mechanical equipment" (§ 79-... definitions, PDF p.1276)
equip.text: Mechanical equipment means necessary or accessory equipment mounted on or adjacent to a principal structure, including, but not limited to, central air conditioning equipment, ventilation equipment, heating equipment, generators, antennas, satellite dishes, window- or wall-mounted air conditioners, refrigeration equipment, solar and conventional hot water heaters, elevator machinery and equipment, backflow prevention devices, and meters and valves for public utilities.

equip.cite: Yard encroachments (§ 78-186(b)(4))
equip.text: Every part of a required yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky, except as otherwise permitted in this chapter, and as provided below: a. Projecting architectural features, including, but not limited to, awnings, hoods, roof overhangs, canopies, or marquees may project not more than four feet into a required setback.... c. Hardscape elements may be permitted in a required yard. (The list does not name generators or A/C equipment; those are covered by § 78-181(c)(3)c.)

equip.cite: Relocation/addition of outdoor utility facilities (§ 78-... administrative amendments, PDF p.706)
equip.text: Utility facilities. Any addition or relocation of outdoor utility facilities, including, but not limited to, the following: chillers, air-conditioning units, above-ground fuel tanks including propane or natural gas, electrical equipment such as junction boxes, and ground-mounted service boxes for public utilities such as telephones and cable television, which are deemed to be substantial by the growth management director. [treated as a development order amendment].

equip.cite: Administrative variance for setback encroachment (§ 78-... PDF p.707)
equip.text: Structural encroachments into setbacks of no more than ten percent. The growth management director may issue an administrative variance for structural encroachments into a setback of no more than ten percent of the setback, provided the structural encroachment does not encroach upon an easement.

volusia_county.source: Code of Ordinances, Chapter 72 (Land Planning), Article II (Zoning), Division 7 -- Establishment of Classifications, Sec. 72-241. Each classification carries it

equip.cite: Accessory structures -- side and rear yards (§ 72-277(a)(7))
equip.text: Accessory structures located in side or rear yards may be located no closer than five feet from the corresponding lot lines, except for fences, walls, and hedges pursuant to section 72-282. Applies in the FR, RC, A-1 through A-4, RR, RA, R-1 through R-6, R-9, MH-1 through MH-8, B-8, PUD, OMV, OUR, OTR, ORE, OCR, and SWR classifications.

equip.cite: Accessory structures -- front yards (§ 72-277(a)(8))
equip.text: Accessory structures shall not be located in front yards, including standard lots, double frontage lots, and corner lots, except for fences, walls, and hedges pursuant to section 72-282. On any corner lot, no structure, fence, wall, or hedge shall cause any obstruction to vision of motorists.

equip.cite: Accessory structures over 500 sq ft (§ 72-277(a)(5))
equip.text: Accessory structures exceeding 500 square feet in area shall meet the same yard requirements as the principal structure.

equip.cite: Accessory structures -- other limits (§ 72-277(a)(1),(2),(3),(4),(9))
equip.text: No accessory structure shall be constructed on any lot until a principal structure is either constructed or permitted for construction on the same lot (except seawalls on an ocean front lot in a defined gap, and docks). Accessory structures shall not be located in any platted easement. On an atypical lot, accessory structures are not permitted within the rear yard. The cumulative area of all structures, excluding docks and seawalls, pools and screen enclosures, shall not exceed the maximum lot coverage in the applicable zoning classification. Maximum height of an accessory structure shall not exceed 25 feet.

equip.cite: Permitted projections into a yard (§ 72-277(a)(13))
equip.text: Awnings, chimneys, fireplaces, pilasters, roof overhangs, unenclosed balconies, and unenclosed stairways may project into any yard for either three and one-half feet or half the yard, whichever is less. Generators, A/C condensers and pool equipment are NOT named in this list.

equip.cite: Structures above the roof (§ 72-277(c))
equip.text: Spires, belfries, cupolas, clerestory windows, antennas, water tanks, ventilators, solar panels, windmills, chimneys, penthouses or other similar accessory structures customarily required to extend above the roof level may extend for an additional 25 feet above the maximum building height prescribed for the classification.

equip.cite: Accessory structures to single-family dwellings in B-8 (§ 72-241, B-8 Tourist)
equip.text: Accessory structures shall be located behind the frontmost part of the principal single-family dwelling and shall have the following setbacks: Rear yard: 5 feet. Waterfront yard: 25 feet. Side yard: 5 feet.

equip.cite: Pools, hot tubs, spas (§ 72-277(a)(6))
equip.text: In-ground pools, above-ground pools, hot tubs, spas, and other similar water features shall be located no closer than eight feet, as measured from the water's edge, from any side or rear lot line, with accompanying screen enclosures, if any, located no closer than five feet from any side or rear lot line. On waterfront lots these shall meet waterfront lot setbacks.

equip.cite: Generators -- noise (§ 50-476(d)(13))
equip.text: Generators that are used to provide power during an outage are exempt, providing that the generator is operating in accordance within the manufacturer's specifications, with all standard equipment, and is in proper operating condition. Manual and automatic exercising or testing of any generator shall be limited to the hours of 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Monday through Saturday.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment -- nonresidential development (§ 72-303(h)(2))
equip.text: Loading areas or docks, outdoor storage, waste disposal, mechanical equipment, satellite dishes, truck parking and other service support equipment shall be located behind the building line and shall be fully screened from the view of adjacent properties both at ground and roof top levels with masonry, brick or durable manmade material wall.

equip.cite: Roof-mounted mechanical equipment (§ 72-303)
equip.text: Mechanical equipment located on roofs shall be integrated into the overall design of a building by screening it behind parapets or by recessing equipment into hips, gables, parapets or similar features.

homestead.name: Homestead
homestead.source: Code of Ordinances Chapter 30 ZONING, Article III "District Regulations" (Divisions 1–27, §§ 30-66 through 30-396.582), read district by district. District list

equip.cite: Projections into a required yard (§ 30-402(2))
equip.text: "Every part of a required yard or court shall be open from its lowest point to the sky unobstructed, except for the ordinary projections of sills, belt courses, cornices, buttresses, ornamental features and eaves. None of the above projections shall project into a minimum court more than twenty-four (24) inches nor into a minimum side yard more than twenty-four (24) inches." This is the only yard-encroachment allowance in Chapter 30 and it does NOT name generators, air-conditioning equipment or pool equipment. Homestead therefore grants no encroachment for mechanical equipment into a required yard.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment placement, R-3 (§ 30-208(b)(13))
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment shall not be installed near the entrances to individual dwelling units or approachways to them, or be visible from the street. This provision shall not apply to essential emergency equipment such as fire extinguishers and alarm boxes."

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening, mixed use and non-residential development (Article IV, Division 9)
equip.text: "Screening requirements. All mechanical equipment including but not limited to heating, ventilating, air conditioning machinery, accessory communications equipment, public utility service fixtures, and elevator facilities shall be screened from the public view. All solid waste disposal facilities, such as dumpsters and similar facilities, shall be screened on all four (4) sides from the public view." The same section requires the developer or private utility to "provide adequate landscaping with shrubs and plants to screen all utility facilities permitted above ground, except for city electrical substations."

"All rooftop equipment including, but not limited to mechanical equipment and vents, shall be screened by a parapet wall or similar solid materials as may be approved by the department of development services." Repeated verbatim for B-1A, B-1, B-2, B-3, I-1, I-2, I-3 and the SWPUN. The BMU, NMU and TMU versions (§§ 30-396.515, 30-396.546, 30-396.570) read: "All rooftop mechanical equipment including but not limited to heating, ventilating, air conditioning machinery, accessory communications equipment, public utility service fixtures, and elevator facilities shall be screened from the public view."

equip.cite: Rooftop screening, multi-family and mixed-use residential (Article IV, Division 10)
equip.text: "Rooftop screening: All rooftop mechanical equipment including, but not limited to heating, ventilating, air conditioning machinery, accessory communications equipment, public utility service fixtures, and elevator facilities shall be screened from the public view by a parapet wall or similar solid barrier as approved by the director of development services."

equip.cite: Propane gas tanks in B-1 and B-2 (§§ 30-256(a), 30-276(a))
equip.text: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, ice machines and propane gas tanks (sales or swap-out programs) which are incidental and ancillary to the principal permitted use, may be located, placed or stored outside subject to approval by the development services director or designee. Ice machines and propane gas tanks shall not be located, placed or stored adjacent to any building entrance, impede pedestrian or vehicular traffic, obstruct emergency vehicular access or present a hazard to the public health, safety and welfare. Ice machines and propane gas tanks shall only be permitted with the installation of bollards or other similar protective safety devices."

equip.cite: Accessory / secondary buildings in the rear yard (§§ 30-83(4), 30-98(4), 30-114(5), 30-127(5), 30-212, 30-229(c))
equip.text: A-1 and A-2: "Where a secondary building is located in the rear yard, there shall be a minimum of ten (10) feet from the rear of the principal building to the front of the secondary building, and a minimum of ten (10) feet from the secondary building to the rear lot line." R-1 and R-2: 10 ft from the rear of the principal building to the front of the secondary building and "A minimum of five (5) feet shall separate the rear of the secondary building from the rear lot line." R-3: "a distance of ten (10) to twenty-five (25) feet from the rear of the principal building to the front of the secondary building, and a minimum of five (5) feet from the rear of the secondary building to the rear lot line." R-4 (§ 30-229(c)): 10 ft behind the principal building and 5 ft from the rear lot line. All of these also allow "a six-foot minimum rear setback for a solid roof screened patio with three (3) open sides."

equip.cite: Accessory storage buildings, R-TH (§ 30-162)
equip.text: "Detached storage buildings shall be setback at least five (5) feet from side and rear lot lines and at least ten (10) feet from the principal building." Minimum floor area 80 sq ft and a maximum height at least six inches below the height of the required wall; confined to the walled area of the site.

equip.cite: Accessory buildings, AU (§ 30-394(b))
equip.text: "Minimum setbacks for accessory buildings are: From front property line, seventy-five (75) feet. From rear property line, seven and one-half (7 1/2) feet. Between buildings on same lot, parcel or tract of land, twenty (20) feet. From interior side property line, twenty (20) feet. From side street property line, thirty (30) feet."

equip.cite: Secondary buildings and street frontage (§ 30-405(c))
equip.text: "No secondary building shall be closer to the front or side of lot abutting street or other public way than the main building."

equip.cite: Generators specifically
equip.text: NOT FOUND. A full-text search of the 1,542-page document for generator, standby power, emergency power, air-conditioning unit/equipment/compressor, condenser, pool pump and pool equipment returns no zoning standard. The only occurrence of "generator" in a regulatory sense is a residential generator permit fee in the building-permit fee schedule (§ 6-52) and an emergency radio-system backup generator requirement. Homestead prints no setback, clearance or separation distance for a standby generator.

A-1.sideNote: § 30-83(3): "The width of each side yard shall be not less than ten (10) percent of the average width of the tract." A percentage, not a distance — no fixed number is printed.
A-1.note: A-1 One Family, One Acre Estate (§§ 30-81–30-83). Minimum building site area one (1) acre excluding right-of-way; 1 × 43,560 = 43,560 sq ft. Height printed "three (3) stories or thirty-five (35) feet". Minimum living area 1,500 sq ft, excluding garages, storage rooms, porches and patios. Rear yard: 25 ft for the principal building.

A-2.sideNote: § 30-98(3): "The width of each side yard shall be not less then ten (10) percent of the average width of the tract." A percentage, not a distance.
A-2.note: A-2 One Family, One-Half Acre Estate (§§ 30-96–30-98). Minimum building site area one-half acre; 0.5 × 43,560 = 21,780 sq ft. Height "three (3) stories or thirty-five (35) feet". Minimum floor area 1,500 sq ft. Same rear-yard secondary-building and screened-patio rules as A-1. No minimum lot width printed.

R-1.frontNote: § 30-114(3): 25 ft, "unless the front building line is already established in the block at a lesser distance by two (2) or more existing residences. If so, the minimum front yard requirement shall be twenty (20) feet. If the front building line is already established in the block at a greater distance than the twenty-five (25) feet, then all future residences shall conform to such greater distance."
R-1.sideNote: § 30-114(4): "The width of each side yard shall not be less than ten (10) percent of the average width of the lot, minimum five (5) feet zero (0) inches. Corner setbacks shall be minimum fifteen (15) feet zero (0) inches." The requirement is a percentage of lot width with a 5 ft floor, so no single number is recorded.
R-1.note: R-1 One Family (§§ 30-111–30-114). Minimum site area 7,500 sq ft "Such parcels or lots shall have an average width of at least sixty (60) feet." NOTE: the § 30-397 summary table prints lot width 75 ft and a side-yard footnote "Minimum is 5 ft.; Maximum is 7.5 ft." — both differ from § 30-114; Article III governs by the table's own terms, so 60 ft is recorded. Height "three (3) stories or thirty-five (35) feet".

R-2.sideNote: § 30-127(4): "not less than ten (10) percent of the average width of the lot, minimum five (5) feet zero (0) inches. Corner setbacks shall be minimum fifteen (15) feet zero (0) inches."
R-2.note: R-2 Duplex district (§§ 30-126–30-127). § 30-127(1) prints no duplex-specific site area; it says "Where applicable, R-1 development within the R-2 zoning district shall comply with the requirements set forth in section 30-114" — so the 7,500 sq ft / 60 ft figures come from § 30-114 by cross-reference, not from a separate R-2 number. Height "three (3) stories or thirty-five (35) feet".

R-TH.sideNote: § 30-156: "A minimum side yard requirement of ten (10) feet shall be provided between the end of a group of townhouses and exterior side lot line. If the end of a group of townhouses faces a public or private street, a minimum side yard requirement shall be ten (10) feet, to the side lot line.
R-TH.note: R-TH Townhouse (§§ 30-141–30-175). § 30-153 lot area for each unit: "No townhouse lot shall contain an area of less than two thousand (2,000) square feet." § 30-150 minimum development site 5 acres (217,800 sq ft). § 30-152 minimum width of a townhouse 25 ft. § 30-151 maximum height 35 ft (no story limit printed). § 30-155 rear 20 ft "except where rear yard parking is allowed".

R-CH.sideNote: § 30-188: "No minimum side yard required on one (1) side. Ten (10) feet required on opposite side."
R-CH.note: R-CH Clusterhouse (§§ 30-176–30-202). § 30-185 lot area for each unit not less than 3,000 sq ft. § 30-181.1 minimum development site 2 acres (87,120 sq ft) — the § 30-397 table prints 5 acres; Article III governs. § 30-182 minimum clusterhouse width 25 ft. § 30-183 maximum height 35 ft. § 30-186 front 20 ft, parking permitted on the front setback. § 30-187 rear 20 ft.

R-3.frontNote: § 30-210: "There shall be a twenty-five-foot front yard required, but in no case shall the front yard be less than fifteen (15) feet."
R-3.sideNote: § 30-211: "There shall be side yards totaling twenty (20) feet in width, but the width of either shall not be less than five (5) feet." 5 is the per-side floor; the two sides must total 20.
R-3.note: R-3 Multiple Apartment (§§ 30-206–30-220). § 30-208(a) minimum site area 13,000 sq ft per multiple family structure, average width at least 100 ft. § 30-212 rear 25 ft; secondary building 10 to 25 ft behind the principal building and min 5 ft from the rear lot line; 6 ft for a solid roof screened patio.

R-4.sideNote: § 30-229(b): "There shall be side yards totaling twenty (20) feet in width, but the width of which shall not be less than five (5) feet."
R-4.note: R-4 Hotel-Motel and Institutional (§§ 30-226–30-235). § 30-228: minimum site area for hotel and motel use 10,000 sq ft with average width at least 100 ft; "The minimum building site area for multiple family use [residential mixed use] shall be the same as the R-3 district" (13,000 sq ft / 100 ft). § 30-229(c) rear 25 ft; secondary building min 10 ft behind principal and min 5 ft from the rear lot line.

B-1A.frontNote: § 30-244(a): 20 ft "unless setback is already established at a lesser distance by two (2) or more buildings in the block, but no setback shall be less than fifteen (15) feet. B-1A.rearNote: § 30-244(c): "There shall be a rear yard of not less than ten (10) feet in depth where no alley exists and a twenty (20) foot depth where an alley exists, unless waived by the city council." The 10 recorded is the no-alley case.
B-1A.heightNote: § 30-242: "seventy (70) feet or six (6) stories whichever is less."
B-1A.note: B-1A Professional Business Restricted (§§ 30-241–30-251). No minimum building site area or lot width is printed. § 30-243 coverage 80 percent.

B-1.heightNote: § 30-257: "seventy (70) feet or six (6) stories whichever is less."
B-1.note: B-1 Restricted Retail Commercial (§§ 30-256–30-267).

B-3.sideNote: § 30-298(b): "There are no side yard requirements in the B-3 district." § 30-298(d): 10 ft side and 20 ft rear minimum where a B-1, B-2 or B-3 zone abuts A-1, A-2, R-1, R-2, R-TH, R-CH, R-3 or R-4.
B-3.heightNote: § 30-305.1: "seventy (70) feet or six (6) stories whichever is less."
B-3.note: B-3 Liberal Business (§§ 30-296–30-305.3). § 30-297: "There are no minimum building site requirements in the B-3 district." § 30-299: minimum 500 sq ft of floor area per store. § 30-305.2 coverage 85 percent.

I-1.sideNote: § 30-317: "No minimum side yard setback shall be required except when lots in the I-1 district abut lots zoned A-1, A-2, R-1, R-2, R-TH, R-CH, R-3 or R-4, or lots containing residential uses, in which case the minimum interior side yard setback adjacent to such zoning district or use shall be ten (10) feet."
I-1.rearNote: § 30-307: "There shall be no minimum area, side and rear yard requirements."
I-1.note: I-1 Light Industrial (§§ 30-306–30-320). § 30-309 front building line setback for industrial uses minimum 20 ft. § 30-316 height 70 ft or 6 stories whichever is less. § 30-318 coverage 90 percent. No minimum lot area or width.

I-2.sideNote: § 30-332: no minimum side yard except 10 ft interior side where the lot abuts A-1, A-2, R-1, R-2, R-TH, R-CH, R-3 or R-4 or a lot containing residential uses.
I-2.rearNote: § 30-322: "There shall be no minimum area, side and rear yard requirements."
I-2.note: I-2 Medium Industrial (§§ 30-321–30-335). § 30-324 front setback minimum 20 ft. § 30-331 height 70 ft or 6 stories whichever is less. § 30-333 coverage 90 percent.

I-3.sideNote: § 30-347: no minimum side yard except 10 ft interior side where the lot abuts A-1, A-2, R-1, R-2, R-TH, R-CH, R-3 or R-4 or a lot containing residential uses.
I-3.rearNote: § 30-337: "There shall be no minimum area, side and rear yard requirements."
I-3.note: I-3 Heavy Industrial (§§ 30-336–30-350). § 30-339 front setback minimum 20 ft. § 30-346 height 70 ft or 6 stories whichever is less. § 30-348 coverage 95 percent.

P.note: P Parking District (§§ 30-351–30-358). § 30-351(a): "In the P parking district no building of any kind shall be constructed." No setbacks, height, lot area or coverage are printed. A five-foot masonry wall not less than six inches thick is required around the perimeter where the district adjoins or faces residentially zoned property.

G.note: G General Use District (§ 30-366). Applies to newly annexed, undeveloped property, which "shall be considered unclassified and unzoned by the City of Homestead and no permits will be issued until such time as the property shall be zoned." The code sets no dimensional envelope for G.

GP.note: GP Government Property District (§§ 30-381–30-382). The code prints only the use statement and an affordable-housing density (maximum 30 dwelling units per net acre; 25 in the civic/government subarea of the SWPUN). No setback, height, lot area or coverage standard is printed for GP.

RMH.frontNote: § 27-65(a): "Front yard—Ten (10) feet from inside edge of street pavement." Measured from pavement, not a lot line.
RMH.sideNote: § 27-65(a): "Sides—Ten (10) feet minimum to any other mobile home or structure whether said structure be opened or closed." A separation distance, not a lot-line setback.
RMH.rearNote: § 27-65(a): "Rear—Twenty (20) feet between structures." § 27-65(b): "There shall be no construction of any nature within the aforementioned front and side setback requirements."
RMH.note: RMH Residential Mobile Home Park (§ 30-388), which provides only that "The standards and setbacks and regulations in this district shall be as provided in section 27-46 et seq." § 27-56 minimum mobile home space size: single-wide 4,050 sq ft, double-wide 4,050 sq ft; minimum space width 45 ft; minimum travel trailer space 1,200 sq ft / 20 ft wide; motor home space 1,000 sq ft; camper space 800 sq ft.

AU (lots of one acre or more).sideNote: § 30-394(a): "From interior side property line, fifteen (15) feet. From side street property line, twenty-five (25) feet."
AU (lots of one acre or more).note: AU Agricultural (§§ 30-391–30-396). § 30-392: "Lots for any use in AU district shall contain a minimum of five (5) acres, and have a minimum street frontage of two hundred (200) feet" (5 × 43,560 = 217,800 sq ft); the § 30-397 table footnote q notes several exceptions in § 30-392(1), (2) and (3). § 30-393 lot coverage 15 percent for lots of one acre or larger.

AU (lots 10,000 sq ft to one acre).sideNote: § 30-394(a): interior side 15 ft, side street 25 ft.
AU (lots 10,000 sq ft to one acre).note: The second setback schedule in § 30-394(a), printed for "the smaller lots (ten thousand (10,000) square foot lots to one acre)". § 30-393 coverage for these smaller lots is 25 percent.

R-TND.sideNote: § 30-396.15: "A minimum side yard requirement of five (5) feet shall be provided between a unit and exterior side lot line. A spacing of not less than ten (10) feet shall be provided between any such units."
R-TND.note: R-TND Residential Traditional Neighborhood Development (§§ 30-396.1–30-396.29). § 30-396.9 minimum development site 1 acre, "but shall not encompass less than one (1) city block." § 30-396.10 maximum height 35 ft. § 30-396.11 minimum lot width 40 ft. § 30-396.12 minimum 3,200 sq ft per unit site, "but in no event more than ten (10) units per acre." § 30-396.14 rear 20 ft "except where rear yard parking is allowed.

BMU.frontNote: § 30-396.505(a): commercial and mixed-use 20 ft "unless setback is already established at a lesser distance by two (2) or more buildings in the block, but no setback shall be less than ten (10) feet; or unless rear yard parking is provided, in which case a front setback of ten (10) feet is permitted." Free-standing residential buildings 25 ft (10 ft with rear yard parking).
BMU.sideNote: § 30-396.505(b): "No side yard shall be required for commercial and mixed-use property." Freestanding residential buildings: side yards totalling a minimum of 20 ft, neither side less than 5 ft. § 30-396.505(d): where a BMU zone abuts A-1, A-2, R-1, R-2, R-TH, R-CH, R-3 or R-4, side setbacks minimum 10 ft and rear minimum 20 ft.
BMU.rearNote: § 30-396.505(c): 20 ft for commercial and mixed-use property; 25 ft for every principal free-standing residential building, with a secondary building 10 to 25 ft behind the principal and 5 ft from the rear lot line, and 6 ft for a solid roof screened patio.
BMU.heightNote: § 30-396.502: "The minimum height limit on buildings within the BMU district shall be two (2) stories. The maximum height on buildings within this district shall be seventy (70) feet or six (6) stories, whichever is less."
BMU.note: BMU Business Mixed Use (Division 24, §§ 30-396.500–30-396.516). § 30-396.503 coverage 90 percent including parking. § 30-396.504 maximum residential density 15 units per gross acre. No minimum lot area or width is printed. The Northwest Neighborhood Overlay District (§ 30-396.516) applies within part of BMU.

NMU.frontNote: § 30-396.536(a): commercial and mixed-use 20 ft, but no less than 10 ft where a lesser line is established, or 10 ft where rear yard parking is provided; free-standing residential buildings approved before this district was created 25 ft (10 ft with rear yard parking); properties abutting Krome Avenue 5 ft minimum.
NMU.sideNote: § 30-396.536(b): "No side yard shall be required for commercial and mixed-use property, except a setback of no less than ten (10) feet shall be required on the street side of corner lots." Pre-existing freestanding residential buildings: side yards totalling a minimum of 20 ft, neither less than 5 ft. § 30-396.536(d): 10 ft side / 20 ft rear minimum where the NMU zone abuts A-1, A-2, R-1, R-2, R-TH, R-CH, R-3 or R-4.
NMU.rearNote: § 30-396.536(c): 20 ft for commercial and mixed-use properties; 25 ft for pre-existing principal free-standing residential buildings.
NMU.heightNote: § 30-396.533: maximum 60 ft or 5 stories for conforming freestanding multi-family residential structures approved before the district was created; 70 ft or 6 stories for freestanding commercial structures and mixed residential/commercial. Minimum height 20 ft or 2 stories for freestanding commercial and mixed structures; no minimum for pre-existing conforming residential.
NMU.coverageNote: § 30-396.534: "(a) The existing lot coverage for conforming residential structures approved prior to the effective date of the creation of this zoning district; (b) Eighty-five (85) percent of the total lot area for commercial and mixed residential/commercial structures." The 85 recorded is the commercial/mixed case.
NMU.note: NMU Neighborhood Mixed Use district (Division 25, §§ 30-396.531–30-396.547). Maximum gross residential density 10 units per acre (§ 30-396.535). This is the citywide NMU zoning district and is distinct from the Neighborhood Mixed Use subarea of the SWPUN below. No minimum lot area or width printed.

TMU.note: TMU Technology Mixed Use District (Division 26, §§ 30-396.560–30-396.572). The code prints no setback, height or lot-coverage numbers; § 30-396.563 requires a master site plan and regulating plan and a minimum site of 40 gross acres (10 acres or greater but less than 40 may be eligible). § 30-396.564 requires private and common open space of at least 20 percent of the development lot area.

SWPUN \u2014 Traditional Single Family N.frontNote: "Minimum—Ten (10) feet. Maximum—Twenty (20) feet or twenty (20) percent of the lot depth (whichever is less)." A build-to band, so only the minimum is a setback.
SWPUN \u2014 Traditional Single Family N.sideNote: "Minimum—Five (5) feet for each side and a total of twenty (20) percent of the lot width for both sides."
SWPUN \u2014 Traditional Single Family N.heightNote: "Up to three (3) stories not to exceed forty-two (42) feet dependent on building types and regulations as set forth in the southwest neighborhood master plan."
SWPUN \u2014 Traditional Single Family N.note: Subarea of the Southwest Planned Urban Neighborhood (§ 30-396.62). Minimum lot depth 50 ft. Maximum density 6 units per acre. Coverage includes buildings and parking. § 30-396.48 also allows detached single-family structures on parcels as small as 3,600 sq ft where other detached single-family structures on the same block are on lots of the same size, less than 5,000 sq ft.

SWPUN \u2014 Traditional Multifamily Nei.frontNote: "Minimum—Ten (10) feet. Maximum—Twenty (20) feet or twenty (20) percent of the lot depth (whichever is less)."
SWPUN \u2014 Traditional Multifamily Nei.heightNote: "Minimum of two (2) and a maximum of five (5) stories not to exceed seventy (70) feet depending on building types and regulations as set forth in the southwest neighborhood master plan."
SWPUN \u2014 Traditional Multifamily Nei.note: Subarea of the SWPUN (§ 30-396.62). Minimum lot depth 50 ft; minimum lot width 20 ft for a townhouse. No minimum lot size is printed for this subarea, so § 30-396.48's 5,000 sq ft SWPUN residential minimum applies. Density 20 units per acre, except a single residential parcel may reach 31 du/ac for a mixed-use multifamily senior residential community. No more than eight townhouse units in a row.

SWPUN \u2014 Neighborhood Mixed Use suba.frontNote: "Minimum—Five (5) feet. Maximum—Fifteen (15) feet or fifteen (15) percent of the lot depth (whichever is less)."
SWPUN \u2014 Neighborhood Mixed Use suba.sideNote: "Side and rear setbacks are not required unless an adjacent building existing at the time of development has windows facing side or rear; any new building abutting development shall then provide at least ten (10) feet of separation between the existing and new building; except for the first twenty (20) feet from the frontage line."
SWPUN \u2014 Neighborhood Mixed Use suba.rearNote: Same conditional side/rear rule as above — no fixed rear setback is printed.
SWPUN \u2014 Neighborhood Mixed Use suba.heightNote: "Up to five (5) stories not to exceed seventy (70) feet depending on building types and regulations as set forth in the southwest neighborhood master plan."
SWPUN \u2014 Neighborhood Mixed Use suba.note: Subarea of the SWPUN (§ 30-396.62), distinct from the citywide NMU district. Minimum lot depth 50 ft. Maximum residential density 15 du/ac. Parking must be placed a minimum of 20 ft behind the front facade.

SWPUN \u2014 Downtown Mixed Use subarea.frontNote: "Minimum—Five (5) feet. Maximum—Fifteen (15) feet or fifteen (15) percent of the lot depth (whichever is less)."
SWPUN \u2014 Downtown Mixed Use subarea.sideNote: "Side and rear setbacks are not required unless an adjacent building existing at the time of development has windows facing side or rear; any new building abutting development shall then provide at least ten (10) feet of separation between the existing and new building; except for the first twenty (20) feet from the frontage line."
SWPUN \u2014 Downtown Mixed Use subarea.rearNote: Same conditional rule; no fixed rear setback printed.
SWPUN \u2014 Downtown Mixed Use subarea.heightNote: "Up to five (5) stories not to exceed seventy (70) feet depending on building types and regulations as set forth in the southwest neighborhood master plan."
SWPUN \u2014 Downtown Mixed Use subarea.note: Subarea of the SWPUN (§ 30-396.62). Minimum lot depth 50 ft. Maximum residential density 15 du/ac. Balconies, arcades and colonnades may encroach into the public right-of-way to a distance of four feet from the face of the curb; stoops may encroach no more than three feet. A Downtown Mixed Use Multi-Modal Transportation Overlay District (MMTOD) overlays part of this subarea.

SWPUN \u2014 Commercial subarea.frontNote: "Minimum—Five (5) feet. Maximum—Fifteen (15) feet or fifteen (15) percent of the lot depth (whichever is less)."
SWPUN \u2014 Commercial subarea.sideNote: "Side and rear setbacks are not required unless an adjacent building existing at the time of development has windows facing side or rear; any new building abutting development shall then provide at least ten (10) feet of separation between the existing and new building, except for the first twenty (20) feet from the frontage line."
SWPUN \u2014 Commercial subarea.rearNote: Same conditional rule; no fixed rear setback printed.
SWPUN \u2014 Commercial subarea.heightNote: No subarea height is printed. § 30-396.47 governs: "The maximum height within the entire SWPUN is five (5) stories and shall not exceed seventy (70) feet."
SWPUN \u2014 Commercial subarea.note: Subarea of the SWPUN (§ 30-396.62). Minimum lot depth 50 ft.

SWPUN \u2014 Industrial subarea.heightNote: No subarea height printed; § 30-396.47 caps the whole SWPUN at 5 stories and 70 feet.
SWPUN \u2014 Industrial subarea.note: Subarea of the SWPUN (§ 30-396.62). Minimum lot depth 50 ft. No barbwire; screening measured from the street edge closest to the respective use.

SWPUN \u2014 Civic/Government subarea.heightNote: No subarea height printed; § 30-396.47 caps the whole SWPUN at 5 stories and 70 feet.
SWPUN \u2014 Civic/Government subarea.note: Subarea of the SWPUN (§ 30-396.62). Minimum lot depth 50 ft. Vehicle access limited to one curb opening a maximum of 30 ft wide. Affordable housing in this subarea is capped at 25 du/ac (§ 30-382).

SWPUN \u2014 Parks/Open Space subarea.heightNote: No subarea height printed; § 30-396.47 caps the whole SWPUN at 5 stories and 70 feet.
SWPUN \u2014 Parks/Open Space subarea.note: Subarea of the SWPUN (§ 30-396.62). Minimum lot depth 50 ft.

RTDO (Rapid Transit Development Overlay).heightNote: § 30-396.578 prints maximum height only in storeys: Subzone 1 four storeys at every distance band; Subzone 2 four storeys; Subzone 3 three storeys; Subzone 4 three storeys. No figure in feet is printed.
RTDO (Rapid Transit Development Overlay).note: Overlay district (Division 27, §§ 30-396.573–30-396.582). § 30-396.575: "The various zoning and land development regulations which underlay the RTDO continue to regulate land development actions in relation to setbacks, fences, landscaping, signage, and use areas" — the overlay sets no setbacks of its own.

gen.cite: Permanent generators - minimum setback requirements (Sec. 30-60.5(a), PDF p.801) [THE EQUIPMENT/CLEARANCE TABLE]
gen.text: "Sec. 30-60.5. Permanent generators. (a) Minimum setback requirements. (1) Residential properties: Front setback: Behind principal building line / Rear setback: 5 feet / Interior setback: 5 feet / Side street setback: 10 feet. (2) Commercial properties: Front setback: Behind principal building line / Rear setback: Same as principal building / Interior setback: Same as principal building / Side street setback: 15 feet when abutting commercial / Side street setback: 25 feet when abutting residential".

gen.cite: Permanent generators - remaining conditions (Sec. 30-60.5(b)-(h), PDF p.801-802)
gen.text: "(b) The generator system shall be designed to withstand applicable hurricane wind loads as provided for under the Florida Building Code. (c) The generator system shall meet elevation requirements under the village's floodplain regulations, at Division 30-100. (d) The generator system shall be designed and installed to prevent damages to adjacent structures due to vibration. (e) The generator system shall be installed on a minimum six-inch thick concrete slab or with a weather-protected metal frame and be properly grounded. (f) The generator system shall be installed with approved durable natural or manmade screening so that the equipment is not visible from outside the property line up to a height of ten feet. (g) The generator system shall be placed at least ten feet away from any windows, vents, or doors. (h) The generator system shall comply with the Florida Building Code, Village Code and all applicable permitting regulations."

gen.cite: Wireless equipment buildings housing generators (Sec. 30-60.30 definitions, PDF p.506)
gen.text: "Wireless equipment building shall mean any building/cabinet, shelter, or structure associated with a wireless supported service facility constructed for the primary purpose of housing the electronics, mechanical equipment, backup power, power generators and other free standing equipment associated with the operation of the facility."

equip.cite: Accessory buildings and structures (Sec. 30-60.3(a))
equip.text: "Accessory buildings/structures or uses shall conform to the setbacks as specified within each zoning district except as provided by section 30-60.3 herein." Sec. 30-60.3(b)(2): "Utility sheds larger than 144 square feet shall comply with the setbacks required of accessory structures within the applicable zoning district."

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment enclosures above the roof (Sec. 30-50.1, PDF p.539)
equip.text: "Chimneys, conveyors, cooling towers, elevator bulkheads and shafts and enclosures for mechanical equipment, fire towers, and parapet walls shall not extend more than five feet above the height of the building upon which it rests. Any required airplane beacons shall comply with Federal Aviation Regulations."

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical equipment in the B-1 District (Sec. 30-50.16(g)(9))
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment and elevator towers shall not exceed a maximum of 15 feet in height measured from the rooftop slab, and shall not encroach closer than 15 feet to any parapet wall or edge of roof."

equip.cite: Rooftop equipment in the Downtown Zoning District (Sec. 30-50.23.4-04(3), PDF p.756)
equip.text: "Any equipment such as mechanical equipment, rooftop landscape or recreational equipment shall not exceed maximum 15 feet in height measured from the top of the roof and shall be setback 15 feet perpendicular to the nearest parapet wall. Stair and elevator towers shall be exempt from this requirement only if they provide [roof access]."

equip.cite: Dumpster and mechanical equipment requirements in the OC District (Sec. 30-50.24(k), PDF p.789)
equip.text: "Any exterior garbage receptacles, dumpsters or mechanical equipment must be placed on a concrete slab, screened and landscaped from view of any right-of-way or a residential lot with 100 percent opaque material which is compatible with the front facade of [the building]... In addition, garbage receptacles and dumpsters must maintain a minimum of a five-foot setback from any property line, be located on private property and accessible for waste management service."

equip.cite: Aboveground propane tanks in the FT&I District (Sec. 30-50.18, PDF p.688)
equip.text: "Commercial trucks shall be stored or parked within an enclosed building or an area enclosed by a fence, wall or hedge, and out of the view from adjacent properties. Aboveground propane and chlorine storage tanks shall be prohibited."

equip.cite: Shading of A/C units (Sec. 30-50.23.6-01, PDF p.766)
equip.text: "Trees shall be planted to provide shade to residences to maximize energy conservation. All exterior ground story air conditioning units shall be shaded by trees and/or shrubs." Chapter 30 landscaping: "All exterior air conditioning units, except for air conditioning units placed on the roof, shall be shaded by trees and/or shrubs as referenced in the landscape manual."

equip.cite: Pergolas, trellises and similar structures in required setbacks (Sec. 30-60.3(g))
equip.text: "Pergolas, trellises, and other similar structures may be sited within the required setbacks of a principal building provided: (1) The structure is located within a R-1, R-1M, E-M, E-S, E-1, E-1C, E-2, R-2, or R-TH district; (2) The encroachment does not exceed 20 feet of the required principal building setback; (3) That at no time the structure is closer than five feet to any property line, with the exception of R-1, R-1M, R2, and R-TH, which shall permit a minimum setback of three feet from an interior property line; (4) The structure cannot exceed 400 square feet in total area; (5) The maximum height cannot exceed 12 feet as measured from grade to its highest point of the structure; (6) The structure shall be open on all four sides, with no one supporting column wider than six inches; (7) Only one such structure is permitted to encroach into a required principal building setback; and (8) The structure shall be open from floor to sky."

equip.cite: Steady mechanical noise (Sec. 30-60.29, PDF p.832 and p.836)
equip.text: "...whine, hum or buzz. The measured sound levels of such a source must not fluctuate by more than plus or minus three dB. Such sound sources include, but are not limited to, heating, ventilating or air-conditioning units, refrigeration units and transformers." And: "Fans and air conditioners. It shall be deemed unlawful to create any excessive loud noise by the use or operation of any noise-creating air conditioner, compressor unit, power fan or blower or the electric motor or any engine used to drive such device, the operation of which causes the sound level to exceed [the applicable limit]."

AG.note: Agricultural District, Sec. 30-50.2. Minimum lot area printed as 'Five acres in area including ROW'; converted 5 x 43,560 = 217,800 s.f. Maximum density one unit per five acres including ROW. Minimum lot depth 330 feet from centre line of ROW. Maximum lot coverage 0.16 of lot including all buildings. Minimum open space 0.84 of lot area. Minimum landscaped pervious area 0.30.

R-1.frontNote: Setback table, principal structure: 'Front - 15 feet for 0.50 of the house width; 25 feet for balance of house width; except 20 feet for attached garage.' Not a single number.
R-1.rearNote: Setback table, principal structure: 'Rear - 15 feet for 0.50 of the house width; 25 feet for balance of house width.' Not a single number.
R-1.heightNote: Maximum building height 35 feet; maximum number of stories two. Accessory building height not exceeding 15 feet above grade to the roof ridge.
R-1.note: Single-Family Residential District, Sec. 30-50.3. Maximum density one unit per 7,500 net square feet. Minimum lot depth 100 feet. Maximum lot coverage 0.37 of net lot area including accessory buildings. Minimum open space 0.63 of net lot area. Minimum landscaped pervious area 0.30 of the lot area. Minimum building size 1,125 square feet. Side street setback 15.

R-1M.frontNote: Setback table, principal structure: 'Front - 15 feet for 0.50 of the house width; 25 feet for balance of house width; except 20 feet for attached garage.'
R-1M.rearNote: Setback table, principal structure: 'Rear - 15 feet for 0.50 of the house width; 25 feet for balance of house width.'
R-1M.note: Modified Single-Family District, Sec. 30-50.35. Maximum density one unit per 5,000 net square feet. Minimum lot depth 100 feet. Maximum lot coverage 0.42 of net lot area including accessory buildings. Minimum open space 0.58 of net lot area. Minimum landscaped pervious area 0.30. Minimum building size 1,000 square feet. Maximum number of stories two, not including non-livable areas.

E-M.note: Estate Modified Single-Family District, Sec. 30-50.4. Maximum density one unit per 15,000 net square feet. Minimum lot depth 115 feet. Maximum lot coverage 0.32 net lot area including accessory buildings. Minimum open space 0.68 of net lot area. Minimum landscaped pervious area 0.35 of lot area. Minimum building size 1,500 square feet. Maximum number of stories two.

E-S.note: Estate Suburban Single-Family District, Sec. 30-50.5. Minimum lot area 25,000 square feet including ROW; maximum density one unit per 25,000 square feet including ROW. Minimum lot depth 135 feet. Maximum lot coverage 0.32 including accessory building. Minimum open space 0.68 of lot area. Minimum landscaped pervious area 0.35 of lot area. Minimum building size 2,000 square feet. Maximum number of stories two.

E-1.note: One Acre Estate Single-Family District, Sec. 30-50.6. Minimum lot area 'One acre including ROW'; converted 1 x 43,560 = 43,560 s.f. Maximum density one unit including ROW. Minimum lot depth 200 feet from centre line of ROW. Maximum lot coverage is conditional and so is not recorded: '0.17 of lot area including accessory buildings, or 0.22 if all construction on the property is limited to one story'.

E-1C.note: 2.5 Acres Estate Single-Family District, Sec. 30-50.7. Minimum lot area '2.5 acres including ROW'; converted 2.5 x 43,560 = 108,900 s.f. Minimum lot depth 250 feet from centre line of ROW. Maximum lot coverage.16 of lot area including accessory buildings. Minimum open space.84 of lot area. Minimum landscaped pervious area.55 of lot area. Minimum building size 3,000 square feet. Maximum number of stories two.

Minimum lot depth 330 feet from centre line of the ROW. Maximum lot coverage 0.16 including accessory buildings. Minimum open space 0.84 of lot area. Minimum landscaped pervious area 0.55 of the lot area. Minimum building size 3,000 square feet. Maximum number of stories two.

R-2.sideNote: Setback table, duplex (one structure, two units): interior side '10% of the lot width, 5 feet minimum, 7.5 feet maximum'. Side street '10 feet to property line; 15 feet to pavement'.
R-2.note: Two-Family Residential District, Sec. 30-50.9. Minimum lot area '3,750, each net lot area'. Maximum density two units. Minimum lot frontage each lot min. 37.5 feet, with a 25-foot front setback line. Minimum lot depth 100 feet. Maximum lot coverage 0.30 including accessory buildings. Minimum open space 0.70 of net lot area. Minimum landscaped pervious area 0.30 of lot area. Minimum building size 1,125 square feet.

R-TH.frontNote: Note i to the setback table: 'There shall be a 15-foot minimum distance from the nearest edge of roadway pavement to the front building line.
R-TH.sideNote: Note iii: 'There shall be a 15-foot minimum provided between the end of a group of townhouses to a public or private street pavement, eight feet of which shall be unencumbered by walls, fences or other structures or buildings.' R-TH.rearNote: Note ii: 'There shall be a ten-foot minimum rear building setback. A minimum greenbelt of ten feet shall be provided between rear lot lines; provided, however, that rear lot lines may abut without a greenbelt if a rear building setback of 15 feet is provided.'
R-TH.note: Townhouse District, Sec. 30-50.10. Minimum development site one net acre. Minimum lot area for each unit 1,250 net square feet; minimum average lot area for a group 1,500 net square feet. Minimum unit size 600 net square feet; minimum average unit size for a group 800 net square feet. Maximum grouping length 240 feet. Maximum density 8.5 units per net acre. Common open space 0.30 of net lot area.

R-3M.heightNote: Sec. 30-50.12(a)(2)d: 'Building or structure or part thereof shall be erected or altered to a height of two stories and shall not exceed 35 feet.'
R-3M.note: Apartment District, Sec. 30-50.12. Minimum lot width/frontage 100 feet, minimum lot area 16,884 square feet. Maximum area covered by all buildings 30 percent of the lot. Side street setback 25. Minimum setback between buildings 20 feet, except 30 feet where doors, windows or other openings face a wall. Floor area ratio: 1-story 0.30, 2-story 0.50. Maximum 13 dwelling units per net acre.

R-4L.sideNote: Sec. 30-50.13(a)(1)c.ii: 'Minimum setback from interior side property line shall be 15 feet for structures of not more than two stories and 20 feet for structures over two stories.' The setback table prints '15 feet for up to two stories; 20 feet for between three to six stories.'

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - Sec. 64-50(c) (verbatim)
gen.text: 'Permanent generators shall not be placed in the required front, street side or street rear yard setbacks. Permanent generators shall meet or exceed the setbacks required for accessory structures as set forth in the town's Land Development Code. In cases where the accessory setback cannot be reasonably achieved, one permanent generator shall be allowed in a required side or rear yard provided it is set back a minimum of five feet from the property line. Additionally, permanent generators shall be placed a minimum of five feet from all windows and doors, and from any neighboring houses. The following criteria will apply to the location of all permanent generators: (1) These distances are to be measured from the actual generator and exclude the generator's enclosure. (2) Permanent generators are to be installed in a fashion where they are completely screened from the street and abutting neighbors. (3) Screening methods to be employed include, but are not limited to, the use of a concrete wall and a hedge around the perimeter of the permanent generator.'

equip.cite: A/C and pool equipment - Sec. 64-50(a) (verbatim)
equip.text: 'No part of an air conditioning unit, swimming pool maintenance unit and the like, or any equipment or apparatus related thereto, shall be exposed or visible from the front of the primary building structure or be placed within the front yard setback. For purposes of this section, front yard shall be defined as in section 64-1(d), and shall not include canal frontages. No part of an air conditioning unit, swimming pool maintenance unit and the like, or any equipment or apparatus related thereto, may be placed within ten feet of the side or rear lot line of any lot. Customary yard accessories and ornaments and furniture shall be an exception to this section. Any rooftop mechanical equipment shall be screened on all sides from view from off-site properties. The screening of the rooftop equipment shall, at a minimum, equal the height of the proposed equipment. Mechanical equipment shall not be placed on a flat roof permitted for a residential single-family dwelling or an accessory building to a single-family residential dwelling unless specifically authorized in section 67-37. Existing permitted rooftop equipment shall not extend more than 30 inches above the flat roof surface, however, exact change out equipment permit applications are exempt from this provision as determined by the building official.'

equip.cite: Accessory uses, buildings and structures - Sec. 64-41(b)
equip.text: '(1) Location. All accessory uses, buildings and structures shall be located on the same lot as the principal or main use and not within any required yard setbacks, except as provided in this land development code... (2) Height. No accessory use, building or structure shall exceed the height permitted for a one story structure. (3) Use. Such accessory building shall not be rented or otherwise used as a separate dwelling unit.' Sec. 64-41(c): 'Only one utility shed/storage building shall be allowed per lot... No utility sheds/storage building shall be allowed in any setbacks, drainage detention areas, easement areas or front yard area, unless as set forth below' (prefabricated sheds not exceeding 100 sq ft or seven feet in height are treated separately).

equip.cite: Yard projections - Sec. 64-52(b)(1)
equip.text: 'Projections. The roof overhang may project onto the required yard area (set back area) no more than three feet. This provision shall not apply to any other projection or overhang into the required yard area.' Separately, in the RSF and RSE blocks: 'Exterior balconies, bay windows, exterior chimneys, or other architectural features which do not measure more than 25 square feet in the horizontal plane, and eaves which do not extend more than three feet from the vertical wall of the building shall not be considered as encroachments in the setback.'

equip.cite: Height exceptions - Sec. 64-52(a)
equip.text: 'The height limitations stipulated in the zoning districts described in this land development code apply to all structures and appurtenances thereto. The following may be considered by application as special exceptions to the height requirements: (1) Church spires. (2) Church belfries. (3) Monuments. (4) Water towers. (5) Air conditioning cooling towers. (6) Elevator bulkheads. (7) Flagpoles. (8) Antennas, when attached to the primary structure.'

equip.cite: Underground utility service lines - Sec. 64-58
equip.text: 'At the time that any new buildings and/or structures are being constructed or located on any privately owned proper[ty]...' - utility service lines are required to be placed underground (Sec. 64-58).

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment placement - commercial and industrial abutting residential
equip.text: Printed twice, identically, in Chapter 107 - Supplemental Use Regulations, at 107-41.5 Mechanical Equipment and again at 107-42.1 Mechanical equipment: 'On property zoned for or used for commercial or industrial purposes, no mechanical equipment (air conditioners, exhaust fans, mechanical pumps, etc.) shall be placed within required setbacks when such setback area abuts residentially zoned or used property. Additionally, if mechanical equipment is placed outside the setback and within the buildable area of the lot abutting a residentially used or zoned property, such mechanical equipment, if not screened from such abutting property by a building or other solid barrier, shall be screened by a solid barrier approved by the zoning administrator.' This is a prohibition on placing equipment in the required setback in that situation, not a distance of its own. It is written for commercial and industrial property only; it does not reach a generator at a single-family house.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening - applicability
equip.text: Chapter 105, 105-25.5.3.1 Applicability: 'The standards of this section shall apply to all of the following: (a) Electrical and gas-powered mechanical equipment. (b) Ductwork and major plumbing lines used to heat, cool, or ventilate. (c) Power systems for the building or site upon which the equipment is located. (d) Roof and/or wall-mounted antennas and vent openings shall not be considered mechanical equipment for purposes of these mechanical equipment screening standards. The standards of this section are not intended to impede systems that use solar or wind energy to reduce the costs of energy, if such systems are otherwise in compliance with applicable building codes and zoning requirements.' A standby generator is a 'power system for the building or site' and so falls inside (c).

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening - ground-mounted
equip.text: 105-25.5.3.2, opening: 'For all developments other than single-family residential, the following mechanical equipment screening standards shall apply to the maximum practical extent.' Paragraph (c): 'Ground-Mounted Mechanical Equipment - Ground-mounted mechanical equipment shall be screened from view by landscaping or by a decorative wall that is compatible with the architecture and landscaping of the development site. The wall shall be of a height equal to or greater than the height of the mechanical equipment being screened. 1. Ground mounted mechanical equipment is prohibited in the front yard.' The front-yard prohibition is the strongest placement rule in the Dunedin code for a generator pad, and by the section's own opening words it does not apply to single-family residential development.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening - roof and wall mounted
equip.text: 105-25.5.3.2(a): 'Roof-mounted mechanical equipment shall be screened by a parapet wall or similar feature that is an integral part of the building's architectural design. The parapet wall or similar feature shall be of a height equal to or greater than the height of the mechanical equipment being screened. Roof-mounted mechanical equipment is prohibited on single-family residential dwellings.' 105-25.5.3.2(b): 'Wall-mounted mechanical equipment that protrudes more than six inches from the outer building wall shall be screened from view by structural features that are compatible with the architecture of the subject building. Wall-mounted mechanical equipment that protrudes six inches or less from the outer building wall shall be designed to blend with the color and architectural design of the subject building.'

equip.cite: Screening in the street yard
equip.text: 105-25.5 Screening: 'Off-street loading spaces, refuse and outdoor storage areas, antennas, satellite dishes, and mechanical equipment within the street yard shall be screened from all public streets.'

equip.cite: Permitted setback encroachments - what the table does and does not list
equip.text: Chapter 103 Division 5 (103-50, 103-50.1) establishes an encroachment table (printed with the heading 'Table 103-40.1' at CD103:98-99 but referred to in the text as Table 103-50.1). It lists, by structure and by yard (F front, S side, SF secondary front, R rear, W waterfront): arbors, awnings, balconies, masonry barbeques, bay windows, detached carports, attached chimneys, uncovered decks, eaves, fences, wall-mounted flags, outdoor fire pits and fireplaces, detached garages, gazebos, outdoor kitchens, uncovered and covered patios, above-ground and in-ground pools, open porches, disability access ramps, screen enclosures, detached sheds, spas, steps and stairs, stoops, and tiki huts. It does not list a generator, an air conditioning condenser, a heat pump, a pool pump or an LP tank. The nearest analogues it does print: 'Fire pits, Outdoor Fireplaces, Fire Rings, Chimney (detached) - S, R, W - No closer to property line or seawall than 10 ft. Must be located not less than 10 feet from any structure, accessory structure or fence.' and 'Pool, Above Ground - S, SF, R - No closer to property line than 5'; W - No closer to property line or seawall than 8''. 103-50.2 Restrictions: 'When a variance to a setback has been granted, no additional encroachment as set forth in this section is permitted. No structure shall encroach in or over any easement where the structure would interfere with the use of the easement for its intended purpose, as determined by the Engineering Department. Encroachments for a structure or other improvement taller than twelve (12) inches above grade is prohibited within the view triangles of waterfront yards, except fences which are subject to height limitations as established in Chapter 105, Development Standards.'

equip.cite: Accessory structures and uses
equip.text: Chapter 107, 107-20: 'The regulations of this section apply to any subordinate use of a building or other structure, or use of land that is conducted on the same lot and under the same ownership as the principal use or structure.' 107-20.1: '(A) Accessory structures or uses may be constructed concurrently with, and not before the principal use is established. (B) Accessory structures or uses shall not be established on a vacant lot. (C) Accessory structures shall not be used for dwelling purposes except where permitted in Land Development Code Use Matrix Table 103-60.1.' 107-20.2 Dimensional and Density Standards: 'A See Chapter 103 - Zoning'. 107-20.3 Height: 'Accessory structures or uses shall not exceed: A The height regulations of the applicable zoning district when constructed in adherence to principal structure setbacks; or B The height of an accessory structure shall not exceed the height of the principal structure unless it is necessary for the normal operation of the accessory structure. C See also maximum heights in Table 103-50.1.' Accessory structures therefore take the principal structure's setbacks unless the encroachment table gives them relief, and the encroachment table does not name mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: Height exemption for roof equipment
equip.text: 103-40.11 Modification of Maximum Height: 'The following portions of structures may exceed the height requirements by a maximum of 20 percent of the permitted height as set forth in § 103-40.2 Maximum Height without additional setback, but with the written permission of the zoning administrator, or designee: (A) Belfries and spires. (B) Chimneys and smoke stacks. (C) Cooling towers, water towers and tanks, and fire towers. (D) Elevator and/or stairwell bulkheads. (E) Flagpoles, ornamental towers, statuary, and monuments. (F) Radio, television, and telephone transmission towers. (G) Solar panels. (H) Wind turbines. (I) Architectural features designed to add quality to the design.'

equip.cite: Noise-generating equipment
equip.text: In the industrial and commercial development standards: 'Noise generating mechanical equipment shall be enclosed or soundproofed if necessary to meet or exceed the noise regulations of the city and the county.' 107-42.2 Vibration: 'No use or structure shall be so operated that ground vibration inherently and recurrently generated shall be noticeable to the building official at the lot line of the premises.'
