equip.cite: No generator, A/C, pool-equipment or LP-tank placement rule
equip.text: Washington County's Land Development Code contains NO provision on where a standby generator, an air-conditioning condenser, a pool pump or an LP/propane tank may sit relative to a lot line. The only hits were: an air-conditioning contractor licensing definition (Ch. 18 of the Code of Ordinances); 'air conditioning units' cited as an example of machinery in the noise ordinance definition of 'machinery' (Ch. 30); mechanical equipment named as a kind of litter (Ch. 26 and Ch. 66); hazardous-waste generator classifications; trip generation rates in the road impact fee chapter; and flood-ordinance rules for above-ground tanks (see the flood entry below). None of these sets a setback.

equip.cite: Accessory structures -- the rule that governs a generator pad (§ 2.04.03)
equip.text: 'Barns, pole barns, pool and bath houses, sheds, shops and workshops, and storage buildings, as well as utility buildings, greenhouses, and attached and detached carports and garages. A. Storage buildings, shops, utility buildings, greenhouses, garages, carports, and other accessory structures setbacks shall be established in Table 2.02.06 and shall be determined by the Future Land Use Map category of the property. Accessory structures shall not be located closer than ten (10) feet from any structure. B. Motor vehicles, manufactured homes, mobile homes, trailers, or recreational vehicles shall not be used as storage buildings, utility buildings, or other like uses. C. Building permits are not required for non-residential buildings used for agricultural purposes on bona-fide agricultural properties per F.S. Sec. 604.50(1).' Restated at § 5.01.01.A.5: 'All accessory structures shall meet the setback requirements established in Table 2.02.06, Land Development Code.' In other words, an accessory structure gets the SAME front/side/rear setback as a principal building -- there is no reduced accessory setback in this code.

equip.cite: Separation between structures (§ 2.02.07)
equip.text: 'In addition to the setbacks outlined in Table 2.02.06, and the natural resources setbacks included in Chapter 4, the following setbacks will apply: 1. A minimum ten-foot setback shall be required between buildings and structures.'

equip.cite: Swimming pools (§ 2.04.04)
equip.text: 'A. Swimming pool setbacks shall be established in Table 2.02.06 and shall be determined by the Future Land Use Map category of the property. B. Setbacks for a swimming pool shall be measured from the water's edge. C. Swimming pools shall not be located closer than ten (10) feet from any structure.'

equip.cite: Above-ground tanks in flood hazard areas (Appendix A, Floodplain Management Ordinance, § 306.2)
equip.text: 'Above-ground tanks that do not meet the elevation requirements of Section 306.3 of this ordinance shall be permitted in flood hazard areas provided the tanks are anchored or otherwise designed and constructed to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions of the design flood, including the effects of buoyancy assuming the tank is empty.' This is an anchoring rule, not a setback.

equip.cite: Resource-protection setbacks that can control a pad location (Article IV)
equip.text: § 4.04.02.A: 'No development (other than boardwalks, docks, or other shoreline access structures) shall be located within a minimum of thirty (30) feet of a wetland, as measured landward from the upland edge of the wetland.' § 4.04.02.B: 'A minimum fifty-foot development setback is required from the ordinary mean high-water line of all surface water bodies, excluding the Choctawhatchee River, Econfina Creek, Holmes Creek, and Pine Log Creek, which shall require a one-hundred-foot development setback.' § 4.02: 'A setback of five hundred (500) feet shall be required for all development abutting or within five hundred (500) feet of a public water supply well.' § 4.03.02: a minimum 100-foot permanent natural vegetative buffer adjacent to Pine Log State Forest, Falling Waters State Recreational Area, Choctawhatchee Water Management Area, Holmes Creek State Canoe Trail and Econfina State Canoe Trail. Table 4.03 setbacks from specified features: 1st and 2nd magnitude springs 500 ft; 3rd and smaller magnitude springs 500 ft; spring runs 100 ft; sinkholes 100 ft; steephead ravines 100 ft; caves 300 ft; swallets 100 ft.

tamarac.source: Code of Ordinances Chapter 10, Land Development Code, Article 2 (Zoning Districts): Table 10-2.2 Dimensional Standards for Residential Districts; Table 10-2.3 D

gen.cite: Mechanical equipment - Sec. 10-2.6(C)(6)(b)(ix)
gen.text: "(ix) Mechanical Equipment. A/C units, swimming pool equipment, irrigation pumps, propane tank generators, and backflow devices shall be prohibited in the front yard, and shall comply with the setback provisions in Article 2: Zoning Districts.". This is the operative rule: the equipment gets no projection allowance, is barred from the front yard, and must meet the full district setback.

gen.cite: Screening of accessory structures - Sec. 10-4.4(M)(1)
gen.text: "(1) Accessory Structures. Generators, air conditioning units, bottled gas tanks, irrigation pumps, swimming pool pumps and heaters, garbage containers at ground level, utility boxes, and similar accessory structures shall be screened with shrubs or an opaque fence on all applicable sides. Shrubs planted for this purpose shall be in addition to the requirements in Table 10-4.6 above. A hedge, berm, wood fence, or wall, maintained at a minimum of six inches above the items to be screened, may be used to satisfy the screening requirements as approved by the Director."

gen.cite: Generator noise (community gardens / urban agriculture) - Sec. 10-3.3
gen.text: "(d) Operation of power equipment or generators shall not occur between the hours of 10:00 P.M. and 7:00 A.M."

gen.cite: Generators serving wireless communication facilities - Sec. 10-3.3
gen.text: "No generators utilized in connection with WCFs may be placed in the public rights-of-way, except temporarily in the case of emergency and if approved in advance by the City Engineer."

gen.cite: Temporary generator during emergency housing - Sec. 5-401
gen.text: "d. Electrical service to a commercial source (FPL) must be established. If there is no power available from FPL, the use of a generator will be allowed until power is restored. The use of the generator shall be suspended within seven (7) days of power restoration."

equip.cite: Allowed projections into required setbacks - Sec. 10-2.6(C)(6)
equip.text: "Setbacks shall be unoccupied and unobstructed by any structure or portion of a structure from 30 inches above grade upward, except that certain structures may project into required front, side, or rear setbacks as specified in this subsection." The listed exceptions are unroofed patios and terraces (at least five feet from the lot line), unroofed landings/decks/stairs/balconies, incidental architectural features (not more than three feet), pergolas and trellises (five feet from all side and rear lot lines, prohibited in the front yard), handicap ramps, swimming pools (setbacks measured five feet from the edge of the pool), fences/walls/hedges, freestanding ornamental features, and mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: Projections into easements and rights of way - Sec. 10-2.6(C)(7)
equip.text: "Projections shall not extend or encroach into any easement(s) or right(s)-of-way."

equip.cite: Accessory structures location - Sec. 10-3.4(C)(3)
equip.text: "The accessory use shall be conducted and/or located on the same lot(s) as the principal use and to the rear of the front setback line, unless otherwise approved by the Director. No accessory structure shall be located within ten feet of the site's principal structure. When located to the rear of the primary structure, accessory buildings need not comply with the side or rear setback lines applicable to the primary structure provided that the accessory building is not located closer than ten feet from any alley and not closer than five feet from any property line."

equip.cite: Walkways and driveways - Sec. 10-2.6(C)(5)
equip.text: "Whenever a walkway or driveway is to be located on a lot, it shall be a minimum of three feet from the rear and side property line, except for double-frontage lots."

equip.cite: Air conditioning, mechanical and maintenance equipment - Sec. 9-130(e)(7) (property maintenance, all residential property)
equip.text: "(7) Air conditioning, mechanical and maintenance equipment placed in any front, side or rear yard shall be screened or walled in so as not to be visible from the public rights-of-way and shall not be placed on the roof of any building or structure unless such air conditioning or mechanical equipment is completely screened or walled in so as not to be visible from the public rights-of-way or adjoining properties." The same subsection adds: "(6) All gas and oil tanks must be placed and maintained below ground level or in walled-in areas so as not to be visible from adjacent properties."

equip.cite: Air conditioning or other mechanical equipment - Woodlands Overlay, Sec. 10-2.7(C)(4)(g)
equip.text: "(g) Air conditioning or other mechanical equipment placed in any front, side or rear yard shall be screened or walled in so as not to be visible from the public rights-of-way and shall not be placed on the roof of any building or structure unless such air conditioning or mechanical equipment is completely screened or walled in so as not to be visible from the public rights-of-way or adjoining properties." Subsection (f): "All gas and oil tanks must be placed and maintained below ground level or in walled-in areas so as not to be visible from adjacent properties."

equip.cite: Roof-mounted A/C and accessory equipment - Sec. 5-33 (Chapter 5, Buildings)
equip.text: "(a) The height of exterior walls of all buildings in all zoning districts except R-1, R-1B, R-1C and R-2 shall be higher than the total height of all accessory equipment installed on the roof of the proposed building other than that which is wind-driven. (b) All air-conditioning units, condensers and/or electrical fans attendant thereto, except those that are wind-driven, shall be prohibited from being installed on residential and accessory roof areas, in R-1, R-1B, R-1C and R-2 zoning districts unless the same meets the following requirements: (1) The proposed air-conditioning unit shall be placed on a structural element meeting the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Broward County Amendments... (3) Permanent, obscure screen shall be placed along all sides of the unit which is viewed by the public, the minimum height of which shall be one (1) foot above the top of the unit." NOTE: R-1B and R-1C are districts of the repealed Chapter 24; the cross-reference in this section is to '§ 24-101 et seq.'

equip.cite: Utility sheds - Sec. 5-32(a)
equip.text: "Utility sheds may be permitted providing that they meet the standards set forth in chapter 23 of the Broward Edition of the South Florida Code and provided that such utility shed is not placed in any required setback. A building permit shall be required in any residential district of the city."

palm_beach_county.source: Unified Land Development Code (ULDC), Art. 3, Overlays and Zoning Districts. Primary table: Table 3.D.1.A, Property Development Regulations (Art. 3.D.1.A), whic

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.1)d), Location and Setbacks, PDF p.940
gen.text: 'Generators shall meet the district setback requirements for principal structures, but shall not be located between the front or side street facade of a building and a R-O-W or in an easement, unless: (1) Encroachment is limited to ten percent of setback; (2) Where applicable, the Applicant indicates that an HOA has been notified of the application for Building Permit; (3) The generator shall be screened from view from any public rights-of-way or adjacent property lines by an opaque fence/wall; and, (4) If this criteria cannot be met, the Applicant may apply for a Type 1 Variance, pursuant to Art. 2.C.5.F.' THIS IS THE GOVERNING RULE FOR A STANDBY GENERATOR PAD IN PALM BEACH COUNTY.

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - residential setback exception, Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.2)b), PDF p.941
gen.text: 'Generators less than five feet in height measured from the top of the supporting platform may be allowed within the required side and rear setbacks. The generator rear and side setbacks shall be a minimum of five feet. For SFDs and residential uses within a SFD, the generator side setback shall be a minimum of three feet, and rear setback shall be a minimum of five feet.' Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.2a, Number: 'A maximum of one generator shall be allowed on a lot with a single dwelling unit. A maximum of one generator per structure shall be permitted for Multifamily developments, with exception to condominiums, which shall be permitted one generator per unit.' Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.4, Non-Residential: 'There is no limitation to the number of generators.'

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - screening, sound and exercise, Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.1), PDF p.940
gen.text: a Maximum Permissible Sound Level: refer to Art. 5.E.4.B.2 and Table 5.E.4.B, Maximum Sound Levels. b Screening: 'Generators that are not located within, or completely screened by a building, shall be screened from view when adjacent to or visible from a public R-O-W or parcels with a conservation or residential FLU designation or use. Screening may include the use of fences, walls or hedges, or a combination thereof.' c Maintenance Cycle: 'Generators may be operated for exercising purposes one time per week, excluding Sundays, for a period not exceeding 30 minutes between the hours of 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.'

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - when one is required, Art. 5.B.1.A.19.a, PDF p.939-940
gen.text: 'Use of permanent generators shall be permitted during periods of electrical power outages in utility systems maintained by the utility service provider or when the BCC declares a State of Emergency.' 'A permanent emergency generator or alternative power source shall be required for all assisted living facilities, excluding personal residences (owner occupied) used as an assisted living facility for five or fewer residents, nursing homes, intermediate care facilities for people with developmental disabilities, or transitional living facilities for brain and spinal cord injury patients, pursuant to F.S. 400.492 and Rule 59A-8.027, F.A.C., and PDD or TDD clubhouses 20,000 square feet, or greater.' Exemptions: developments with a BCC or DRO-approved plan graphically indicating a clubhouse, except projects exceeding 75 percent or more of the Improvement Value; renovations or additions not exceeding 75 percent of Improvement Value; a PDD or TDD clubhouse in the Coastal High Hazard Area; and a PDD or TDD that already has one compliant clubhouse generator. Required capacity (Art. 5.B.1.A.19.b.3): essential electrical systems, lighting for a minimum of 30 percent of GFA, air conditioning for 30 percent of GFA including the largest meeting room, and fuel storage sufficient to operate the generator for a minimum of 72 hours at full load capacity.

gen.cite: PERMANENT GENERATORS - Type 1 Waiver in a PIPD Industrial Pod, Table 3.B.4.F, PDF p.342
gen.text: 'Art. 5.B.1.A.19, Permanent Generators - Permanent generators may be allowed within required side or rear building setbacks' - criteria: 'When all parcels adjacent to the generator location are within an Industrial Pod of the PIPD.' The same table also waives the ground-mounted mechanical equipment screening requirement of Art. 5.B.1.A.20.a.2a in that circumstance.

gen.cite: HVAC units permitted in setbacks - Art. 3.D.1.D.5.a.11), PDF p.473
gen.text: The list of 'Structures, Projections, and Improvements Permitted in Setbacks' includes, at item 11, 'Heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning units (including compressors and condensers)'. NO distance is attached to this item - it is an unqualified permission to place an HVAC unit within a required setback. Related items on the same list: item 23 'Utility transmission lines and associated structures'; item 22 'Wells'; item 28 'Fire hydrants and other government service/utility structures required to be in certain locations by applicable Codes and Ordinances'; item 16 'Roof overhangs projecting into the required setback a maximum of two and one-half feet'; item 3 'Permanent/retractable awnings, canopies, or Bahama shutters projecting a maximum of three feet into a setback'; item 15 'Recreational equipment and structures in the rear setback of residential districts'; item 24 'Basketball goals, provided there is a minimum three-foot setback from the rear and side property lines and a minimum 15-foot setback from the front and side street property lines'. Note the contrast: HVAC is on this list, generators are NOT - generators are governed separately by Art. 5.B.1.A.19 and must meet the principal-structure setback except as that section allows.

gen.cite: Definition of Fixed Mechanical Equipment - Art. 1.H, PDF p.89
gen.text: 'Fixed Mechanical Equipment - mechanical equipment, such as an air-conditioning unit, water-cooling tower, swimming pool pump, irrigation pump, well water pump, fan, POWER GENERATOR, or other similar power source equipment, permanently affixed to land or structure, as distinguished from temporary, portable, non-fixed mechanical equipment.' This definition is what brings a standby generator inside the Art. 5.E.4.B sound-level standards.

equip.cite: MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT - Art. 5.B.1.A.20, PDF p.942
equip.text: a.1a Setback Exceptions: 'Setback exceptions shall be applied pursuant to Art. 3.D.1.D.5, Setback Exceptions.' b Height Exceptions: 'Height exceptions shall be applied pursuant to Art. 3.D.1.E.4, Height Exceptions.' 2 Screening Requirements: 'New and replacement equipment shall be screened on all sides by an opaque barrier constructed of materials, and color compatible with the building or structure, or equivalent landscaping for ground-mounted equipment, to a minimum height equal to the highest point of the equipment.' Roof-mounted screening exemptions: equipment less than one foot in height measured from the roof deck and painted to match; any industrial use with an industrial FLU designation adjacent to a parcel with an industrial use and industrial FLU designation; where a certified letter from a Florida-registered structural Engineer or Architect shows the roof cannot support the screening weight; or any industrial use with an industrial FLU designation where a Line of Sight Analysis shows the equipment cannot be viewed from the adjacent R-O-W.

equip.cite: FUEL, GAS, OR CHEMICAL STORAGE TANKS (LP/propane) - Art. 5.B.1.A.7, PDF p.920
equip.text: 'Above-ground accessory fuel, gas, or chemical storage tanks, three feet or greater in height shall be subject to the zoning district setbacks or the minimum setbacks required by the Florida Building and Fire Prevention Codes, whichever is greater, and screening. New and replacement storage tanks shall be screened from view if adjacent to a residential use or FLU designation and visible from an adjacent R-O-W. The screening shall consist of an opaque barrier or equivalent landscaping a minimum height equal to the highest point of the storage tanks.'

equip.cite: Accessory structures - general location rule, Art. 5.B.1.A.1.b, PDF p.903
equip.text: 'All accessory uses and structures except for approved off-site parking, shall be located on the same lot as the principal use. No accessory structure shall be located in the front or side street yard except for dumpsters, or unless stated otherwise herein.' General Exceptions (Art. 5.B.1.A.1.b.1) allow fences and walls, entry features for access ways internal to a PUD, bike racks, outdoor recreation amenities and support structures such as cabanas within a Neighborhood Recreation Facility or Recreation Pod, and the structures, projections and improvements listed in Art. 3.D.1.D.5 - but that exception EXPRESSLY EXCLUDES 'mechanical equipment accessory to a building' from being allowed within front or side street yards.

equip.cite: Accessory structure setbacks - Art. 5.B.1.A.1.d, PDF p.904-906
equip.text: Residential Districts: Accessory Living Quarters (Guest Cottages, Grooms Quarters, other Accessory Quarters) shall meet the minimum setback in Table 3.D.1.A, except properties with an RR FLU designation which are subject to a 25-foot side or rear setback. Townhouse: accessory structures shall meet Table 3.D.2.A, and no detached accessory building other than permitted fences or walls on any lot less than 30 feet wide. ZLL: accessory structures shall meet Table 3.D.2.B. Single Family and Multifamily in residential zoning districts and AR lots less than one acre: 'Accessory structures ten feet or less in height shall meet a minimum five-foot setback from the side and rear property lines. Accessory structures over ten feet in height shall meet the minimum setbacks in Table 3.D.1.A.' Within the AR district on lots one acre and greater: lots five acres or greater, minimum 25 feet; lots one acre or greater and less than five acres, minimum 15 feet. Accessory structures, excluding fences, shall be a minimum of five feet from all established drainage easements in AR districts. Accessory structures shall NOT be located within a required landscape buffer, or in an established easement unless exempted by Art. 5.F.2.A. Non-residential districts: accessory structures shall meet the Table 3.D.1.A setbacks. In the U/S Tier, all accessory structures on a parcel in a residential district shall not occupy more than 25 percent of the distance between property lines.

equip.cite: Setback reductions - Art. 3.D.1.D.4, PDF p.472
equip.text: 'No setback reduction shall be used in combination with any other setback reduction allowed by this Code.' a Open Space: in residential zoning districts in the U/S Tier, or the Residential Pod of an AGR-PUD, the rear and side setbacks along the length of a property line adjacent to dedicated open space defined by a minimum of 50 feet in width may be reduced by 25 percent. b Alleys: in commercial and industrial districts, the rear and side setbacks from an alley may be reduced by 50 percent. c Railroad R-O-W: in industrial districts, the setback from a railroad R-O-W may be reduced to the width of the required landscape buffer.

equip.cite: Dumpsters - Art. 5.B.1.A.8.c, PDF p.920
equip.text: 'Shall be set back a minimum of 25 feet from all property lines adjacent to residential zoning districts and uses. If adjacent to a non-residential zoning district or use, the landscape buffer width shall serve as the setback.' Storage areas shall have a minimum dimension of ten feet by ten feet and shall not encroach into easements, landscape buffers, or parking spaces.

equip.cite: Electric Transmission Substations - PDF p.777
equip.text: 'Buildings used for Electric Transmission Substations shall be set back a minimum of 50 feet from all property lines. Setbacks for mechanical equipment, related structures, and fencing shall be a minimum of 75 feet, or a minimum of 150 feet when adjacent to or visible from a street or parcels with a [residential FLU designation].'

gen.cite: Definition - 'Outdoor Mechanical Equipment, Residential' (Article 10, PDF p.531)
gen.text: "OUTDOOR MECHANICAL EQUIPMENT, RESIDENTIAL. Electric generators and accessories, utility meters, swimming pool heaters and pumps, and other similar features." This is the definition that brings a standby generator under the rules below.

gen.cite: Site plan exemption - Sec. 2.x Site Plan applicability (PDF p.77)
gen.text: The following development is exempt from site plan review: "3. Installation of generators or other mechanical equipment for operation of a permitted use on site."

equip.cite: Placement - Sec. 4.3.4(n), Outdoor Mechanical Equipment, Residential
equip.text: "Outdoor mechanical equipment shall be located to the rear or side of the principal building on the lot."

equip.cite: Encroachment - Table 10.2.4(a): Allowable Encroachments beyond Setbacks/Build-to Zones
equip.text: The rows 'Air conditioner compressor unit', 'Outdoor mechanical equipment, residential' and 'Solar energy collection facility, small scale' share one entry: "May be located beyond the setback in any side or rear yard, subject to the limitations in Sec. 4.3.4, Specific Standards for Accessory Uses and Structures." 'Accessory structures other than those listed above' read: "May be located beyond the setback in a side or rear yard, subject to the limitations in Sec. 4.3.3, Standards for All Accessory Uses and Structures."

equip.cite: Accessory-structure setbacks - Sec. 4.3.3(c)
equip.text: "Accessory uses and structures shall comply with the minimum yard requirements for the principal structures for which they are accessory in Article 3: Zone Districts, unless otherwise stated in this LDC, and except as follows: (1) On lots with one front yard: (A) Accessory uses and structures other than accessory dwellings such as cottage residences shall be located at least seven-and-one-half (7.5) feet from a rear property line. Cottage residences shall not be in a required rear yard. (B) No accessory uses and structures shall be in required front or side yards. (2) On lots with two (2) front yards (e.g. double frontage, through, or corner lots) in Residential zone districts: (A) Accessory structures may not be in either front yard but may be in one of the required side yards. (B) Any accessory use or structure shall be located at least seven-and-one-half (7.5) feet from any side yard property line." Sec. 4.3.3(b)(3)(C) adds that in Residential zone districts an accessory structure shall "Not be constructed closer to the lot line in a front yard than the principal building or structure to which the use is subordinate," and (b)(5) that it shall "Not intrude into the sight triangle along any street."

equip.cite: Air conditioner compressor - Sec. 4.3.4(a)(1)(A), Residential zone districts
equip.text: "For all residential uses in Residential zone districts, an air conditioner compressor placed in a required side or rear yard setback shall have its nearest point located no further than three (3) feet from the principal structure which it serves."

equip.cite: Air conditioner compressor replacement - Sec. 4.3.4(a)(1)(B)
equip.text: For nonresidential uses in Residential zone districts, where a compressor was in a required rear or side yard as of May 24, 2004, a replacement may be installed in the same location if it is less than five (5) tons and, outside Winfield Units 1 and 2, "replacement air conditioner compressors that are closer than five (5) feet from any side or rear property line or that are within the required side or rear yard and are higher than thirty (30) inches above ground level, shall be subject to the sound rating requirements in Table 4.3.4(a)(1)(B)." Table 4.3.4(a)(1)(B): 4 tons and below 80 decibels; between 4 and 5 tons 84 decibels, measured per AHRI Standard 270-2015.

equip.cite: Air conditioner compressor - Sec. 4.3.4(a)(2), Mixed-Use and Nonresidential districts
equip.text: "in all Mixed-Use and Nonresidential Districts, a new air conditioner compressor, chiller, and/or evaporator unit of an air handler system shall not be located in any required yard."

equip.cite: Pool equipment screening - Sec. 4.3.4 (swimming pools), PDF p.268
equip.text: "In Winfield Units 1 and 2 (single-family residential subdivisions) annexed by Ordinance No. 970, if the pool is located within any front or street side yard, the pool equipment shall be screened from view by landscaping, except if the screening would create a hazardous obstruction to visibility of vehicles or pedestrians."

equip.cite: Swimming pool - Table 10.2.4(a)
equip.text: "May be located beyond the setback, but neither the pool nor enclosure shall be less than five feet from a lot line."

equip.cite: Fence and wall heights around equipment - Table 5.8.4(a)
equip.text: Front yard in RSF-1, RSF-2, RSF-3, RSF-D, R-MF and MX districts 4 feet; front yard in WS, GAP, NC and PD districts 6 feet; side, street side or rear yard (all districts) 8 feet.

equip.cite: Yard and measurement of setbacks (Sec. 16-139(1)) - the operative rule
equip.text: "Every part of front, side, and rear yards shall be unoccupied and vacant from the ground upward, except for eaves, trees, shrubs, landscaping materials, driveways, sunken garbage collection containers, and in rear or side yards, accessory buildings as permitted by this chapter." Mechanical equipment is NOT on this list, so a ground-mounted generator is treated as an accessory structure and falls under Sec. 16-176.

equip.cite: Yard projections (Sec. 16-139(3))
equip.text: "Open or enclosed fire escapes, outside stairways and balconies projecting into a minimum yard or court, and the projection of chimneys and flues are permitted into yard areas, but not to exceed 32 inches."

equip.cite: Accessory structure placement (Sec. 16-176(b)(3))
equip.text: "For residential lots less than two acres, no detached accessory structure shall be located in any required front yard area. Detached accessory structures may be located in the required rear or side yards. For residential lots exceeding two acres, detached accessory structures may be located in the front yard, rear yard, or side yard. On a corner lot, no accessory structure shall be located closer to the side street right-of-way line than the principal structure."

equip.cite: Accessory structure separation and non-residential limits (Sec. 16-176(c)(1))
equip.text: "A detached accessory structure shall not be closer than four feet to the principal building, or closer than five feet to any other accessory building on the same lot. Within nonresidential districts, accessory structures, except for carports, are prohibited within the side and rear yards of lots adjacent to a neighborhood district."

equip.cite: Accessory structure size and height (Sec. 16-176(c)(2)-(3))
equip.text: "Any number of accessory structures are permitted provided that the maximum lot coverage of all accessory structures shall not exceed 50 percent of the total area of the required yards. The total floor area of all accessory structures may not exceed a maximum of 2,500 square feet." "Accessory structures shall not exceed height requirements of the respective zoning district. For residential zoning districts, accessory structures may not exceed 25 feet in height." Table 16-176.1 lists the permitted accessory structures; mechanical equipment is not among them, but the table ends with "Any other building or use that the development director determines is customarily incidental to the permitted principal use or principal building - All zoning districts", and Sec. 16-176(e) allows the development director to determine other accessory uses by interpretation.

equip.cite: Height exceptions (Sec. 16-137(a))
equip.text: "Any chimney, water, fire, radio and television tower, church spire, dome, cupola, cooling tower, elevator bulkhead, smoke stack, flagpole, parapet wall and similar structures and their necessary mechanical appurtenances must have approval of the town council to be located above the height limits herein established; however the heights of these structures or appurtenances thereto shall not exceed the height limitations set forth by FAA regulations affecting the height."

equip.cite: Generators and noise (Sec. 20-65)
equip.text: The noise ordinance's list of exempt sounds includes "(9) Generators used during or as a result of an emergency." A generator run outside an emergency (e.g. a weekly exercise cycle) is not exempted by that clause.

equip.cite: Air conditioning condensate (sewer use ordinance)
equip.text: "Also prohibited are the following: connection of down spouts or air conditioning condensate lines into the sewer system."

equip.cite: Antenna support equipment (wireless telecommunications section)
equip.text: "Stealth design means a method that would hide or conceal an antenna, supporting electrical or mechanical equipment, or any other support structure that is identical to, or closely compatible with, the color to the supporting structure so as to make the antenna and related equipment as visually unobtrusive as possible." Applies to tower/antenna equipment only.

Where not specified in the PUD, the applicable standards of this Code shall apply. Standards that may be varied shall include the following: (1) Setbacks. (2) Lot coverage. (3) Height." Sec.

gen.cite: Generators and associated above ground fuel tanks -- permanent facilities (§ 911.15(2)(u))
gen.text: '1. Above ground fuel tanks having a capacity in excess of five hundred (500) gallons are subject to the requirements of [subsection] 917.06(1). 2. A generator or above ground fuel tank not located within five (5) feet of a building may be located no closer than ten (10) feet from a side or rear property line. 3. Where allowed by applicable building and fire codes, a generator or fuel tank located within five (5) feet of a building may be allowed within five (5) feet of any side or rear property line. For a legally created lot of record that is less than seventy (70) feet wide, a generator or fuel tank may be located no closer than two and one-half (2.5) feet from a side or rear property line where allowed by applicable building and fire codes. 4. A generator or above ground fuel tank may be allowed to encroach up to five (5) feet into a required front yard setback. 5. Generators and above ground fuel tanks shall be screened from adjacent neighboring side and rear yards by a four (4) foot tall opaque feature which may consist of existing or planted vegetation, a wall, a fence, or other improvements approved by the planning division. 6. No generator or fuel tank (above ground tank or below ground tank) shall be located within a public right-of-way or drainage and/or utility easement.' The same provision is restated verbatim for single-family development at § 912.07(6)t.

equip.cite: Air conditioners, pool heaters and similar mechanical equipment (§ 911.15(2)(c))
equip.text: 'Air conditioning equipment, pool heaters, sprinkler system controls and similar mechanical equipment (including utility pad mounted equipment) may project into any required yard provided that the equipment is mounted adjacent to the building. In order to minimize potential noise nuisance to adjacent properties, air conditioners, pool heaters and similar mechanical equipment in planned developments and small-lot subdivisions with reduced yard setbacks shall be: Located adjacent to a garage or other non-living area, and not located adjacent to an outdoor living area such as a porch or patio; or Located at least ten (10) feet from all property lines; or County-approved as a "quiet" low decibel model unit or installed with a county-approved sound barrier or other county-approved noise-mitigating improvement.' Restated at § 912.07(6)c.

equip.cite: General yard rule (§ 911.15(2))
equip.text: 'Every part of a required yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky, except as hereinafter provided or as otherwise permitted in this ordinance. No structure shall be erected within any easement, except as specifically authorized by this ordinance.'

equip.cite: Utility buildings / sheds (§ 911.15(2)(k))
equip.text: 'Utility buildings or sheds of one hundred (100) square feet or less may be located within a required side or rear yard, provided a minimum of five (5) feet is maintained from the side or rear property line and clear of all easements. Only one (1) such utility building or shed may be allowed to encroach into a required yard on a single lot or parcel of land. A utility building or shed (one hundred (100) square feet or less) that is to be located to within five (5) feet of a side or rear property line shall be located no closer than ten (10) feet to the principal structure and shall not exceed the height of the principal structure.'

equip.cite: Structures exempt from yard requirements (§ 911.15(2)(o))
equip.text: 'The following structures shall be exempted from the minimum yard requirements: underground utility equipments, clothes lines, flag poles, mail boxes, police call boxes, traffic signals, fire hydrants, light poles, or any similar structure or device as approved by the community development director.'

equip.cite: Screening enclosures, patios and decks (§ 911.15(2)(q))
equip.text: 'No screening enclosures, patios, or decks shall be located closer than five (5) feet to any rear property line or within any easement for utilities, drainage, or access.'

equip.cite: Swimming pools and pool decks (§ 911.15(2)(f))
equip.text: 'No swimming pool shall be located closer than ten (10) feet to any rear property line or within any easement for utilities, drainage or access.' 'No deck or patio constructed in conjunction with any swimming pool shall be located within an easement or closer than five (5) feet to any property line.' 'No screen enclosures for swimming pools shall be located within an easement or closer than ten (10) feet to: the rear property line on interior lots, the rear or side property line on corner and multi-frontage lots.'

equip.cite: Above ground storage of fuel (§ 917.06(1))
equip.text: 'Where aboveground storage of gasoline, petroleum oils or other flammable fluids are permitted, any such facility for storage having a capacity in excess of five hundred (500) gallons shall be in compliance with the National Fire Protection Association requirements.' A site plan application must be filed if required by Chapter 914; environmental health reviews for secondary containment and/or monitoring wells. No property-line distance is printed here -- the distance is the one in § 911.15(2)(u).

equip.cite: Accessory structures generally (§ 917.04)
equip.text: 'No accessory structure shall be built prior to the construction of the principal use, except for single-family docks on vacant lots as specified in Chapter 971.' 'All accessory uses and structures shall comply with the use limitations applicable in the zoning district in which located.' § 917.05(4): 'No accessory use or structure may be located in any corner visibility triangle as established in the general provisions section of Chapter 911, Zoning.' Chapter 917 prints no numeric side/rear setback of general application for accessory structures.

equip.cite: No generator, A/C, condenser or LP-gas placement rule found
equip.text: The only 'generator' hits are in the solid-waste chapter (waste generator, § 50-61) and the only mechanical-equipment placement reference is an architectural-submittal requirement in the community redevelopment district architectural standards: the elevation exhibit 'shall include colors, materials, building dimensions, location of service areas and mechanical equipment, screening devices, site furnishings, lighting fixtures'. Placement of a standby generator therefore falls under the general accessory-structure and yard rules quoted below.

equip.cite: Accessory structures (§ 30-510, PDF p.351-352)
equip.text: '(a) Applicability. This section shall apply to accessory structures only in single-family and duplex residential zoning districts. (b)... Any enclosed buildings, gazebos and cabanas exceeding 150 square feet shall meet all setback requirements imposed for the principal structure for the zoning district in which the accessory structure is located.... (c)(3) The accessory structures are not erected in a required building setback adjacent to a public street or closer to a public street than any wall of the principal structure on the same lot, whichever is more restrictive. (4) The accessory structures are not erected within a recorded easement or right-of-way. (5) The accessory structures are included in all calculations of impervious surface and surface water runoff.... (8) The accessory structures are not erected in a front or side yard and do not encroach into an easement. When the lot is located on two streets... the accessory structures shall be erected in the rear yard, or the side yard between the rear lot line and the rear of the principal building, including covered porches and garages, and shall not encroach into an easement. Accessory structures 100 square feet or smaller shall have a minimum rear and side setback of five feet. Those larger than 100 square feet or higher than seven feet shall have minimum rear and side setbacks of ten feet.'

equip.cite: Customary yard structures (§ 30-510(f), PDF p.352)
equip.text: 'Customary yard structures shall be allowed provided they are not located in a front yard or within five feet of the rear or side property lines and do not exceed ten feet in height. In no event shall they encroach into any easement of record.' Subsection (b) defines customary yard structures as 'barbeque pits, playground equipment, etc.'; the code does not say whether a generator pad is one.

equip.cite: Prohibited accessory uses (§ 30-510(h), PDF p.352)
equip.text: 'Accessory structures shall not be used for living quarters, business uses, home occupations (other than storage), commercial equipment, or commercial kennels.'

equip.cite: Minor encroachments (§ 30-201(c), PDF p.280)
equip.text: 'The building official is authorized to allow minor encroachments up to four inches within any required setback for new construction.'

equip.cite: Administrative deviations from setbacks (§ 30-303(5), PDF p.286)
equip.text: 'The building official is authorized to grant deviations from the setback provisions contained in sections 30-407 through 30-416 (various zoning district regulations) for street, rear, side, or waterbody setbacks to permit structures to encroach with regard to a specific setback only under the following circumstances: 1. Bay windows, chimneys and similar architectural features that may encroach into the setback provided the encroachment does not protrude beyond a two-foot overhang. 2. Where American Disability Act (ADA) standards will be applied... 3. Street, rear, side, or waterbody setbacks may be modified to allow the replacement of stairs or decking that provides access into an existing dwelling unit.' No mechanical-equipment category is listed.

equip.cite: No generator / mechanical equipment rule
equip.text: Liberty County's code contains no provision on the placement of standby generators, A/C condensers, pool equipment or LP tanks relative to a lot line. The only equipment provision found is Sec. 16-303 (flood): 'Utility equipment that serves manufactured homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential, § R322.'

equip.cite: Projections into a yard (Sec. 101-59 definitions)
equip.text: 'Yard, front, means a yard extending across the front of a lot... being the minimum horizontal distance between the street line and the principal building or any projections thereof, other than the projections of uncovered steps, uncovered balconies or uncovered porches.' The rear-yard definition excludes 'the projections of uncovered steps, balconies or porches.' The side-yard definition allows no projection exclusion — it is measured to 'the side of the main building or any projection thereof.' Mechanical equipment is not named.

equip.cite: Off-street parking setbacks (Sec. 103-51 / parking article, PDF p.307)
equip.text: 'All off-street parking areas shall be set back a minimum of ten feet from the front property line and five feet from the side and rear property lines.'

equip.cite: LP gas (Sec. 103-49(g)(5) and (i))
equip.text: LP gas storage and/or distribution facilities for up to 1,000 gallons are a public service/utility use; over 1,000 gallons is an industrial use. No separation distance is printed.

equip.cite: Building setback for future four-laning (subdivision article, PDF p.325)
equip.text: 'Buildings shall be set back 75 feet from the centerline of existing right-of-way, or 25 feet from the existing property line, whichever is greater, in order to facilitate future four-laning.'

alachua_county.name: Alachua County
alachua_county.source: Unified Land Development Code, Chapter 403 (Zoning Districts). District list from Table 403.02.1 Zoning Districts. Rural/agricultural from Table 403.04.1 Standa

equip.cite: Setback encroachment prohibited
equip.text: Sec. 407.04: 'The minimum setbacks required by these regulations shall not be encroached upon, except in accordance with Section 407.05.'

equip.cite: Allowable projections — what may enter a required setback
equip.text: Sec. 407.05: 'Every part of a required setback shall be open from its lowest point to the sky, unobstructed, except that certain building features and structures are allowed to project into required setbacks...' The complete list is (a) marquees, canopies and awnings in non-residential districts, mixed-use/commercial portions of TNDs and TODs, or for zero-lot-line buildings; (b) uncovered ingress/egress improvements such as steps or ramps, not more than four (4) feet (porches, open or closed fire escapes, outside stairways and balconies shall NOT extend into any required setback); (c) sills, cornices, ornamental features, chimneys and flues, eaves and gutters, up to thirty-six (36) inches; (d) driveways and similar concrete slabs; (e) patios and similar pads provided they are made of removeable materials so as to not be permanent in nature. Mechanical equipment, generators, A/C condensers, pool equipment and LP tanks are NOT on this list, so the ULDC gives them no setback encroachment.

equip.cite: Accessory structures — where they may be placed
equip.text: Sec. 407.02(a): 'The principal building or buildings on any lot or parcel of land shall be erected within the area bounded by the setback requirements. Accessory structures, and similar structures as determined by the Zoning Administrator may be erected within the side or rear buildable area as established by the zoning district. Accessory structures may be erected within front yards subject to the following: (1) On lots less than one (1) acre: a. A single accessory structure is allowed. b. Must not encroach in any required buffer, easement, sidewalk, sight triangle or right-of-way of any public road. c. Not exceed four hundred (400) square feet. d. Not higher than fifteen (15) feet. e. Compliant with the Florida Building Code. (2) On lots greater than one acre: a. Two accessory structures are allowed. b. Must not encroach in any required buffer, easement, sidewalk, sight triangle or right-of-way of any public road. c. Must be at least twenty-five (25) feet from the front property line. d. Not higher than fifteen (15) feet. e. Compliant with the Florida Building Code.' 407.02(b): accessory structures placed on lots in a previously approved platted subdivision where accessory setbacks were not provided may meet the least restrictive standard of either the platted setback or the accessory setback of the zoning district.

equip.cite: Accessory building setbacks on residential lots
equip.text: Table 403.07.2: accessory buildings are 'Same as principal building except rear is 7.5 ft.' on lots less than one acre in size, and 'Same as principal building except rear is 10 ft.' on lots one acre or greater.

equip.cite: Accessory building setbacks on the agricultural districts and on nonconforming agricultural lots
equip.text: Table 403.04.1 (A and A-RB): 'Rear lot line setback - accessory buildings, min (ft): 25'. Table 408.16.1 (nonconforming agricultural lots of 0—3 acres, Sec. 408.16(c)): Front 25, Rear 20, Interior side 10, Street side 15, 'Rear lot line setback - accessory buildings, min. (ft): 7'. (p.1726).

equip.cite: Screening of mechanical equipment at neighborhood convenience centers
equip.text: Sec. 404.71.5(b)(7): 'All commercial waste receptacles, storage areas, and electrical and mechanical equipment, such as heat pumps and air conditioners, shall be screened from view from a public right-of-way and from any residential development.'

equip.cite: Ground-mounted HVAC placement and screening (SW 13th Street / Williston Road design standards)
equip.text: Sec. 405.23: 'Ground mounted HVAC equipment. All ground mounted exterior HVAC equipment shall be placed at the rear or side of the building. All HVAC equipment shall be screened from ground level public view by one of the following methods: 1. A vegetative screen; or 2. A walled enclosure whose materials complement the main building.' The same section requires all roof-mounted HVAC and mechanical equipment to be located so as to be screened from public view at ground level.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment in industrial districts
equip.text: Sec. 403.16(c): 'Mechanical equipment, lights, emissions, shipping/receiving areas, and other components of an industrial use that are outside enclosed buildings, shall be located away from residential areas, schools, parks and other non-industrial areas.'

equip.cite: Agricultural processing or packaging buildings
equip.text: Table 403.04.1 footnote 4: 'Unless otherwise specified for a specific use in Chapter 404 of this ULDC, buildings used for agricultural processing or packaging shall not be less than one hundred (100) feet from all lot or property lines.'

equip.cite: Noise from fixed mechanical equipment
equip.text: Alachua County Code Sec. 110.04(g) 'Fixed mechanical equipment': 'The use or operation of any noise-creating air conditioner, compressor unit, power fan or blower, fixed electric motor or engine which causes such excessive and unnecessary noise, unless such noise is muffled and deadened by adequa[te]...' Sec. 110.04(e) then states that air conditioners and lawn mowers are exempt from provisions of that chapter. This is the county noise ordinance, not the ULDC, and carries no distance.

equip.cite: Rooftop photovoltaic solar systems (the only ULDC rule for roof-mounted accessory equipment height)
equip.text: Sec. 407.09.5(a): 'The height of rooftop photovoltaic solar systems shall not exceed the roof line as defined in Chapter 410. For flat roofs with or without a parapet, the rooftop photovoltaic solar system shall not be greater than five feet above the roof.'

equip.cite: Solid waste enclosures
equip.text: Sec. 407.10(a): all garbage and recycling bins or dumpsters shall be located within designated areas in a principal building or within a rear or interior side setback; 407.10(b) requires complete screening on all sides with an opaque, lockable gate on one side, of masonry walls or wood fencing with a minimum height of six feet.

naples.source: Code of Ordinances, Chapter 58 Zoning, Article II Zoning Districts, Divisions 2-31 (per-district sections: Minimum lot area / Minimum lot width / Minimum yards

gen.cite: Mechanical equipment - general (Sec. 56-41(a))
gen.text: Mechanical equipment installed with new construction or with additions or alterations exceeding 50 percent of the assessed value of the existing structure may not be located in a required yard regardless of the height or projection of the equipment. Air conditioning and pool equipment permitted and installed prior to the effective date of this ordinance may be maintained and replaced provided the new equipment does not encroach more than 36 inches into any required yard. New generators may be installed adjacent to existing single-family homes permitted and constructed prior to the effective date of the ordinance codified in this section; provided, that the new equipment does not encroach more than 36 inches into any required side yard. All new and replaced mechanical equipment must be screened from view to the full height of the equipment consistent with all applicable fencing and landscaping requirements and manufacturer's specifications. Screening walls and fences around replacement equipment may exceed the allowable height limitations provided the height is the minimum required to screen from view to the full height of the equipment and the projection into the required yard is the minimum encroachment necessary per manufacturers' specifications.

gen.cite: Permanently installed generators - fuel type within 15 feet of a property line (Sec. 56-41(c))
gen.text: Permanently installed generators within 15 feet of a property line shall use propane, natural gas or fuel with similar exhaust impacts. Gasoline or diesel-powered generators shall be prohibited within 15 feet of a property line.

gen.cite: Generator exercise/cycling hours (Sec. 56-41(d))
gen.text: Automatic cycling of generators shall take place between 9:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m., Monday through Thursday.

gen.cite: R1-15A mechanical equipment - screening and elevation (Sec. 58-116(4))
gen.text: Mechanical equipment screening and elevation, including air conditioning, pool equipment, generators or other noise generating machinery. a. Permanent screening shall be required around all mechanical equipment. The equipment shall be fully screened as viewed from the street, neighboring properties and adjacent waterways. b. Mechanical equipment may be placed on a second story roof only if it is recessed and completely concealed by the roof structure. c. When mechanical equipment is located on the side of the residence it shall be located with its base no more than six inches above the greater of either the minimum FEMA first habitable floor elevation or the State Department of Environmental Protection requirement for first habitable floor.

gen.cite: R1-15A encroachments - absolute bar on generators in a setback (Sec. 58-116(5)b)
gen.text: Structures less than 36 inches in height, as measured from the crown of the road shall not be considered as encroachments, except that under no circumstances shall air conditioning, pool mechanical equipment or generators encroach into any required setback area.

equip.cite: Rooftop HVAC shielding (Sec. 56-41(b))
equip.text: In all zone districts except C3, C4 and I, heating, ventilating and air conditioning equipment and ductwork and the like located on building rooftops shall be shielded from ground level view within 1,000 feet of the building. If shielding cannot be accomplished by judicious placement of the equipment, ornamental screening visually compatible with the building is required.

equip.cite: Encroachments into required yards (Sec. 56-54(a))
equip.text: Structures less than 30 inches in height, other than swimming pools, are not considered encroachments upon minimum required yards. Every part of every required yard will be open and unobstructed from 30 inches above the ground, as measured from the average elevation of the crown of road along the property frontage, except as provided in this section or section 56-45, Pools. Subsection (1)e: 'Mechanical equipment is governed under section 56-41, Mechanical equipment.' Subsection (3): 'Flagpoles, play equipment, wires, lights, mailboxes, and outdoor furniture are not considered yard encroachments. Fire pits, fire torches, and portable grills are not considered yard encroachments in the side and rear yards.'

equip.cite: Height-limitation exceptions for rooftop equipment (Sec. 56-39(a),(b))
equip.text: Chimneys, elevator shafts or overruns, stair tower roofs, rooftop heating, ventilating and air conditioning equipment, ornamental screening for such equipment, energy producing devices such as solar panels and wind turbines and architectural embellishments may extend seven feet above the peak of the building roof; however, in no case shall the maximum commercial building height limit of 42 feet as measured from the required first floor elevation be exceeded to accommodate such structure or equipment. Rooftop heating, ventilating and air conditioning equipment and ornamental screening for such equipment are NOT exempt in single-family residence districts. In single-family residence districts, exemptions to the maximum height limitation may only extend a maximum of five feet above the maximum height limitation.

equip.cite: Commercial districts - no height exceptions (Sec. 56-39(d))
equip.text: In commercial zoning districts as defined in section 44-8, no building shall exceed three floors and a building height of 42 feet to the peak of the roof or any appurtenances, whichever is higher, measured from the first floor, base flood elevation plus one foot as required by the Florida Building Code, and no exceptions, [including, but not limited to, exceptions such as listed in subsection (a) above], shall be allowed in such districts.

equip.cite: Downtown district - mechanical equipment placement (Sec. 58-911(10))
equip.text: Mechanical equipment and screening for such equipment must be designed as an integral part of the building and located away from the frontage line.

equip.cite: Waterfront yards and coastal setback (Sec. 58-3(5))
equip.text: On waterfront lots, the shoreline shall be construed to be the property line for the purpose of determining minimum required waterfront yards. The coastal area setback line, if greater, shall take precedence over setbacks listed in individual districts.

equip.cite: Coastal construction setback line (Sec. 52-33)
equip.text: There is hereby established for the city a coastal construction setback line (CCSL) for construction of single-family, multifamily and commercial structures, as established and approved on June 27, 1989, by the governor and cabinet of the state, such line lying within the boundaries and limits of the city and to be recorded in the coastal setback line book of the public records of the county, and set forth in F.A.C. 62B-26.022, titled 'Description of the Collier County Coastal Construction Control Line.' It shall be unlawful for any person to construct any structure, make any excavation, deposit any fill, remove any beach material or otherwise alter existing ground elevations seaward of the setback line without a permit. Sec. 58-873(b) further defines two city setback lines as being 150 feet landward of the mean high-water line and 75 feet landward of the vegetation line, requiring a site-specific survey to establish their exact position along with the position of the coastal construction control line.

equip.cite: Mechanical change-out permit (Sec. 22 / p.404 of the PDF)
equip.text: Any contractor or homeowner that changes an existing mechanical compressor unit or air handling unit, or similar item, for maintenance reasons, with the same or equal type unit, must first obtain a permit and pay a flat rate.

RE.sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet. This side yard applies to the first 15 feet of vertical height measured from the greater of: the lowest floor elevation as required by the Florida Building Code for the first habitable floor height requirement; 18 inches above the state department of environmental protection requirement for the first habitable floor structural support.
RE.heightNote: Maximum height of structures in the RE district is 30 feet, measured from the greater of the four flood/grade datums listed in Sec. 58-58; where the May 16, 2012 FEMA FIRM lowest floor elevation is higher than the current FIRM, the applicant may elect the 2012 elevation and height is then measured from it.
RE.coverageNote: Maximum building area is a graduated schedule by lot-size increment, not a single percentage: First 5,000 sq ft = 48%; Next 5,000 = 35%; Next 10,000 = 24%; Next 30,000 = 20%; Next 50,000 = 15%; Thereafter = 10%. (Sec. 58-60).
RE.note: Minimum lot area printed as 2 1/4 acres (Sec. 58-54); converted 2.25 x 43,560 = 98,010 sq ft. Sheltering structures for equine animals must be no less than 20 ft from any lot line and at least 100 ft from any existing residence on adjacent property.

R1-E.sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet, applying to the first 15 feet of vertical height measured from the greater of the four datums in Sec. 58-86; additional height must remain within a 12:12 slope beyond the initial setback. Guesthouses and staff residences must meet the above setback plus 0.5 feet for every foot of height above the first 15 feet of vertical height.
R1-E.rearNote: Rear yard: 35 feet. Rear yards abutting a public alley may be reduced to 15 feet for garages and carports with direct vehicular access from the alley, or utility sheds not exceeding 100 square feet. Unroofed pools or pools enclosed only with open mesh screening may be located in rear yard setback areas but no closer than 15 feet to any rear lot line.

R1-E.coverageNote: Graduated maximum building area: First 5,000 sq ft = 48%; Next 5,000 = 35%; Next 10,000 = 24%; Next 30,000 = 20%; Next 50,000 = 15%; Thereafter = 10%. (Sec. 58-90).

R1-15A.coverageNote: Graduated maximum building area (roof-perimeter basis): First 5,000 sq ft = 48%; Next 5,000 = 35%; Next 10,000 = 24%; Next 30,000 = 20%; Next 50,000 = 15%; Thereafter = 2%. (Sec. 58-120).

R3-12.sideNote: Side yard: one-story buildings 7 1/2 feet; two-story buildings 10 feet; three-story buildings 12 1/2 feet. Side yards no less than 7 1/2 feet may be approved for single-family homes on individually platted lots within the same development through site plan review. (Sec. 58-296(2)).

Sec. 56-40(a) additionally steps coverage down by building height (25% at <=30 ft to 19% at 80.1-87.0 ft).
R3-12.note: Maximum allowable density 12 dwelling units per net acre (Sec. 58-301).

R3T-12.frontNote: Front yard: 25 feet, six feet of which shall be landscaped in accordance with chapter 50.
R3T-12.sideNote: Side yard: one-story buildings 7 1/2 feet; two-story buildings 10 feet; three-story buildings 12 1/2 feet. Side yards no less than 7 1/2 feet may be approved for single-family homes on individually platted lots within the same development through site plan review. (Sec. 58-326(2)).
R3T-12.heightNote: 30 feet, except that development on any R3T-12 property immediately adjacent to, or across an alley from, any R1 zoned property is limited to two stories in height; measured from the greatest of the four datums in Sec. 58-328 (chapter 16 art. III first habitable floor elevation; 18 in above FDEP support requirement; 18 in above average crown of adjacent roads; average grade to the roof reference point).
R3T-12.coverageNote: Maximum lot coverage for all buildings other than individual single-family residences is 25 percent (Sec. 58-330(b)); Sec. 56-40(a) steps coverage down by building height.
R3T-12.note: Maximum allowable density 12 dwelling units per net acre (Sec. 58-331).

R3-15.sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet, PLUS one foot for each one foot of building height over 30 feet. Side yards no less than 7 1/2 feet may be approved for single-family homes on individually platted lots within the same development through site plan review. (Sec. 58-356(2),(4)).

(Sec. 58-358).
R3-15.coverageNote: Maximum lot coverage for all buildings other than individual single-family residences is 25 percent (Sec. 58-360(c)); Sec. 56-40(a) steps combined coverage down by building height from 25% at 30.0 ft or less to 19% at 80.1-87.0 ft.
R3-15.note: Maximum allowable density 15 dwelling units per net acre (Sec. 58-361). The front/side/rear figures recorded are the base minimums that apply to a building 30 feet or less in height; the printed 'plus one foot per foot of height over 30 feet' is captured in the rule fields.

R3-15 (Coquina Sands CS).frontNote: Front yard: 25 feet, PLUS one foot for each one foot of building height over 30 feet; six feet of which shall be landscaped. (Sec. 58-386(1)).
R3-15 (Coquina Sands CS).sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet, PLUS one foot for each one foot of building height over 30 feet. Side yards no less than 7 1/2 feet may be approved for single-family homes on individually platted lots within the same development through site plan review.

R3-15 (Moorings MOR).sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet, PLUS one foot for each one foot of building height over 30 feet. Side yards no less than 7 1/2 feet may be approved for single-family homes on individually platted lots within the same development through site plan review.
R3-15 (Moorings MOR).rearNote: Rear yard: 25 feet, PLUS one foot for each one foot of building height over 30 feet.
R3-15 (Moorings MOR).heightNote: Three habitable stories, up to a maximum height of 50 feet, as measured from the AVERAGE GRADE of the property to the ceiling of the highest story, PLUS six feet from the ceiling to the highest point of a flat roof, parapet wall or mansard detail, or six feet from the ceiling to the mean distance between the eaves and ridge of a gable, hip or gambrel roof. (Sec. 58-418).
R3-15 (Moorings MOR).coverageNote: Maximum lot coverage for all buildings other than individual single-family residences is 25 percent (Sec. 58-420(c)); Sec. 56-40(a) steps coverage down by building height.
R3-15 (Moorings MOR).note: Maximum allowable density 15 dwelling units per net acre (Sec. 58-422).

R3-18.frontNote: Front yard: 30 feet, PLUS one foot for each TWO feet of building height over 45 feet; six feet of which shall be landscaped. (Sec. 58-446(1)).
R3-18.sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet, PLUS one foot for each two feet of building height over 45 feet. (Sec. 58-446(2)).
R3-18.rearNote: Rear yard: 25 feet, PLUS one foot for each two feet of building height over 45 feet. (Sec. 58-446(3)).

(Sec. 58-448).
R3-18.coverageNote: Maximum lot coverage for all buildings other than individual single-family residences is 25 percent (Sec. 58-450(c)); Sec. 56-40(a) steps combined coverage down by building height to 19% at 80.1-87.0 ft.
R3-18.note: Maximum allowable density 18 dwelling units per net acre (Sec. 58-451).

R3T-18.heightNote: 75 feet, plus an additional 12 feet if at least 75 percent of the ground floor is devoted to automobile parking and there are no dwelling units on the ground floor except one manager's apartment. (Sec. 58-478).
R3T-18.coverageNote: Maximum lot coverage for all buildings other than individual single-family residences is 25 percent (Sec. 58-480(c)); Sec. 56-40(a) steps coverage down by building height.
R3T-18.note: Maximum allowable density 18 dwelling units per net acre (Sec. 58-481).

(Sec. 58-536(2)) This is an either/or standard, not a single setback distance.

(Sec. 58-568).

C1-A.lotWidthNote: There is no minimum lot width requirement for the C1-A district. (Sec. 58-565).

(Sec. 58-598).
