C2-A.coverageNote: Marinas or marine research, development and testing operations: 50 percent. All other buildings: 40 percent. (Sec. 58-630).

C3.frontNote: Front yard: 10 feet, 6 feet of which shall be landscaped in accordance with chapter 50.
C3.sideNote: Side yard: Buildings may be placed either on the side lot line or a minimum of 10 feet from it, except when the adjoining lot is in another zone with a different side yard requirement, in which case a minimum side yard of 10 feet shall be provided. (Sec. 58-656(2)).
C3.heightNote: 3 stories and 42 feet, measured from the 1st-floor FEMA elevation to the peak of the roof or the highest point of any appurtenance attached to the roof, except that development on any C3 zoned property adjacent to or across the street from any R1 zoned property is limited to 2 stories in height. (Sec. 58-658).
C3.minLotNote: There is no minimum lot area requirement for the C3 district. (Sec. 58-654).
C3.lotWidthNote: There is no minimum lot width requirement for the C3 district. (Sec. 58-655).

C4.frontNote: Front yard: 10 feet, 6 feet of which must be landscaped in accordance with chapter 50.
C4.sideNote: Side yard: Buildings may be placed either on the side lot line or a minimum of 10 feet from it, except when the adjoining lot is in another zone with a different side yard requirement, in which case a minimum side yard of 10 feet shall be provided. (Sec. 58-686(2)).
C4.heightNote: 3 stories and 42 feet, measured from the 1st-floor FEMA elevation to the peak of the roof or the highest point of any appurtenance attached to the roof. (Sec. 58-688).
C4.minLotNote: There is no minimum lot area requirement for the C4 district. (Sec. 58-684).
C4.lotWidthNote: There is no minimum lot width requirement for the C4 district. (Sec. 58-685).
C4.note: C4 is the Naples Municipal Airport district; development also requires substantial compliance with an approved overall master development plan.

I.frontNote: Front yard: 25 feet, 6 feet of which shall be landscaped in accordance with chapter 50.
I.sideNote: Side yard: Buildings may be placed either on a side lot line or a minimum of 10 feet from it, except when the adjoining lot is in another zone with a different side yard requirement, in which case a minimum side yard of 10 feet shall be provided. (Sec. 58-716(2)).
I.heightNote: 3 stories and 42 feet, measured from the 1st-floor FEMA elevation to the peak of the roof or the highest point of any appurtenance attached to the roof. (Sec. 58-717).
I.minLotNote: There is no minimum lot area requirement for the I district. (Sec. 58-714).
I.lotWidthNote: There is no minimum lot width requirement for the I district. (Sec. 58-715).

M.frontNote: Front yard: 20 feet, 6 feet of which must be landscaped in accordance with chapter 50.
M.sideNote: Side yard: Buildings may be placed either on the side lot line or a minimum of 7 1/2 feet from it, except when the adjoining lot is in another zone with a different side yard requirement, in which case a minimum side yard of 7 1/2 feet shall be provided. (Sec. 58-746(2)).
M.heightNote: 30 feet measured from the 1st-floor FEMA elevation to the peak of the roof, with exceptions as allowed by section 56-39, except that development on any M zoned property adjacent to or across the street from any R1 zoned property is limited to 2 stories in height. (Sec. 58-748).
M.coverageNote: Nursing or rest homes and other residential buildings: 25 percent. All other buildings: 40 percent. (Sec. 58-750).
M.minLotNote: There is no minimum lot area requirement for the M district. (Sec. 58-744).
M.lotWidthNote: There is no minimum lot width requirement for the M district. (Sec. 58-745).
M.note: Residential conditional uses in M follow the R3-12 district requirements for minimum lot width, minimum yards, minimum floor area, maximum height and minimum off-street parking (Sec. 58-743(2)).

O.frontNote: Front yard: 20 feet, 6 feet of which shall be landscaped in accordance with chapter 50.
O.sideNote: Side yard: Buildings may be placed either on the side lot line or a minimum of 10 feet from it, except when the adjoining lot is in another zone with a different side yard requirement, in which case a minimum side yard of 10 feet shall be provided. (Sec. 58-776(2)).
O.heightNote: 30 feet measured from the first floor FEMA elevation to the peak of the roof, with exceptions as allowed by section 56-39, except that development on any O zoned property adjacent to or across the street from any R1 zoned property is limited to two stories in height. (Sec. 58-778).
O.minLotNote: There is no minimum lot area requirement for the O district. (Sec. 58-774).
O.lotWidthNote: There is no minimum lot width requirement for the O district. (Sec. 58-775).

PD.frontNote: The PD district sets no fixed yards. Sec.
PD.sideNote: yards are established through the PD rezoning and approved development plan.
PD.rearNote: yards are established through the PD rezoning and approved development plan.
PD.heightNote: Sec. 58-809: 'Within the planned development district, the maximum height of all COMMERCIAL buildings shall be limited to three stories and 42 feet, measured from the first floor FEMA elevation to the peak of the roof or the highest point of any appurtenance attached to the roof.' No fixed maximum height is printed for non-commercial buildings in a PD.
PD.coverageNote: No fixed lot coverage is printed for PD. Sec. 56-40(a) applies the height-stepped coverage table (25% at <=30 ft down to 19% at 80.1-87.0 ft) to PD districts designated for multifamily residences, transient lodging facilities, or nursing/group/rest homes.
PD.note: Where the comprehensive plan does not specify a density limit, PD is limited to eight dwelling units per net acre for permanent residential units (Sec. 58-802).

PS.frontNote: Sec. 58-836: 'Each yard requirement in the PS District shall be the same as the yard requirement for the most restrictive adjacent zone district, but yard requirements shall in no case be less than the following:' (1) Front yard: 20 feet, six feet of which shall be landscaped. The recorded numbers are floors, not the operative setback where an adjacent district is more restrictive.
PS.sideNote: Side yard: 10 feet, subject to the 'most restrictive adjacent zone district' rule in Sec. 58-836.
PS.rearNote: Rear yard: 25 feet, subject to the 'most restrictive adjacent zone district' rule in Sec. 58-836.
PS.heightNote: 30 feet for principal buildings. Because of the wide diversity of uses allowed, structures in excess of this height (church spires, water towers, etc.) may be approved as part of the conditional use process provided they do not affect public health, safety or welfare. (Sec. 58-838).
PS.minLotNote: 30,000 square feet, provided however there is no minimum lot area for municipally owned land in the PS district used by the city for public utilities, public services, passive parks, infrastructure and other similar uses. (Sec. 58-834).
PS.lotWidthNote: 150 feet, with the same municipally-owned-land exception. (Sec. 58-835).
PS.note: For approved community theater and community hospital conditional uses on city-owned land, city council establishes the standards for minimum yards, maximum height, off-street parking, lot coverage and signage, and those standards supersede these district regulations (Secs. 58-841, 58-842).

C (Conservation).note: Division 29 (Secs. 58-861 through 58-880) regulates the C Conservation district by resource subcategory (mangrove wetlands, tidal swamp and marsh, freshwater swamp and marsh, gulf beaches and dunes, Class II waters and shorelines) with permitted/conditional use lists and submittal requirements. No dimensional envelope - no minimum lot area, lot width, yards, height or lot coverage - is printed for the C district.

TC (Transitional Conservation).heightNote: Sec. 58-876(e) standards for residential development in transitional land: 'd. Maximum height is 35 feet.' No measuring datum is stated in that subsection.
TC (Transitional Conservation).coverageNote: 'b. Maximum cleared or disturbed area per homesite is 10,000 square feet. c. Maximum building envelope is to be determined through a site check, in accordance with clearing provisions and percentage requirements applicable to specific vegetative cover of the site. e. Maximum disturbed area, excluding areas heavily impacted by exotics, shall not exceed 10 percent of the total upland portion of the TC zoned area.'
TC (Transitional Conservation).note: Density shall not exceed 1 unit per 5 net acres, increasable only through transfer of density. A PD rezone is required which also meets all conditional use criteria. No yards are printed for the TC district. The TC district includes high-hazard unplatted non-CBRA areas seaward of the coastal construction control line.

D (Downtown).frontNote: Setback zone B: build-to line ten feet from property line. Setback zone C: ten-foot minimum, 20-foot maximum from property line (first five feet landscaping only). Setback zone D: ten-foot minimum, 25-foot maximum. Setback zone G: as required by the Goodlette Road corridor management standards, Secs. 58-1041 through 58-1051.
D (Downtown).sideNote: Side yard: If adjacent to an alley, a ten-foot setback is required; otherwise, buildings may be placed on the side yard line or a minimum of ten feet from it. (Sec. 58-909(2)).
D (Downtown).rearNote: Rear yard: A ten-foot setback, i.e., not a build-to line, is required with a five-foot landscaped strip. (Sec. 58-909(3)).
D (Downtown).heightNote: Throughout the downtown district the maximum height for any building, including residential, is limited to three stories and 42 feet, measured from the 1st-floor FEMA elevation to the peak of the roof or the highest point of any appurtenance attached to the roof, EXCEPT where commercial property is adjacent to, or across the street or alley from, property zoned residential, buildings at the street line cannot be higher than the height permitted in the residential zone.
D (Downtown).minLotNote: Minimum lot size for newly created lots is 15,000 square feet; exception for fee-simple townhome lots, each of which shall have a minimum area of 2,000 square feet. (Sec. 58-905).
D (Downtown).note: Maximum residential density 12 dwelling units per acre; no maximum density for transient lodging facilities. Commercial first floors may not be elevated more than 1 foot above the level of the adjacent sidewalk; if the FEMA elevation exceeds 1 foot above the sidewalk the building must be floodproofed.

BP.frontNote: Front yard: 25 feet, six feet of which shall be landscaped in accordance with chapter 50.
BP.sideNote: Side yard: 'The total of all side yards shall equal 20 percent of lot width, maximum of 50 feet total. No side yard shall be less than ten feet. A unified plan is allowed for lots under common ownership. For lots adjacent to residential zoning district, minimum side yard is 50 feet.' (Sec. 58-936(2)) The recorded 10 is the absolute floor, not the governing figure on most lots.
BP.rearNote: Rear yard: 15 feet, except for lots adjacent to a residential zoning district, on which the minimum rear yard requirement is 50 feet; and for lots adjacent to a water body, on which the minimum rear yard requirement is 25 feet. (Sec. 58-936(3)).
BP.heightNote: Three stories and 42 feet, measured from the first floor FEMA elevation to the peak of the roof or the highest point of any appurtenance attached to the roof. (Sec. 58-938).

R3-15CS.frontNote: 25 ft base, +1 ft per ft of height over 30 ft; 6 ft of front yard landscaped per Chapter 50.
R3-15CS.sideNote: 15 ft base, +1 ft per ft of height over 30 ft. Pools 15 ft from side line; not in any utility/drainage easement.
R3-15CS.rearNote: 25 ft base, +1 ft per ft of height over 30 ft. Pools no closer than 15 ft to rear lot line; not in any utility/drainage easement.

R3-15MOR.frontNote: 25 ft base, +1 ft per ft of height over 30 ft; 6 ft of front yard landscaped per Chapter 50.
R3-15MOR.sideNote: 15 ft base, +1 ft per ft of height over 30 ft. Pools 15 ft from side line; not in any utility/drainage easement.
R3-15MOR.rearNote: 25 ft base, +1 ft per ft of height over 30 ft. Pools no closer than 15 ft to rear lot line; not in any utility/drainage easement.

marco_island.name: Marco Island
marco_island.source: Land Development Code (Code of Ordinances Chapter 30), Article II Zoning Districts, Divisions 2-13 (Secs. 30-85, 30-105, 30-125, 30-145, 30-165, 30-185, 30-205,

gen.cite: Generators, pool equipment, A/C units and LP gas tanks - projection into a required yard (Sec. 30-1004(a)(4))
gen.text: Ground-mounted, wall-mounted, pad-mounted, cube-mounted, or cantilevered generators, swimming pool equipment, air-conditioning units, above-ground LP gas tanks, and any other mounted mechanical equipment shall not project more than four feet into any required yard.

gen.cite: Accessory buildings and structures - setbacks and CCCL (Sec. 30-1002(a))
gen.text: Accessory buildings and structures must be constructed simultaneously with or following the construction of the principal structure and shall conform to the following setbacks and building separations. IN THOSE CASES WHERE THE COASTAL CONSTRUCTION CONTROL LINE IS INVOLVED, THE COASTAL CONSTRUCTION CONTROL LINE WILL APPLY. The Accessory Structure Setbacks tables (one for non-waterfront/non-golf-course lots, one for waterfront and golf course lots) cover parking garages/carports, parking structures, swimming pools and screen enclosures, tennis courts, utility buildings, chickee and barbeque areas, and attached screen porches. 'SPS' means calculated same as principal structure; 'N' means none. Utility buildings on a non-waterfront lot: front SPS, rear 10 feet, side SPS, 10 feet structure-to-structure; on a waterfront or golf course lot: front SPS, rear SPS, side SPS, 10 feet structure-to-structure. No line item for a generator or mechanical equipment appears in these tables - generators are governed by Sec. 30-1004(a)(4).

equip.cite: Pool equipment and pad-mounted air conditioners permitted in required yards (Sec. 30-1004(a)(8))
equip.text: Fences, walls, privacy walls, vegetative materials, hedges, pool equipment and pad-mounted air conditioners are permitted in required yards, subject to the conditions contained herein.

equip.cite: Window-mounted air-conditioning units (Sec. 30-1004(a)(3))
equip.text: Window-mounted air-conditioning units, chimneys, fireplaces, bay windows, or pilasters shall not project over two feet into a required yard.

equip.cite: General yard obstruction rule (Sec. 30-1004(a))
equip.text: Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from 30 inches above the general ground level of the graded lot upward except as listed below. Such exceptions, when utilized in yards where recorded easements exist, are allowed with the explicit understanding that any structural improvement(s) or vegetation located within a recorded easement are subject to removal, at the owner's sole expense, when authorized entities must enter upon such easement area to repair, improve, reconstruct or make such lawful improvements as deemed necessary.

equip.cite: Accessory structure size limit (Sec. 30-1002(b))
equip.text: Accessory buildings and structures footprint area shall not exceed 100 percent of the principle structure area and must be within the required setbacks. Docks are not included in this calculation.

equip.cite: Utility storage structures in RSF districts (Secs. 30-85(b), 30-86(e))
equip.text: Freestanding utility storage structures of any type or material are prohibited. Utility storage structures (sheds) shall be physically attached to, and architecturally integrated into the principal structure. Such attachment may be located below the base flood elevation if devoted solely to storage use.

equip.cite: Exclusions from height limits (Sec. 30-1003)
equip.text: The height limitations do not apply to spires, belfries, cupolas, water tanks, fire towers when operated by a branch of government, ventilators, chimneys, or other appurtenances usually required to be placed above the roof level. Human occupancy, even casual use, is prohibited except for routine maintenance. (The RSF version, Sec. 30-85(c)(3), adds 'approved communications towers'.)

equip.cite: Essential services (Sec. 30-1008(b))
equip.text: Where structures are involved other than structure supporting lines or cables, such structures shall comply with the regulations for the district in which they are located or as may be required on an approved site development plan per article IX. In addition, the structures shall conform insofar as possible to the character of the district in which they are located as to development standards as well as architecture and landscaping, with utilization of screening and buffering compatible with the district.

equip.cite: Waterfront yards and the coastal construction control line (Sec. 30-1004(c))
equip.text: It is the intent and purpose of this section to permit the placement of principal structures, except single-family, two-family and duplex dwelling units, at the bulkhead line or shoreline where such placement at the water's edge can enhance the character of waterfront development... If the provisions of this section are met, such provisions govern regardless of any requirement for waterfront yards in the zoning district involved. IN THOSE CASES WHERE THE COASTAL CONTROL LINE IS INVOLVED, THE COASTAL CONSTRUCTION LINE SHALL APPLY.

equip.cite: Coastal construction control line definition (Sec. 30-10)
equip.text: Coastal construction control line (CCCL) means the Collier County coastal construction control line as depicted on the state department of natural resources, division of beaches and shores, March, 1985, aerial map as adopted in Collier County Ordinance.

equip.cite: Seawall setback in the RSF districts (Sec. 30-85(a) table footnote)
equip.text: * Ten-foot minimum setback from seawall. (Applies to the side-yard column for RSF-2, RSF-3 and RSF-4.)

equip.cite: Fences and walls in residential districts (Sec. 30-1009(b))
equip.text: Fences or privacy walls placed within required yards shall be limited to six feet in height except that no fence placed between the front building line and the front property line of lots or parcels less than 1.25 acres in size shall be greater than four feet in height. Fences or walls placed within the required rear yard of waterfront lots one acre or less in size shall be limited to four feet in height. Fences and walls in commercial districts shall be limited to eight feet in height.

RSF-2.sideNote: Side yard depends on lot width: 'Lots with <100 ft. - 7 1/2 ft.*; Lots with >100 ft. - 8 ft.*' with the footnote '* Ten-foot minimum setback from seawall.' (Sec. 30-85(a) table).
RSF-2.heightNote: Principal structures: Thirty-five feet as measured from required base flood elevation, or applicable measurement point, to the mean height level between eaves and ridge of a gable, hip or gambrel roof.
RSF-2.note: Maximum density 2 units per gross acre. Minimum floor area (living area) 1,500 sq ft. No maximum lot coverage is printed for the RSF districts. Accessory structures must be constructed simultaneously with or following the principal structure.

RSF-3.sideNote: Side yard depends on lot width: 'Lots with <100 ft. - 7 1/2 ft.*; Lots with >100 ft. - 8 ft.*' with the footnote '* Ten-foot minimum setback from seawall.' (Sec. 30-85(a) table).
RSF-3.heightNote: Principal structures: Thirty-five feet as measured from required base flood elevation, or applicable measurement point, to the mean height level between eaves and ridge of a gable, hip or gambrel roof. Accessory structures: Twenty feet from existing average ground elevation. (Sec. 30-85(c)).
RSF-3.note: Maximum density 3 units per gross acre. Minimum floor area (living area) 1,500 sq ft. No maximum lot coverage printed.

RSF-4.sideNote: Side yard depends on lot width: 'Lots with <100 ft. - 7 1/2 ft.*; Lots with >100 ft. - 8 ft.*' with the footnote '* Ten-foot minimum setback from seawall.' (Sec. 30-85(a) table).
RSF-4.heightNote: Principal structures: Thirty-five feet as measured from required base flood elevation, or applicable measurement point, to the mean height level between eaves and ridge of a gable, hip or gambrel roof. Accessory structures: Twenty feet from existing average ground elevation. (Sec. 30-85(c)).
RSF-4.note: Maximum density 4 units per gross acre. Minimum floor area (living area) 1,500 sq ft. No maximum lot coverage printed.

RMF-6.heightNote: Principal structures: 35 feet, as measured from the required FEMA base flood elevation to the mid-point of the roof. Accessory structures: 15 feet. (Sec. 30-105(4)).
RMF-6.minLotNote: Minimum lot area: a. Single-family, duplex and two-family dwellings: 7,260 square feet per dwelling unit. b. Multiple-family and townhouse: One acre. the multifamily minimum is one acre (43,560 sq ft).
RMF-6.note: Maximum density six dwelling units per gross acre. Minimum floor area 750 sq ft. Distance between any two principal structures on the same parcel shall be 15 feet or one-half the sum of their heights, whichever is greater. Nonconforming lots of record: single-family and two-family minimum lot area per dwelling unit 6,000 sq ft.

RMF-12.sideNote: Side yards: One-half of the building height as measured from each exterior wall or wing of a structure, with a minimum of 15 feet. (Sec. 30-125(3)b) This is a height-dependent standard, not a fixed distance; 15 feet is only the floor.
RMF-12.heightNote: Maximum height: 50 feet, measured per the Sec. 30-10 flood-elevation definition of building height.
RMF-12.note: Minimum lot area printed as 'One acre'; converted to 43,560 sq ft. Maximum density 12 units per gross acre. Minimum floor area: efficiency 450 sq ft; one bedroom 600 sq ft; two or more bedrooms 750 sq ft. Distance between any two principal structures on the same parcel: 15 feet or one-half the sum of their heights, whichever is greater.

RMF-16.frontNote: Front yard: One-half of the building height as measured from each exterior wall or wing of a structure, with a minimum of 30 feet. (Sec. 30-145(3)a) Height-dependent; 30 feet is the floor only.
RMF-16.sideNote: Side yards: One-half of the building height as measured from each exterior wall, with a minimum of 15 feet.
RMF-16.rearNote: Rear yard: One-half the building height as measured from each exterior wall or wing of a structure, with a minimum of 30 feet.
RMF-16.heightNote: Maximum height: 75 feet, measured per the Sec. 30-10 flood-elevation definition of building height.
RMF-16.note: Minimum lot area printed as 'One acre'; converted to 43,560 sq ft. Maximum density 16 dwelling units per gross acre. Minimum floor area: efficiency 450 sq ft; one bedroom 600 sq ft; two or more bedrooms 750 sq ft. Distance between any two principal structures: 15 feet or one-half the sum of their heights, whichever is greater.

RT.frontNote: Front yard: One-half the building height as measured from each exterior wall or wing of a structure, with a minimum of 30 feet. (Sec. 30-165(3)a) Height-dependent; 30 feet is the floor only.
RT.sideNote: Side yards: One-half the building height as measured from each exterior wall, with a minimum of 15 feet.
RT.rearNote: Rear yard: One-half the building height as measured from each exterior wall, with a minimum of 30 feet.
RT.heightNote: Maximum height: Ten stories or a maximum of 100 feet as measured to the mid-point of the roof. (Sec. 30-165(4)) The starting point is the Sec. 30-10 flood-elevation datum.
RT.note: Residential Tourist district. Minimum lot area printed as 'One acre'; converted to 43,560 sq ft. Maximum density 26 units per acre for hotels and motels, 16 units per acre for timeshares and multifamily structures. Floor area: timeshare 500 sq ft min per unit; multifamily efficiency 450 / one bedroom 600 / two or more bedrooms 750.

C-1 / C-1/T.sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet. Minimum yard requirement from any residentially zoned or used property: 25 feet. (Sec. 30-185(3)b,d).
C-1 / C-1/T.rearNote: Rear yard: 15 feet. Minimum yard requirement from any residentially zoned or used property: 25 feet.
C-1 / C-1/T.heightNote: Maximum height of structures: 35 feet, measured per the Sec. 30-10 flood-elevation definition of building height.
C-1 / C-1/T.coverageNote: 76 percent of the total lot area, subject to the land development code.
C-1 / C-1/T.note: Division 7 establishes both the C-1 Commercial Professional and C-1/T Commercial Professional Transitional districts and applies one set of dimensional standards to both. Minimum floor area of principal structure: 1,000 sq ft for each building on the ground floor.

C-2.sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet. Any yard abutting a residential parcel: a minimum of 25 feet. (Sec. 30-205(3)b,d).
C-2.heightNote: Maximum height: 35 feet, measured per the Sec. 30-10 flood-elevation definition of building height.
C-2.coverageNote: 76 percent of total lot area, subject to the land development code.
C-2.note: Minimum floor area of structures: 1,000 sq ft for each building on the ground floor. There shall be no outside storage or display of merchandise.

C-3.sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet. Any yard abutting a residential parcel: 25 feet. Waterfront: 25 feet, except none for marinas. (Sec. 30-225(3)).
C-3.rearNote: Rear yard: 15 feet. Any yard abutting a residential parcel: 25 feet. Waterfront: 25 feet, except none for marinas.
C-3.heightNote: Maximum height: 50 feet, measured per the Sec. 30-10 flood-elevation definition of building height.
C-3.coverageNote: 76 percent of total lot area, subject to the land development code.
C-3.note: Minimum floor area of principal structure: 700 sq ft gross floor area for each building on the ground floor.

C-4.frontNote: Front yard: 25 feet PLUS one foot for each one foot of building height over 50 feet. (Sec. 30-245(3)a) The recorded 25 is the base for buildings 50 feet or less.
C-4.sideNote: Side yard: Zero or a minimum of 15 feet except where the adjacent parcels are developed, in which case the required side yard may be zero to 15 feet; however in no case shall the separation between structures be less than 15 feet. Side yards located within the Marco Lake Subdistrict: zero or a minimum of five feet with a minimum separation of ten feet unless attached.
C-4.rearNote: Rear yard: Ten feet. Principal and accessory buildings shall be setback a minimum of 25 feet from an alley right-of-way when vehicular parking spaces take direct access from the alley, or ingress/egress is provided into the building. Any yard abutting a residential parcel: 25 feet. Waterfront: 25 feet, except none for marinas.
C-4.heightNote: Sec. 75 feet beginning January 1, 2005. Maximum height is 40 feet within the Marco Lake District (lots 1-62, Block 5, and lots 1-4, Block 1, Marco Highlands). Maximum height is 40 feet within the Village Commercial District (Old Marco).' The 75-foot figure is recorded because the January 1, 2005 step-down has taken effect; the printed 100 is the pre-2005 figure.
C-4.note: Minimum floor area: 700 sq ft gross floor area for each building on the ground floor. Floor area ratio: (Reserved.) Maximum density 16 units per acre for hotels, motels and timeshares within the Marco Lake and Village Commercial (Old Marco) Districts; 26 units per acre outside them. Sec.

C-5.sideNote: Side yard: Zero or a minimum of ten feet except where the adjacent parcels are developed, in which case the required side yard may be zero to ten feet; however in no case shall the separation between structures be less than ten feet. (Sec. 30-265(3)b).
C-5.rearNote: Rear yard: Five feet. Principal and accessory buildings shall be setback a minimum of 25 feet from an alley right-of-way when vehicular parking spaces take direct access from the alley. Any yard abutting a residential parcel: 25 feet. Waterfront: 25 feet, except none for marinas.
C-5.heightNote: Maximum height: 35 feet. Height to be measured from the base flood elevations to the midpoint of the roof. (Sec. 30-265(4)).
C-5.note: Minimum floor area: 700 sq ft gross floor area for each building on the ground floor. Maximum density 26 units per acre for hotels, motels and timeshare facilities. Sec. 30-267 sets separate standards for the Port Marco Subdivision.

CON.heightNote: Maximum height: 35 feet, measured per the Sec. 30-10 flood-elevation definition of building height.
CON.note: Conservation district. Minimum lot area printed as 'Five acres'; converted 5 x 43,560 = 217,800 sq ft. Maximum density one dwelling unit for each five gross acres. No maximum lot coverage printed.

P.frontNote: Minimum yard requirements: The yard requirements of the most restrictive adjoining district shall apply to all portions of the site within 100 feet of the adjoining district. (Sec. 30-305(3)) No fixed number is printed.
P.heightNote: Maximum height: The height of the most restrictive adjoining district within 100 feet of such district. (Sec. 30-305(4)) No fixed number is printed.
P.note: Public Use district.

CF.sideNote: Side yard: 15 feet. Any yard abutting a residential parcel: 25 feet. (Sec. 30-325(3)).
CF.rearNote: Rear yard: 15 feet. Any yard abutting a residential parcel: 25 feet.
CF.heightNote: Maximum height of structures: 30 feet, except for antennas and towers, which is 40 feet. (Sec. 30-325(5)) Measured per the Sec. 30-10 flood-elevation definition of building height.
CF.note: Community Facility district. Minimum distance between structures: 25 feet, or one-half the sum of the building heights, whichever is greater. Minimum floor area of principal structure: 1,000 sq ft for each building on the ground floor. Floor area ratio: (Reserved.)

GC.frontNote: Minimum yard requirements: 'A 50-foot yard setback requirement together with landscaping and buffering pursuant to the land development code, buffer type B, shall be provided adjacent to any residential district which is contiguous to the area of the golf course upon which is located the clubhouse and all related activities to the clubhouse, and adjacent to all maintenance buildings.' (Sec. 30-344(3)) This 50 feet applies only adjacent to a contiguous residential district around the clubhouse and maintenance buildings.
GC.heightNote: Maximum height: 35 feet, measured per the Sec. 30-10 flood-elevation definition of building height.
GC.coverageNote: Sec. 30-344(8) prints 'Minimum lot coverage: Not applicable.' No maximum lot coverage is stated.
GC.note: Golf Course district. Maximum density: Not applicable; however, a maximum of two residential units for use by golf course employees may be allowed. Distance between structures and minimum floor area: Not applicable.

A.frontNote: Front yard: 50 feet. Yard requirements for nonconforming lots of record: front yard 40 feet.
A.sideNote: Side yard: 30 feet. Yard requirements for nonconforming lots of record: side yard ten percent of the lot width, not to exceed a maximum of 20 feet on each side.
A.rearNote: Rear yard: 50 feet. Yard requirements for nonconforming lots of record: rear yard 30 feet.
A.heightNote: Maximum height: 30 feet, except as provided in the land development code. (Sec. 30-365(5)).
A.note: Rural Agricultural district. Minimum lot area printed as 'Five acres'; converted 5 x 43,560 = 217,800 sq ft. Minimum floor area 1,200 sq ft for single-family dwelling units. Maximum density one dwelling unit for each five acres. No maximum lot coverage printed.

PUD.frontNote: Sec. 30-385: 'Dimensional standards within any tract or increment of the proposed PUD shall conform to the minimum dimensional and other standards of the zoning district to which it most closely resembles...' The PUD district establishes no fixed envelope of its own; standards are fixed in the approved PUD document.

sanibel.name: Sanibel
sanibel.source: Land Development Code (Code of Ordinances Chapter 126 Zoning), Article VI Districts Generally (Sec. 126-241), Article VII Residential Districts Divisions 2-10 (

gen.cite: Generators and HVAC - purpose and administrative waiver (Sec. 126-1305)
gen.text: The purpose of this division is to establish application requirements and procedures for the installation of heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) units and electrical power generators. In the interest of public safety and the general welfare, providing air conditioning and emergency electrical power is encouraged and shall be accommodated. To that end, the city manager or the manager's designee is authorized to approve deviations from limits on: (1) impermeable coverage; and (2) developed area and vegetation removal to facilitate the issuance of a development permit for such air conditioning or emergency electrical power service. Such deviations may be issued only upon a finding by the city manager, or the manager's designee, that the standards of section 126-1307 have been met.... This division establishes standards for the operation, placement, screening and sound attenuation of emergency electric power generators to minimize their visual and noise impact upon abutting properties.

gen.cite: Generator required setbacks (Sec. 126-1307(c))
gen.text: (1) Front yard. There shall be a front yard setback for generator and air conditioning machinery and associated structure of no less than 75 feet from the centerline of minor arterial or collector roads and 50 feet from the centerline of any other street, except where a special setback is imposed, as set forth in article XIV, division 3, subdivision II, of this chapter. (2) Side and rear yard. There shall be side and rear yard setbacks for generator and air conditioning machinery and associated structure of no less than ten feet from any such property line. (3) Open body of water. The accessory structure shall not be located within 20 feet of any open body of water.

gen.cite: Generator noise limit (Sec. 126-1307(a))
gen.text: (1) An emergency electrical power generator operating when the primary electric service (Lee County Electric Cooperative) is disrupted, or during the generator's performance testing cycle, shall not exceed a maximum sound pressure level of 78 dB(A), when measured at any point of any property line. (2) Electrical power generators for general, unrestricted use are subject to the maximum permissible sound levels established in chapter 30, article III, section 30-64 of the city's Code of Ordinances. Unrestricted use means that there are no restrictions on the operation of an electrical power generator which limit its use to times when the primary electrical service is out or for the performance testing cycle of the generator.

gen.cite: Generator exercise cycle hours (Sec. 126-1307(b))
gen.text: The exercise cycle of the generator shall occur only between the hours of 10:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Monday through Saturday.

gen.cite: Generator visual buffer and sound barrier wall (Sec. 126-1307(e))
gen.text: The generator shall be effectively screened from views from off the subject property by a sound barrier wall, a fence, vegetation or other means. (1) Sound barrier walls that are higher than six feet above the ground shall comply with the setbacks required for the principal structure. (2) Sound barrier walls shall be architecturally compatible with the principal building and effectively screened from the adjacent property by use of native vegetation. Per the Table 3 footnote: a sound barrier wall can only be used in the sound calculation for a generator located so that the bottom of the generator is no higher than four feet above the finished grade of the ground; the wall must extend from the ground to a minimum of two feet higher than the top of the generator and extend a minimum of two feet past the sides of the generator, with no gaps, holes or penetrations. Walls of masonry, concrete block or wood construction meeting the above requirements are considered adequate. Foliage is not an adequate sound barrier.

gen.cite: Generator permits and application (Sec. 126-1306)
gen.text: No development permit is required for the operation of a portable electrical power generator. A development permit and building/electrical permits are required for the installation of a permanently installed electrical power generator. A short form development permit application may be available for a permanently installed emergency electrical power generator that complies with the standards set out in section 126-1307. A long form development permit application is required for an electrical power generator intended for unrestricted use. The application must include a site development plan with a plan to visually buffer the equipment from view off-site; the sound barrier wall if needed; and must 'Demonstrate compliance with all required setbacks from property lines and indicate the relationship of the generator's location to any dwelling unit or structure within 20 feet of the generator.' It must also identify the generator's manufacturer, model name and number, and load capacity or running watts; the manufacturer's certification of sound pressure level in dB(A) at seven meters (23 feet) under normal or average load; the generator or HVAC stand type (aluminum stand, wooden platform, hurricane/concrete pad); documentation of compliance with the Florida Building Code and National Electric Code; and the sound pressure calculation using 'Generator's corrected dB(A) = Gen + A + B + C' with the correction tables for distance to the property line, reflected sound from the home, and presence of a sound barrier wall.

gen.cite: Generator coverage/vegetation waiver eligibility (Sec. 126-1307(d))
gen.text: Administrative waiver of applicable limitations of (impermeable) coverage, vegetation removal and developed area may be issued specifically for HVAC and emergency electrical power generators, or solar energy system components up to the minimum necessary required for each respective improvement. Properties developed after June 7, 2022, are NOT eligible for an administrative waiver for HVAC or emergency electrical power generators but may request approval of a variance from the planning commission. The waiver granted must be the minimum necessary to mitigate the hardship demonstrated.

gen.cite: Generator compliance verification (Sec. 126-1308)
gen.text: No completion certificate or other final city approval shall be issued by the city manager, or city manager's designee, for a permanently installed electrical power generator until the city has measured the sound pressure level of the permitted generator and determined that it complies with the permit and the standards in section 126-1307. A permanently installed electrical power generator must remain in compliance with the permit and the standards in section 126-1307. The measurement of sound pressure levels shall be performed in conformance with Code of Ordinances, section 30-67.

equip.cite: Accessory structure requirements (Sec. 126-852)
equip.text: (a) Height. Accessory structures shall comply with the height limitations for principal structures, but in no event shall an accessory structure exceed the height of a principal structure located on the same lot. (b) Separation. Accessory buildings or structures shall be at least ten feet from any principal building located on the same lot, unless attached to and an integral part of such principal building, and shall be at least six feet from any other accessory building or structure located on the same lot. (c) Side and rear yard setbacks. Accessory buildings and structures shall comply with the side and rear yard setback requirements for a principal structure, except [for revetments, seawalls, erosion control structures, docks, boat davits and boat lifts]. (d) Open body of water setback. Accessory buildings and structures shall comply with the open body of water setback requirements for a principal structure, except [docks, boat davits, boat lifts, revetments, seawalls, conservation-land boardwalks, certain driveway crossings and de minimis impacts].

equip.cite: Accessory structures in front yards (Sec. 126-853)
equip.text: Accessory buildings are prohibited in actual front yard areas (between principal structure and front lot line), unless the accessory building is located more than 150 feet from the front lot line. All accessory structures are prohibited within required front yard setbacks (including all street-side setbacks for multiple-frontage lots), except for: (1) Ground-level walkways, driveways, bike paths, and parking areas...; (2) UTILITY FACILITIES; (3) Lamp posts and mailboxes; (4) Planters and statuary up to three feet in height; and (5) Street graphics in accordance with chapter 106.

equip.cite: Height exceptions (Sec. 126-932)
equip.text: The height limitations of [the listed chapters and articles] shall not apply to detached water towers, bird nesting platforms, public utility structures, anti-bird nesting devices of a type approved by the building official and installed a maximum of 16 inches above the top of a chimney, and [continued] - see also Sec. 126-1534 for telecommunications devices.

equip.cite: Encroachment upon open areas (Sec. 126-931)
equip.text: No open area, contiguous to any building, shall be encroached upon or reduced in any manner except in conformance with the yard setback, lot, area, building location, percentage of developed area, off-street parking space and such other regulations designated elsewhere... In the event of any such unlawful encroachment or reduction, such building shall be deemed in violation of this chapter and is hereby declared a public nuisance and the certificate of occupancy for such building shall become null and void.

equip.cite: Required yards and multiple-frontage lots (Secs. 126-937, 126-933)
equip.text: Every lot must provide a front, rear and side yards equivalent to at least the yard setbacks required for the zone in which it is located. All front yards must face upon a public or private street. Where a lot is bounded by more than one street, the front yard setback requirement shall be met on each abutting street; provided that on lots qualifying under the 'existing parcels' provision (section 86-92) which are of insufficient width or depth to meet this requirement, the principal structure may project as close to the abutting side or rear street as one-half the setback requirement.

equip.cite: Minimum distance between buildings (Sec. 126-939)
equip.text: In all zoning districts, except for the reconstruction of buildings in the Resort Housing District, the minimum distance between any two buildings on the same lot shall be either 20 feet or the distance required under the formula S = (1a + 1b + ha + hb) / 6, whichever is greater.

equip.cite: Coastal Construction Control Line (Sec. 126-1052 series / Resort Housing)
equip.text: Pursuant to Policy 3.1 in the Coastal Zone Protection Element (Section 3.2.1) of the Sanibel Plan, new development and redevelopment in the Gulf Beach Zone (i.e., seaward of the 1975 Coastal Construction Control Line) is prohibited.

equip.cite: Noise from mechanical equipment in certain operations (Sec. 126-... p.952 of the PDF)
equip.text: In connection with the permitted operations, no mechanical equipment may be used of a nature or sufficient size which would result in the production of noise outside the boundaries of the parcel that would constitute [a violation], and such equipment shall be placed at a minimum distance of 50 feet from the side and rear lines of the parcel.

fort_myers_beach.name: Fort Myers Beach
fort_myers_beach.source: Land Development Code (Code of Ordinances Chapter 34), Article III Zoning District Regulations. Conventional districts: Table 34-3, Dimensional Regulations in C

gen.cite: Mechanical equipment including generators - setback encroachment (Sec. 34-638(d)(1)g)
gen.text: Mechanical equipment such as air conditioners, GENERATORS, service panels, meters, and pool equipment, associated with new homes, may encroach up to three feet into rear and waterbody primary structure setbacks but must meet the same street and side setbacks as the building it serves. 1. On lots where the side setbacks are not equal on both sides, mechanical equipment may not be placed on the side of the house with the smaller setback unless the smaller setback is 20 feet wide or more. 2. For existing homes, mechanical equipment may be replaced or elevated in the original location it was installed, in conformance with prior regulations. 3. New, elevated, mechanical equipment, for existing homes, may be located or relocated into the rear, side or side street setback. The equipment may encroach no more than three feet or the same encroachment of the existing equipment, whichever is greater. An access ladder may be installed which encroaches no more than three feet into the side yard or side street setback and is removable or movable.

equip.cite: Essential services exemption from setbacks (Secs. 34-638(d)(1)e, 34-1617)
equip.text: Sec. 34-638(d)(1)e: 'Essential services. Essential services and essential service equipment shall not be required to meet the minimum setbacks for the district wherein located (see § 34-1617 of this chapter).' Sec. 34-1617: 'Essential services or essential service equipment shall be exempt from the property development regulations which set forth minimum lot size, area, dimensions, and setbacks, except that above-ground essential services or essential service equipment may not be placed closer than three feet to any sidewalk or bike path or to the right-of-way of Estero Boulevard.'

equip.cite: Essential service equipment screening and buffering (Sec. 34-1616)
equip.text: (a) Structures or equipment (excluding transmission poles) exceeding three feet in height, or which individually or collectively on the same parcel exceed 27 cubic feet in volume, must be of neutral, non-glare color or finish so as to make them as visually unobtrusive as possible. (b) Structures or equipment (excluding transmission poles) exceeding three feet in height, or which individually or collectively on the same parcel exceed 80 cubic feet in volume, must be of neutral, non-glare color or finish and be shielded on all sides by shrubs at least three feet high at time of planting consistent with the requirements of § 10-420 of this LDC.

equip.cite: Essential service structures per residential block (Sec. 34-1615)
equip.text: Not more than one structure or group of structures which collectively exceed 150 cubic feet in volume shall be permitted on the same side of a street within any residential block, unless a minimum separation of four lot widths is observed between the structures.

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical appurtenances above the height limit (Sec. 34-631(b)(3))
equip.text: Mechanical or structural appurtenances such as elevator and stairwell enclosures, air conditioning equipment, and antennas may also extend above the height limit provided these appurtenances: a. Do not exceed 250 square feet per type; and b. Screening is provided as required by this code (see, for example, § 6-2(f) of this LDC for rooftop mechanical equipment).

equip.cite: Accessory structure setbacks - side and rear (Sec. 34-1174(d))
equip.text: Unless the side or rear property line abuts a body of water, the following setbacks shall apply: (1) Residential accessory buildings and structures. Except as provided in §§ 34-1175 and 34-1176, all accessory residential buildings and structures shall be set back a minimum of: a. Five feet from any rear property line that does not have access to an alley. b. Zero feet from any rear property line that is served by an alley. c. For non-waterfront lots, five feet from any side property line. d. For waterfront lots, the same distance as is required from any side property line for principal buildings in that zoning district. (2) Commercial and resort accessory buildings and structures shall be set back: a. In accordance with the side and rear setback requirements for a principal building in that zoning district or the minimum buffering requirements of ch. 10, whichever is greater, when abutting any district other than commercial or resort. b. When abutting another commercial or resort zoning district: 1. Rear setbacks are not required. 2. For non-waterfront lots, side setbacks are not required. 3. For waterfront lots, the same distance as is required from any side property line for principal buildings in that zoning district.

equip.cite: Accessory structure setback from streets and water (Sec. 34-1174(b),(c))
equip.text: (b) No accessory use, building or structure shall be located closer to a street right-of-way line or street easement than the principal building, except for fences and walls, signs, outdoor display of merchandise, garbage enclosures, a single flagpole on a lot, certain recreation facilities accessory to multifamily or hotel/motel uses, as provided for in the exceptions to setbacks in § 34-638(d), and on through lots. (c) No building or structure (except marine structures, which are subject to ch. 26, article II) may be located closer to a bay, canal, or other body of water than the minimum setbacks required in § 34-638(d)(3).

equip.cite: Gulf of Mexico and waterbody setbacks (Sec. 34-638(d)(3))
equip.text: a. Gulf of Mexico. Except as provided in this section or elsewhere in this code, no building or structure shall be placed closer to the Gulf of Mexico than set forth in ch. 6, articles III and IV of this LDC, or 50 feet from mean high-water, whichever is the most restrictive. See also special regulations for the EC zoning district in § 34-652 of this chapter and the coastal zone restrictions in § 34-1575 of this chapter.

equip.cite: Wetlands buffer (Sec. 34-638(c))
equip.text: New development must maintain a 75-foot separation between wetlands and buildings or other impervious surfaces, in accordance with Policy 4-C-12 of the Fort Myers Beach Comprehensive Plan. This requirement does not apply to lawfully existing subdivided lots, nor to a previously approved development order to the extent it cannot reasonably be modified to comply.

equip.cite: Other setback encroachments (Sec. 34-638(d)(1)b,c,d)
equip.text: b. Overhangs. An overhang which is part of a building may be permitted to encroach into any setback as long as the overhang does not extend more than three feet into the setback and does not permit any balcony, porch, or living space located above the overhang to extend into the setback. c. Shutters. A shutter which is attached to a building may be permitted to encroach one foot into the setbacks. d. jacksonville.name: Jacksonville
jacksonville.source: Jacksonville Ordinance Code, Chapter 656 (Zoning Code), Part 3 "Schedule of District Regulations" (Sec. 656.300-656.399.75), read district section by district s

gen.cite: Air conditioning compressors and other equipment serving the main structure - Sec. 656.403(a)(3)
gen.text: "Accessory uses shall not be located in required front or side yards in a residential district except as follows:... (3) Air conditioning compressors or other equipment designed to serve the main structure may be located in a required yard but not less than two feet from a lot line." (CD656:416). This is the provision that governs a standby generator pad serving a house; the Zoning Code contains no separate section naming generators.

gen.cite: Yard encroachments - Sec. 656.406
gen.text: "Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky, except as otherwise permitted in the Zoning Code and except as follows: (a) Sills, belt courses, chimneys, fireplaces or pilasters may not project over two feet in a required yard. (b) Fire escapes, stairways and balconies which are unroofed and unenclosed may not project over three feet into a required side yard of a multiple-dwelling, hotel or motel. (c) Awnings, hoods, roof overhangs, canopies, bay windows or marquees may not project over three feet into a required yard. (d) Flagpoles, fences, walls and hedges or ornamental features are permitted in required yards, subject to the provisions of Section 656.402. (e) Required off-street parking shall not be located in a required front yard in an Residential Low Density (RLD) District.". This list does NOT name generators, A/C equipment or pool equipment; those are handled by Sec. 656.403(a)(3).

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures generally - Sec. 656.403(a), (d)
equip.text: "Accessory uses and structures are permitted in all districts, if those uses and structures are of a nature customarily incidental and clearly subordinate to a permitted or permissible principal use or structure and, unless otherwise provided, these uses and structures are located on the same lot (or a contiguous lot in the same ownership) as the principal use." "(a) Accessory uses shall not be located in required front or side yards in a residential district except as follows: (1) On double frontage lots, through lots and corner lots, accessory uses and structures may be located only in a required side yard except where a double frontage lot has frontage on a navigable waterway. (2) Accessory structures for the housing of persons shall not be located in a required yard." "(d) Accessory use height: (1) Accessory uses or structures less than 15 feet in height may be located in a required rear of side yard, but not less than five feet from a lot line. (2) Accessory uses or structures greater than 15 feet in height shall meet the same setback requirements as the primary structure and shall not exceed the height of the primary structure. (3) Accessory uses or structures greater than 15 feet in height in the Residential Rural-Acre (RR-Acre) Zoning District, or on a lot at least one acre in size, shall meet the same setback requirements as the primary structure and may exceed the height of the primary structure, up to a maximum height of 35 feet."

equip.cite: Essential services
equip.text: "Essential services, including water, sewer, gas, telephone, radio, television and electric, meeting the performance standards and development criteria set forth in Part 4" are listed as a permitted use (and in several districts also as a permissible use by exception) in every base district in Part 3.

equip.cite: Height measurement and rooftop equipment - Sec. 656.1601 definition of height
equip.text: "Spires, belfries, cupolas, and chimneys that are not intended for human occupancy shall not count towards height measurement. Other roof-top appurtenance and mechanical equipment not intended for human occupancy may be placed above the roof line provided it is not visible from an adjacent right-of-way."

equip.cite: Height limits - Sec. 656.405
equip.text: "The height limitations contained in Part 3 do not apply to spires, belfries, cupolas, antennas, water tanks, ventilators, chimneys or other appurtenances usually required to be placed above the roof level and not intended for human occupancy; provided, however, that notwithstanding the permitted maximum height limitations allowed in the various zoning districts, no structure (including appurtenances and structures normally erected above roof level) shall be erected to a height above adjacent ground level exceeding the most restrictive of the following: (a) Five hundred feet. (b) The height zones established in Subpart C, Part 10. (c) Elevations prescribed by the Federal Aviation Administration..."

equip.cite: Riverside/Avondale Zoning Overlay - ground-level mechanical equipment, Sec. 656.399.29
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment at ground level shall be placed on the parking lot side of the building away from view from adjacent Street frontage and shall be screened from view of any street by fencing, vegetations, or by being incorporated into a building. Loading docks, truck parking, outdoor storage, utility meters, HVAC equipment, trash dumpsters, trash compaction, and other service functions should be incorporated into the overall design of the building by walls of a material compatible with the material, style, color, texture, pattern, trim, and details of the main building and landscaping." (CD656:301).

equip.cite: Renew Arlington Zoning Overlay - screening and separation, Sec. 656.399.62
equip.text: "Any exterior garbage receptacles, dumpsters, open storage areas or mechanical equipment must be screened from view from Street rights-of-way and adjacent residential uses with 95 percent opaque material that is visually similar to materials used on the nearest facade of the principal structure, such as wood or vinyl. Additionally, garbage receptacles, dumpsters, open storage areas and/or mechanical equipment must be a minimum 25 feet from adjacent residential uses and shall be incorporated into the main structure as a part of new construction or Major Renovation, as defined in this Subpart." This clause is repeated for each Renew Arlington character area.

equip.cite: San Marco Overlay Zone - building separation, Sec. 656.399.7
equip.text: "The area that is considered the width separation between buildings shall meet the following standards: (i) Mechanical equipment, service areas may not be located in between the buildings. (ii) Pool enclosures are not permitted in this location. (iii) Landscape and pedestrian walkways are permitted within the buildings."

equip.cite: Downtown Overlay Zone - rooftop mechanical equipment, Sec. 656.361.6.2
equip.text: "Permanent roof structures such as mechanical equipment, elevator overruns, stair towers, and permanent roofs over bars or other areas will not count toward the height calculation except within the Riverfront Zones B and C, as shown on Table 6.2.H and Map 6.2.H." and "All mechanical equipment, appurtenances, and access areas shall be intentionally grouped and screened architecturally within fully cover[ed]...". Rooftop features including mechanical equipment "may extend up to 15 feet above the building roof, as long as the combined coverage of all features listed in this subsection does not exceed 20 percent of the roof area, or 25 percent if the total includes stair or elevator penthouses or screened mechanical equipment".

equip.cite: Performance standards - Sec. 656.417
equip.text: "A use, building, structure, development or process regulated by the Zoning Code shall comply with local, State and federal regulations related to environmental protection, including those applicable to noise, vibration, smoke, radiation, odor, toxic emissions and water or air pollution, and the standards adopted or implemented by the Neighborhoods Department.". No numeric residential noise limit for mechanical equipment is printed in the Zoning Code; the only dBA figures are the IH district's 75 dbA (adjoining a commercial district) and 65 dbA (adjoining a residential district) in Sec. 656.323(i).

equip.cite: Mechanical and fire equipment (noise) - Sec. 36-8
equip.text: "It shall be unlawful to operate mechanical and fire equipment, including air conditioning compressors, pumps, blowers, exhaust fans, filters and other similar noise-producing equipment, in all residential, institutional, commercial and industrial zoned property, when such equipment emits noise which exceeds the following noise levels, measured at the receiving property line nearest to the source; such sound levels shall be measured with a sound level meter manufactured according to standards prescribed by the American National Standards Institute:" Maximum permitted sound level in dBA at the property line or beyond - Single-family: 5 dBA above ambient or maximum of 55 dBA (10:00 p.m.-7:00 a.m.) / 10 dBA above ambient or maximum of 60 dBA (7:00 a.m.-10:00 p.m.). Multifamily, institutional, parks and noise-sensitive zones: 5 dBA above ambient or max 60 dBA / 10 dBA above ambient or max 65 dBA. Retail commercial (offices, retail, restaurants and movies): 5 dBA above ambient or max 65 dBA / 10 dBA above ambient or max 65 dBA. Wholesale commercial and industrial: 5 dBA above ambient or max 70 dBA / 10 dBA above ambient or max 75 dBA.

equip.text: "All electrical, heating, air conditioning equipment, ventilation, plumbing, and other service facilities, including duct work, shall be elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus one foot...". Also Sec. 20-1: "Location of all main electrical and mechanical equipment, structures, storage facilities for chemicals, explosives, buoyant materials, flammable liquids or other toxic materials which could be hazardous to the public health, safety, and welfare in a manner which will..."

equip.cite: Emergency power generators - assisted living / certain facilities
equip.text: "[T]he plan must provide for components that address emergency evacuation transportation; adequate shelter arrangements; post-disaster activities, including provisions for emergency power generators with sufficient capacity to power the facility's fixed or portable heating, ventilation and air conditioning ('HVAC') system in order to maintain an ambient temperature of 81 degrees or less in one or more designated rooms for a period of a minimum of 96 hours in the event of the loss of electrical power.". This is an operational/capacity requirement, not a siting or setback rule.

tallahassee.name: Tallahassee
tallahassee.source: Land Development Code, Chapter 10 (Zoning), Article IV. Division 3 (Secs. 10-236 to 10-272) gives one 'Development Standards' chart per district, keyed by use c

gen.cite: Electrical generators, air compressors, large A/C compressors and transformers
gen.text: Sec. 10-411(b)(3)a: 'New development. No exterior utility accessories used for service loading entries, parking for commercial vehicles with cargo volumes greater than ten cubic yards (referred to below as "loading zones"), solid waste facilities with capacities greater than one cubic yard (referred to below as "trash enclosures"), nonresidential air conditioning compressors greater than ten tons, air compressors, electrical generators, or overhead electrical transformers shall be located nearer than ten feet from any property line or 200 feet from any property line adjoining a low-density residential zoning district.' Sec. 10-411(b)(3)b defines 'protected residential' for the relief provisions as any property zoned RP-1, RP-2, RP-MH, RP-R, RP-UF, R-1, R-2, R-3, R-5, UF, LP, MH or RA. The relief provisions that follow (locating to within 50 feet with a buffer) are written for loading zones and trash enclosures only - the code does not extend them to generators or compressors. Sec. 10-411(b)(3)e exempts subsection (b)(3) where the adjacent protected residential property is already developed with a legally existing non-conforming use, where it is an isolated protected-residential property of fewer than three units on fewer than three contiguous lots, and for a change of use that is not more intense.

equip.cite: General accessory structure setback
equip.text: Sec. 10-411(a)(2): 'All accessory structures shall setback ten feet from any property line, except where the permitted principal development setback is less in which case the accessory structure shall comply with the principal structure setback.' Sec. 10-411(a)(3): 'Accessory structures shall not be located in a required buffer or landscape area nor in the front yard or side corner yard.' Sec. 10-411(a)(4): accessory structures are included in all calculations of impervious surface and stormwater runoff. Sec. 10-411(a)(6): 'Accessory structures shall be located at least six feet from any other structure on the same lot.'

equip.cite: Hazardous storage accessory buildings
equip.text: Sec. 10-411(b)(1): 'No accessory buildings used for industrial storage of hazardous, incendiary, noxious or deadly materials shall be located nearer than 100 feet from any property line.'

equip.cite: Stormwater earthwork near residential
equip.text: Sec. 10-411(b)(3)d: 'No earthwork disturbances for stormwater swales, detention ponds or retention ponds shall be located nearer than 30 feet from any (existing) property line adjoining a low-density residential zoning district.' Redevelopment projects must comply with a 15-foot distance for retention or detention ponds.

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening in the MMTD and Downtown Overlay
equip.text: Sec. 10-284.3(a)(3): 'Roof-mounted mechanical equipment shall not be visible from adjacent right-of-way. All mechanical equipment and trash containment devices, including compactors and dumpsters, shall be screened from public right of way and placed in the second (2nd) or third (3rd) layer.' Sec. 10-282.2(g) (design review districts): 'All outdoor mechanical equipment, including heating, air conditioning, and ventilation systems, shall be placed on the roof, to the rear or side of a building, or be otherwise visually screened from the street. In no case shall mechanical equipment be allowed along the street frontage.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening in other districts
equip.text: R-4, Sec. 10-247 note 10.f: 'Solid waste facilities and mechanical equipment serving non-residential facilities shall be screened with a material consistent with the principle structure.' NBO (Sec. 10-266), GO-1 (Sec. 10-270) and GO-2 (Sec. 10-271) each carry: 'The off-site visual impacts associated with outdoor service functions or areas such as loading areas, trash collections, outdoor storage, or mechanical equipment shall be mitigated by the use of screening material consistent with the materials and design treatments of the primary facade of the primary building and/or evergreen landscape plant material.' IC, Sec. 10-264 note 7.b: 'All buildings shall screen utility connections, roof top equipment and meter locations with materials found on the building exterior or with evergreen landscaping.' Sec. 10-320 exemption list: rooftop mechanical equipment added to an existing building is exempt from a certificate of appropriateness 'if the mechanical equipment is setback from the edges of the roof and screened from the street.'

equip.cite: Swimming pools
equip.text: Sec. 10-411(c): 'Swimming pools shall be permitted only in side and rear yards, and shall not encroach into any required building setback.' All pools must be enclosed by a wall, fence or other substantial structure not less than four feet in height with self-closing and self-latching doors.
