gen.cite: Emergency generators in residential districts (Sec. 10-66(3), PDF p.494-495)
gen.text: "The following provisions shall apply to emergency generators in all residential districts. Emergency generators installed in all residential districts shall be exempt from the sound rating values set forth in section 10-72, Code of Ordinances when operated during power outages; provided however, in no event shall the sound rating value of emergency generators in any residential district exceed 72 dBA. Emergency generators in all residential districts may be operated for testing purposes 1 time for a period not to exceed 30 minutes in any 7-day period. Testing of emergency generators in all residential districts is permitted between the hours of 11 a.m. through 5 p.m., Monday through Saturday. No testing of emergency generators in any residential districts is permitted on Sundays or federal holidays." NOTE: this is a noise and testing-hours rule. It sets no distance from a property line, window, air intake or LP tank.

gen.cite: Accessory structures in residential districts (Sec. 28-1295(2), PDF p.1663)
gen.text: "Accessory structures in residential districts that do not meet the definition of an accessory building, including, but not limited to, permanently affixed children's play apparatus, landscape trellises, barbecues and similar accessory structures, shall be subject to the following requirements: (a) In no event shall an accessory structure be located in a required front yard, or in any location between the main building and the front plot line. (b) In the event an accessory structure is located in a required yard, such accessory structure shall not exceed 15 feet in height; and shall be a minimum of 5 feet from any plot line. An accessory structure that is not located in a required yard shall not be subject to the requirements of this subsection (2)(b)." -- This is the nearest thing in Chapter 28 to a generator-pad rule: a pad-mounted generator is an accessory structure, so in a residential district it may not sit in a required front yard or between the house and the front plot line, and if it sits in a required side or rear yard it must be at least 5 ft from any plot line.

gen.cite: Permitted encroachments into required yards (Secs. 28-1352 and 28-1353, PDF p.1686-1690)
gen.text: The encroachment list names roof overhangs, eaves, gutters and decorative architectural features (36 in.), sills, belt courses, pilasters and chimneys (12 in.), covered front porches, open balconies/walkways/stairways, porte-cocheres, canopies and marquees, fire escapes (5 ft), accessory buildings and structures where specifically authorized by § 28-1295 or the district regulations, uncovered patios, terraces and pool decks (not more than 4 ft into a required front yard and not closer than 7 ft to an interior plot line), driveways, fences, walls, gates and hedges, permanently affixed decorative water features in a required front yard, and screen enclosures with a screen roof (no closer than 7 ft to an interior plot line). Generators, air-conditioning condensers, pool pumps and mechanical equipment are NOT named anywhere in this division, so they get no encroachment allowance.

gen.cite: Generators serving wireless communications facilities (Secs. 28-1442 area, PDF p.1767 and p.1772)
gen.text: "Any unstaffed communication building shall be a permanent structure not to exceed 250 square feet in floor area, but may be up to 400 square feet in floor area if the city approves placement of a generator within such building." And for a related unstaffed equipment building: "shall not contain more than 250 square feet of gross floor area but may be up to 400 square feet in gross floor area if the city approves placement of a generator within such equipment facility, but should not be more than ten feet in height." Aggregate floor-area caps of 1,200 / 1,600 / 2,000 sq ft apply where the installation accommodates three, four or five users and "provisions are made for a generator for each user on the site".

gen.cite: Outdoor cooking appliances, including LP-gas (Sec. 7-x, PDF p.388)
gen.text: "'Outdoor cooking appliance' shall mean any portable or non-portable cooking appliance, grill, stove, or smoker, fueled or powered by electricity, wood, charcoal, liquefied petroleum gas, natural gas, gasoline, kerosene, naphtha, alcohol or other liquid or gaseous fuel used or intended to be used outdoors. Outdoor cooking appliances shall not be used less than 20 feet from the exterior wall..." (Recorded because it is the only LP-gas separation distance printed in the code; it governs grills and smokers, not tanks serving a generator.)

equip.cite: Air conditioning equipment placement (Sec. 10-66(1)-(2), PDF p.494)
equip.text: "It shall be unlawful to create any excessive and unnecessary loud noise by the use or operation of any noise-creating air conditioner, compressor unit, power fan or blower or the electric motor or any engine used to drive such device... unless such noise is muffled and deadened by adequate noise suppression and muffling devices..." "Upon the effective date of this article, the location and placement of all new or replacement air conditioning equipment on the outside of the building or structure it serves shall be specified by the city manager or designee, and shall be so shown and designated on the plans and specifications for such construction as the city manager or designee directs. In addition, the city manager or designee shall require compliance with all reasonable sound abatement measures and sound screening which may be necessary or desirable to prevent such air conditioning equipment from creating excessive or unnecessary noise. All such air conditioning equipment hereafter installed in the city shall carry the manufacturer's certification of the sound rating thereof... which sound rating shall not exceed a value which will cause the limits of section 10-72 to be exceeded." -- i.e. outdoor A/C placement is set case by case by the city manager, not by a printed setback.

equip.cite: Noise limits that govern fixed mechanical equipment (Sec. 10-72, PDF p.500-501)
equip.text: "At no point on the boundary of or within a residential area zoned for 1- or 2-family dwellings and as a result of any fixed mechanical or electrical noise source outside of the property in question may the following sound pressure levels be exceeded: Day: 55 dBA. Night: 50 dBA." Apartment-zoned residential: Day 55 / Night 50 dBA. Retail or commercial: Day 60 / Night 60 dBA. Light or restricted industry, at 50 ft or more from the boundary: Day 60 / Night 60 dBA. Industrial, at 50 ft or more: Day 65 / Night 65 dBA. Day is 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.; night is 7:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m.

equip.cite: Accessory buildings in residential districts (Sec. 28-1295(1), PDF p.1662-1663)
equip.text: Maximum height of an accessory building located wholly or partly in a required yard is 15 ft (governed instead by the district regulations in R-3-A, R-3-B, R-3-C, R-4, R-5 and R-5-A); no more than 1 accessory building per plot may be in a required yard; it may never be in a required front yard or between the main building and the front plot line; if in a required yard it may only be in the rear yard, a minimum of 5 ft from any plot line (including eaves) and, on a corner plot, in the quarter section furthest from the street(s); it is limited to 500 sq ft; it must be at least 10 ft from any main building; and no accessory building may be in the required rear yard of a waterfront plot except gazebos, chickee/tiki huts or similar open-air accessory buildings.

equip.cite: Accessory buildings and structures in nonresidential districts (Sec. 28-1295(3), PDF p.1663)
equip.text: "Accessory buildings and accessory structures in nonresidential districts shall be limited to no greater than 15 feet in height, shall not be located in a required front yard, shall be at least 10 feet from any rear or side plot line, shall be architecturally compatible with the main building, and shall be maintained in the condition as approved. Covered parking, excluding parking structures, shall be considered an accessory structure, and shall not be located closer than 10 feet from any interior plot line. Parking structures shall be subject to the same required yards as a main building."

equip.cite: Required yards must otherwise be clear (Sec. 28-1351, PDF p.1686)
equip.text: "Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed by any use or structure, from the ground to the sky, except as expressly provided in this division or as otherwise expressly provided in this Code."

equip.cite: Screening and walls where a nonresidential district abuts a residential one (Sec. 28-304, PDF p.1429)
equip.text: "Where a motel-business, business or commercial district directly abuts on a residential district without any division or separator between them such as a street, alley, park or other public open space, any plot in the above districts which abuts on the residential district shall be provided with a yard at least 25 feet in depth adjacent to the residentially zoned property... a 6-foot unpierced masonry wall, smoothly finished on both sides, shall be constructed in such a manner as to preclude horizontal vision... Where an industrial district directly abuts on a residential district, any plot in the industrial district which abuts on the residential district shall be provided with a yard at least 30 feet in depth adjacent to the residentially zoned property."

R-2.sideNote: "There shall be provided a side yard on each side of every plot not less than 10 feet in width; provided, that in those areas which were subdivided prior to August 18, 1941, with plots less than 60 feet in width, the side yards shall not be less than 5 feet in width.
R-2.rearNote: "Every plot in R-2 districts other than a corner or through plot shall have a rear yard not less than 25 feet in depth."
R-2.heightNote: "No building or structure in R-2 districts shall be erected or altered to a height exceeding 25 feet. Permitted nonresidential buildings except accessory structures may be erected or altered to a height not exceeding 50 feet, if approved by the council as being not injurious to surrounding property..." (§ 28-391).
R-2.note: Two-family dwellings. § 28-389: max 5 units per gross acre; plot not less than 13,000 sq ft and not less than 100 ft wide; however in areas subdivided prior to November 1, 1968 a lot of record not less than 75 ft wide and 7,500 sq ft may be used for a duplex or single-family residence, and 25-ft lots of record may be combined by unity of title to form plots of not less than 75 ft wide and 8,800 sq ft for duplexes.

R-3.frontNote: "Every plot in R-3 districts shall have a front yard not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 200 feet in length. On a corner plot only 1 street line shall be considered as a front plot line for setback purposes."
R-3.sideNote: "A side yard shall be provided on each side of every plot not less than 25 feet in width for a building or structure up to and including 200 feet in length; provided, that in those areas which were subdivided of record prior to August 18, 1941, for plots less than 60 feet in width the side yards shall not be less than 7 1/2 feet in width."
R-3.heightNote: "No building or structure in R-3 districts shall be erected or altered to a height exceeding 35 feet. Such height limitation shall be subject to the height of buildings as defined in section 28-2." (§ 28-421).
R-3.note: Multifamily. Plot: not less than 100 ft wide, 100 ft deep and 20,000 sq ft (15,000 sq ft for a permitted nonresidential structure or use). Max 9 units per gross acre; convalescent/nursing homes max 75 beds per acre. § 28-422(4): for all buildings over 200 ft in length, all front, side and rear yards are each increased 1 ft for each additional 2 ft of length.

R-3-A.frontNote: "Every plot shall have a front or street yard not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height; provided, that when the building or structure exceeds 25 feet in height, the yard shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof until the maximum height has been reached."
R-3-A.sideNote: "A side yard shall be provided on each side of every plot of not less than 15 feet in width; provided, that when the building or structure exceeds 25 feet in height such yards shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof until the maximum height has been reached."
R-3-A.rearNote: "Every plot shall have a rear yard not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height; provided, that when the structure exceeds 25 feet in height, the depth of the rear yard shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof above 25 feet in height until the maximum height has been reached.
R-3-A.heightNote: "No building or structure or part thereof in an R-3-A district shall be erected to a height exceeding 75 feet." "No accessory building or structure shall be erected to exceed 15 feet. When such accessory building serves more than 1 multifamily structure, the planning and zoning board may approve an increase in height of such accessory buildings to 25 feet..." (§ 28-451).
R-3-A.note: Plot: not less than 125 ft wide, 100 ft deep and 25,000 sq ft (§ 28-449). Max 15 units per gross acre; convalescent/nursing homes max 75 BPA. The first 5 ft of any yard abutting a street right-of-way must be landscaped, increased to 25 ft where the street separates the district from a single-family district (§ 28-455). No lot-coverage percentage is printed. §§ 28-446 to 28-455.

R-3-B.frontNote: "Every plot shall have a front or street yard not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height; provided, that when the building or structure exceeds 25 feet in height, the yard shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof until the maximum height has been reached."
R-3-B.sideNote: "A side yard shall be provided on each side of every plot of not less than 15 feet in width; provided, that when the building or structure exceeds 25 feet in height such yards shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof until the maximum height has been reached."
R-3-B.rearNote: "Every plot shall have a rear yard not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height; provided, that when the structure exceeds 25 feet in height, the depth of the rear yard shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof above 25 feet in height until the maximum height has been reached.
R-3-B.heightNote: "No building or structure or part thereof in an R-3-B district shall be erected to a height exceeding 50 feet." Accessory buildings 15 ft (25 ft if approved by the planning and zoning board where the accessory building serves more than 1 multifamily structure). (§ 28-481).
R-3-B.note: Plot: not less than 100 ft wide, 100 ft deep and 25,000 sq ft (§ 28-479). Max 15 units per gross acre; convalescent/nursing homes max 75 BPA. No lot-coverage percentage is printed. §§ 28-476 to 28-485.

R-3-C.frontNote: "Every plot shall have a front or street yard not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height; provided, that when the building or structure exceeds 25 feet in height, the yard shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof until the maximum height has been reached."
R-3-C.sideNote: "A side yard shall be provided on each side of every plot of not less than 15 feet in width; provided, that when the building or structure exceeds 25 feet in height such yards shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof until the maximum height has been reached."
R-3-C.rearNote: "Every plot shall have a rear yard not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height; provided, that when the structure exceeds 25 feet in height, the depth of the rear yard shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof above 25 feet in height until the maximum height has been reached.
R-3-C.heightNote: "No building or structure or part thereof in an R-3-C district shall be erected to a height exceeding 50 feet." Accessory buildings 15 ft (25 ft with planning and zoning board approval). (§ 28-511).
R-3-C.note: Plot: not less than 100 ft wide, 100 ft deep and 25,000 sq ft (§ 28-509). Max 13 units per gross acre; convalescent/nursing homes max 75 BPA. No lot-coverage percentage is printed. §§ 28-506 to 28-514.

R-3-D.frontNote: "Any front, street or rear yards of any plot shall be not less than 25 feet in depth. Plots for townhouses, however, as hereinafter defined, shall not be required to have front, street or rear yards of more than 50 feet in depth."
R-3-D.sideNote: "...there shall be provided a side yard of not less than 15 feet in width for every multifamily dwelling or townhouse... Side yards for single and duplex units shall not be less than 10 feet." "For all buildings over 100 feet in length, all setback requirements will be increased by 1 foot for each 1 foot of additional length over the 100-foot dimension."
R-3-D.rearNote: "Any front, street or rear yards of any plot shall be not less than 25 feet in depth... Rear yards abutting a lake or waterway of not less than 60 feet in width need not be greater in depth than 25 feet."
R-3-D.heightNote: "The maximum height of any building in R-3-D districts shall be 25 feet."
R-3-D.note: Plot: not less than 100 ft wide, 100 ft deep and 10,000 sq ft (15,000 sq ft for a permitted nonresidential structure or use). Max 3 units per gross acre. For all yards for nonresidential use the provisions of § 28-422(4) apply. No lot-coverage percentage is printed. Assisted living facilities, convalescent homes and nursing homes are regulated at max 75 beds per acre. §§ 28-536 to 28-544.

R-3-E.frontNote: "Any front, street or rear yards of any plot shall be not less than 25 feet in depth. Plots for townhouses, however, as hereinafter defined, shall not be required to have front, street or rear yards of more than 50 feet in depth."
R-3-E.sideNote: "...there shall be provided a side yard of not less than 15 feet in width for every multifamily dwelling or townhouse... Side yards for single and duplex units shall not be less than 10 feet." "For all buildings over 100 feet in length, all setback requirements will be increased by 1 foot for each 1 foot of additional length over the 100-foot dimension."
R-3-E.rearNote: "Any front, street or rear yards of any plot shall be not less than 25 feet in depth... Rear yards abutting a lake or waterway of not less than 60 feet in width need not be greater in depth than 25 feet."
R-3-E.heightNote: "The maximum height of any building in R-3-E districts shall be 35 feet."
R-3-E.note: Plot: not less than 100 ft wide, 100 ft deep and 10,000 sq ft (15,000 sq ft for a permitted nonresidential structure or use). Max 5 units per gross acre. For all yards for nonresidential use the provisions of § 28-422(4) apply. No lot-coverage percentage is printed. §§ 28-566 to 28-576.

R-3-F.frontNote: "Any front, street or rear yards of any plot shall be not less than 25 feet in depth. Plots for townhouses, however, as hereinafter defined, shall not be required to have front, street or rear yards of more than 50 feet in depth."
R-3-F.sideNote: "...there shall be provided a side yard of not less than 15 feet in width for every multifamily dwelling or townhouse... Side yards for single and duplex units shall not be less than 10 feet." "For all buildings over 100 feet in length, all setback requirements will be increased by 1 foot for each 1 foot of additional length over the 100-foot dimension."
R-3-F.rearNote: "Any front, street or rear yards of any plot shall be not less than 25 feet in depth... Rear yards abutting a lake or waterway of not less than 60 feet in width need not be greater in depth than 25 feet."
R-3-F.heightNote: "The maximum height of any building in R-3-F districts shall be 35 feet." "However, for any property line east of State Road A-1-A which is subject to the coastal construction control line, the maximum height shall be 50 feet." (§ 28-585).
R-3-F.note: Plot: not less than 100 ft wide, 100 ft deep and 10,000 sq ft (15,000 sq ft for a permitted nonresidential structure or use). Max 7 1/2 units per gross acre. For all yards for nonresidential use the provisions of § 28-422(4) apply. No lot-coverage percentage is printed. §§ 28-581 to 28-591.

R-4.frontNote: "All front and street yards in R-4 districts shall be not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height and up to and including 200 feet in length."
R-4.sideNote: "A side yard shall be provided on each side of every plot not less than 25 feet in width for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height and up to and including 200 feet in length."
R-4.rearNote: "Every plot shall have a rear yard not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height and up to and including 200 feet in length. Rear yards abutting a lake or a waterway of not less than 60 feet in width need not be greater than 25 feet in depth."
R-4.heightNote: "No building or structure or part thereof in an R-4 district shall be erected to a height exceeding 50 feet." (§ 28-602).
R-4.note: Multifamily, hotels, motels and apartments. Plot for a hotel, motel or multifamily building: not less than 100 ft wide, 100 ft deep and 25,000 sq ft; plot for a single-family or two-family dwelling: not less than 80 ft wide, 110 ft deep and 8,800 sq ft (§ 28-600). Max 15 units per gross acre; hotels and motels exempt.

R-5.frontNote: "Every plot in an R-5 district shall have a front yard, adjacent to all street frontages, not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height; provided, that when the structure exceeds 25 feet in height, the yard shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet or portion thereof."
R-5.sideNote: "A side yard shall be provided on each side of every plot of not less than 20 feet in width.
R-5.rearNote: "Every plot other than a corner or through plot shall have a rear yard not less than 25 feet in depth for a building or structure up to and including 25 feet in height, provided that when the structure exceeds 25 feet in height, the rear yard shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof."
R-5.heightNote: "No building or structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered in an R-5 district to a height exceeding 85 feet, except within an approved PD master plan of 100 acres or greater, wherein the maximum height shall be 100 feet." (§ 28-641).
R-5.note: Plot: not less than 100 ft wide, 100 ft deep and 25,000 sq ft (§ 28-639). Max 17 1/2 units per gross acre; 1.5 times that for hotel, apartment hotel and motel use. No lot-coverage percentage is printed. §§ 28-636 to 28-645.

R-5-A.frontNote: "Every plot in R-5-A districts shall have a minimum front or street yard of not less than 25 feet in depth; provided that where the structure exceeds 25 feet in height, the front or street yard shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height, until the maximum height of 150 feet has been reached."
R-5-A.sideNote: "A side yard shall be provided on each side of every plot of not less than 25 feet in width; provided that when the structure exceeds 25 feet in height, the side yard shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet in height or portion thereof." Length-based increases apply above 100 ft of building length.
R-5-A.rearNote: § 28-673 prints no rear yard. It prints, instead: "(2) Yards. Yards abutting the Atlantic Ocean shall not be less than 125 feet from the bulkhead line or the mean high-water line." rear is therefore null.
R-5-A.heightNote: "No building or structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered in an R-5-A district to a height exceeding 85 feet. The planning and zoning board, in connection with the site plan approval, may permit an additional 25 feet in height if provision is made to provide an 8 1/2-foot wide public access to the beach adjacent to the site in a manner acceptable to the city attorney." (§ 28-672).
R-5-A.note: Plot: not less than 100 ft wide, 100 ft deep and 25,000 sq ft (§ 28-670). Max 20 units per gross acre. No lot-coverage percentage is printed. §§ 28-667 to 28-676.

NCBD.frontNote: "Every plot in an NCB district shall have front or street setbacks of not less than 25 feet which shall be landscaped."
NCBD.sideNote: "Every plot shall have 5-foot landscaped side yards."
NCBD.rearNote: "Every plot shall have a rear boundary setback of not less than 50 feet. Where no wall is required, then the first 5 feet of the rear yard shall be landscaped."
NCBD.heightNote: "No building or structure or part thereof in an NCB district shall be erected to a height exceeding 25 feet." (§ 28-725).
NCBD.minLotNote: "Any tract of land for which an NCB district application is made shall contain sufficient width and depth to adequately accommodate its proposed use and design. A minimum width of 100 feet and a minimum depth of 100 feet are required for any such plot." (§ 28-722) No minimum plot AREA is printed.
NCBD.note: Neighborhood Convenience Business District; the code writes both "NCBD" (in the § 28-301 list of established districts) and "NCB" (in the division itself).

R-B-1.frontNote: "...for the purpose of this section all yards abutting street frontage in R-B-1 districts shall be considered front yards. For hotel-motel and business building use. Every plot shall have a front or street yard (or yards) not less than 30 feet in depth."
R-B-1.sideNote: "For hotel-motel use. A side yard shall be provided on each side of every plot of not less than 10 feet in width... For business buildings only. A side yard shall be provided on each side of every plot of not less than 10 feet in width. Required side yards of 10 feet may be combined to 25 feet on 1 side only of the plot."
R-B-1.rearNote: "For hotel-motel use. Every plot other than a corner lot shall have a rear yard of not less than 25 feet in depth." (§ 28-748(3)(b), for business buildings only, repeats the 10-ft side yard language rather than stating a rear yard.)
R-B-1.heightNote: "No building or structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered in an R-B-1 district to a height exceeding 50 feet." (§ 28-746).
R-B-1.note: Motel-Business District. Plot used for other than a multifamily dwelling: not less than 100 ft wide, 150 ft deep and 15,000 sq ft (§ 28-744). Not less than 550 sq ft of plot area per hotel/motel room or one-room efficiency (§ 28-747).

B-1.frontNote: "Every plot shall be provided with a yard not less than 10 feet in depth adjacent to all streets upon which the plot abuts, subject to the provisions of section 28-1552." § 28-1552 adds that the street yards along the west side of N.E. 2nd Avenue between N.E. 2nd Street and N.E. 6th Street shall not be less than 25 ft in depth.
B-1.sideNote: No side yard is printed for this district. § 28-1551 sets only a rear yard for business districts and § 28-1552 sets only street yards for B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4 and C-1; the division for this district contains a "Yards" section that states a rear yard and a front/street yard and nothing else. side is therefore null, not zero.
B-1.rearNote: "There shall be a rear yard of not less than 10 feet in depth, all or part of which may be supplied by an alley as specified in section 28-1294."
B-1.heightNote: "No building, structure, or part thereof, shall be erected, or altered in a B-1 district to a height exceeding 30 feet; provided, that permitted buildings may be erected or altered to a height not exceeding 50 feet upon consideration of the planning and zoning board and recommendation to the city council...
B-1.note: No minimum plot area or width is printed for this district; the "Area" section (§ 28-781 / 28-801 / 28-826 / 28-851 / 28-875) sets a minimum BUILDING ground floor area, not a lot size. No lot-coverage percentage is printed; intensity is controlled by the FAR schedule in § 28-307 (0.5 for B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4 and C-1). Minimum building ground floor area 1,000 sq ft. §§ 28-776 to 28-782.

B-2.frontNote: "Every plot shall be provided with a yard not less than 10 feet in depth adjacent to all streets upon which the plot abuts, subject to the provisions of section 28-1552." § 28-1552 adds that the street yards along the west side of N.E. 2nd Avenue between N.E. 2nd Street and N.E. 6th Street shall not be less than 25 ft in depth.
B-2.sideNote: No side yard is printed for this district. § 28-1551 sets only a rear yard for business districts and § 28-1552 sets only street yards for B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4 and C-1; the division for this district contains a "Yards" section that states a rear yard and a front/street yard and nothing else. side is therefore null, not zero.
B-2.rearNote: "There shall be a rear yard of not less than 10 feet in depth, all or part of which may be supplied by an alley as specified in section 28-1294."
B-2.heightNote: "No building, structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered in a B-2 district to a height exceeding 50 feet." (§ 28-800).
B-2.note: No minimum plot area or width is printed for this district; the "Area" section (§ 28-781 / 28-801 / 28-826 / 28-851 / 28-875) sets a minimum BUILDING ground floor area, not a lot size. No lot-coverage percentage is printed; intensity is controlled by the FAR schedule in § 28-307 (0.5 for B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4 and C-1). Minimum building ground floor area 1,000 sq ft.

B-3.frontNote: "Every plot shall be provided with a yard not less than 10 feet in depth adjacent to all streets upon which the plot abuts, subject to the provisions of section 28-1552." § 28-1552 adds that the street yards along the west side of N.E. 2nd Avenue between N.E. 2nd Street and N.E. 6th Street shall not be less than 25 ft in depth.
B-3.sideNote: No side yard is printed for this district. § 28-1551 sets only a rear yard for business districts and § 28-1552 sets only street yards for B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4 and C-1; the division for this district contains a "Yards" section that states a rear yard and a front/street yard and nothing else. side is therefore null, not zero.
B-3.rearNote: "There shall be a rear yard of not less than 10 feet in depth, all or part of which may be supplied by an alley as specified in section 28-1294."
B-3.heightNote: "No building, structure, or part thereof shall be erected or altered in a B-3 district to a height exceeding 100 feet; provided, that in those areas lying within 150 feet of a single-family residential district the height shall not exceed 50 feet." (§ 28-825).
B-3.note: No minimum plot area or width is printed for this district; the "Area" section (§ 28-781 / 28-801 / 28-826 / 28-851 / 28-875) sets a minimum BUILDING ground floor area, not a lot size. No lot-coverage percentage is printed; intensity is controlled by the FAR schedule in § 28-307 (0.5 for B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4 and C-1). Central Business District.

B-4.frontNote: "Every plot shall be provided with a yard not less than 10 feet in depth adjacent to all streets upon which the plot abuts, subject to the provisions of section 28-1552." § 28-1552 adds that the street yards along the west side of N.E. 2nd Avenue between N.E. 2nd Street and N.E. 6th Street shall not be less than 25 ft in depth.
B-4.sideNote: No side yard is printed for this district. § 28-1551 sets only a rear yard for business districts and § 28-1552 sets only street yards for B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4 and C-1; the division for this district contains a "Yards" section that states a rear yard and a front/street yard and nothing else. side is therefore null, not zero.
B-4.rearNote: "There shall be a rear yard of not less than 10 feet in depth, all or part of which may be supplied by an alley as specified in section 28-1294."
B-4.heightNote: "No building or structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered in a B-4 district to a height exceeding 50 feet." (§ 28-850).
B-4.note: No minimum plot area or width is printed for this district; the "Area" section (§ 28-781 / 28-801 / 28-826 / 28-851 / 28-875) sets a minimum BUILDING ground floor area, not a lot size. No lot-coverage percentage is printed; intensity is controlled by the FAR schedule in § 28-307 (0.5 for B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4 and C-1). General Business District. Minimum building ground floor area 1,000 sq ft. §§ 28-846 to 28-851.

C-1.frontNote: "Every plot shall be provided with a yard not less than 10 feet in depth adjacent to all streets upon which the plot abuts, subject to the provisions of section 28-1552." § 28-1552 adds that the street yards along the west side of N.E. 2nd Avenue between N.E. 2nd Street and N.E. 6th Street shall not be less than 25 ft in depth.
C-1.sideNote: No side yard is printed for this district. § 28-1551 sets only a rear yard for business districts and § 28-1552 sets only street yards for B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4 and C-1; the division for this district contains a "Yards" section that states a rear yard and a front/street yard and nothing else. side is therefore null, not zero.
C-1.rearNote: "There shall be a rear yard of not less than 10 feet in depth, all or part of which may be supplied by an alley as specified in section 28-1294."
C-1.heightNote: "No building or structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered in a C-1 district to a height exceeding 4 stories or 50 feet." (§ 28-874).
C-1.note: No minimum plot area or width is printed for this district; the "Area" section (§ 28-781 / 28-801 / 28-826 / 28-851 / 28-875) sets a minimum BUILDING ground floor area, not a lot size. No lot-coverage percentage is printed; intensity is controlled by the FAR schedule in § 28-307 (0.5 for B-1, B-2, B-3, B-4 and C-1). Commercial District. Minimum building ground floor area 1,000 sq ft.

MC.heightNote: "No building or structure or part thereof shall be erected or altered in an MC district to a height of more than 25 feet, with the following exceptions: (a) Hospitals shall be limited to a maximum of 150 feet in height.
MC.note: Medical Center District. Every plot not less than 15,000 sq ft (§ 28-924); no minimum width is printed. § 28-927(5): where a building exceeds 25 ft in height, required yards measured from a plot line abutting (or separated by a street, canal or other right-of-way from) a residential zoning district are increased 1 ft for each 2 ft of height over 25 ft.

POI.frontNote: "All POI plots shall have street yards not less than 30 feet in depth. The 30 feet of each street yard commencing from the property line shall be landscaped..."
POI.sideNote: "A side yard shall not be less than 10 feet in width... Whenever a building or structure exceeds 35 feet in height, the side yards shall be increased by 1 foot for each additional 2 feet, or portion thereof, in building height in excess of 35 feet...
POI.rearNote: "All yards which are not street yards or side yards shall be considered rear yards. Each rear yard shall not be less than 25 feet in width. Whenever a building exceeds 35 feet in height, the rear yard shall be increased 1 foot for each additional 5 feet, or portion thereof, in building height in excess of 35 feet...
POI.heightNote: "No building or structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered in a POI district to a height exceeding 50 feet." (§ 28-898).
POI.note: Professional, Office and Institutional District. Plot: not less than 100 ft wide, 200 ft deep and 20,000 sq ft; where the actual depth is less than 200 ft the minimum depth is the actual depth (unless created to circumvent the requirement), but the area requirement must still be met (§ 28-896). FAR 0.78 (§ 28-307(h)). No lot-coverage percentage is printed. §§ 28-891 to 28-899.

City CG.frontNote: This district's development parameters are NOT printed in the Boca Raton code.
City CG.note: Commercial General. FAR 0.5 per § 28-307(j), reduced to 0.35 for a parcel that is neither developed as a multiple use planned development (MUPD) under ULDC Section 6.8 nor as a planned mobility development (PMD) under § 28-937 or § 28-942.

City CHO.frontNote: This district's development parameters are NOT printed in the Boca Raton code.
City CHO.note: Commercial High Office. FAR 0.5 per § 28-307(k). §§ 28-938 to 28-942.

LIRP.frontNote: "The minimum front yard or street yard shall be 100 feet in depth. The first 50 feet from the front plot line shall be fully landscaped. Yards abutting main line railroad rights-of-way shall not be less than 50 feet in depth." (§ 28-980(f)1.)
LIRP.sideNote: "The minimum side and rear yards shall be 35 feet in depth. The first 10 feet from the plot lines shall be fully landscaped." "Where a structure exceeds 50 feet in height, additional front, side and rear yards of 1 foot for each 2 whole feet in height in excess of 50 feet shall be required." (§ 28-980(f)2., 4.)
LIRP.rearNote: Same as side: 35 ft, first 10 ft fully landscaped; requirements for yards adjacent to interior or rear property lines do not apply to buildings or facilities erected adjacent to a railroad siding. (§ 28-980(f)2.-3.)
LIRP.heightNote: "Except as specifically provided in subsection (e), no building or structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered to a height exceeding 85 feet." (§ 28-980(a)) Subsection (e) provides increased maximum height for qualifying new or expanded office buildings.
LIRP.note: Light Industrial and Research Park District. "Required plot area. Each plot shall have an area of not less than 2 1/2 acres and an average width of not less than 250 feet" -- 2.5 acres converted at 43,560 sq ft/acre = 108,900 sq ft; a former City of University Park parcel of record as of January 21, 1971 that was under 2 1/2 acres is exempt. "Percentage of plot covered.

W-1.frontNote: "Every plot in an W-1 district shall have a front landscaped yard not less than 50 feet in depth, unless a greater depth is required under the provisions of section 28-304." "If a plot is separated by a street from a single-family residential district, the street landscaped yard shall be increased to 75 feet in depth from the property line."
W-1.sideNote: "There shall be a minimum landscaped side yard of 35 feet on each side of every plot, unless a greater depth is required under the provisions of section 28-304."
W-1.rearNote: "Every plot shall have a landscaped rear yard not less than 35 feet in depth from the property line, unless a greater depth is required under the provisions of section 28-304."
W-1.heightNote: "No building or structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered in a W-1 district to a height exceeding 50 feet, except for communication antennas which shall be limited to a height that, should an antenna fall to the ground, it shall not extend beyond the boundaries of the plot on which it is located, or to a height limited by federal regulations, whichever is less." (§ 28-1021).

IG/S1.frontNote: "Each plot in an IG/S1 district is required to have a minimum front landscaped yard of 15 feet abutting the street to which it is adjacent. These provisions shall prevail over section 28-304. Structures, equipment, parking, paths or driveways are not permitted in the front landscaped yard." (§ 28-1047(1)).
IG/S1.sideNote: "Side yards. No side yards are required, except as may be required by the fire-rescue services department, but not to exceed 5 feet." (§ 28-1047(2)) -- a conditional standard, so side is null.
IG/S1.rearNote: "Rear yards. No rear yards are required." (§ 28-1047(3)) -- rear is null because the code sets none, not because it is zero.
IG/S1.heightNote: "A building or structure, or part thereof, erected or altered in the IG/S1 district shall be limited to a height not exceeding 20 feet." (§ 28-1048).
IG/S1.note: Industrial General-Special District #1. "Each plot in the IG/S1 district is required to have an area of not less than 10,000 square feet" (§ 28-1044); no minimum width is printed. FAR 0.4 (§ 28-307(p), printed there as "1G/S1"). No lot-coverage percentage is printed. §§ 28-1041 to 28-1053.

M-1.frontNote: "Every plot in an M-1 district shall have a front yard not less than 25 feet in depth, unless a greater depth is required by section 28-304." (§ 28-1075).
M-1.sideNote: "There shall be a side yard on each side of every plot in M-1 districts, not less than 10 feet in width, but side yards may be combined to 20 feet on 1 side only of the plot, excepting on plots abutting on N.W. 20th, N.W. 40th and N.W. 51st Streets, which shall have a minimum side yard of 25 feet, unless a greater width is required by section 28-304."
M-1.rearNote: "Every plot in an M-1 district shall have a rear yard not less than 10 feet in depth, unless a greater depth is required by section 28-304."
M-1.heightNote: "No building or structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered in an M-1 district to a height exceeding 2 stories or 30 feet." (§ 28-1074).
M-1.note: Light Industrial District. No minimum plot area or width is printed. § 28-1078: where a plot directly abuts a railroad right-of-way no setback from that right-of-way is required. The first 5 ft of any yard abutting a street right-of-way must be landscaped, increased to 30 ft if the plot is separated by a street from a single-family district (§ 28-1079). FAR 0.4 (§ 28-307(q)). No lot-coverage percentage is printed.

M-2.frontNote: "Every plot in M-2 districts shall have a front yard not less than 25 feet in depth, unless a greater depth is required by section 28-304."
M-2.sideNote: "There shall be a side yard, on each side of every plot, not less than 10 feet in width, but side yards may be combined to 20 feet on 1 side only of the plot, except on plots abutting on N.W. 20th, N.W. 40th and N.W. 51st Streets, which shall have a minimum side yard of 25 feet, unless a greater width is required in section 28-304."
M-2.rearNote: "Every plot shall have a rear yard not less than 10 feet in depth, unless a greater depth is required by section 28-304."
M-2.heightNote: "No building or structure, or part thereof, shall be erected or altered in an M-2 district to a height exceeding 4 stories or 60 feet." (§ 28-1099) Separately, "No student housing facility shall be erected or altered in the M-2 district to a height exceeding 50 feet" (§ 28-1110(2)).
M-2.note: General Industrial District. No minimum plot area or width is printed for general development; § 28-1104 sets a minimum parcel size for student housing. Max density for student housing 15 du/gross acre. § 28-1102: no setback required from a railroad right-of-way the plot directly abuts. FAR 0.5 (§ 28-307(r)). No lot-coverage percentage is printed. §§ 28-1096 to 28-1110.

M-3.frontNote: "All plots in the M-3 district shall have the following minimum street or front yards, unless a greater depth is required by section 28-304: 1. Twenty-five feet in depth, unless otherwise specified herein. 2. Fifty feet in depth for those plots which have a front or street yard abutting Clint Moore Road, Congress Avenue, Interstate Route 95 or N.W. 51st Street (Yamato Road)."
M-3.sideNote: "Each plot shall have a minimum side yard of 10 feet in depth on each side of the lot, and the side yards may be combined on 1 side only on a plot, unless provided otherwise herein. Side yards for plots abutting Glades Road, N.W. 20th Street, N.W. 40th Street, N.W. 51st Street, Congress Avenue, Clint Moore Road and Interstate Route 95 shall have a minimum side yard of 25 feet in depth.
M-3.rearNote: "Every plot shall have a rear yard of not less than 10 feet in depth, unless a greater depth is required by section 28-304. The first 5 feet of a rear yard shall be landscaped."
M-3.heightNote: "Except as provided herein, a building or structure, or part thereof, shall not be erected or altered in an M-3 district to a height exceeding 30 feet.
M-3.note: Manufacturing Industrial District. "Every plot in M-3 districts shall be not less than 150 feet in width and 1 gross acre (43,560 square feet) in area" (§ 28-1128). "Maximum lot coverage. The gross floor area of any principal building and accessory structures in M-3 districts shall not exceed 60 percent of the plot on which it is constructed" (§ 28-1130). FAR 0.5 (§ 28-307(s)). §§ 28-1122 to 28-1132.1.

equip.text: "On any lot which has a septic system or a septic system drain field located in the rear yard to meet the requirements of the city's lot fill and underground utilities ordinance, Ordinance No. 01-20, one minimum side yard may be reduced to five feet providing:... (4) No equipment or accessory structures may be located within the opposite side yard or within ten feet of the opposite side lot line from the rear of the principal building on that side to a line representing an extension of the rear line of the septic tank drain field; and (5) The change in setbacks is necessary to allow the passage to the rear yard of equipment that is necessary to maintain or replace the septic system."

gen.cite: Mechanical and utility equipment (§ 27-296(s))
gen.text: "Mechanical and utility equipment. Mechanical equipment refers to air conditioning units, emergency generators, pool equipment, and other similar features, whether located on a roof or on ground level. The equipment shall not be located within a utility easement unless it is equipment serving that specific easement. (1) Mechanical equipment and similar features may be located within an interior side yard setback or a rear yard setback. (2) The minimum distance from a property line to the structure shall be no less than the structure's height, but shall be located at least three (3) feet from a side or rear lot line. (3) All equipment shall be screened from view by a fence, wall, or landscape materials as provided for in this Code. (4) These requirements shall not apply to municipal or franchise utilities such as power, phone, cable, communication or drainage equipment which is located within a public utility easement. (5) Mechanical equipment in non-residential districts may be roof mounted provided they: a. Cover no more than 25 percent of the roof area of the structure to which it is attached; b. Extend above the applicable maximum height limit no more than 25 percent of the height limit (unless otherwise allowed in the Code). (6) Mechanical equipment that is roof mounted shall be screened as follows: [the subsection ends there in the published text]."

gen.cite: Communications tower equipment pads (Ch. 27 wireless section)
gen.text: "...placed on the pad shall not exceed a height of eight (8) feet above the pad. The equipment pad shall contain no more than one permanent generator and one above-ground fuel tank (not to exceed two hundred and fifty (250) gallons in size). Each tower may have an underground fuel tank which exceeds the above-ground tank capacity, provided fire department approval is obtained. An eight-foot high opaque or solid PVC fence or a wall, as measured from the finished grade [is required]..."

equip.cite: Accessory uses, general (§ 27-296(a))
equip.text: "Accessory uses shall not be permitted within a required yard or bufferyard area, except as set forth below. In no event shall an accessory use be construed to authorize a use not otherwise permitted in the district in which the principal use is located and in no event shall an accessory use be established prior to the principal use to which it is accessory. Permanent structures shall not be permitted within drainage or utility easements without the prior written approval of the appropriate utilities and the concurrence of the City Engineer and/or Utilities Director."

equip.cite: Liquefied petroleum gas aboveground storage tanks (§ 8-3(d))
equip.text: "(1) Liquefied petroleum gas aboveground storage tanks, with a storage capacity of up to and including two hundred fifty (250) gallons, shall be considered a permitted use in all zoning districts; (2) Liquefied petroleum gas aboveground storage tanks, with a storage capacity greater than two hundred fifty (250) gallons, shall not be permitted in any zoning district; (3) All liquefied petroleum gas aboveground storage tanks shall be located so they minimize, to the extent reasonably practicable, location conflicts with vehicles using driveways and parking areas while remaining accessible for fueling and fire department operations; (4) All liquefied petroleum gas aboveground storage tanks shall be installed, operated and maintained in accordance with all applicable requirements of the city's adopted state minimum building codes, the adopted minimum fire standards and uniform fire standards, and any other city requirements; (5) The placement of liquefied petroleum gas aboveground storage tanks is prohibited on roofs or balconies and shall not be mounted above any structure in any manner whatsoever; (6) No liquefied petroleum gas storage tanks shall be permitted inside buildings or structures with the exception of liquefied petroleum gas cylinders having a maximum capacity of two and five-tenths (2.5) pounds."

equip.cite: Flammable and combustible liquid aboveground tanks (§ 8-3(b),(c))
equip.text: "(b) Flammable liquid aboveground storage tanks are not permitted within any zoning districts. (c)(1) Combustible liquid aboveground storage tanks are prohibited within all residential zoning districts. (2) Combustible liquid aboveground storage tanks, shall have a permit and shall not exceed a storage capacity of up to twelve thousand (12,000) gallons in any one location, shall be considered a permitted use in all nonresidential zoning districts. Such tanks shall comply with UL-2085 listing or equivalent standard, have integral secondary containment, an engineered concrete outer vault, and impact resistance. Such tanks, as required by its location, shall be protected on all sides by six (6) inch, concrete filled, steel bollards set in concrete. Such bollards shall be a minimum of four (4) feet in the ground spaced no more than four (4) feet on center. Tanks with a capacity not exceeding two hundred fifty (250) gallons are permitted to comply with UL-142 listing or similar."

equip.cite: Carports (§ 27-296(g))
equip.text: "Carports shall comply with the structural setbacks of the residential single-family zoning district in which they are proposed to be located."

"(1) Side setback: Same as required structure setback; however, patios on attached multi-family units must maintain at least a 2-foot side setback and outside any dedicated easement. (2) Rear setback: Five feet and outside of any dedicated easements."

equip.cite: Screen enclosures (§ 27-296(x)(3))
equip.text: "a. Rear setback: The rear setback for screen enclosures with screen roofs (regardless of whether the screen enclosure contains a swimming pool) on lots in single family residential or PRD residential zoning districts shall be ten (10) feet from the lot's rear property line to the enclosure's nearest structural point... b. Side setback: The side yard setback shall be the same as the structural setback requirement of the zoning district." Lots in the county-platted RS districts marked with an asterisk in Table 72-4 "are permitted a rear setback of five (5) feet from screen enclosures of pools."

equip.text: "Accessory structure location standards - Applicants may be allowed modifications up to twenty (20) percent of the principal building setback requirement for accessory structures only. For accessory structures proposed on lots that are required to follow residential infill standards according to Section 8.3, the DCO may apply modifications up to fifty (50) percent of the required setback standards as shown in Table 8-2: Infill Development Standards."

equip.cite: Mechanical or utility equipment in the TEC overlays (Section 7.3.2.I(1)c.iii)
equip.text: "Mechanical or utility equipment (e.g. electrical conduits, meters, HVAC equipment) shall be located, screened, and/or shielded to minimize visual and noise impacts on adjacent land uses and public rights-of-way, as follows: 1. In no instance shall mechanical or utility equipment be located within the front yard setback or within five (5) feet of any property line, unless approved by the DCO. 2. Mechanical equipment that is visible from the right-of-way or an adjacent residential land use shall be screened from view with a material that is compatible with the architecture of the principal structure or landscaping. 3. When feasible, roof-mounted mechanical equipment shall be incorporated into the roof design in such a way that it becomes an integral part of the architecture or is concealed from view. 4. Noise-producing mechanical equipment on sites adjacent to properties currently developed with, or eligible for development with, residential uses shall be located and directed away from neighboring homes, and, where feasible, shielded with noise-attenuating materials. 5. Screening or shielding shall not inhibit the proper, safe operation of the mechanical equipment, nor shall it encroach into the required clearances for service and operation, as specified by the manufacturer."

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening in the CRDs (Sections 7.2.3 and 7.2.4 building design)
equip.text: "All mechanical equipment (either ground mounted or rooftop) must be shielded from pedestrian view with materials consistent and compatible with the architectural style of the building and equal to the height of the equipment..." (and p.209).

equip.cite: Utility equipment screening in Activity Centers (Section 7.2.5)
equip.text: "Utility equipment - Mechanical equipment or other utility hardware on roofs, ground, or buildings shall be screened from public view with architectural and/or landscape materials consistent with the building, or they shall be located so as [to be out of view]."

equip.cite: Site design review (Section 3.7.7)

fort_pierce.name: Fort Pierce
fort_pierce.source: Code of Ordinances, Ch. 125 Zoning, Art. IV Districts, §§ 125-188 through 125-212 (per-district 'Basic use standards' blocks); district list from § 125-156 Desi

equip.cite: Projections from buildings into yards (§ 125-278)
equip.text: "Cornices, roof eaves and fascia, balconies, gutters, canopies, screened enclosures, awnings, chimneys, flues and mechanical projections, such as window air conditioners and similar features, may project out to a maximum distance of 30 inches into a required yard except as provided for by sections 125-194(b)(2)f and 125-195(b)(2)f."

equip.cite: Rooftop equipment, South Beach Overlay District (§ 125-157(1)c.4.(i))
equip.text: "Height in excess of maximum. Equipment, including, but not limited to, satellite dishes and heating and air conditioning equipment may be installed on top of buildings provided that the equipment is screened from horizontal view."

equip.cite: Accessory buildings (typical per-district clause, e.g. § 125-188(c)(1))
equip.text: "Accessory buildings shall comply with all yard, lot coverage and building height requirements of this chapter, except that buildings not on double-frontage lots may be in the rear yard if they are at least seven feet from the rear lot line." The rear-lot-line distance varies by district: 7 ft in E-1, E-2, E-3, R-1 and R-2; 6 ft in R-3; 5 ft in R-4, R-4A and R-5. In C-1, C-2, C-3, C-4, C-5, C-6, I-1, I-2, I-3, CP-1 and OS-1 accessory buildings simply comply with all yard, lot coverage and height requirements with no such exception.

equip.cite: General exceptions to building height limitations (§ 125-279)
equip.text: "Vertical projections such as chimneys, spires, aerials, flagpoles and similar objects not used for human occupancy are not subject to the building height limitations of this chapter."

equip.cite: Environmental performance standards (§ 125-311)
equip.text: "(c) Noise. No use shall exceed the applicable standards for noise." Purpose clause: standards "are intended to help prevent nuisances due to a variety of causes, including noise, electromagnetic interference, smoke, humidity, heat, radiation, fire, explosives or toxic or noxious matter."

equip.cite: Edgartown Settlement sound levels (§ 125-197(p))
equip.text: "Between the hours of 7:00 a.m. and 11:00 p.m. each day, subject to the exemptions in chapter 26, article II, section 26-41, sound levels shall not exceed 55 dBA, 55 dBC, or 55 dBZ when measured from the property line of the nearest receiving single-family residential property."

equip.cite: Communications facilities — backup power (Ch. 125 definitions)
equip.text: "Accessory equipment building means any building, cabinet, or equipment enclosure constructed for the primary purpose of housing the electronics, backup power, power generators and other free standing equipment associated with the operation of antennas."

equip.cite: Generators -- noise exemption (Sec. 15-8.5(c), PDF p.465)
equip.text: Generators - exemption. Notwithstanding the foregoing prohibited acts, the use of gasoline or propane powered generators is permitted during periods of power outage following natural disasters and during periods of maintenance. Operation for purposes of maintenance of the generator shall only occur during daylight hours on weekdays and only for the minimum amount of time required by the manufacturer. Any person using a generator, except during periods of power outage, is subject to the restrictions on noise generation as otherwise set forth in this chapter.

equip.cite: Fixed mechanical equipment -- prohibited act (Sec. 15-8.5(b)(7), PDF p.464)
equip.text: Fixed mechanical equipment. Operating or causing the operation of fixed mechanical equipment located on real property including HVAC equipment, motors, engines, pumps, compressors, fans, tools, machinery, and its component parts, or any other similar stationary mechanical devices and their component parts except as otherwise exempted in section 15-8.6(f).

equip.cite: Fixed mechanical equipment -- exemption (Sec. 15-8.6(f), PDF p.465)
equip.text: Fixed mechanical equipment. Noise generated by the operation and use of air conditioning units in residential districts.

equip.cite: Permit exception for single-family/duplex (Sec. 10-2 area, PDF p.302)
equip.text: Nothing in this section shall apply to single-family or duplex residential units. Exceptions: fire sprinkler systems, generators, gas installations and photovoltaic systems.

equip.cite: Note
equip.text: None of the above is a setback or placement rule. No accessory-structure setback, required-yard encroachment, mechanical-equipment screening or separation-distance standard appears anywhere in the reprinted portion of this Code -- those live in the Land Development Regulations, which this document does not contain.

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures -- residential districts (Sec. 122-254, PDF p.1475)
equip.text: In residential districts, accessory uses and structures shall be allowed as follows: (1) Side yards. a. Motor vehicles, not associated with a structure as defined in this chapter, may be permitted to park in the side yards. b. Garages and carports may be permitted in the side yard subject to the following provisions: 1. The required side yard setback must be provided; 2. The structure may not exceed 18 feet in height. c. Sheds, not exceeding ten feet in height, and swimming pools may be permitted in the side yard subject to the following provisions: 1. The required side yard setback must be provided; 2. A screen pool enclosure for a swimming pool may be attached to the main building. (2) Rear yards. a. All accessory uses and structures are permitted in the rear yard subject to the following provisions: 1. The use or structure must be located at least three feet from the rear property line, at least five feet from any main building, and meet the required side yard setbacks; 2. The structure may not exceed 18 feet in height; 3. A screen pool enclosure for a swimming pool may be attached to the main building.

equip.cite: Yard encroachments (Sec. 122-252, PDF p.1473)
equip.text: (a) Every part of every required yard shall be open and unobstructed from the ground to the sky except as otherwise permitted in this chapter. (b) Sills or belt courses shall not project over 12 inches into a required yard. (c) Movable awnings shall project not over three feet into a required yard, provided that where the yard is less than five feet in width the projection shall not exceed one-half the width of the yard. (d) Chimneys, fireplaces or pilasters shall project not over two feet into a required yard. (e) Fire escapes, stairways and balconies which are unroofed and unenclosed shall project not over five feet into a required rear yard, or not over three feet eight inches into a required side yard, of a multiple dwelling, hotel or motel. (f) Hoods, canopies or marquees may project not over three feet into a required yard, but shall not be closer than one foot to any plot line. (g) Fences, walls and hedges shall be permitted in required yards subject to the provisions of section 122-253. (h) Accessory uses and structures may be located in required rear yards, and in side yards subject to the provisions of section 122-254. (i) Except as provided in section 122-253, nothing in this section shall be so construed as to prevent any type of landscaping or private nonprofit gardening on any plot. (j) Accessory parking may be located in a required rear or side yard. (k) Flagpoles, clotheslines, bird houses and other yard accessories are permitted in any yard if they do not constitute substantial impediments to vision or free flow of light and air across the yard. [NOTE: this list does not name generators, A/C condensers, pool pumps or LP tanks. In Ocala such equipment is governed as an "accessory use or structure" under Sec. 122-254 via subsection (h) above.]

equip.cite: Accessory buildings on corner and through lots (Sec. 122-250, PDF p.1473)
equip.text: On corner plots and through plots, front yards, when required, shall be provided on both streets, and accessory buildings shall not be located in either front yard.

equip.cite: Exclusions from height limits (Sec. 122-255, PDF p.1475)
equip.text: The height limitations contained in this chapter will not apply to spires, belfries, cupolas, water tanks, ventilators, electrical power transmission towers, chimneys or other appurtenances usually required to be placed above the roof level and not intended for human occupancy. The height of these structures or appurtenances shall not exceed the height limitations prescribed by any airport zoning ordinance adopted by the city.

equip.cite: Essential services (Sec. 122-258, PDF p.1476)
equip.text: Essential services shall be permitted as authorized and regulated by state or national public utility commissions or owned by the city. As used in this section, the term essential services specifically includes electric, water and sewer utilities of the city.

equip.cite: Zero lot line wall (Sec. 122-398(6), PDF p.1513)
equip.text: Unit design. The wall of the dwelling unit located on the zero lot line side shall have no windows, doors, air conditioning units or other types of openings. [The only place in Chapter 122 that names air conditioning equipment.]

equip.cite: Shopping centers -- separation from residential property (Sec. 122-923(c), PDF p.1583)
equip.text: If a shopping center on 40 acres or more or with 400,000 or more square feet of gross leasable area abuts property that has a residential dwelling on it, all buildings of the shopping center, trash collection receptacles, trash collection devices and trash collection areas, and rear yards, alleys, service courts and loading zones of the shopping center must be located at least 150 feet away from common property line. Sec. 122-923(a) also provides: "The location, size and architectural features of buildings, service areas, trash collection areas, loading zones, mechanical systems, lighting, traffic circulation and parking in a shopping center or single retail store development shall be designed so as to not have a negative impact on adjacent properties."

equip.cite: Telecommunications facilities -- hazardous materials (Secs. at PDF p.1607, 1608, 1610)
equip.text: If volatile, flammable, explosive, or hazardous materials (such as LP gas, propane, gasoline, natural gas, corrosive or other dangerous chemicals) except standard battery back up systems typically used in the telecommunications industry [are to be used], the applicant shall submit the necessary building plans to the building official. [Applies to wireless communication facilities only, not to dwellings.]

equip.cite: NOT FOUND
equip.text: Chapter 122 contains no section naming a standby or emergency generator, no permanent-generator siting standard, no mechanical-equipment or condenser screening standard, and no separation distance to windows, air intakes or LP tanks. Chapter 34 Art. VIII (Noise, Secs. 34-171 to 34-175) was also searched and prints no generator exemption. The controlling rule for a generator pad in Ocala is therefore Sec. 122-254 (accessory uses and structures) read with Sec. 122-252(h).

equip.cite: Permanently installed stand-by generators -- LDR Sec. 5-107 (TEXT NOT IN THIS DOCUMENT)
equip.text: The Code Index (code page 3006) lists, under LAND DEVELOPMENT REGULATIONS (Chapter 29), Development standards, Accessory uses and structures: "Permanently installed stand-by generators... 5-107 / General... 5-107(A) / Standards for a permanent generator in all residential districts... 5-107(B) / Standards for a permanently installed stand-by generator in nonresidential districts... 5-107(C)". North Miami therefore DOES have a dedicated permanent-generator section, but its text is on Gridics, not in this PDF. Related indexed sections, also absent: 5-101 Accessory uses and structures; 5-110 Solid waste containers/mechanical equipment; 5-112 Unattached accessory structures; 5-113 Paving on side and rear yards.

equip.cite: Fixed mechanical equipment -- definition, Sec. 12-14 noise article (PDF p.404)
equip.text: Fixed mechanical equipment means mechanical equipment, such as an air conditioning unit, water cooling tower, swimming pool pump, irrigation pump, well water pump, fan, power generator or other similar power source equipment, permanently affixed to real property, as distinguished from temporary, portable, non-fixed mechanical equipment.

equip.cite: Movable mechanical equipment -- prohibited act, Sec. 12-15(15) (PDF p.406)
equip.text: Movable mechanical equipment. Operating or permitting the operation of any such equipment including trucks, portable generators, forklifts, cranes, pile drivers and commercial machinery and vehicles of any kind, in such a manner as to create any noise which would unreasonably loud and raucous and can be heard across the property line of any residential property between 8:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m.

equip.cite: Note
equip.text: Both quoted rules are noise provisions (Ch. 12, Art. IV) governing when equipment may run, not where it may sit. No setback, yard-encroachment, screening or separation distance for generators appears anywhere in the reprinted portion of this Code.

gen.cite: Permanent standby generators - residential buildings (Sec. 27-2307(c)(4))
gen.text: 'The setback for permanent standby generators for residential buildings, except residential apartment or condominium buildings, may be reduced to three feet from the interior side property line and five feet from the rear property line, provided it is: a. Fueled by natural gas or liquid propane gas; b. Does not exceed four feet in height; c. Screened from public view.'

gen.cite: Permanent standby generators - general rule (Sec. 27-2307(c)(3))
gen.text: 'Air compressors, permanent standby generators, unless specifically allowed in subsection (4) of this section, or other similar mechanical equipment are required to meet the established setbacks for the primary building.'

gen.cite: Definition - permanent standby generator (Secs. 13-1 and 27-1)
gen.text: 'Generator, permanent standby, means a fixed device that converts mechanical energy obtained from a combustion engine into electrical energy and operates automatically as a secondary source of electrical power.' 'Generator, portable, means a device that can be moved with a handle, or is mounted on a hand-cart or trailer, which when operated converts mechanical energy obtained from a combustion engine into electrical energy.'

gen.cite: Definition - mechanical equipment (Secs. 13-1 and 27-1)
gen.text: 'Mechanical equipment means implements and tools produced or operated by a machine, that are used to provide energy, light, heat, air or broadcast telecommunication services to a building, structure and/or property. This includes, but is not limited to, air-conditioning units, pool equipment, satellite dishes, gas tanks (aboveground only), solar panels, antennas and generators.'

gen.cite: Noise exemption during an outage (Sec. 13-139)
gen.text: Exempt from the town sound standards is 'Sound from a portable generator or a permanent standby generator during a power utility outage, or for the time it takes to perform a [test/maintenance run].'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment, nonresidential and multi-story residential (Sec. 27-2307(c)(1))
equip.text: 'Mechanical equipment (including air-conditioning units) for nonresidential and residential multi-story apartment or condominium buildings may encroach upon a side setback up to 50 percent, provided it is not less than three feet from the property line.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment, other residential buildings (Sec. 27-2307(c)(2))
equip.text: 'The setback for mechanical equipment from residential buildings, other than multi-story apartment or condominium buildings, may be reduced to two feet from the interior side property line and five feet from the rear property line provided the mechanical equipment is entirely screened from public view.'

equip.cite: Landscape buffers and easements (Sec. 27-2307(e), (h))
equip.text: 'No mechanical equipment shall be permitted within any required landscape buffer.' 'No structures shall encroach into utility easements, unless approval is granted from the utility holder and a hold harmless agreement is submitted to the town, and approved as to legal form and sufficiency by the town attorney.'

equip.cite: Grandfathering and discretionary increase (Sec. 27-2307(d), (g), (i))
equip.text: 'The replacement of mechanical equipment which existed prior to November 16, 2004 is exempt from these requirements.' 'When a property has reduced setbacks for the principal structures, such as nonconforming lots of record and approved planned unit developments, the accessory structures shall be permitted the same reduced setbacks as the principal structure.' 'The director of the department of planning and zoning or his designee may impose a greater setback than is provided for herein if the director or his designee determines that a structure or use of a structure is inconsistent or incompatible with the neighboring uses, or is substantially likely to cause or result in a nuisance.'

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical equipment and height (Sec. 27-2305(a)(7) and (b))
equip.text: Height limits do not apply to 'Screened rooftop mechanical equipment in nonresidential or mixed-use buildings, provided the area it encompasses does not exceed 20 percent of the square footage of the entire roof area.' 'Enclosed rooftop mechanical equipment rooms may exceed the maximum building height by no more than ten percent. Rooftop mechanical equipment rooms shall be setback from the edge of the roof at a one-to-one ratio to the height of the mechanical equipment room.'

equip.cite: Accessory structures in residential districts (Sec. 27-1910(a))
equip.text: 'All accessory uses, buildings and structures shall be located on the same lot as the principal or main use and not within any required yard setback except as established in section 27-1910 and subsection 27-2307(g).' Sheds: 'Minimum side interior setback shall be three feet. Minimum side corner setback shall be 15 feet. Minimum rear setback shall be five feet. On lots abutting an alley, the minimum rear setback shall be three feet. If a greater easement width exists, the width of the easement shall be the minimum setback.' Maximum shed size 144 sq ft, maximum height eight feet.

equip.cite: Accessory structures in commercial and industrial districts (Sec. 27-1910(b))
equip.text: 'All accessory uses, buildings and structures in commercial and industrial zoning districts, shall meet the required setbacks and regulations of the district in which it is located.'

equip.cite: Unattached structures generally (Sec. 27-2307(b))
equip.text: 'The following unattached structures are not required a setback: Fences and walls. Recreational equipment are required a minimum setback of three feet when placed in a side or rear yard.'

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment screening in the IOZ overlay (Sec. 27-1526(1))
equip.text: 'Screening of mechanical equipment. All mechanical equipment, including, but not limited to, heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning machinery; accessory communications equipment such as antennas, signal sending and receiving dishes, etc.; public utility service fixtures, including telephone, telegraph, electric, natural or propane gas, potable water, sewer facilities; and elevator facilities, shall be screened from public view.'

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures must be in the rear yard (Sec. 13-373(a))
equip.text: 'All accessory uses and structures in residential districts shall be located in rear yards' with the exception of fall-out shelters, flagpoles, entrance guardhouses not exceeding 300 square feet, and accessory buildings and structures for essential public facilities (which 'shall not be subject to the dimensional requirements of any zoning district, but shall be subject to the locational requirements of the city engineer').

equip.cite: Accessory use setbacks (Sec. 13-373(d)(1))
equip.text: 'Buildings or structures may be located within the rear yard, provided the distance from the accessory building or structure to the rear lot line is not less than required by the applicable zoning district. Side yard requirements applicable to principal buildings shall also be applicable to accessory buildings or structures.'

equip.cite: Accessory structure limits (Sec. 13-373(c), (e), (f), (g))
equip.text: 'The minimum distance between the principal building and an accessory building or structure in the A-1 or RS-1 zoning district shall be twenty-five (25) feet.' 'An accessory building or structure shall not be of greater height than a principal building on the lot.' 'Accessory structures shall not occupy more than thirty-five (35) percent of the required yard area.' 'No accessory structures, except for fences and walls, shall be placed within any easement.'

equip.cite: Screening of mechanical equipment in landscape code (Sec. 13-443(9)a)
equip.text: 'Storage areas, dumpsters and mechanical equipment such as air conditioning compressors, pool pumps, sprinkler pumps and electrical transformers shall be screened on at least three (3) sides. Such screening shall meet the minimum requirements of section 13-444(c)(1)c at time of planting and shall exceed the vertical height of the object by at least six (6) inches within two (2) years of issuing a certificate of occupancy.'

equip.cite: Ground-level mechanical equipment, property maintenance (Sec. 6-36(8))
equip.text: 'Mechanical equipment. Filtration systems, air conditioning units and gas tanks at ground level on new installations shall be concealed by a fence or landscape border so that the equipment will not be seen from the street or adjacent properties.'

equip.cite: Screening of service and mechanical equipment on outparcels (Sec. 13-359(b)(12))
equip.text: 'All garbage and trash containers or compactors, bottled gas tanks and irrigation system pumps must be underground or placed in walled-in areas or landscaped screened areas. All air-conditioning units, mechanical equipment, and the like, whether roof mounted or at grade, shall be shielded and hidden so that they shall not be visible from a point six (6) feet above the ground from any abutting public or private right-of-way and/or property line. Wood may not be used as a screening material.' Applies to all outparcels in the B-2, B-3, B-4, PUD and PCD districts.

equip.cite: Roof-mounted equipment (Sec. 13-373(h))
equip.text: 'Roof-mounted accessory structures, including air conditioning systems shall be screened from view from abutting public road rights-of-way. Vent pipes, nonmotorized turbines, skylights, cupolas, steeples, and chimneys shall not be subject to this provision.'

equip.cite: Height-limit exclusion for mechanical appurtenances (Sec. 13-331(h))
equip.text: 'The height limitations of this article shall not apply to spires, belfries, minarets, cupolas, and domes, not used for human occupancy; nor to bridges, chimneys, ventilators, skylights, water tanks, bulkheads or similar features and necessary mechanical appurtenances usually carried above the roof level, such as elevator penthouses, air-conditioning equipment, etc.'

equip.cite: Townhouse accessory structures (Sec. 13-338(d)(17)a)
equip.text: 'No accessory buildings or structures shall be permitted on individual townhouse sites with the exception of pools, spas, hottubs, decks, cabanas, screen enclosures, walls, fences, awnings, trellises, and mechanical equipment with its enclosure.'

equip.cite: Easements (Sec. 13-407 area, PDF p.513)
equip.text: Easements 'shall not contain permanent improvements including but not limited to patios, decks, pools, air conditioners, structures, utility sheds, poles, fences, trees, shrubs, hedges, plants and landscaping, except that utilities...'

equip.cite: Underground utilities in a PUD (Sec. 13-348(d)(7))
equip.text: 'All utilities within planned unit developments, including telephone, television cable, and electrical systems shall be installed underground... Large transformers shall be placed on the ground and contained within pad mounts, enclosures or vaults. The developer shall provide adequate landscaping with shrubs and plants to screen all utility facilities permitted above ground.'
