anna_maria.name: City of Anna Maria
anna_maria.source: Code of Ordinances, Subpart B (Land Development Regulations), ch. 114 (Zoning), art. V (District Regulations), §§ 114-191 through 114-362. Anna Maria prints no

equip.cite: § 70-1 (Definitions — Setback)
equip.text: Setback means required minimum distance between the street right-of-way line or any other lot or property line in the outer most vertical plane of any building or structure which is over 12 inches in height. It is intended that a setback is a clear zone void of any structures or mechanical devices over 12-inches in height. Notwithstanding the foregoing, roof overhangs and minor, non-structural protrusions such as lighting fixtures and shutters, may intrude into a required setback no more than 24 inches.

equip.cite: § 114-222(5)c (R-1 and, by § 114-346, CON-1 — minimum setbacks)
equip.text: Mechanical equipment including, but not limited to, air conditioner/heater, pool pumps, pool heaters, shall not be located within the setbacks.

equip.cite: § 114-422 (Measurement of setbacks)
equip.text: (a) All setbacks, with the exception of waterfront setbacks, will be measured from the adjacent property line or right-of-way boundary, as the case may be, to the outermost vertical plane of the closest structure which is over 12 inches in height. All setback measurements shall be taken on a horizontal plane. (b) Waterfront setbacks, on waterfront property the setback shall be measured from the mean high-water line or retaining wall, whichever is closer to the lot or parcel, and the closest building line.

equip.cite: § 114-222(4) (R-1 swimming pools)
equip.text: Caged and uncaged swimming pools, hot tubs and the swimming pool and hot tub equipment shall be set back from the lot line or property line the minimum setback required for the particular yard with the exception of the side yard setback which shall be ten feet. Uncaged swimming pools located on through lots shall be set back a minimum of five feet from the adjoining lot line or property line if the pool is located in the street yard which does not contain the structure's main entrance. Pools permitted prior to January 1, 2016, shall be deemed as grandfathered related to the side yard setbacks.

equip.cite: § 114-282(4)d (ROR swimming pools)
equip.text: Caged and uncaged swimming pools, hot tubs and the swimming pool and hot tub equipment shall be set back from the lot line or property line the minimum setback required for the particular yard with the exception of the side yard setback which shall be ten feet. Uncaged swimming pools located on through lots shall be set back a minimum of five feet from the adjoining lot line or property line if the pool is located in the street yard which does not contain the structure's main entrance.

equip.cite: § 114-302(6) (PSP swimming pools)
equip.text: Caged and uncaged swimming pools, hot tubs and the swimming pool and hot tub equipment shall be set back from the lot line or property line the minimum setback required for the particular yard. Uncaged swimming pools located on through lots shall be set back a minimum of five feet from the adjoining lot line or property line if the pool is located in the street yard which does not contain the structure's main entrance.

equip.cite: § 114-412 (Accessory buildings)
equip.text: (a) No accessory building shall be constructed upon any lot until construction of the main building has commenced. (b) No accessory building shall be used for dwelling purposes. (c) Accessory buildings shall meet all setback requirements.

equip.cite: § 114-262(4)d (C-1) and § 114-282(4)b (ROR) — Access for emergency personnel
equip.text: These side setback areas must be kept clear of any form of obstruction at all times so that safe and convenient passage of police or firefighters or other emergency personnel will be constantly maintained. All fencing within the side yard must contain an unlocked access gate.

equip.cite: § 114-261(c)(2) (C-1 accessory uses) and § 114-281(c)(1) (ROR accessory uses)
equip.text: Outdoor storage, staging, assembly or erection of equipment directly accessory to the operation of the principal permitted use on the premises; provided, however, that areas used for such purposes shall be completely screened from view with a fence six feet high and such storage shall not be within the front yard setback.

equip.cite: § 114-421(a) (Uses within right-of-way)
equip.text: With the exception of the planting of grass or 250 filter mix, no encumbrances of any kind, such as trees, bushes, rocks, stones, plantings, pea gravel, crushed shell, etc., shall be placed or constructed on the right-of-way within eight feet of the edge of pavement without the written approval of the director of public works and a majority of the members of the city commission; provided, however, that regulatory signage pertaining to traffic control, safety structures, and public utility equipment are permitted by right within the right-of-way.

equip.cite: § 114-423(c)(11) (Swimming pool enclosures)
equip.text: Swimming pools, if located within the building area and if not within a screened cage, shall be enclosed on all open sides by a fence of a minimum of four feet above the existing ground grade and a maximum of six feet above the existing ground grade. Pools located within the required yard area shall be enclosed on all open sides by a fence of a height of four feet above the existing ground grade. All pool fences must have gates with safety locks.

equip.cite: § 114-424 (Dumpsters)
equip.text: All permanent dumpsters must be screened from view on four sides with hedges, walls or fences. Temporary dumpsters are those located for a consecutive period of no longer than 15 days and are not required to be screened.

equip.cite: § 82-244 (Accessory structures — flood)
equip.text: Accessory structures are permitted below the base flood elevation provided the accessory structures are used only for parking or storage and: (1) If located in special flood hazard areas (Zone A/AE) other than coastal high hazard areas, are one-story and not larger than 600 sq. ft. and have flood openings in accordance with Section R322.2 of the Florida Building Code, Residential. (2) If located in coastal high hazard areas (Zone V/VE), are not located below elevated buildings and are not larger than 100 sq. ft. (3) Are anchored to resist flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from flood loads. (4) Have flood damage-resistant materials used below the base flood elevation plus one foot. (5) Have mechanical, plumbing and electrical systems, including plumbing fixtures, elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus one foot.

equip.cite: § 82-307 (Utility equipment)
equip.text: Utility equipment that serves manufactured/mobile/mobile homes, including electric, heating, ventilation, plumbing, and air conditioning equipment and other service facilities, shall comply with the requirements of the Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322, as applicable to the flood hazard area.

equip.cite: § 82-346 (Underground tanks)
equip.text: Underground tanks in flood hazard areas shall be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions of the design flood, including the effects of buoyancy assuming the tank is empty.

equip.cite: § 82-347 (Above-ground tanks not elevated)
equip.text: Above-ground tanks that do not meet the elevation requirements of section 82-348 of this article shall: (1) Be permitted in flood hazard areas (Zone A) other than coastal high hazard areas, provided the tanks are anchored or otherwise designed and constructed to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions of the design flood, including the effects of buoyancy assuming the tank is empty and the effects of flood-borne debris. (2) Not be permitted in coastal high hazard areas (Zone V) or Coastal A Zones.

equip.cite: § 82-348 (Above-ground tanks, elevated)
equip.text: Above-ground tanks in flood hazard areas shall be attached to an elevated to or above the design flood elevation on a supporting structure that is designed to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement during conditions of the design flood. Tank-supporting structures shall meet the foundation requirements of the applicable flood hazard area.

equip.cite: § 82-349 (Tank inlets and vents)
equip.text: Tank inlets, fill openings, outlets and vents shall be: (1) At or above the design flood elevation or fitted with covers designed to prevent the inflow of floodwater or outflow of the contents of the tanks during conditions of the design flood; and (2) Anchored to prevent lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads, including the effects of buoyancy, during conditions of the design flood.

equip.cite: § 82-242 (Buildings and structures seaward of the coastal construction control line)
equip.text: If extending, in whole or in part, seaward of the coastal construction control line and also located, in whole or in part, in a flood hazard area: (1) Buildings and structures shall be designed and constructed to comply with the more restrictive applicable requirements of the Florida Building Code, Building Section 3109 and Section 1612 or Florida Building Code, Residential Section R322. (2) Minor structures and non-habitable major structures as defined in F.S. § 161.54, shall be designed and constructed to comply with the intent and applicable provisions of this article and ASCE 24.

equip.cite: § 82-241 (Design and construction of buildings, structures and facilities exempt from the Florida Building Code)
equip.text: Pursuant to section 82-103 of this article, buildings, structures, and facilities that are exempt from the Florida Building Code, including substantial improvement or repair of substantial damage of such buildings, structures and facilities, shall be designed and constructed in accordance with the flood load and flood resistant construction requirements of ASCE 24. Structures exempt from the Florida Building Code that are not walled and roofed buildings shall comply with the requirements of subdivision VII of this division.

equip.cite: § 82-243 (Critical facilities)
equip.text: Construction of new and substantially improved critical facilities shall be located outside the limits of the special flood hazard area. Construction of new critical facilities shall be permissible within the special flood hazard area if no feasible alternative site is available. If permitted, critical facilities shall be designed in accordance with the City of Anna Maria's local technical amendment to the Florida Building Code, Building, which requires elevation or protection to or above the base flood elevation plus three feet or the 500-year (0.2 percent chance) flood elevation, whichever is higher. Flood proofing and sealing measures must be implemented to ensure that toxic substances will not be displaced by or released into floodwaters. Access routes elevated to or above the base flood elevation shall be provided to all critical facilities to the maximum extent possible. Critical facilities shall be designed to remain operable during such an event.

equip.cite: § 82-371 (General requirements for other development)
equip.text: All development, including man-made changes to improved or unimproved real estate for which specific provisions are not specified in this article or the Florida Building Code, shall: (1) Be located and constructed to minimize flood damage; (2) Be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrostatic loads, including the effects of buoyancy, during conditions of the design flood; (3) Be constructed of flood damage-resistant materials.

equip.cite: § 74-41(a)(2) (FBC, Building technical amendment 1612.4.3, Elevation requirements)
equip.text: 1612.4.3 Elevation requirements. The minimum elevation requirements shall be as specified in ASCE 24 or the base flood elevation plus 2 feet or 12 feet NAVD, whichever is higher.

equip.cite: § 74-41(a)(2) (FBC, Building technical amendment 1612.4.4 and 1612.4.5)
equip.text: 1612.4.4 Coastal A Zones. In Coastal A Zones as defined in Chapter 82 (Floodplain Management), backfilled stem walls are not permitted. 1612.4.5 Critical facilities. In addition to the requirements of ASCE 24 and the local floodplain management ordinance, the minimum elevation requirements for critical facilities, as defined in the local floodplain management ordinance including Flood Design Class 3 and Flood Design Class 4 buildings, shall be at or above the higher of the elevation specified in ASCE 24, the base flood elevation plus 3 feet, or the 500-year (0.2 percent) flood elevation.

equip.cite: § 74-41 (FBC, Residential technical amendment R322.3.2)
equip.text: R322.3.2 Elevation requirements. 1. Buildings and structures erected within coastal high-hazard areas and Coastal A Zones shall be elevated so that the bottom of the lowest horizontal structural members supporting the lowest floor, with the exception of pilings, pile caps, columns, grade beams and bracing, is elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus 2 feet or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher.

equip.cite: § 26-154 (Existing fuel storage tanks)
equip.text: All fuel storage tanks located within the city shall be maintained in accordance with applicable codes to resist the effects of buoyancy and lateral forces of wind and wave action. Fuel storage tanks not in compliance with this section on the effective date of this article shall come into compliance no later than June 1, 2006.

equip.cite: § 26-155 (Stationary outdoor equipment)
equip.text: All stationary outdoor equipment shall be permanently installed and/or maintained to resist the effects of buoyancy and lateral forces of wind and wave action so as not to become debris that may float or become airborne causing damage to buildings, structures, and utilities. Any stationary outdoor equipment not installed in accordance with this section on the effective date of this article shall come into compliance no later than June 1, 2006. [§ 26-153 defines: 'Stationary outdoor equipment means items of personal property that are not normally expected to change in status, condition or place and installed for indefinite use at a particular location and are not connected and secured to a building or other structure. Stationary outdoor equipment includes, but is not limited to, appliances, vending cabinets, vending machines, ornamental structures and fountains.']

equip.cite: § 26-90 (Pool, spa, hot tub quiet hours)
equip.text: Swimming pools, spas and hot tubs may be utilized at any time of day or night; provided, however, no noise shall be generated from such use or related to such use that can be heard beyond the property lines of the property on which the pool, spa or hot tub is located, between the hours of 10:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. the next day. Generation of such noise during such prohibited hours shall be considered to be a violation of pool, spa, hot tub quiet hours.

equip.cite: § 74-73 (Construction site noise abatement) — the only section of the code that uses the word 'generator' in a regulatory sentence
equip.text: Generators shall not be used on construction sites without the authorization of the building official in writing. Generators are only allowed on an emergency basis. See 'Service utilities' section for temporary power requirements.

equip.cite: § 26-91 (Construction site noise)
equip.text: The use of generators, pumps and gas-powered air compressors shall be in accordance with section 74-73 as amended. The following shall be required for the use of generators, pumps, gas-powered air compressors and similar equipment on construction sites; (1) All equipment shall be retrofitted with noise damping device including, but not limited to, insulated cabs, baffle box, sound blankets and intake silencers. (2) The use of generators, pumps and gas-powered air compressors shall only be used during allowable construction hours consistent with section 26-93.

R-1.sideNote: Side yard 7 ft for structures 27 feet or less in height; 10 ft for structures greater than 27 feet in height. 'If any portion of the structure is greater than 27 feet in height, then the entire structure shall comply with the greater side yard setback of ten feet.'
R-1.coverageNote: 'The LAR shall not exceed 40 percent for any lot or parcel area up to 15,000 square feet, plus 35 percent for that area of the lot or parcel between 15,001 square feet to 21,000 square feet, plus 30 percent for that area of the lot or parcel over 21,000 square feet.' Separately: 'Maximum impervious surface including building coverage: 40 percent of the lot or parcel.' The code sets no single flat building-coverage percentage.
R-1.note: § 114-222. Maximum density 6.0 dwelling units per acre. Minimum open space five percent of the lot or parcel. Lot width: 'lot width is at least 50 feet of frontage on a single public street.' Waterfront setback 15 (excluding water bodies wholly contained within a single lot or parcel). Corner lot side street yards 10. Through lots 20 (setback from streets).

R-2.note: R-2, Two-Family is established as a district by § 114-192 and described in § 114-193(2), but the code prints NO dimensional standards for it. Editor's note at § 114-261: 'Ord. No. 09-699, § 4, adopted March 26, 2009, repealed chapter 114, article V, division 3, sections 114-241 and 114-242 in their entirety, which pertained to the R-2, two-family district use regulations.

C-1.frontNote: Front yard 35 ft 'With Lot Depth at Least 140 Feet'; 29 ft 'With Lot Depth Less Than 140 Feet.'
C-1.note: § 114-262. Coverage is 'Maximum building coverage: 40 percent'; 'Maximum impervious surface, not including building coverage: 20 percent.' Lot width: 'Lots shall have a minimum of 50 feet of frontage on a single public street.' Street side yard 20. The rear yard is printed only for two conditions, both 10 in each lot-depth column: 'Adjacent to R-1 or R-2 district 10' and 'Adjacent to alley 10'.

ROR.frontNote: Front yard 35 ft 'With Lot Depth at Least 140 Feet'; 29 ft 'With Lot Depth Less Than 140 Feet.'
ROR.sideNote: Table prints two side-yard rows, the same in both lot-depth columns: 'Side yard 7(Up to 27')' and 'Side yard 10(+27' to 37').'
ROR.coverageNote: 'The LAR shall not exceed 40 percent for any lot or parcel area up to 15,000 square feet, plus 35 percent for that area of the lot or parcel between 15,001 square feet to 21,000 square feet, plus 30 percent for that area of the lot or parcel over 21,000 square feet.' Separately: 'Maximum impervious surface including building coverage: 40 percent of the lot or parcel.'
ROR.minLotNote: Minimum area 5,000 sq ft 'For lots platted prior to February 15, 2009'; 7,500 sq ft 'For lots platted after February 15, 2009.'
ROR.lotWidthNote: Minimum width 50 ft for lots platted prior to February 15, 2009; 75 ft for lots platted after February 15, 2009. Footnote: 'Residential lot depth may be adjusted so long as minimum area requirements are complied with and lot width is at least 50 feet of frontage on a public road or approved private access.' Depth column is printed only as an asterisk.
ROR.note: § 114-282. Minimum open space five percent of the lot or parcel. Street side yard 20. Rear yard 10; 'Adjacent to alley' 10. Waterfront 15 (except adjacent to water bodies wholly contained within a lot or parcel). Through lots 20 from each street. Buildings limited to three usable floors. Height measured from crown of road.

PSP.frontNote: Front yard 35 ft 'With Lot Depth at Least 140 Feet'; 29 ft 'With Lot Depth Less Than 140 Feet.'
PSP.note: § 114-302. Minimum lot depth 100 feet. Coverage is 'Maximum building coverage: 40 percent'; 'Maximum impervious surface coverage: 60 percent.' Street side yard 20. The rear yard is printed only for two conditions, both 10: 'Adjacent to R-1 or R-2 10' and 'Adjacent to alley 10.' Waterfront 15 (except water bodies wholly contained within a lot or parcel).

PRA.frontNote: Front yard 35 ft 'With Lot Depth at Least 140 Feet'; 29 ft 'With Lot Depth Less Than 140 Feet.'
PRA.note: § 114-322. Minimum lot depth 100 feet. Coverage is 'Maximum building coverage: 40 percent'; 'Maximum impervious surface coverage: 60 percent.' Street side yard 20. Waterfront 15 (excluding water bodies contained wholly within a lot or parcel). 'All through lots shall have 20-foot setbacks from each street.' Only the front yard varies between the two lot-depth columns. Height measured from crown of road.

CON-1.sideNote: Side yard 7 ft for structures 27 feet or less in height; 10 ft for structures greater than 27 feet in height (§ 114-222(5), applied by § 114-346).
CON-1.coverageNote: LAR tiered 40/35/30 percent as in § 114-222(3); maximum impervious surface including building coverage 40 percent of the lot or parcel.
CON-1.note: § 114-346: 'Lot, yard, bulk and parking regulations for the CON-1 district are set forth in section 114-222 of the residential district.' Values above are therefore the R-1 values. § 114-346 continues: 'For lots or parcels which contain both the R-1 or R-2 and the CON-1 districts, the entire lot or parcel may be used in determining setbacks, building coverage and lot coverage requirements.

CON-2.note: §§ 114-361, 114-362. The code prints no lot, yard, bulk or parking regulations for CON-2. Conservation uses are permitted; boat docks, piers and shelters and public or private parks, playgrounds and recreational facilities are allowable only as special exceptions. Formerly the E-2 Conservation District, renamed by Ord. No. 12-740.

bradenton_beach.name: Bradenton Beach
bradenton_beach.source: NOT PRESENT. The zoning / dimensional standards are NOT in this document. Chapter 34, LAND DEVELOPMENT CODE, is the chapter that would carry them, and it has be
bradenton_beach.offsite: The zoning chapter is not in this jurisdiction's Municode document — the copy held here is a supplement or a stub. Nothing on this card is a setback for this jurisdiction; read the adopted code before siting anything.

equip.cite: § 26-115(b) — Fans, air conditioners and pool equipment; LOCATION AND PLACEMENT (PDF p.264, CD26:16.6; Ord. No. 21-527, § 3, 4-8-2021)
equip.text: "Upon the effective date of this article, the location and placement of all new or replacement pool equipment or air conditioning equipment on the outside of the building or structure it serves shall be specified by the city building official or designee, and shall be so shown and designated on the plans and specifications for such construction as the building official or designee directs. In addition, the building official or designee shall require compliance with all reasonable sound abatement measures and sound screening which may be necessary or desirable to prevent such air conditioning equipment from creating excessive or unnecessary noise. All such pool equipment or air conditioning equipment hereafter installed in the city shall carry the manufacturer's certification of the sound rating thereof, which sound rating shall not exceed a value which will cause the limits of section 26-107 to be exceeded. All pertinent information and data as to the sound ratings of such equipment shall be furnished to the building department at the time application for the building permit is made." [This is the only placement rule for outdoor mechanical equipment in the document. It prints NO distance and NO setback — placement is delegated wholly to the building official. It does not name generators.]

equip.cite: § 26-115(a) — Fans, air conditioners and pool equipment; noise (PDF p.263, CD26:16.5; Ord. No. 21-527, § 3, 4-8-2021)
equip.text: "It shall be unlawful to create any excessive and unnecessary loud noise by the use or operation of any noise-creating pool equipment or air conditioner, compressor unit, power fan or blower or the electric motor or any engine used to drive such device, the operation of which causes such excessive and unnecessary noise, unless such noise is muffled and deadened by adequate noise suppression and muffling devices to eliminate annoyance and disturbance to persons within the range of hearing."

equip.cite: § 26-104(6) — Noise exceptions; EMERGENCY GENERATORS (PDF p.255-256, CD26:13-14; Ord. No. 21-527, § 3, 4-8-2021)
equip.text: "Emergency machinery or equipment including generators, whether permanently installed or portable in the event of loss of electrical power caused by a hurricane or other act of nature, as long as such machinery or equipment has a muffler or other noise reduction device at least as effective as that recommended by the manufacturer or provided as original equipment. This exemption is not applicable for any property or location where power is unavailable, such as delinquent Florida Power and Light accounts, unpermitted construction sites, or camp-like housing, including, but not limited to tents, recreational vehicles, mobile homes." [This is the only permanently-installed-generator provision in the entire document. It is an exemption from the noise article, NOT a siting or setback rule; it prints no distance and no lot-line relationship. Verified against the page image at.]

equip.cite: § 26-107(a), (d) — Noise limits and where they are measured (PDF p.257-258, CD26:15-16; Ord. No. 21-527, § 3, 4-8-2021)
equip.text: Table 26-02 maximum dBA: Residential areas or zoning districts — 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. 85 dBA; 7:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. 75 dBA; 10:00 p.m. to 2:00 a.m. 65 dBA; 2:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. 55 dBA. Commercial areas or zoning districts & waterways within or adjacent to the city — 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. 70 dBA; 7:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. 65 dBA; 10:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. 55 dBA; 2:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m. 55 dBA. "Correction for character of sound. For any source of sound which emits a pure tone, the maximum sound level limits set forth above shall be reduced by five dBA." Measurement, § 26-107(d): "Measurements shall be made at the receiving land, approximately five feet above ground." [Relevant because a generator or condenser is judged at the receiving property, not at the source; but this prints no setback.]

equip.cite: § 14-33(4) — Setbacks on private property, temporary outdoor dining and retail (PDF p.214, CD14:11; Ord. No. 20-516, § 4, 5-21-2020)
equip.text: "Setbacks on private property. Temporary placement of equipment such as wash stations, hand sanitizing stations, stations for staff set up and service are not required to meet required yard setbacks. No seating may be placed in setback areas bordering a residential property." [A yard-encroachment rule for temporary food-service equipment only. Does not reach generators, condensers, pool pumps or LP tanks.]

equip.cite: § 14-5(c)(1)l. — Mobile food dispensing vehicle GENERATORS (PDF p.211, CD14:7; Ord. No. 22-542)
equip.text: "All generator(s) used by a mobile food dispensing vehicle may operate at a sound decibel level of 60 db or less, measured at a distance of ten feet from the generator." [The ten feet is a MEASUREMENT STANDOFF for the sound reading, not a setback from a lot line, and it applies only to a vehicle-mounted generator on a food truck.]

equip.cite: § 14-5(c)(1)g. — Mobile food dispensing vehicle location (PDF p.210, CD14:6)
equip.text: "A mobile food dispensing vehicle shall not be located within 25 feet of any street intersection or pedestrian crosswalk unless the responsible party has obtained a city-issued special event permit, or is part of a city-approved site plan." [Vehicle siting, not equipment siting; included only because it is the sole printed distance-to-a-line rule in the document.]

holmes_beach.name: Holmes Beach
holmes_beach.source: Code of Ordinances, Land Development Code art. VI (Zoning), § 6.6 District regulations - a per-district '3. Development standards' prose block for each district

gen.cite: LDC art. VI, § 6.8Z.1.b [PDF p.702] - the controlling generator rule
gen.text: Except as otherwise permitted herein, heat pumps, pool pumps, air conditioning units, recreation or fitness equipment, trampolines, and generators are not permitted in required setbacks regardless of their height.

gen.cite: LDC art. VI, § 6.8Z.8 (Allowable encroachments into the secondary front setback) [PDF p.704]
gen.text: Allowable encroachments into the secondary front setback. Restrictions set forth in the preceding subsections (1) through (6), notwithstanding, the following items may encroach up to, but not more than, five feet into a secondary front setback: a. Air conditioning unit; b. Generator; and c. Heat and pool pumps not exceeding 48 inches in height (measured from adjacent grade), provided the unit is screened to a height equal to or greater than the height of the pump by vegetation along all sides of the pump that do not face an exterior wall of the principal structure.

gen.cite: Code of Ordinances § 30-54(6) (Noise - outdoor mechanical equipment) [PDF p.297-298]
gen.text: Operation of any air-conditioning or air handling unit; pool pump and filtration system, or other outdoor mechanical equipment such as generators, in such a manner as to not exceed any of the following noise levels: a. Any point on neighboring property line..... 60 dB(A); b. Centering of nearest neighboring patio or porch..... 50 dB(A); c. Outside a neighboring living area window nearest the equipment location..... 50 dB(A). Said equipment must be maintained in reasonable mechanical condition and be operating with the standard noise and vibration control systems provided by the manufacturer.

gen.cite: Code of Ordinances §§ 14-4 and 14-6 (Construction-site generators) [PDF p.207]
gen.text: Sec. 14-4. Use of generators prohibited. The use of generators by contractors and subcontractors on a construction site permitted by the City of Holmes Beach shall be prohibited beyond the first lintel stage of construction unless the building official has authorized the use of a generator in writing. Electric power on all construction sites shall be supplied via a temporary electric pole as set forth in section 14.3 above. Sec. 14-6. Buffering of noise from generators. Generators in use on a permitted construction site shall be buffered to minimize noise impact on adjacent sites.

gen.cite: LDC art. XI, § 11.3N.2 (Telecommunications facilities - backup generators) [PDF p.835]
gen.text: Backup generators shall only be operated during power outages and for testing and maintenance purposes. If the facility is located within 250 feet of a residential dwelling unit, noise attenuation measures shall be included to reduce noise levels at the facility to a maximum exterior level of 60 decibels at the facility's property line and a maximum interior noise level of 45 decibels. Testing and maintenance shall only take place on weekdays between the hours of 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m.

equip.cite: LDC art. VI, § 6.8Z.1 (Permitted setback encroachments) [PDF p.702]
equip.text: Except for fences as set forth in section 6.8F[8.27], every part of every required setback shall be open and unobstructed from structures 36 inches above the ground upward. Notwithstanding this section, no encroachment may violate the State Building Code or the State Fire Prevention Code.

equip.cite: LDC art. VI, § 6.8Z.1.a [PDF p.702]
equip.text: Utility facilities, lamp posts, mailboxes, horticultural growths, and garden accoutrements including, but not limited to, pergolas, arbors, and trellises greater than 36 inches in height are permitted to encroach in required setbacks so long as they do not create a traffic hazard as determined by the traffic engineer.

equip.cite: LDC art. VI, § 6.8Z.5 (LP and propane tanks) [PDF p.703]
equip.text: LP and propane tanks. All permitted above ground liquified petroleum (LP) and propane tanks may encroach three feet into the side and rear setbacks; however, all gas tanks, regardless of location, must be screened by vegetation equal to or greater than the height of the gas tank. Buried tanks which do not protrude above ground are not subject to the setback limitations of this zoning code.

equip.cite: LDC art. VI, § 6.8Z.7 [PDF p.703-704]
equip.text: The replacement for an existing air conditioning unit or pool pump, made nonconforming as a result of the adoption of this provision on August 12, 2014 may be installed in the same location as the pre-existing unit provided all the following are met: a. The replacement results in no greater encroachment into any required setback area than the unit it replaces and meets all other requirements of the LDC; b. The replacement pool pump is a variable speed unit; c. The replacement air conditioning unit is a new, not previously owned, unit that was manufactured not more than two years prior to the date of installation.

equip.cite: LDC art. VI, § 6.8C.2 (Building height limitations and exceptions thereto) [PDF p.689]
equip.text: The following features are exempt from the height limitations set forth in this section and under the individual district regulations, provided they conform to the requirements set forth in subsection 2.b.: a. Exempt features. (1) Chimneys, house of worship spires and elevator shafts, (2) Flagpoles and similar devices, (3) Heating and air conditioning, solar collectors, and similar equipment with appropriate screening. b. Requirements for exemption. (1) Not more than one-third of the total roof area may be consumed by such features. (2) The features described in subsection 2.a., above, must be set back from the edge of the roof a minimum distance of one foot for every foot by which such features extend above the roof surface of the principal building to which they are attached.

equip.cite: LDC art. VIII, § 8.26.4 (Accessory structures - location, setbacks, and lot coverage) [PDF p.745]
equip.text: Location, setbacks, and lot coverage. All accessory structures are subject to lot coverage and impervious surface coverage requirements, required setbacks as provided for within the applicable zoning district except as otherwise permitted under section 6.8Z, Permitted setback encroachments.

equip.cite: LDC art. VIII, § 8.26.3.e (Accessory structures - flood prevention) [PDF p.745]
equip.text: Have mechanical, plumbing, and electrical systems, including plumbing fixtures, elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus three feet or elevation approved by the Florida Department of Environmental Protection for coastal high hazard areas and areas west side of the coastal construction line (CCCL).

equip.cite: LDC art. IX, § 9.54.1 (Accessory structures below the base flood elevation) [PDF p.780-781]
equip.text: Accessory structures are permitted below the base flood elevation provided the accessory structures are used only for parking or storage and: (1) If located in special flood hazard areas (zone A/AE) other than coastal high hazard areas and Coastal A zones, are one-story and not larger than 600 square feet and have flood openings in accordance with Section R322.2 of the Florida Building Code, Residential. (2) If located in coastal high hazard areas (zone V/VE) and Coastal A zones, are not located below elevated buildings and are not larger than 100 square feet. (3) Are anchored to resist flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from flood loads. (4) Have flood damage-resistant materials used below the base flood elevation plus three feet. (5) Have mechanical, plumbing and electrical systems, including plumbing fixtures, elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus three feet.

equip.cite: LDC art. IX, § 9.73(4) (General requirements for other development) [PDF p.785]
equip.text: Have mechanical, plumbing, and electrical systems above the design flood elevation, except that minimum electric service required to address life safety and electric code requirements is permitted below the design flood elevation provided it conforms to the provisions of the electrical part of building code for wet locations.

equip.cite: LDC art. IX, § 9.70 (Above-ground tanks, not elevated) [PDF p.784]
equip.text: Above-ground tanks that do not meet the elevation requirements of section 9.71 of this ordinance shall: (1) Be permitted in flood hazard areas (Zone A) other than coastal high hazard areas and Coastal A Zones, provided the tanks are anchored or otherwise designed and constructed to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions of the design flood, including the effects of buoyancy assuming the tank is empty and the effects of flood-borne debris. (2) Not be permitted in coastal high hazard areas (Zone V) and Coastal A Zones.

equip.cite: LDC art. IX, § 9.71 (Above-ground tanks, elevated) [PDF p.784]
equip.text: Above-ground tanks in flood hazard areas shall be attached to and elevated to or above the design flood elevation on a supporting structure that is designed to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement during conditions of the design flood. Tank-supporting structures shall meet the foundation requirements of the applicable flood hazard area.

equip.cite: LDC art. IX, § 9.69 (Underground tanks) [PDF p.784]
equip.text: Underground tanks in flood hazard areas shall be anchored to prevent flotation, collapse or lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads during conditions of the design flood, including the effects of buoyancy assuming the tank is empty.

equip.cite: LDC art. IX, § 9.72 (Tank inlets and vents) [PDF p.785]
equip.text: Tank inlets, fill openings, outlets and vents shall be: (1) At or above the design flood elevation or fitted with covers designed to prevent the inflow of floodwater or outflow of the contents of the tanks during conditions of the design flood; and (2) Anchored to prevent lateral movement resulting from hydrodynamic and hydrostatic loads, including the effects of buoyancy, during conditions of the design flood.

equip.cite: LDC art. IX, § 9.76 (Other development in coastal high hazard areas (Zone V) and Coastal A Zones) [PDF p.786]
equip.text: In coastal high hazard areas and Coastal A Zones, development activities other than buildings and structures shall be permitted only if also authorized by the appropriate federal, state or local authority; if located outside the footprint of, and not structurally attached to, buildings and structures; and if analyses prepared by qualified registered design professionals demonstrate no harmful diversion of floodwaters or wave run-up and wave reflection that would increase damage to adjacent buildings and structures.

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances § 14-28, amending FBC Building 1612.4.3 (Elevation requirements) [PDF p.225]
equip.text: The minimum elevation requirements for buildings and structures in all flood hazard areas, and for buildings and structures seaward of the Coastal Construction Control Line, shall be the higher of the elevation specified in ASCE 24, the base flood elevation plus 3 feet (610 mm), or the elevation required by Section 3109 and the Florida Department of Environmental Protection.

equip.cite: Code of Ordinances § 14-28, amending FBC Residential R322.3.2 (Coastal high-hazard elevation) [PDF p.226]
equip.text: Buildings and structures erected within coastal high-hazard areas (Zone V and those zones seaward of the Coastal Construction Control Line) and Coastal A Zones, shall be elevated so that the bottom of the lowest horizontal structure members supporting the lowest floor, with the exception of pilings, pile caps, columns, grade beams and bracing, is elevated to or above the base flood elevation plus 3 feet or the design flood elevation, whichever is higher.

equip.cite: LDC art. VII, § 7.2A (Setback from the erosion control line) [PDF p.707]
equip.text: Anything to the contrary contained in this ordinance notwithstanding, no person, firm, partnership, corporation or public agency shall construct any structure or building, including any dwelling, hotel, motel, apartment building or other multifamily dwelling, nor construct any structures or facilities appurtenant to existing structures or buildings, including patios, garages, sheds, swimming pools or spas within 50 feet of the erosion control line as established by the State of Florida. 1. Variances. The development special magistrate shall have no authority to grant any variance from the provisions of this paragraph that would permit any excavation or construction as hereinabove specified within 50 feet of the erosion control line as established by the State of Florida.

equip.cite: LDC art. VII, § 7.2B (Construction seaward of the coastal construction control line) [PDF p.707]
equip.text: Construction seaward of the coastal construction control line shall be subject to all laws and regulations of the State of Florida, and the City of Holmes Beach Code of Ordinances unless contrary to state law.

equip.text: Except for pools located in waterfront setbacks with seawalls, pools and associated ancillary structures are subject to the following limitations and requirements: (1) No pool, or other structure ancillary to a pool may be located in any required setback.

palmetto.name: Palmetto
palmetto.source: Code of Ordinances, Appendix B — Zoning Code (adopted by Ord. No. 387, § 1, Nov. 20, 1989). Districts established at Art. II, Sec. 2.1. Dimensional envelope is

equip.cite: Mechanical equipment — Zoning Code Appendix B, Art. V, Sec. 5.3(b) "Permitted projections into required yards" (PDF p.921, code p.2679)
equip.text: "Mechanical equipment, such as air conditioning units, pumps, heating and pool equipment, and similar installations may not project into the required front yard(s), but may project up to five (5) feet into required rear and side yard(s)." (Ord. No. 2019-04, § 1, 6-3-19.) This is the controlling placement rule for condensers, pool pumps and similar installations in Palmetto. It does NOT name a generator. It is a permitted-projection allowance measured as an intrusion into the required yard, not a distance to the lot line; the residual clearance to the lot line therefore depends on the district's required side or rear yard (e.g. 5 ft required side in RS-4 or MHP-1 means the equipment could reach the line, while 10 ft in RS-1 leaves 5 ft).

equip.cite: Architectural features — Appendix B, Art. V, Sec. 5.3(a) (PDF p.921)
equip.text: "Certain architectural features, such as cornices, eaves, stairs, and gutters, may project no more than four (4) feet into the required front yard, five (5) feet into the required rear yard and two (2) feet into the required side yard." Printed immediately above the mechanical-equipment subsection and quoted here to show that the code treats mechanical equipment under a separate, more permissive allowance.

equip.cite: Accessory structures in residential districts — Appendix B, Art. VI, Sec. 6.8(a) (PDF p.926, code p.2680.4)
equip.text: "(1) Accessory structures shall not exceed fifteen (15) feet in height, and the total square footage of all accessory structures shall not exceed forty (40) percent of the total lot coverage. (2) Accessory structures shall not be erected in any required front yard. (3) Accessory structures may occupy required corner or side yards, provided they are located an equal distance from the front property line as any part of the principal structure(s) on the same lot. Accessory structures shall be located a minimum of three (3) feet from the side or corner lot line. (4) Accessory structures may occupy required rear yards, provided they are located a minimum of five (5) feet from the rear lot line." Applies if a generator, tank or equipment enclosure is treated as an accessory structure rather than as mechanical equipment under Sec. 5.3(b); the code does not say which classification governs a pad-mounted generator.

equip.cite: Portable accessory structures — Appendix B, Art. VI, Sec. 6.8(b) (PDF p.927, code p.2680.5)
equip.text: "Portable accessory structures shall meet all of the requirements for permanent accessory structures as outlines in subsection (a) above and shall also meet the following specific requirements: (1) Only one (1) portable accessory structure shall be allowed per lot. (2) The portable accessory structure shall be properly anchored in a method approved by the building department. (3) Portable accessory structures shall not be permitted within the required waterfront setbacks of waterfront property. (4) No mechanical equipment not customarily associated with residential uses shall be operated within or attached to the structure."

equip.cite: Accessory structures in nonresidential districts — Appendix B, Art. VI, Sec. 6.8(c) (PDF p.927)
equip.text: "(1) Accessory structures shall meet all the requirements of subsection (b) above. (2) Trailers, mobile homes, and tractor trailers shall not be used as permanent or portable accessory structures. (3) Said structures shall meet the yard requirements of the zoning district in which it is located. (4) Accessory structures shall not exceed fifteen (15) feet in height."

equip.cite: Swimming pools and pool cages — Appendix B, Art. VI, Sec. 6.7 (PDF p.926, code p.2680.4)
equip.text: "(a) Location: Swimming pools may be located within side, rear, or corner yards but shall not be allowed in the required front yards. Swimming pools shall be located a minimum of five (5) feet from any side, rear, or corner lot line as measured from the water's edge. Locational criteria are subject to the variance provisions of section 13.3 and section 13.6, appendix B, of this Code. (b) Enclosure:... In addition, all screened cages shall be located a minimum of five (5) feet from any side, rear, or corner lot line." (Ord. No. 03-778, § 1, 5-19-03.) Governs the pool and its cage; the pool PUMP is governed by Sec. 5.3(b) above.

equip.cite: Fuel tanks in the Mobile Home Park district — Appendix B, Art. VI, Sec. 6.16(g) (PDF p.933)
equip.text: "Fuel tanks and garbage cans shall be allowed only at the rear of lots and must be enclosed by cement blocks." (Ord. No. 389, § 1, 1-15-90; Ord. No. 01-705, § 1, 4-16-01.) This is the only LP/fuel-tank placement rule in the Palmetto code. It applies to lots within the MHP-1 district only and prints no distance.

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical equipment — Appendix B, Art. V, Sec. 5.2(a) (PDF p.920-921)
equip.text: "Excluded portions of structures: Except as specifically provided herein, the height limitations of this code shall not apply to any roof structures for housing elevators, stairways, tanks, ventilating fans, solar energy collectors, or similar equipment required to operate and maintain the building, provided that such structures shall not cover more than twenty (20) percent of roof area or extend over ten (10) feet in height." A height exemption, not a lot-line rule.

equip.cite: Rooftop mechanical equipment appearance — Code of Ordinances § 7-240(a) (Requirements for roofs, downtown appearance code; PDF p.273)
equip.text: "Chimneys and all other rooftop structures shall be repaired and maintained in the same manner as required for the rear and side walls. Any part of the building visible from the street or from other buildings shall be finished so as to be harmonious with other visible building walls. Television and radio antennas, pipes, duct work and mechanical equipment, such as air conditioning units and auxiliary enclosures or sheds, shall be erected in an inconspicuous manner." (Ord. No. 470, § 4, 12-16-91.) An appearance rule with no distance.

equip.cite: Noise exemptions — Code of Ordinances § 5-3(6) and (7) (PDF p.212-213)
equip.text: "The following activities or sources are exempt from the requirements of this article:... (6) Any air conditioning or pool pump equipment when in reasonable mechanical condition operating with the standard sound and vibration control systems typically provided by the manufacturer. Air conditioning units are presumed to be in reasonable mechanical condition if the unit meets the sound specifications contained in the Air Conditioning, Heating, and Refrigeration Institute's ('AHRI') Applied Directory of Certified Product Performance Variable Air Volume Terminals. (7) Any power generator operating during a state of emergency declared by the governor." This is the ONLY place in the entire Palmetto code where a generator is named. It is a noise-ordinance exemption, not a siting rule — it prints no distance and no relationship to a lot line — so namesGen is false. Note the exemption covers a generator only while a gubernatorial state of emergency is in effect; routine exercise/testing of a standby generator is not exempted by its terms.

gen.cite: Equipment encroachment into required yards — LDR Ch. 26, Art. 7
gen.text: Generators may sit in a required yard. Generators — with A/C units, pool and solar equipment — may encroach up to 4 ft into a required side yard and up to 4 ft into a required rear yard. Where the yard is 5 ft or less wide, the projection cannot exceed half the yard width. Up to 4 ft into a recorded drainage or utility easement is also allowed, but nothing permanent may sit in an easement in use. Screening, for new construction outside the Special Residential Overlay: the equipment must be screened from view at grade from the public right-of-way by 100% landscaping, a landscaping/fence combination, or an architecturally compatible wall or opaque fence panel — screen no more than 6 ft tall, 8 ft long (or the equipment length, whichever is less) and 4 ft wide.

equip.cite: Accessory uses and structures — LDC Ch. 4, variance limit § 5.4.G
equip.text: Moore Haven prints no dedicated generator ordinance. A permanently installed generator is a customary accessory use and structure, so the yard rules govern placement: in the rear yard, accessory buildings and appurtenances may occupy up to 30% of the required rear yard; in a side yard only architectural appurtenances may project. Site the generator in the rear yard, clear of the required front and side yards. Above-ground LP tanks follow the same accessory placement plus Fire Code separation distances. A variance may deviate at most 35% from a district standard (§ 5.4.G). Confirm placement with the Moore Haven Building & Zoning Official before siting.

equip.cite: Accessory structures and mechanical equipment — Code Ch. 36
equip.text: A standby generator is treated as an accessory structure and mechanical equipment: placed in a side or rear yard, no closer than 5 ft to the side or rear lot line, and not in the front yard or in an easement. Sponge Docks and waterfront parcels sit in flood zones, so FBC / ASCE 24 elevation applies on AE and VE lots, along with NFPA 37 listing clearances and NFPA 58 LP-tank distances.
